articles.title: Emergency Department Management of Body-Fluid Exposures Receiving Human Immunodeficiency Virus Post-Exposure Prophylaxis: Adherence to Australian Guideline Recommendations.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate documented adherence to Australian guideline recommendations for emergency department (ED) management of patients receiving human immunodeficiency virus post-exposure prophylaxis (HIV PEP) and explore variation by exposure category.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective, dual-site cohort study included consecutive patients dispensed HIV PEP at two Australian EDs between 1 June 2020 and 1 June 2025. Patients with known HIV infection or managed through a dedicated sexual assault pathway were excluded. Records were reviewed for documented exposure-risk assessment, applicable baseline investigations, antiretroviral regimen, counselling, discharge information and clinician-documented follow-up plan or referral. Exploratory comparisons were undertaken by exposure category.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-seven patients were included. Clinician documented follow-up plan or referral was documented in 73 (94.8%), and 61 (79.2%) received the first-line regimen recommended by the applicable guidance. Complete recommended management was documented in 8 (10.4%), exposure-risk assessment in 36 (46.8%) and complete baseline investigations in 10 (13.0%). Compared with occupational and other community exposures, consensual sexual exposures had lower documented exposure-risk assessment (36.2% vs. 78.9%; OR: 0.16, 95% CI: 0.03-0.57) and complete baseline investigations (5.2% vs. 36.8%; OR: 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01-0.50).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients dispensed HIV PEP, recommended regimens and follow-up were commonly documented, but complete recommended assessment and investigation were uncommon. A structured ED body-fluid exposure pathway should be prospectively evaluated.

articles.title: Effectiveness of intrathecal dexmedetomidine versus fentanyl as additives to hyperbaric bupivacaine on postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing Cesarean section.
Focus Where It Matters: Design and Implementation of a Physiology-Based Care Pathway for Traumatic Shock.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Traumatic shock lacks a consensus definition, and in blunt-predominant systems its causes are heterogeneous. Simple physiological parameters remain the most universally available basis for early recognition. We describe the design and staged implementation of a physiology-based care pathway for traumatic shock and evaluate its implementation through staff experience.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Single-centre quality-improvement and implementation project at an Australian Level 1 trauma centre, reported per SQUIRE 2.0. The pathway comprised physiology-based activation (systolic blood pressure ≤ 90 mmHg, shock index > 1, prehospital blood or senior clinician concern), structured pre-arrival preparation, trauma bay and equipment standardisation, task-based team roles, prioritised life-saving interventions and senior-led disposition, supported by simulation and embedded quality improvement. Components were implemented between June and November 2022. Evaluation comprised pre-intervention (2021) and post-implementation (2025) staff surveys, summarised as top-box favourability, with cross-sectional characterisation of the shocked cohort. Clinical effectiveness was not assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 3667 major trauma patients, 324 (8.8%) met shocked trauma criteria; these patients were younger, more severely injured and had markedly higher mortality (emergency department death 6.8% vs. 0.4%). Favourable ratings of trauma bay equipment and environment rose from approximately one-quarter to 87.0%. Post-implementation, staff reported high favourability for timely life-saving interventions (88.9%), pathway embedding (85.2%) and role confidence (86.5%). Leadership clarity, communication and reliable debriefing did not improve and were identified as ongoing targets.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A physiology-based traumatic shock pathway was feasibly implemented and embedded, with high staff-reported readiness and clear targets for refinement. Effectiveness remains to be established.

articles.title: Inequitable Distribution: The Healthcare Workforce Disparity Facing Regional, Rural and Remote Communities.

abstract.text: The inequitable distribution of healthcare resources between metropolitan and regional, rural and remote (RRR) areas continues to present challenges. Previous research has identified factors likely influencing medical student decisions to practice outside metropolitan areas, including rural origin and rural training rotations. This issue of Trainee Focus will focus on exploring RRR training opportunities and new training requirements for ACEM trainees.

articles.title: The Association of Hospital Characteristics With Medicaid Managed Care Hospital Prices.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the association between various hospital characteristics and Medicaid facility prices for several routine procedures.

abstract.label: STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional study of facility claims data from Elevance Health-affiliated Medicaid plans from 22 states plus D.C. We estimated Poisson regression models where the outcome was facility allowed cost ("price") for procedures of interest, and the exposures were hospital characteristics, including children's hospital, critical access hospital (CAH), rurality, system affiliation, teaching designation, for-profit, religious affiliation, government ownership, and hospital size. We report incidence rate ratios (IRRs) from the regression estimates.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE
abstract.text: We analyzed 2021-2023 facility claims for 11 routine procedures in the outpatient or emergency department (ED) settings, including tympanostomy, colonoscopy, and ED evaluation and management (E/M) Levels 2-5. The claims were joined with data from the American Hospital Directory to identify hospital characteristics. The study included 2,250,325 children and 2,341,063 adults who received at least one of the procedures of interest.

abstract.label: PRINCIPAL FINDINGS
abstract.text: The largest price differences were at children's hospitals and CAHs. For all child procedures, prices were higher at children's hospitals relative to other acute care hospitals: the largest estimate was for ED E/M Level 2 (IRR = 2.51; 95% CI, 2.14-2.95). Children's hospital estimates represented 93%-151% higher prices for ED procedures and 23%-48% higher prices for outpatient procedures. CAHs had higher prices for almost all procedures: for children the largest estimate was for tympanostomy (IRR = 1.78; 95% CI, 1.45-2.18), representing 78% higher prices, and for adults the largest estimate was for MRI (IRR = 2.43; 95% CI, 2.13-2.76), representing 143% higher prices. Results were mixed for other hospital characteristics.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study suggests much higher Medicaid managed care facility prices at children's hospitals and CAHs for several routine procedures. More research is needed to understand what is driving the observed differences in hospital prices.

articles.title: Post-Traumatic Amnesia Testing for Suspected Concussion in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Among patients discharged from the ED after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), 16%-25% experience post-concussive symptoms for up to 3 months after injury. However, the assessment of mTBI in the ED is variable. A common tool for the assessment of mTBI in Australia is the Abbreviated Westmead Post-Traumatic Amnesia Scale (A-WPTAS). The aim of this study was to report the proportion of patients who were detected to have post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) following a head injury and whether this varied by reported loss of consciousness (LOC), age, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and mechanisms of injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a single-centre, retrospective cohort study. Data were extracted from patients' electronic medical records. All patients presenting to the ED between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2021 with a head injury, documented results of A-WPTAS, and aged ≥ 18 years were included for analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 6259 patients included, and 5746 (91.8%, 95% CI: 91.1%-92.5%) passed the A-WPTAS. -PTA was more frequent among patients who presented with GCS 13 or 14, male patients, those with low falls and presenting after hours. Among patients with documented LOC, the pass rate was 90.6% (95% CI: 88.8%-92.4%), and among those without LOC, it was 92% (95% CI: 91.3%-92.8%); p = 0.13.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PTA was detected in a small proportion of patients tested in the ED. PTA was associated with low initial GCS, but not with reported LOC. Among patients discharged from the ED, follow-up for persistent post-concussion symptoms is indicated.

articles.title: The epidemiology of acute respiratory syndromes in children presenting to public hospitals across NSW, Australia, 2013-2019.
articles.journal: Aust N Z J Public Health
articles.journal_full: Australian and New Zealand journal of public health

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The objective of the study is to describe the epidemiology of childhood acute respiratory infection (ARI) across New South Wales (NSW).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Description of demographics, seasonal trends, and incidence rates (IRs) for paediatric ARI emergency departments (ED) presentations using NSW Public Health Rapid, Emergency, Disease and Syndromic Surveillance (PHREDSS) data from 2013 to 2019.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ARI ED presentations were numerous (n=1,099,723). Most presentations were respiratory-specific (72.4%); the leading diagnoses were non-specific ARI (34.5%), asthma/wheeze (18.4%), croup (14.1%), bronchiolitis (10.8%), and pharyngitis/tonsillitis (10.0%). Asthma/wheeze, bronchiolitis, breathing problems, and pneumonia/pneumonitis presentations were most often of high urgency (21.9-28.1%; triage categories 1 or 2) and often led to hospitalisation (38.2-54.7%). Croup was also often of high urgency (17.5%), but few required admission (8.0%). The annualised ARI IR was highest among children <1 year (3,710/10,000 population/year, standard deviation [SD] = 308.46). Bronchiolitis presentations had the highest aged-specific annualised IR at 938/10,000 <1 year (SD = 93.97).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The burden of childhood ARI is substantial. Nearly four in every ten infants present to the ED with ARI each year, with a quarter presenting with bronchiolitis. Croup and asthma/wheeze presentations are also numerous and of high urgency. Non-specific coding is common.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH
abstract.text: More specific coding practices could further enhance syndromic surveillance systems, and current surveillance should target croup and asthma/wheeze for enhanced characterisation.

articles.title: Transcutaneous Pacing in the Prehospital Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Electrical Capture.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Transcutaneous pacing (TCP) treats hemodynamically unstable bradycardia refractory to pharmacologic management. Effective TCP requires electrical and mechanical capture to augment perfusion. Little is known about prehospital TCP and capture incidence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients treated with prehospital TCP by an emergency medical services agency between 2017 and 2024. Continuous electrocardiogram recordings from cardiac monitors were reviewed. Electrical capture was the primary outcome, defined as a widened QRS with a distinct T wave following a TCP spike. Secondary measures included capture duration, clinician-verbalized pulse during pacing, plethysmograph waveform alignment, and changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse oximetry, and end-tidal carbon dioxide.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-six patients received attempted TCP. Median age was 70 years (interquartile range [IQR] 58-85), and 34% were female. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was administered in 59% of patients. Electrical capture was achieved in 18 patients (32%). Among patients who achieved electrical capture, complete capture occurred a mean of 27% (standard deviation 30%) of attempted pacing duration. The median SBP change was +22 (IQR: -2-82) mmHg in patients with electrical capture and 0 (IQR: -29-7) mmHg in those with only rare-to-absent capture (p = 0.031). During TCP, clinicians verbalized a palpable pulse 26 times across 19 patients. Only 4 instances (15%) coincided with electrical capture.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Electrical capture during prehospital TCP occurred in a minority of patients and was often intermittent. Prehospital identification of mechanical capture using routine clinical indicators was difficult and unreliable. Future work should standardize capture definitions and physiologic measurements to determine when TCP produces clinically meaningful perfusion.

articles.title: The Accuracy and Precision of Gravity-Driven Infusions.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: When infusion pumps are unavailable in the prehospital setting, clinicians must estimate fluid flow by counting drops in a drip chamber. We aimed to assess the accuracy and precision of gravity-driven infusions and to estimate the magnitude of inaccuracy and imprecision attributable to human and non-human factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We recruited 55 paramedics to participate in a structured, experimental, simulated study under controlled laboratory conditions, in which each participant set nine drip rates as accurately as possible on a standardized setup. Measurements of flow were made visually (drip rate) and volumetrically (delivered fluid). Volumetric measurements were used to represent overall error, visual measurements were used to represent human error, and the difference was used to represent non-human error. We measured accuracy (percentage error) and precision (mean absolute deviation) using the natural log of error factor to represent the multiplicative decomposition of human and non-human error additively. Mixed effect models were used to assess accuracy and precision across targeted drip rates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Inaccuracy and imprecision varied by targeted drip rate. Overall inaccuracy ranged from -45.3% (95%CI, -52.7% to -36.8%) to 5.8% (95%CI, -8.5% to 22.3%). Human inaccuracy ranged from -38.8% (95%CI, -46.0% to -30.8%) to 44.1% (95%CI, 27.1% to 63.4%). Non-human inaccuracy ranged from -26.7% (95%CI, -30.1% to -23.2%) to -6.8% (95%CI -11.1% to -2.3%). Imprecision was primarily driven by human factors. The degree of human variation between trial participants ranged from 24.2% (95%CI, 15.3% to 33.7%) to 43.7% (95%CI, 33.4% to 54.9%) across targeted rates. The targeted drip rate of 1gtt/s was more accurate than the pool of all other targeted rates (absolute error 31.1% versus 48.5%). Targeted drip rates of whole numbers were more accurate than targeted drip rates of fractional numbers (absolute error 40.7% versus 54.1%). Targeted drip rates below 1gtt/s were more accurate than rates above 1gtt/s (absolute error 35.3% versus 63.1%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Gravity-driven fluid delivery exhibits inaccuracy and imprecision, which varies by targeted rate. While potentially modifiable human factors may improve the accuracy of this technique, non-human error contributes substantially to inaccuracy. There is a need to assess whether this inaccuracy and imprecision adversely affect patient outcomes.

articles.title: Trends in Infant Mortality by Out-of-Hospital Birthplace in the United States From 2017 to 2023.
Co-ordinated swimming and spatial co-occurrence of tiger shark (Galeocerdo cuvier) at the Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, Brazil.

abstract.text: Co-ordinated circular swimming by tiger sharks (Galeocerdo cuvier) was documented by divers in the Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, Brazil, on 1 October 2023 under non-provisioned conditions. At least six individuals maintained circular movement over 20 min. A second observation in October 2024 documented at least three sharks, although co-ordinated swimming could not be confirmed. Passive acoustic telemetry from 12 tagged tiger sharks revealed simultaneous detections of up to three individuals, indicating temporal co-occurrence near the site. These observations document an uncommon behavioral pattern and highlight the need for long-term studies.

articles.title: Acute Stone-Related Healthcare Utilization Before Definitive Stone Surgery: Variation by Surgical Modality and Sociodemographic Characteristics.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterize acute stone-related healthcare utilization during the year before definitive stone surgery and examine variation by surgical modality and sociodemographic characteristics.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Adults (≥ 18 years) undergoing first definitive stone surgery with ureteroscopy, shock wave lithotripsy, or percutaneous nephrolithotomy in Epic Cosmos from 2015 through 2025 were identified. Acute stone event days included unique days involving stone-related emergency department visits or hospitalizations, decompression procedures, or infections during the preceding year. Quasi-Poisson regression evaluated differences by surgical modality and, in separate modality-adjusted models, race, Social Vulnerability Index quartile, and Rural-Urban Commuting Area category.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,074,341 patients, 79.4% underwent ureteroscopy, 16.5% shock wave lithotripsy, and 4.1% percutaneous nephrolithotomy; 69.6% experienced at least one acute stone event day. Compared with ureteroscopy, expected event counts were higher before percutaneous nephrolithotomy (incidence rate ratio 1.18, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.22) and lower before shock wave lithotripsy (incidence rate ratio 0.63, 95% confidence interval 0.61-0.65). Compared with White patients, burden was higher among Black patients (incidence rate ratio 1.12, 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.14). Burden increased progressively across Social Vulnerability Index quartiles, reaching 16% higher in the most versus least vulnerable quartile. No meaningful differences occurred by Rural-Urban Commuting Area category.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Acute stone-related healthcare utilization before definitive surgery was common and varied by surgical modality, race, and neighborhood social vulnerability, but not rurality. These findings identify populations experiencing disproportionate preoperative morbidity and support further evaluation of coordinated pathways from acute presentation to definitive stone care.

articles.title: [Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation in Hungarian emergency departments].

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation (not in cardiac arrest) is a critical, high-risk procedure in emergency care. Internationally, safety improves through standardized procedures, equipment, documentation, and training.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To map current practice in Hungarian emergency departments regarding who performs the procedure, the degree of regulation, the available drugs and devices, documentation practices, and training.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional online questionnaire survey. Based on the department-head registry of the Hungarian Society of Emergency Medicine, we sent the questionnaire to the heads of all 44 Hungarian emergency departments. Data were collected between May and July 2026 and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The response rate was 52% (23/44). In 96% of the departments, the procedure was routinely performed by emergency care providers. A written protocol existed in 48% of the departments (mandatory in 17%). Propofol, a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent, and a bougie were available in all departments. Non-invasive ventilation was available in 96% of departments, videolaryngoscopes in 74%, and capnographs in 78%; however, only 39% mandated capnography. In 52% of the responding departments, no dedicated procedural documentation was produced, and 57% had no regular topic-specific training.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: In the responding departments, the procedure was performed predominantly by emergency clinicians, and the basic pharmacological and equipment requirements were largely met. However, organizational safeguards for patient safety - a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation, and regular training - were often lacking, indicating both deviations from international recommendations and clear targets for improvement.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In the responding Hungarian emergency departments, the airway management practice for patients with preserved circulation was highly heterogeneous and insufficiently standardized. Priorities for improvement include a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation and a national registry, and regular training. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1835-1842.

articles.title: Beyond hemoglobin thresholds: identifying clinical predictors for red blood cell transfusion in pediatric severe anemia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: We aimed to evaluate the etiological causes of severe anemia and identify clinical and laboratory predictors for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in the pediatric emergency department (PED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 186 children (1 month-18 years) with severe anemia as per the WHO age criterion in a tertiary PED (2023-2025). LASSO and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of transfusion, while quantile regression analyzed Hb increment.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median age was 8 years 2 months, and 57.5% were female. Impaired red cell formation was the primary mechanism (70.4%), predominantly nutritional anemia (53.2%). Transfusion was performed in 88 patients (47.3%). Multivariable analysis identified heart murmur (OR = 16.08, p = 0.004), hepatomegaly (OR = 8.25, p = 0.021), splenomegaly (OR = 5.33, p = 0.026), tachycardia (OR = 5.28, p < 0.001), lower Hb (OR = 0.26, p < 0.001), normocytosis (OR = 8.99, p = 0.002), and elevated RDW (OR = 0.04, p = 0.007) as independent predictors. Quantile regression predicted a median Hb increment of 1.80 g/dL per 10 mL/kg transfusion (p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our results demonstrate that symptomatic severe anemia is strongly associated with transfusion. The administration of RBC transfusion should not rely solely on absolute Hb thresholds; rather, bedside clinical indicators and laboratory findings are necessary to optimize pediatric emergency management.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: RBC transfusion administration is driven by a combination of absolute Hb levels, specific laboratory markers, and bedside clinical signs of hemodynamic instability, rather than strict Hb thresholds alone. This study identifies robust independent predictors for transfusion using a LASSO regression model and quantifies the expected median Hb increment (1.80 g/dL per 10 mL/kg) via quantile regression. These findings contextualize the management of severe pediatric anemia by highlighting the necessity of integrating bedside clinical assessments with Hb values to evaluate urgent transfusion needs. Emphasizing the evaluation of multi-lineage cytopenias facilitates the earlier identification of underlying malignancies.

articles.title: Anticipatory anxiety as a factor associated with the experience of venipuncture: a prospective study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Anticipatory anxiety may affect how children experience invasive procedures, although its role in pain and procedural anxiety has not been fully established. The aim of our study was to analyze its association with the experience of venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheterization and assess whether the association remained significant after accounting for other procedural factors.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational study in a pediatric emergency department between October 2023 and October 2024. The sample consisted of children aged 3-12 years undergoing venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheter insertion. Anticipatory anxiety, procedural anxiety, and pain were assessed. We analyzed the correlations between these variables and fitted multivariable logistic regression models to identify factors associated with severe pain and severe procedural anxiety.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 140 patients were included; 39.3% had severe anticipatory anxiety, 39.3% severe pain, and 55.7% severe procedural anxiety. Anticipatory anxiety was significantly correlated to procedural anxiety (ρ=0.611) and pain (ρ=0.382), with stronger correlations in the group of patients aged 8-12 years (ρ=0.776 and ρ=0.603, respectively). Severe anticipatory anxiety was associated with a higher likelihood of severe procedural anxiety and severe pain, and these associations remained significant after the different adjustments.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Severe anticipatory anxiety was independently associated with a worse experience during venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheter insertion. The stronger association observed in children aged 8-12 years suggests that assessing the emotional state of the child before the procedure may help identify patients at greater risk of severe pain and procedural anxiety.

articles.title: [Diving and women's health: a literature review].

abstract.text: The proportion of women practising self-contained underwater breathing apparatus diving is steadily increasing, making an accurate assessment of the specific risks and benefits of this activity in women necessary. This review synthesizes the available data on the influence of sex on the risk of decompression sickness (DCS), barotrauma and narcosis, as well as the effects of diving on the menstrual cycle, contraception, menopause, fertility and pregnancy. The most robust studies do not show a clear excess risk of DCS in women compared with men for a similar diving profile, although a self-reported database (127,957 dives) reported an excess risk in women, the significance of which is limited by major methodological biases. Data on barotrauma differ according to the organ involved: conflicting for middle-ear barotrauma, but consistent for immersion pulmonary edema, for which female sex is an established independent risk factor; no sex-specific data exist, however, for nitrogen narcosis. An increased risk of DCS during the early menstrual cycle is suggested by several series but remains debated, while no data suggest, conversely, that diving itself alters the cycle. High-risk patent foramen ovale constitutes a significant risk factor for DCS regardless of sex. Data on female fertility and diving are virtually non-existent, and menopause is not in itself a contraindication. Regarding pregnancy, no prospective controlled study is available for ethical reasons; retrospective human data and animal models suggest an increased risk of malformations and fetal complications, particularly during the first trimester. All scientific societies therefore recommend discontinuing scuba diving as soon as pregnancy is planned and throughout pregnancy, while snorkeling remains permitted.

articles.title: Development and Implementation of the Orange Bracelet Program to Increase Recognition of Women Who Recently Gave Birth.
articles.journal_full: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe the development and implementation of the orange post-birth alert bracelet program and provide related resources for clinicians and emergency personnel.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Quality improvement project.

abstract.label: SETTING/LOCAL PROBLEM
abstract.text: Two rural community hospitals in the United States: west central Florida and northwest Illinois.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: We included all patients who gave birth, support persons, maternity staff, emergency department (ED) personnel, and local emergency medical services (EMS) personnel.

abstract.label: INTERVENTION/MEASUREMENTS
abstract.text: An orange silicone bracelet labeled "Post-Birth Alert" was created. Immediately after birth, women and their support persons were educated on warning signs of postpartum complications using the Association of Women's Health, Obstetric and Neonatal Nurses POST-BIRTH Warning Signs program. The women were encouraged to wear the orange bracelet for 12 weeks as a way for emergency personnel to quickly recognize their postpartum status. We educated maternity staff, ED, and EMS personnel. We measured bracelets distributed and the time patients arrived in the ED to the time they were assessed by the emergency care team before and after the implementation. We tracked the number of regional EMS departments that provided education about postpartum emergencies and the orange bracelet program.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Data indicated that the use of the orange bracelet increased the proportion of women recognized as postpartum by ED personnel within 15 min in both hospitals.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The educational campaign and use of the orange post-birth alert bracelet improved the timeliness of recognition of postpartum status. We successfully educated and enhanced collaboration among maternity staff, ED, and EMS personnel about risks to women in the postpartum period.

articles.title: Early recurrence of febrile seizures in the pediatric emergency department: development and internal validation of FSERS, a practical bedside risk score.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Febrile seizures (FS) are common and generally benign. Early recurrence within 24 h does not itself mandate admission or treatment but may prompt reassessment before discharge, particularly when atypical or evolving features raise concern for an alternative acute neurologic diagnosis. We aimed to develop and internally validate a bedside score for early FS recurrence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We included 400 children with confirmed FS presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department (PED) between January 2020 and December 2024. Complex-phenotype FS was defined by focal onset or prolonged duration only. Backward stepwise multivariable logistic regression derived a parsimonious model, followed by 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Early recurrence occurred in 45/400 children (11.2%). Independent predictors were neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.345), seizure duration (aOR 1.154), C-reactive protein (CRP; aOR 1.187), serum sodium (aOR 0.606), and fever-to-seizure interval (aOR 0.821). The continuous model achieved an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.924 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.897. The derived integer FS Early Recurrence Score (FSERS) had an apparent AUC of 0.905 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.887.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: FSERS integrates five readily available variables into an internally validated estimate of early FS recurrence risk. It is not an admission rule, treatment trigger, or diagnostic model for central nervous system infection or acute encephalopathy, and should complement clinical reassessment and red-flag evaluation. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before score-based changes in observation or disposition are considered.

articles.title: Trends in cold-related injuries among patients experiencing homelessness across Ontario, 2018-2025: A retrospective population-based cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Prior research has demonstrated disparities in cold-related injuries among patients experiencing homelessness (PEH) compared to patients not experiencing homelessness (PNEH). We sought to assess regional variation in risks and evaluate trends following recent improvements to local homelessness winter services.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study using linked health administrative data from April 2018 to March 2025 METHODS: PEH were identified via a validated algorithm and frequency-matched 1:1 to PNEH on age, sex, and health region (LHIN). We observed emergency department (ED) visits for cold-related injury over the study period, estimating visit rate ratios (RR) across periods using modified Poisson regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The final matched cohort included 1,312,078 ED visits representing 289,054 patients. PEH (n = 144,527) had significantly higher cold-related injury visit rates provincially (RR 12.4 [95% CI 10.4-14.7] and regionally (ranging from 6.22 [95% CI 2.61-14.85] to 32.30 [95% CI 5.47-190.70]). In 2024/2025, cold-related injury rates among PEH rose significantly province-wide (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12-1.65) and in the City of Toronto (RR 1.46, 95% CI 1.21-1.76). Regional increases were significant in six of 14 health regions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There is strong variation in disparities in cold-related injuries between PEH and frequency matched PNEH. Despite improved homelessness winter programming in certain regions, disparities worsened across Ontario in 2024/2025. Stronger government and community responses to unsheltered homelessness are required to address such exposure-related outcomes.

articles.title: Smart Alerting in Smartphone-Based First Responder Systems and Arrival Before Emergency Medical Services:The ALARM Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Smartphone alerting systems (SAS) aim to increase the proportion of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) cases in which a community first responder (CFR) arrives before emergency medical services (EMS). Many use fixed-radius alerts and ignore estimated arrival times. We compared different alerting strategies to maximize CFR arrival before EMS.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a prospective, randomized three-arm trial, smart alerting (SMA) was compared with fixed-radius strategies (600 m and 2500 m). The primary endpoint was the rate of CFR arrival before EMS. In the SMA arm, responders were dispatched based on individually estimated travel times versus expected ambulance time. Binary endpoints were analyzed using chi-square tests, reporting risk differences and 95% confidence intervals; continuous endpoints used non-parametric tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across 823 activations, 1482 CFR were dispatched. CFR arrived before EMS in 31%, 57%, and 58% of missions in the 600 m, 2500 m, and SMA groups, respectively. Compared with the 600 m strategy, SMA increased pre-EMS arrival (risk difference +26.8%, 95% CI 18.6-34.4; p < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed compared with the 2500 m strategy (risk difference +1.2%, 95% CI -7.0-+9.3; p = 0.80). Response rates were 56%, 83%, and 87%, respectively. In the SMA group, 31% of accepting CFR were excluded because predicted arrival exceeded EMS arrival. Response times were longer with smart alerting reflecting greater dispatch distances.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Smart alerting increased the likelihood of CFR arriving before EMS while reducing dispatches unlikely to achieve pre-EMS arrival. Further research should evaluate its impact on patient outcomes.

articles.title: To cradle or not: assessing the use of a lumbar puncture cradle on lumbar puncture success rates.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Neonatal and infant lumbar puncture success rates range from 50 to 80%, while traumatic lumbar punctures are reported in 30-50%. A novel lumbar puncture cradle, SMöLTAP®, designed to standardize seated positioning may improve procedural outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the first-pass success and traumatic lumbar puncture rates using the cradle compared to the lateral decubitus.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a single-center cohort study from August 2020-October 2024 in a tertiary pediatric emergency department. Term and corrected preterm infants (≥ 37 weeks, ≤ 3 months) requiring a lumbar puncture were identified through an EPIC report. Unstable infants, those requiring opening pressure, performed under sedation or using ultrasound guidance, and charts with missing documentation were excluded. Lumbar punctures using the cradle were identified first, and a stratified random sampling technique was used to select the non-exposed cohort, in which lumbar punctures were performed in the lateral decubitus position. Chi-square analysis and logistic regression were used to analyze lumbar puncture success rates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 142 infants were included (mean age 26 days, 57% male). Cradle use was associated with a higher first-pass success rate: 63%, as opposed to 41% in the control lateral decubitus group p = 0.01. It remained significantly associated with first-pass success after a multivariable logistic regression (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.06-4.68, p = 0.03). Cradle use was associated with fewer traumatic lumbar punctures, 36% versus 59% (p = 0.01), percent difference 23% (95% CI 6.6-37.8). There was no difference in the overall success rate, 80% versus 70%, p = 0.17.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The cradle is a promising tool that may improve first-pass success, reduce traumatic lumbar punctures, and provide more precise management of febrile infants requiring a lumbar puncture, thereby reducing clinical diagnostic and management challenges.

articles.title: Comparison of Individual Clinical and Health Services Use Profiles Between Deaths From Unintentional Opioid and Other Drug Poisoning and Deaths From Suicide: A Quebec Linked Health Databases Study: Comparaison entre les décès par intoxications non intentionnelles dues aux opioïdes et à d'autres drogues et les décès par suicide selon les profils individuels d'utilisation des services cliniques et des services de santé : une étude de bases de données du Québec sur la santé.
articles.journal_full: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie

abstract.text: ObjectiveWe sought to compare unintentional opioid and other drug poisoning (OODP) and suicide deaths regarding clinical and service use profiles.MethodWe undertook a retrospective, administrative data-based study to identify these deaths in Quebec from 2003 to 2018. Descriptive variables were chosen among those available in the Quebec Integrated Chronic Disease Surveillance System, classified according to Anderson's model of health services as determinants of health outcomes. We also used multivariable logistic regression to compare OODP and suicide deaths.ResultsWe identified 2,002 OODP deaths and 16,555 suicides. In both groups, a considerable proportion were male, aged 30-64 years, and pertained to materially and socially deprived areas, and most presented with at least one mental health or substance-related disorder (SRD) and used primary and specialist healthcare services in the last year before death. When comparing the two groups, some factors predominantly characterized OODP deaths (e.g., living in the Montreal area, several past-year physical comorbidities, SRDs) or suicide deaths (e.g., male sex, depression and bipolar disorder, psychiatrist visit). Similarities also emerged, including several psychiatric comorbidities (anxiety disorder, cluster B personality disorder, schizophrenia and other psychotic disorder), most past-year physical comorbidities and several factors regarding service use in the last year before death (e.g., hospitalizations and general practitioner visits/psychotherapy visits).ConclusionsWhile some distinctions in individual clinical and service use emerged between OODP and suicide deaths, several similarities also arose, including the generally high burden of mental disorders for both populations. Suicide prevention recommendations of better detection, engagement and management of individuals with depression or SRDs at the primary care and general hospital levels, with support from coordinated mental health and addiction services, might also represent a potentially effective strategy alongside existing overdose prevention efforts and key involvement of peer-led and community-based resources to decrease OODP deaths.

articles.title: Cerebral Air Embolism Following Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Stent Removal: A Rare and Fatal Complication.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a generally performed procedure for biliary pathology. Although usually safe, air embolism is an exceptionally rare but potentially fatal complication.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We report the case of a 79-year-old female (ASA II) with a history of dyslipidemia and obesity, who presented for elective ERCP and biliary stent removal. She had previously undergone ERCP and open cholecystectomy for choledocholithiasis. During this time, sedation was administered by using fentanyl, midazolam, and propofol via target-controlled infusion. The procedure was initially uneventful; however, at its conclusion, the patient developed sudden desaturation, bradycardia, and a reduced level of consciousness. Computed tomography (CT) imaging revealed multiple cerebral air emboli. Despite intensive care management and ventilatory support, the patient deteriorated and died 2 days later.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the importance of maintaining vigilance for air embolism, even in seemingly straightforward ERCP procedures, especially in elderly patients. Early recognition and immediate management are vital to improving outcomes.

articles.title: Trends in Care and Outcomes Among Emergency Department Patients With Chest Pain Without Myocardial Infarction.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterize trends in hospitalization, downstream care, and outcomes among emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain without acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed claims data from a large national commercial insurer (2007-2021) and identified ED visits with a principal diagnosis of chest pain. We excluded visits with secondary diagnoses of AMI or other significant cardiopulmonary conditions and those preceded by cardiac testing, coronary procedures, AMI admissions, or chest pain ED visits within 6 months. Usage outcomes included index hospitalization (principal), 7-day cardiac testing, and 30-day coronary revascularization. The principal clinical outcome was 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization. Adjusted annual rates were estimated using generalized estimating equations, and trends were assessed using inverse-variance-weighted linear regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 773,250 index chest pain ED visits (mean age 54.2 years; 54.3% women). Adjusted hospitalization rates declined from 42.7% to 18.6%, and 7-day noninvasive testing decreased from 26.7% to 9.1%. Revascularization within 30 days declined from 5.8% to 3.6%. Overall, 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization showed no significant temporal trend, ranging from 0.8% to 1.2%. However, a modest increasing trend was observed among patients aged 70 years and older.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among ED patients with chest pain without AMI diagnosis, hospitalization, cardiac testing, and revascularization declined substantially from 2007 to 2021. Overall, downstream AMI hospitalization remained stable, although those in older adults experienced modest rises. Although efforts continue to identify additional low-risk patients for safe discharge, future research should quantify the potential benefits of hospitalization and cardiac testing, particularly for older adults and high-risk patients.

articles.title: Concepts in Practice: Understanding and Addressing Name-Based Microaggressions in Health Care.

abstract.text: Names are important markers of identity, culture, and belonging. In health care settings, individuals with ethnically distinct names may experience repeated mispronunciations, unsolicited nicknames, or avoidance of their names. Repeated mispronunciations without sincere efforts to learn or improve, as well as the avoidance, dismissal, or replacement of names with unsolicited nicknames, may function as name-based microaggressions and can negatively affect psychological safety, professional identity formation, and workplace inclusion. In this manuscript, we discuss the effect of name-based microaggressions on health care professionals and trainees, with particular focus on the emergency department. We review the 3 major categories of microaggressions-microassaults, microinsults, and microinvalidations-and use clinical vignettes to demonstrate how these behaviors may appear in both interpersonal and institutional settings. We also propose practical interpersonal and institutional strategies to promote more inclusive workplaces and foster respectful engagement with ethnically distinct names. By encouraging greater awareness, curiosity, humility, and intentionality around names, health care organizations can help cultivate clinical environments where individuals feel respected, included, and valued.

articles.title: A High-Yield Solution to the Emergency Medicine Resident Scholarly Activity Requirement.
Live Versus Delayed Video-Based TEAM Assessment During Real-World Cardiac Arrest: Agreement and Exploratory Differences by Rater Experience.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate agreement between immediate live and delayed video-based assessment of nontechnical skills during real-world adult cardiac arrest resuscitation, and whether agreement differed by rater experience.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational study of adult cardiac arrest resuscitations in a tertiary emergency department in Taiwan in 2024. For each event, one trained physician or nurse who participated in the resuscitation completed the Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) immediately afterward and re-rated the same event from video approximately 30 days later. Live-video agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 105 recorded resuscitations, 80 had complete paired assessments. Mean global ratings were similar between modalities (8.25 versus 8.22; mean paired difference, -0.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.25 to 0.20), whereas teamwork scores were modestly lower on video review (mean paired difference, -1.00; 95% CI -1.77 to -0.23). Event-level agreement was limited: intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.21 (95% CI 0.00 to 0.41) for total TEAM score and 0.16 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.37) for global rating. Total TEAM video ratings averaged 1.24 points lower than live ratings, with limits of agreement from -12.28 to 9.80. Agreement was higher among senior raters.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Delayed video-based TEAM assessment produced similar group-level scores but limited event-level agreement during real-world cardiac arrest. Agreement appeared higher among senior raters. Video review may support debriefing and monitoring, but appraisal of a specific resuscitation or other higher stakes use likely requires experienced raters and structured safeguards.

articles.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

articles.title: Comprehensive 3-Year Pediatric Resident Resuscitation Simulation Curriculum on the Care of the Severely Ill Pediatric Patient.
articles.journal_full: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Pediatric residents must be able to manage severely ill patients by the end of training. Simulation provides training in low-frequency, high-risk clinical situations. A longitudinal simulation curriculum could provide consistent training for residents to develop these essential skills.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We utilized Kern's 6 steps of curriculum development. A needs assessment identified content gaps. We implemented a 3-year, 9-case resuscitation simulation curriculum for pediatric residents targeting shock (septic, hypovolemic, obstructive), arrhythmias (supraventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, asystole), and respiratory failure (with bradycardia, seizures, hypoventilation). Each year, participants completed 3 simulation cases over 3 hours utilizing high-technology manikins. Patients ranged from 10 days to 10 years. We assessed the curriculum using Kirkpatrick's model, including reaction data assessing for change in self-reported confidence recognizing and managing targeted clinical events from pre/postsurveys, free-text responses noting areas of improved knowledge on postsurveys, and chart review of code events assessing for behavior change if residents led actual codes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ninety-two pediatric residents completed the curriculum. Participation was associated with improved confidence recognizing and managing targeted clinical events (pre: median 3-4, interquartile range [IQR] 3-5; post: 4-5, IQR 4-5; P < .05). Themes of lessons learned included increased knowledge in clinical management, crisis resource management skills, and local resources. Residents were more likely to assume the code leader role in actual patient codes postcurriculum (10% pre vs 40% post).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Participation in the curriculum was associated with increased resident confidence recognizing and managing targeted content, improved knowledge, and greater resident participation as code leaders in actual codes.

articles.title: CrossBoneNet: An Ultralightweight Hybrid CNN-ViT Architecture via Asymmetric Reversed Cross-Attention for Radiographic Fracture Detection.
articles.journal_full: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

abstract.text: Misdiagnoses in emergency departments are often associated with the difficulty in interpreting radiological findings on bone fractures due to millimetric fractures, overlapping bones, or superimpositions. Despite the high efficiency of state-of-the-art models in diagnosing such cases, their massive computational requirements severely hinder their implementation on resource-constrained devices in real-world clinical settings. In this study, we propose an ultralightweight CNN-ViT model, CrossBoneNet, which is designed for edge AI compatibility with minimal memory requirements. CrossBoneNet combines local microfracture detection using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and global anatomical recognition using vision transformers (ViTs). The model merges features from both architectures using the proposed asymmetric reversed cross-attention, where CNN features act as queries and ViT features act as keys and values-to efficiently map fine-grained local anomalies into a broader global anatomical context. Operating with a minimal parameter count (0.593 M) and low computational cost (1.527 GFLOPs), CrossBoneNet achieved a PR-AUC of 0.8498 ± 0.0086 and a ROC-AUC of 0.8427 ± 0.0072 on the MURA dataset in a patient-wise isolated evaluation. It achieves highly competitive performance-remaining within a 4% margin of the 88.59 million parameter ConvNeXt-Base model-while delivering over 99% memory savings. After fine-tuning on the FracAtlas dataset, CrossBoneNet achieved a specificity of 0.9760 ± 0.0080 and PR-AUC of 0.7568 ± 0.0414, demonstrating effective cross-domain transfer learning. With a compact footprint (< 3 MB) and high specificity at the default 0.50 operating threshold, CrossBoneNet demonstrates potential as a point-of-care decision support and worklist prioritization tool on resource-constrained devices, while calibrating the decision threshold (e.g., τ = 0.3837 and τ = 0.3449 ) enables high-sensitivity screening modes (achieving 85.03% and 89.96% sensitivity on MURA, respectively), pending prospective validation. This retrospective study establishes proof of concept; future work will focus on prospective clinical trials and expansion to multiclass fracture classification.

articles.title: Inhaler technique in acute wheezing: Factors associated with adequate knowledge.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess knowledge and skills in the use of spacer devices among children presenting to a pediatric emergency department with an acute exacerbation of wheezing or asthma and among their caregivers, and to identify associated factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive study in 134 children aged 2-15 years with previous spacer use who presented with an acute exacerbation of wheezing or asthma. Eligible patients had either a prior physician diagnosis of asthma or a history of recurrent wheezing (≥3 previous episodes). Knowledge and skills were assessed in caregivers and children capable of using the device independently ("autonomous children") by means of a checklist developed in house based on current guidelines. Performance was classified into four levels according to the percentage of correctly performed items. We conducted logistic regression analyses to identify factors associated with adequate knowledge.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 63.4% of participants showed a high level of knowledge regarding spacer use. Caregivers demonstrated better performance compared to autonomous children (77.7% vs 30%). Better knowledge was directly associated with younger age and follow-up in pediatric pulmonology department in autonomous children, and inversely associated with age in caregivers. Despite generally favorable results, relevant technique errors were frequent, particularly among autonomous children.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Most caregivers demonstrated adequate knowledge of spacer use; however, significant errors persist, especially among autonomous children. These findings highlight the need for repeated and structured educational interventions.

articles.title: Decoding suicidal crises in the emergency medical dispatch setting: protocol for a nationwide Swedish mixed-methods study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency medical dispatch centres (EMDCs) represent a critical, understudied setting for understanding and preventing suicidal crises. Individuals experiencing suicidal crises may contact EMDCs directly or be identified through emergency calls from relatives, healthcare professionals or members of the public. Although telephone-based services provide opportunities for risk assessment and intervention, little is known about how suicidal crises are communicated, identified and managed within emergency medical dispatch settings or how emergency call characteristics relate to subsequent suicide and self-harm. This study aims to improve understanding of how suicidal crises are communicated, identified and managed within the Swedish emergency medical dispatch system by integrating nationwide emergency call data, national registers and qualitative analyses.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: This nationwide mixed-methods study comprises five substudies using approximately 500 000 emergency calls to Sweden’s national emergency number (112) concerning psychiatric and/or suicidal content between 2015 and 2025. Calls will be identified through SOS Alarm dispatch classifications and AI-assisted review of free-text call descriptions. Emergency medical dispatch data from SOS Alarm will be linked to nationwide healthcare, prescription and mortality registers to investigate sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, psychiatric healthcare utilisation, self-harm and suicide outcomes. AI-based methods, including natural language processing and machine learning will be used to identify communication patterns associated with suicide and self-harm and to improve identification of suicide-related calls. Quantitative analyses will include descriptive statistics, survival analyses and predictive modelling, while qualitative content analysis of emergency call transcripts and interviews with emergency medical dispatch operators will examine how suicidal crises are communicated, assessed and managed.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: The study has been approved by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (2024-08127-01 (approved 12 January 2025), 2026-02444-02 (approved 19 May 2026)). Privacy and confidentiality will be protected through pseudonymisation, restricted-access secure data environments and offline processing of audio data. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences and stakeholder communication to support training, service development and future suicide prevention research.

articles.title: Facilitators and barriers to nurses' adherence to traumatic brain injury management guidelines at the accident and emergency unit in a national referral hospital in Uganda: a qualitative study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study explored the facilitators and barriers to adherence to traumatic brain injury management guidelines among nurses at the accident and emergency unit in a national referral hospital in Uganda.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: An exploratory qualitative study was conducted among nurses. Data collection and analysis were guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The study was conducted in the Accident and Emergency unit at the Mulago National Referral Hospital in Kampala, Uganda.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: The participants included nurses working at the Accident and Emergency unit of Mulago National Referral Hospital.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 15 nurses were enrolled in the study, but transcripts for 13 of them were analysed as two audio recordings were corrupted before transcription. The facilitators of TBI management guidelines included the perceived simplicity of stepwise assessment, nurses’ motivation, experience and knowledge of TBI care, supportive peer relationships and nurses’ ability to adapt during emergencies. Conversely, barriers to TBI management guidelines included inaccessible or outdated protocols, severe understaffing, inadequate in-service training, shortages of equipment, sundries and medicines, delays in imaging fee-waiver processes, limited dissemination of TBI guidelines, external pressure from political actors and family members, overcrowding, unpredictable patient surges and difficulty maintaining monitoring fidelity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nurses’ adherence to TBI management guidelines was shaped by the interaction between individual commitment, guideline accessibility and the wider emergency care environment.

articles.title: Moving towards integrated people-centred primary healthcare for non-communicable diseases in Bangladesh: a qualitative study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore gaps and challenges in health systems at the primary healthcare (PHC) level and develop strategic directions for non-communicable disease (NCD) care delivery through an integrated people-centred-primary healthcare model.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A qualitative study employing stakeholder consultation and key informant interviews (KII).

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Purposively selected health facilities across different tiers of health systems and the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Policymakers from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MOH&FW) and the DGHS, programme personnel, facility managers, physicians, specialists from a medical college, development partners and researchers. Consultation with stakeholders was conducted before data collection to identify the key informants (KIs) and finalise interview guidelines and later to validate the study findings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The findings revealed that PHC facilities in Bangladesh were not robust enough to ensure protocol-based management of NCDs, especially in multimorbidity, particularly among older people. PHC facilities struggled to provide quality preventive and promotive care due to inadequate staff and budget and lack of protocol. Stabilising cardiovascular emergencies and timely referral with ambulance service were not available. The absence of a digitised database for record-keeping resulted in high patient loads at secondary and tertiary facilities and increased out-of-pocket expenditure. However, the study findings revealed that some Upazila Health Complexes at the subdistrict level supported by development partners are providing good protocol-based NCD care with digitised record-keeping and individual-level follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The study highlighted key barriers in implementing policies for NCD management and prevention at the PHC level in Bangladesh. Strengthening PHC as the first point of contact may help ensure integrated care and advance towards universal health coverage, with potential relevance to other low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: Delayed pancytopenia following ingestion of wild mushrooms consistent with Hypholoma fasciculare: A case report.

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: Hypholoma fasciculare (sulfur tuft) is a toxic mushroom commonly associated with gastrointestinal symptoms. However, hematologic toxicity related to Hypholoma species has rarely been reported. In particular, delayed-onset pancytopenia following mushroom ingestion remains poorly understood.

abstract.label: PATIENT CONCERNS
abstract.text: A 57-year-old man presented to the emergency department after ingesting self-collected wild mushrooms. Approximately 10 days after ingestion, he developed fever and generalized weakness.

abstract.label: DIAGNOSES
abstract.text: Laboratory evaluation revealed delayed-onset pancytopenia. Extensive infectious, autoimmune, and hematological investigations, including viral serology and bone marrow examinations, excluded primary hematological malignancies, aplastic anemia, and infectious causes. Based on the clinical course and the exclusion of alternative etiologies, toxin-mediated bone marrow suppression following mushroom ingestion was considered the most plausible diagnosis.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: The patient was conservatively managed with close monitoring and supportive care. No specific antidotal or immunosuppressive agents were administered.

abstract.label: OUTCOMES
abstract.text: Hematological parameters gradually recovered without targeted interventions. Follow-up laboratory tests demonstrated complete resolution of the pancytopenia, and the patient remained clinically stable without recurrence during outpatient follow-up.

abstract.label: LESSONS
abstract.text: This case highlights delayed pancytopenia as a potential manifestation of toxic mushroom ingestion, even in the absence of severe initial symptoms. Recognition of this pattern may facilitate a timely diagnosis and appropriate monitoring.

articles.title: Early post-discharge pain persistence, not opioid use, is associated with new-onset chronic pain among opioid-naive emergency department patients: a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort.

abstract.text: Chronic pain may develop after emergency department (ED) visits for acute pain, but early predictors of new-onset chronic pain among opioid-naïve patients are incompletely understood. We conducted a secondary analysis of a prospective observational cohort of opioid-naïve adults presenting to two urban EDs primarily for pain and discharged home with a new opioid prescription. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 48 h, two weeks, and six months. The primary outcome was new-onset chronic pain at six months, defined as pain occurring on >50% of days during the six months after ED discharge. Of 699 participants in the parent cohort, 562 (80.4%) provided six-month outcome data, including 483 participants without chronic pain at baseline. Among these participants, 129 (26.7%) met criteria for new-onset chronic pain at six months. In multivariable models, neck/back pain and longer pain duration before the ED visit were consistently associated with higher odds of new-onset chronic pain. Pain sometimes/usually/always at 48 h versus never/rarely was associated with higher odds of new-onset chronic pain (OR 2.77, 95% CI: 1.40-5.48). When 48-hour and two-week pain frequency were included simultaneously as predictors, two-week pain frequency remained associated with new-onset chronic pain (OR 2.36, 95% CI: 1.39-4.00), whereas the 48-hour estimate attenuated. Moderate/severe pain at two weeks was associated with new-onset chronic pain (OR 2.20, 95% CI: 1.37-3.53). Opioid use at 48 h and two weeks was not associated with new-onset chronic pain. Baseline pain characteristics and early post-discharge pain persistence may help identify patients at elevated risk for new-onset chronic pain. PERSPECTIVE: Persistent pain after an emergency department visit may provide an early signal of risk for subsequent chronic pain. Among opioid-naive patients discharged with a new opioid prescription, pain frequency and intensity during the first two weeks, but not early opioid use, were associated with new-onset chronic pain.

articles.title: Predictors of longer recognition time in acute aortic dissection: a retrospective observational study.
articles.journal_full: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) carries a high mortality risk closely tied to diagnostic timeliness. Delays remain prevalent, driven by atypical presentations-particularly in patients without a chief complaint of pain. This study identified predictors of a longer recognition time, as indicated by prolonged door-to-CT times, and developed a cumulative prediction model for patients presenting without pain complaints.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective study of 197 adult patients diagnosed with AAD at a tertiary emergency department (ED) from 2016 to 2023. Patients were classified as having a shorter (< 74 min) or longer (≥ 74 min; cohort median) door-to-CT completion time. Predictors were identified by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized logistic regression and decision tree analysis. A subgroup analysis characterized pain-complaint-free patients using a stepwise identification algorithm.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A longer door-to-CT time was associated with female sex, older age, and physiological instability. The strongest multivariable predictors were absence of abrupt pain (odds ratio [OR] 2.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-5.46) and non-severe triage classification (OR 4.70, 95% CI 1.71-15.29). Dyspnea (OR 2.14) and elevated diastolic blood pressure (OR 1.02/mmHg) also independently predicted a longer door-to-CT time. Among pain-complaint-free patients (n = 46), a stepwise combination of mediastinal widening on chest radiography, Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and Shock Index > 1.0 was present in all identified cases (cumulative case coverage 46/46; 95% CI 92.3%-100%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study identifies a high-risk profile for a longer recognition time of AAD, particularly in older female patients and those presenting without sudden pain. For patients unable to report pain, chest radiography, shock index, and comorbidity burden may be considered to help identify atypical presentations warranting urgent evaluation.

articles.title: SwimmingIndividuals: A high-performance agent-based model for marine ecosystems.

abstract.text: Because they are based on established theory, mechanistic models are essential for projecting ecological responses to novel conditions. Yet mechanistic agent-based model (ABM) applications have often been limited by computational constraints. This paper introduces SwimmingIndividuals, an open-source ABM framework that advances our ability to simulate physiological processes, animal movement, higher trophic level marine ecosystem dynamics, and fisheries removals at large ecological scales. The software's key contributions are a suite of mechanistic sub-models governing the full life cycle of each agent, including visual prey detection, adaptive behaviors such as diel vertical migration (DVM), a flexible bioenergetics engine with three taxon-specific metabolic architectures, and a spatial pathfinding algorithm for habitat-seeking movement. These processes are made computationally tractable through a hybrid CPU/GPU architecture written in Julia. Unlike prior ABMs that use fixed perception radii or single-equation bioenergetics, SwimmingIndividuals enables emergent ecological dynamics across populations of superindividual agents. We demonstrate the framework through three Gulf of America simulations. The model reproduced DVM, cetacean diving patterns, size-based trophic shifts, and von Bertalanffy growth curves consistent with published King Mackerel stock assessments. Long-term simulations generated realistic population dynamics and quantified impacts of fishery harvest control rules across five fleets. SwimmingIndividuals provides a powerful, flexible, open-source platform for mechanistic marine ecosystem research and ecosystem-based fisheries management.

articles.title: Calculating trauma undertriage rates: Are we using the wrong formula-and the wrong definition?
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Undertriage (UT) is central to trauma center quality improvement, yet UT definitions vary, and no data-driven consensus target exists for interfacility benchmarking. We compared facility-level UT rates across four methods and assessed the impact on facility benchmarking.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included patients aged 18 to 89 from Level I & II trauma centers in the ACS TQP Files (2021-2023). Facility-level UT was calculated using the Cribari Matrix Method (CMM), modified Cribari Matrix Method (mCMM), Standardized Triage Assessment Tool (STAT), and High-Intensity Time-Sensitive (HITS) intervention-based definition representing trauma team actions. Paired facility-level UT rates were compared across methods. To estimate benchmarking impact, we calculated within-facility rank change (higher rank = higher UT) relative to CMM.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 2,643,881 patients and 515 facilities were included. Median facility-level UT significantly differed by method: CMM 11% [interquartile range: 9-14], mCMM 60% [50-67], STAT 6% [5-8], and HITS 30% [22-40] (all P<0.001). At individual hospitals, the median range of maximum UT values between methods was 53% [44-60]. The median absolute facility rank change between the CMM method and other tools was 129 [54.5-236.5] for mCMM, 48 [17-90] for STAT, and 142 [62.5-252.5] for HITS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These UT data highlight a concerning level of variation and uncertainty in the calculation and interpretation of a key trauma center performance metric. Until a UT definition is standardized and data-driven UT target goals established, cross-center benchmarking using UT should be interpreted cautiously and may be better suited for within-center trending.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, therapeutic/care management.

articles.title: Transanal irrigation to treat refractory constipation: a short-term real-life study.

abstract.text: The treatment of patients complaining of chronic constipation is still far from ideal, and there is a discrete percentage of them that are labeled as refractory to the usual therapeutic approaches. In these patients there is often the need to use alternative approaches. Among these, transanal irrigation seems promising. Our aim was to evaluate the effect of transanal irrigation on symptoms and quality of life in patients with severe refractory constipation. To this end, we retrospectively analyzed the charts of 31 such patients undergoing transanal irrigation, and evaluated them basally and one and three months after the treatment. Data were collected by means of the Wexner score and the SF12 questionnaire for quality of life. Overall, there was a significant decrease of the constipation scores and an improvement of quality of life score after treatment, after both one and three months. No important side effects were documented. In conclusion, treatment with transanal irrigation may be useful, alone or as combination therapy, in patients with constipation refractory to the conventional therapeutic approaches, but studies in more numerous cohorts of subjects are needed to firmly validate this approach.

articles.title: Fever in a child after a trip to rural Saskatchewan.
Inclusive Mass Fatality Management and Planning in Cremation-Dominant Societies: Policy Challenges and Recommendations From Japan.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Even in societies where cremation is widespread in normal times, mass fatality management and planning that encompasses minorities who do not follow the custom of cremation are necessary. However, in Japan, the country with the highest cremation rate in the world (99.97% in 2023), little consideration is afforded to such minorities during disasters. We evaluated Japan's past disaster responses and current disaster management plans, demonstrating that unidentified remains are highly likely to be cremated after a certain period, contrary to the will of the deceased or their families. Furthermore, we proposed actions and measures that the government, local authorities, and minorities could take to reduce this likelihood, such as securing refrigeration facilities, considering temporary burials, carrying identification cards stating one's burial preference, and ensuring minorities' participation in response and planning efforts. Since cremation is becoming increasingly widespread internationally, evaluations and proposals from Japan can contribute to inclusive mass fatality management and planning in other countries.

articles.title: Ebola Bundibugyo reaches Nigeria: implications for global travel, Hajj and Umrah.
Evidence-Informed Recommendations for Child Sex Trafficking Identification and Response in Ontario Pediatric Emergency Departments: A Modified Delphi Method Study.

abstract.text: Children who experience sex trafficking often access emergency departments (EDs) while they are being exploited for related health and psychosocial concerns. However, few clinical resources exist to support ED providers in identifying and responding to presentations of child sex trafficking (CST) in Canada, an internationally recognized source, destination, and transit site for trafficking. This study used a modified Delphi method to propose evidence-informed recommendations for CST identification and response in pediatric EDs. Between July 6 and October 18, 2023, N = 58 Ontario health and social service providers completed three iterative surveys on CST identification, intervention, and referral practices. Providers rated statements using a 4-point Likert scale and provided write-in responses to expand on their survey selections. We analyzed closed-ended responses using descriptive and Kappa statistics, and write-in responses using content analysis. Experts endorsed 57 of the 84 components (68%) to inform clinical practice recommendations for CST identification and response in pediatric EDs, which center on three categories: (1) assessing CST vulnerability factors and indicators, (2) intervention practices that center a culturally responsive, trauma- and violence-informed approach, and (3) in-hospital and community referrals to support the short- and long-term service needs of children who experience sex trafficking. Pediatric ED providers are encouraged to adopt a trauma- and violence-informed approach when incorporating CST identification into existing patient-interviewing methods, such as the pediatric HEADS-ED assessment tool. This population may require specialized services, such as through Sexual Assault/Domestic Violence Treatment Centres and anti-human trafficking community services.
