While these findings can inform the development of inter-institutional care transition protocols, readily achievable response practices in the ED include providing patient education on safer sexual health and online practices and establishing community linkages to anti-human trafficking services.

articles.title: Hydrogen Peroxide in Operative Wounds and Cavities: Oxygen Generation, Gas Embolism, Recognition, Response, and System Safeguards.

abstract.text: Hydrogen peroxide irrigation can generate a large oxygen burden, causing gas embolism, cardiovascular collapse, or neurologic injury. This narrative review integrates selected operative cases, quantitative physiological estimates, regulatory warnings, and contemporary gas embolism guidance. Complete decomposition of 1 mL of 3% weight-per-volume solution theoretically yields approximately 9.9 mL of oxygen at 0°C and 1 atmosphere, or 11.2 mL at 37°C at the same pressure. Operative reports describe suspected pulmonary, demonstrated intracardiac, and cerebral gas events; they establish neither incidence nor a safe exposure threshold. Clinical benefits are setting-specific and must be distinguished from laboratory antimicrobial effects. Management prioritizes exposure cessation, oxygenation, resuscitation, and urgent specialist assessment, with selective interventions and positioning adapted to context. A case table, evidence summary, and management algorithm separate peroxide-specific observations from broader gas embolism evidence. Prevention requires appropriate alternative irrigants, recognition of hazardous anatomy and delivery, and clear team communication.

articles.title: Lead poisoning: an important differential diagnosis in acute colonic pseudo-obstruction.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Lead poisoning remains an important public health concern. We highlight the findings in a patient with a high blood lead concentration. These images can assist clinicians in making the correct diagnosis.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 44-year-old male presented with a 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and obstipation. The diagnosis was intestinal obstruction, which failed to respond to conservative management. After exploratory laparotomy and colostomy failed to identify an etiology of acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome), lead poisoning was diagnosed based on anemia, basophilic stippling of erythrocytes, and a whole-blood lead concentration of 71.87 µg/dL (reference <10.00 µg/dL). The patient recovered with chelation therapy.

abstract.label: IMAGES
abstract.text: Abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan revealed copious intraluminal feces and gas within the bowel. Peripheral smear revealed poikilocytosis with basophilic stippling.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In patients with acute colonic pseudo-obstruction, abdominal pain and anemia, a detailed history is essential, and lead poisoning should be suspected.

articles.title: Rotational thromboelastometry and endothelial-derived extracellular vesicle changes in thrombotic microangiopathy versus other envenoming syndromes following hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Thrombotic microangiopathy is an uncommon complication of snakebite with unclear pathophysiology. We explore the mechanisms of venom-induced consumption coagulopathy, thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury in hump-nosed pit viper bites.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective observational study was conducted at District General Hospital Horana, Sri Lanka (June 2023 to December 2024). Thirty-five patients were recruited, including: local envenoming alone (20), venom induced consumption coagulopathy (2), thrombotic microangiopathy (5) and acute kidney injury without thrombotic microangiopathy (8). Laboratory tests were performed every 12 hours, and rotational thromboelastometry (delta and platelet) and flow cytometry for extracellular vesicles at the earliest diagnosis of envenoming.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All thrombotic microangiopathy cases developed severe acute kidney injury, with 4/5 requiring dialysis. All eight cases of isolated acute kidney injury had mild kidney dysfunction that resolved. The international normalized ratio was normal in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy and acute kidney injury, however rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, including fibrinogen dysfunction despite normal fibrinogen levels, in patients with thrombotic microangiopathy. Isolated acute kidney injury had mild to moderate rotational thromboelastometry abnormalities. Endothelial-derived extracellular vesicles were proportionally highest in the thrombotic microangiopathy (median 12.6%) group. Red cell-derived extracellular vesicles were raised in thrombotic microangiopathy and isolated acute kidney injury groups.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Thrombotic microangiopathy and severe acute kidney injury are associated in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming. Rotational thromboelastometry revealed coagulation abnormalities, missed by conventional coagulation testing. Thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming was associated with raised endothelial- and red cell-derived extracellular vesicles.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Rotational thromboelastometry is more sensitive than conventional coagulation testing for detecting coagulopathy and the associated risk of developing thrombotic microangiopathy and AKI in hump-nosed viper bites. Endothelial injury may be a factor in the pathogenesis of thrombotic microangiopathy in hump-nosed pit viper envenoming.

articles.title: Gender differences in acute poisoning: a 35-year cohort study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Drug overdose is an increasingly common cause of death, more commonly in males. In contrast, women present more commonly to emergency departments with overdose. We therefore aim to investigate gender differences in the characteristics and severity of acute poisoning.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adult (18-64 y) poisoning admissions to a tertiary toxicology service were reviewed (1990-2024), and females were compared to males. Data were extracted from a prospective database, including drug/toxin ingested, clinical effects, treatment, length of stay, intensive care admission and death. Primary outcomes were death, intensive care admission and intubation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 22,316 (75%) deliberate self-poisonings - 14,101 females (63%), 8,178 males and 37 transgender; 2,101 (7%) recreational overdoses - 695 (33%) females and 1,406 (67%) males. Females ingested more paracetamol/analgesics, antidepressants and quetiapine, while males ingested more alcohol, amphetamines and opioids. Median age for deliberate self-poisoning in females (33 years [IQR:24-44 years]) was similar to males (34 years [IQR:25-44 years]). There were 1,268 females (9.0%) admitted to intensive care, compared to 912 males (11.2%), which was significantly different (absolute difference 2.2%;95% CI:1.3-3.0%; P < 0.001). Less females were intubated than males (790 [5.6%] vs 549 [6.7%]; P = 0.001). Inpatient mortality was similar for females (32; 0.2%) and males (24; 0.3%), and no difference in length of stay. More females had hypotension, while more males developed coma and hepatotoxicity. Males were more likely to receive sedation and naloxone. Gender differences were similar for recreational poisoning, except greater mortality in males. Gender remained an independent predictor of intensive care and intubation in a multivariate logistic regression model, with males more likely to be intubated and admitted to intensive care.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: More males took recreational overdoses, including opioids, and females had more deliberate self-poisoning, with less toxic medications. Female deliberate self-poisoning patients were less commonly intubated and admitted to intensive care. Drug type did not account for the gender difference in outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: We found only minor differences between inpatient morbidity and mortality for females compared to males. Males were more likely to be admitted to intensive care and be intubated, mainly due to higher rates of coma.

articles.title: Incarceration Status and Access to Care Following Hand and Wrist Fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Incarcerated individuals face well-documented care disparities, but whether these extend to acute upper-extremity trauma is unclear. We evaluated the association of incarceration with specialist evaluation, rehabilitation utilization, and postoperative complications following hand and wrist fractures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively studied consecutive adults treated for hand or wrist fractures at a safety-net level I trauma center from 2018 to 2024, comparing incarcerated with nonincarcerated patients. Key process outcomes included the presence of the first specialist evaluation and the number of documented hand therapy visits. Secondary clinical outcomes included documented postoperative complications among surgically treated patients.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1597 eligible patients, 197 (12.3%) were incarcerated and 1400 (87.7%) were nonincarcerated. The incarcerated cohort had a higher prevalence of bipolar disorder (13% vs 4.3%; P < .001), schizophrenia (7.1% vs 2.0%; P < .001), and self-inflicted injury (25% vs 12%; P < .001). First specialist evaluation occurred more often in the outpatient clinic for incarcerated patients (55% vs 18%) and more often in the emergency department for nonincarcerated patients (71% vs 43%; both P < .001). Rates of cross-sectional imaging (16% vs 20%; P = .20) and operative treatment (34% vs 30%; P = .30) were similar. Incarcerated patients completed fewer therapy visits (median, 1.8 vs 3.8; P = .004). Rates of documented postoperative complications did not differ significantly between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Incarceration was associated with outpatient rather than emergency-department first specialist evaluation and significantly reduced hand therapy utilization, a pattern suggesting less direct access to timely specialist care. System-level interventions to standardize referral and optimize rehabilitation access are needed to reduce care disparities for this vulnerable population.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III.

articles.title: Critical adverse events during emergency department ketamine-propofol sedation in children.: A secondary analysis of a multicentre study.
Time to antibiotics and outcomes for children hospitalized with community acquired pneumonia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: It is unclear whether time to antibiotics changes outcomes for hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and whether observation is safe.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Our objective was to compare outcomes among children with CAP admitted to the hospital who did and who did not receive antibiotics within 4 h of presentation to the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study using data from four hospitals obtained from the Pediatric Health Information System. Children aged 3 months to 18 years, with a chest X-ray, admitted to the hospital from the ED with suspected CAP who received antibiotics were enrolled. Our primary outcome was a composite of escalation of care (escalation in respiratory support, transfer to the intensive care unit, vasopressor use, or chest tube placement). Secondary outcomes were length of stay, duration of oxygen use, and cost of stay. Inverse propensity weighted logistic regression and log gamma regression to evaluate the association of early versus late antibiotics and outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 758 children hospitalized with CAP who met inclusion criteria, of which 451 (59%) received antibiotics within 4 h. There was no statistical difference in escalation of care between those who received early versus late antibiotics (3% vs. 2%; odds ratio [OR]: 1.46 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57,3.73]). There were no statistical associations with secondary outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study provides an opportunity for antibiotic stewardship by showing that more time to observe patients with CAP without antibiotics does not change outcomes. This time may identify patients who will improve without antibiotics, limiting side effects.

articles.title: AI for reducing claims and compensation payments from missed fractures on radiographs.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the potential of BoneView, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for fracture detection on radiographs in claims cases related to missed fractures that resulted in financial compensation.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, multicenter study included all patients who submitted a claim and received financial compensation for missed fractures on radiographs between January 2013 and December 2019 across the 38 university hospitals of the Greater Paris area (AP-HP-France). For each claimant, 5 control patients were selected from a contemporary single-center cohort of patients who underwent radiographs of the same anatomical regions (with or without fracture) performed in the emergency department of a university hospital, irrespective of fracture status. Three radiologists (musculoskeletal fellow, 5-year fellowship-trained radiologist, and > 20-year expert) independently performed blinded, unassisted, and AI-assisted interpretations following a 3-month washout. Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated with and without AI and for standalone AI. Compensation amounts were used to estimate potentially avoidable payouts.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 156 patients (mean age, 42.2 years; 113 (72.4%) males), including 26 claimants with missed fractures on radiographs and 130 controls, were evaluated. 27/130 (20.8%) of the control cohort had fractures. Standalone AI sensitivity was 80.8% (21/26; 95% CI [60.7-93.5]) for claimants and 96.3% (26/27; 95% CI [81.0-99.9]) for the control cohort (p = 0.10). AI assistance did not significantly improve sensitivity, with expert reader sensitivity increasing from 81.1% to 92.5% (p = 0.10). Total compensation was €282,850 (€10,878 per case). AI-assisted detection could have potentially mitigated €265,314, representing a 93.8% theoretical reduction in institutional financial liability.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: AI-assisted fracture detection identified most missed fractures on radiographs leading to compensation and may help reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden.

abstract.label: KEY POINTS
abstract.text: Question Can AI-assisted fracture detection identify fractures missed by radiologists on radiographs that led to compensated medicolegal claims and institutional financial liability? Findings Standalone AI detected 21/26 (80.8%) of missed fractures in patients with compensated claims, corresponding to €265,314/€282,850 (93.8%) of total compensation in this cohort. Clinical relevance AI-assisted fracture detection can potentially increase radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Implementing AI tools in emergency settings may significantly mitigate patient harm and institutional costs associated with missed fractures.

articles.title: Sports-related peripheral neuropathies in athletes: mechanisms, imaging evaluation, and sport-specific patterns.

abstract.text: Peripheral neuropathy in athletes is increasingly recognized as a significant source of morbidity, with injury patterns varying according to the biomechanical demands of specific sports. Although peripheral nerve disorders in athletes may result from acute trauma, they more commonly arise from chronic, repetitive mechanical stress inherent to athletic activity. Despite their frequency, they frequently remain underdiagnosed, as clinical manifestations often overlap with other musculoskeletal disorders. Mechanisms of injury include compression, traction, laceration, ischemia, and repetitive microtrauma. Distinct athletic modalities are associated with characteristic neuropathies reflecting sport-specific kinematics and loading patterns. Awareness of these biomechanical factors and recognition of typical clinical presentations are essential for accurate assessment of athletes with suspected nerve injury. Diagnostic evaluation frequently requires advanced imaging modalities, particularly magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) and high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS), which enable detailed structural assessment of peripheral nerves and detection of secondary imaging findings. Electrodiagnostic studies may provide complementary functional information in selected cases. Early and precise diagnosis is critical to guide management, facilitate safe return to sport, and prevent long-term functional deficits. While most nerve disorders respond to conservative treatment, severe, progressive, or refractory cases may warrant surgical intervention to restore function and enable return to play (RTP). This review examines mechanisms of injury, clinical evaluation, classification systems, imaging findings, and sport-specific patterns of peripheral nerve injury across diverse athletic disciplines.

articles.title: Results of Operating the 2025 "Heat-related Illness Emergency Department Surveillance System".

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to analyze the characteristics and health impacts of heat-related illnesses during the summer of 2025 in the Republic of Korea and to provide evidence for prevention and response measures to minimize heat-related health risks associated with climate change.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Since 2011, the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) has operated the nationwide "Heat-related Illness Emergency Department Surveillance System." Between May 15 and September 25, 2025, data on patients with heat-related illnesses and suspected heat-related deaths were collected from 517 participating emergency departments through the "Disease and Health Integrated Management System." These data were analyzed based on major epidemiological characteristics, including sex, age, type of illness, region, and place of occurrence. Daily surveillance results were publicly released on the KDCA website.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 4,460 heat-related illness cases and 29 suspected deaths were reported in 2025. Compared with 2024, the cases increased by 20.4%, whereas suspected deaths decreased by 14.7%. Most patients were male (79.7%), with individuals aged 50-59 years accounting for the largest proportion of cases (19.4%). Older adults aged ≥65 years accounted for 30.1% of all cases and 58.6% of deaths. Heat exhaustion was the most common diagnosis (62.0%), and most incidents occurred outdoors (79.2%), particularly in workplaces (32.1%) and farms (12.2%) or fields.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Heat-related illnesses predominantly affected older adults and outdoor workers during the summer of 2025. Strengthening prevention measures targeting vulnerable populations, timely dissemination of public information, and interagency collaboration are needed to reduce the growing health impacts of heat waves associated with climate change.

articles.title: A Case of Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Complicated With Compartment Syndrome Treated by Hyperbaric Oxygen.

abstract.text: In severe carbon monoxide poisoning complicated by compartment syndrome, prompt fasciotomy combined with hyperbaric oxygen and multidisciplinary supportive care was associated with full neurological recovery and limb salvage. Brain MRI abnormalities did not parallel the favorable clinical course in this patient.

articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) approach defines safe zones for W-plate fixation of the anterior pelvic ring.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To define the procedure-specific surgical anatomy of the pre-symphyseal region relevant to W-plate fixation by characterizing the soft-tissue layers, identifying critical neurovascular structures, and defining quantitative safe zones for dissection and plate placement.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Fresh-frozen adult cadavers underwent standardized low Pfannenstiel dissections reproducing the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) exposure required for W-plate fixation. Pre-symphyseal soft-tissue layers were sequentially dissected from the skin to the anterior pubic symphysis. The locations of critical neurovascular structures relative to the pubic midline and pubic tubercles were recorded, together with anatomical layers, dimensions of the prepubic ligamentous-aponeurotic complex, soft-tissue thickness, sex-related anatomical differences, and surgical safe zones.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three reproducible anatomical layers were identified in ten specimens. The superficial layer contained the pre-symphyseal fat pad and superficial epigastric vessels. The intermediate layer contained the spermatic cord or round ligament, ilioinguinal and genitofemoral nerves, and suprapubic artery, with these critical structures located at a mean distance of approximately 3.2 cm from the midline. The deep layer was consistently formed by the Pyramidalis-anterior pubic Ligament-Adductor longus Complex (PLAC), which covered the anterior pubic symphysis and measured a mean of 4.6 × 3.1 cm. No critical neurovascular structure crossed the central trajectory corresponding to W-plate placement. Female specimens demonstrated greater preperitoneal soft-tissue thickness, whereas lateral surgical safe zones were narrower in male specimens.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The pre-symphyseal region demonstrated a reproducible three-layer surgical anatomy with a predictable distribution of critical neurovascular structures. Quantitative anatomic mapping defined procedure-specific safe zones for extrapelvic W-plate fixation and provided practical guidancefor surgical exposure, implant positioning, and avoidance of iatrogenic injury.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level IV, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Risk factors for complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures carries a substantial risk of postoperative complications, particularly surgical site infection, yet the relative contribution of fracture pattern and associated soft tissue injury to this risk remains incompletely defined.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe the rate and spectrum of complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures and to identify factors independently associated with these complications, with particular attention to acute surgical site infection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective, single-center cohort study of 126 patients who underwent surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures between December 2014 and November 2024, reported in accordance with the STROBE statement. Candidate demographic, injury-related, and treatment-related exposures were compared against a composite primary outcome (any postoperative complication) and against acute infection using Fisher's exact test, Pearson chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and multivariable logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 39 of 126 patients (31.0%) experienced at least one postoperative complication; chronic pain (22.2%) and acute surgical site infection (16.7%) were the most frequent individual components. In bivariate analysis, the presence of a Morel-Lavallée lesion at baseline was significantly associated with both the composite outcome (OR 12.65, 95% CI 1.42-112.27, p = 0.011) and acute infection (OR 12.12, 95% CI 2.06-71.37, p = 0.007); Young-Burgess fracture pattern was also associated with infection (p = 0.018). After multivariable adjustment for infection, a Morel-Lavallée lesion (adjusted OR 17.69, 95% CI 2.46-126.95, p = 0.004) and combined-mechanism fracture pattern (adjusted OR 8.25 versus anteroposterior compression, 95% CI 1.91-35.58, p = 0.005) remained independently associated with infection. Neither the presence, technique, nor surgical approach of posterior ring fixation was associated with any complication type, and time from injury to definitive fixation (median 13 days) showed no significant association with either outcome.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A Morel-Lavallée lesion identified at initial evaluation was associated with postoperative complications in bivariate analysis and, together with a combined-mechanism fracture pattern, remained an independent predictor of surgical site infection after multivariable adjustment. No statistically significant association was identified between posterior fixation technique and complication risk.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Acute-on-Chronic Valproic Acid Overdose: A Toxicology Simulation Case for Medical Students.
articles.journal_full: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Overdose of valproic acid, an antiepileptic medication prescribed for seizure disorders, bipolar disorder, and migraine prophylaxis, is common but underrepresented in medical school curricula. Because valproic acid is widely prescribed and toxicity can occur at both therapeutic and supratherapeutic doses, medical students need a foundation in recognizing and managing it. To close this gap, we built a multimodal educational intervention combining didactic instruction with an experiential simulation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Fourth-year toxicology elective students completed a knowledge pretest and a confidence-based Likert questionnaire before attending a lecture, then worked in small groups through a 15-minute simulated encounter with a patient with acute-on-chronic valproic acid overdose, followed by a 15-minute debrief. The scenario's critical actions comprised a focused history, neurologic exam, valproic acid and ammonia levels, L-carnitine administration, and toxicology/psychiatry consultation; required materials were a manikin, intravenous supplies, and pharmaceuticals. A posttest and follow-up Likert questionnaires captured knowledge change, reactions, and intended practice change.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across 10 sessions, 48 students completed both tests; scores rose from a mean of 58% (SD = 21%) to 97% (SD = 6%) (Wilcoxon W = 0.0; P < .001), and every group completed the critical actions checklist. Confidence in all four domains (identifying manifestations, obtaining diagnostic studies, interpreting diagnostic studies, and initiating treatment) rose from a median of 3-4 to 5 (Mann-Whitney P < .001 for all). Reactions to the workshop were favorable, and most learners reported intent to change practice.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This multimodal simulation was an effective way to teach valproic acid overdose management.

articles.title: Forecasting the rate of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn in the United States based on recent trends in prehospital transfusion.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: As prehospital transfusion becomes more common in the United States (US), cases of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) might increase. This study forecasted the number of HDFN cases in 2029 resulting from RhD-positive prehospital transfusions.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: A regression was performed on the number of females of childbearing potential (FCP) who received RhD-positive prehospital transfusions between 2020 and 2024 in the US to forecast the total number of FCPs who would receive transfusions in 2029. Then, a model using current nativity and population demographics was used to calculate the regional rate of HDFN in 2029 (Model 1). In addition, the frequency of transfusing FCPs in the four US census regions in 2029 was varied based upon the regional uptake of prehospital low titer group O whole blood transfusion between 2024 and 2025 (Model 2) and the uptake of prehospital transfusion by ground ambulances between 2019 and 2026 (Model 3). Each model was instantiated 500 times.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: It was forecasted that 779 FCPs would receive prehospital transfusions in 2029 throughout the US. In Model 1, the number of years required for one case of HDFN to occur was calculated to range from 0.5 (South)-20.0 (Northeast). When the regional frequency of providing prehospital transfusions was varied, the number of years required for one case of HDFN to occur ranged from 0.6 (South)-13.5 (Northeast) (Model 2), and between 0.7 (South)-4.6 (Northeast) (Model 3).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: As prehospital transfusions increase, the risk of HDFN is predicted to also increase.

articles.title: Trainings and Recommendations for Physician Firearm Secure Storage Counseling for Suicide Prevention: A Scoping Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Suicide is a public health crisis in the USA. Secure storage of firearms can reduce suicide risk by putting time and distance between a suicidal crisis and access to a firearm. However, physicians often do not provide counseling to patients. This scoping review examines educational interventions that provide physicians and physicians-in-training skills to counsel patients about firearm secure storage.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) format. A literature search was conducted across Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, Cochrane Library, CINAHL Plus with Full Text, and Web of Science and included publications through April 9, 2025. Eligibility criteria included articles that (1) involved trainings on firearm secure storage for suicide prevention or provided commentary on what should be included in potential trainings; (2) had study populations that included physicians; and (3) were available in English.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty articles were included: 21 commentaries providing suggestions on physician firearm secure storage counseling education and training and 19 articles involving development and implementation of physician education and training. Training varied and included conversation strategies, facts about suicide, and storage methods and devices. Nineteen articles included study participant details, with emergency medicine (four studies), pediatrics (four studies), and psychiatry (three studies) most included. Most reported increased knowledge relating to firearms, improvements in attitudes and beliefs on importance of speaking with patients about firearm safety, and improvements in confidence and comfort in counseling.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This review found limited but promising literature on training physicians to provide firearm secure storage counseling for suicide prevention. Limitations include that only records published in English were included and that, as a scoping review, the quality of individual studies was not assessed. Standardized, evidence-based curricula are needed for broader implementation.

articles.title: Effects of chronic care model-based intervention offered to elderly patients with diabetes on medication adherence, self-management, and activities of daily living: a randomized controlled trial.

abstract.text: This study was conducted to reveal the effects of a Chronic Care Model (CCM)-based intervention offered to elderly patients with diabetes on their medication adherence, self-management, and activities of daily living. This randomized controlled study was conducted on diabetic patients; older adults received inpatient treatment in an internal medicine clinic of a state hospital; the patients in the trial group were provided with training using the CCM. The comparisons following the trial revealed that the differences between the group mean values were statistically significant in all variables except the Katz ADL (p < 0.05). The mean MARS score and mean total DSMS score of the trial group were found to be statistically significantly higher than those of the control group (p < 0.001). The study confirmed that CCM-based interventions offered to elderly patients with diabetes were effective on medication adherence and self-management.

articles.title: Sources of practice variation in febrile infants aged 8-60 days: a multi-level analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Management decisions for febrile infants vary greatly, with knowledge gaps in identifying sources of practice variation. Thus, we estimated proportions of total and age-stratified (8-28, 29-60 days) variation in hospitalization and lumbar puncture procedures contributed by patient (infant)-, physician-, and hospital-level factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of febrile infants aged 8-60 days seen in emergency departments in New York State from January 2012 to July 2021. We constructed a three-level multi-level logistic regression model with random effects for physician and hospital levels to partition total and age-stratified variation in hospitalizations and lumbar puncture procedures and adjusted for covariates at each level.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 35,756 febrile infants,18,124 were hospitalized (49%) and 12,959 received a lumbar puncture (36%). Adjusted models showed physician- and infant-level factors contributed the most to variation in hospitalization (59.3%) and lumbar puncture management decisions (81.9%), respectively. Hospital-level factors accounted for >10% of variation in hospitalizations and ~10% of variation in lumbar punctures. Hospital-level variation did not differ significantly by age.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Findings show divergent practice variation sources for hospitalization (physician-level) and lumbar puncture (infant-level). Hospital-level factors account for a non-negligible proportion of practice variation, representing opportunities to identify targeted interventions to reduce practice variation.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: Management decisions for febrile infants aged 8 to 60 days vary greatly Little is known about sources of practice variation that may be modifiable In this population-based cohort study, physician- and infant-level factors contributed the most to variation in hospitalization and lumbar puncture Hospital-level factors accounted for at least 10% of variation in hospitalizations and lumbar punctures Findings inform future hospital-level intervention studies.

articles.title: Avascular necrosis of the femur following COVID-19: an updated systematic review.
articles.journal_full: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: One of the complications of COVID-19 infection is avascular necrosis of the femoral head. To date, various studies have reported a wide range of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in patients with COVID-19. The previous systematic review included only 14 studies. So, this systematic review aims to update the findings of these studies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Databases such as PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were systematically searched by two independent researchers on April 1st, 2024.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A literature search revealed 1229 records, 161 full-texts were evaluated, and finally, 55 studies remained for systematic review. Fifty-five studies were included in this systematic review. Four studies were cross-sectional studies, six were retrospective studies, and the remaining (45studies) were case reports or case-series studies. Totally, 864 cases were included. Except for 12 studies, 43 studies reported the administration of steroid therapy in included cases. The most common underlying conditions were hypertension, followed by diabetes. In 274 (31.7%) of included cases, AVN was bilateral, and both hips were involved. In some studies, non-surgical treatments-including supplement therapy, anticoagulant therapy, physiotherapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy-were administered. Several studies reported symptomatic improvement in patients treated with the core decompression approach. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) was the most commonly used surgical treatment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in cases that have survived COVID-19 should be considered carefully as early diagnosis helps to preserve the joint and its function.

articles.title: Epidemiology and outcome of sudden cardiac arrest in elderly Nigerians: a prospective multicentre observational survey.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Limited information is available on sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) care in the elderly population in sub-Saharan Africa, despite the growing incidence of risk factors such as cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to describe the epidemiology and assess the outcomes of out-of-hospital and in-hospital SCA among the elderly population in Nigeria.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Prospective, multicentre observational survey on epidemiology and outcome of SCA arrest in Nigerian adults over a 20-month period.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Six purposefully selected teaching hospitals in the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Patients aged 65 years and above who experienced either out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) brought to the selected hospital or in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA). Data were analysed using IBM-SPSS V.25.0 (SPSS, Chicago, Illinois, USA). Descriptive statistics were used to summarise the data.

abstract.label: OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Main outcome measures were return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) from initial arrest, survival to hospital admission and survival to hospital discharge.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1069 (27.3%) out of the 3909 SCA data collected were elderly (aged ≥65 years). Of this, 91.0% were IHCA and 9.0% were OHCA. The age ranged from 65 years to 105 years, with a median of 75 (IQR 70–81) years for IHCA, and 65 years to 115 years, with a median of 72 (IQR 68–78) years for OHCA. There was a male preponderance in both cohorts, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.971). Arrests were witnessed in 97.2% of IHCA and 94.8% of OHCA events. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) yielded ROSC of 0.3% in IHCA and 3.1% in OHCA, and an overall hospital discharge survival of 0.1% and 2.1%, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The overall survival in both IHCA and OHCA was poor in elderly Nigerians, with a very low rate of bystander CPR in both OHCA and IHCA, despite the high rate of witness presence.

articles.title: 2026 International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Consensus on Science With Treatment Recommendations: Summary from the Basic Life Support; Advanced Life Support; Pediatric Life Support; Neonatal Life Support; Education, Implementation, and Teams; and First Aid Task Forces.

abstract.text: This is the annual summary of the International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Consensus on Science With Treatment Recommendations; a comprehensive review was completed in 2025. This latest summary addresses the most recent published resuscitation evidence reviewed by International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation task forces, including Basic Life Support; Advanced Life Support; Pediatric Life Support; Neonatal Life Support; Education, Implementation, and Teams; and First Aid. Members from these 6 task forces assessed the certainty of the evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation criteria, and their statements include consensus treatment recommendations. Highlights from task force discussions and insights into how decisions regarding treatment recommendations were made are provided in the Justification and Evidence-to-Decision Framework Highlights sections. The task forces also listed priority knowledge gaps for further research.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in older adults: a scoping review.

abstract.text: Multimorbidity, non-specific symptoms, and atypical disease manifestations are common in adults aged 65 years or older, complicating diagnostic and prognostic assessment. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides real-time bedside imaging that can support clinical decision making in this population; however, evidence on its use in older adults has not been systematically mapped. This scoping Review, endorsed by the European Geriatric Medicine Society, mapped POCUS utilisation across health-care settings, application domains, clinical indications, and outcomes. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles investigating the use of POCUS in older adults (defined as studies that exclusively enrolled older adults ≥65 years or reported a mixed-age study population with a mean age of 65 years or older) and published in English or another language represented within the review team (Italian, French, German, Spanish, Danish, or Turkish) with no restrictions on publication date. Of the 3897 records, 240 (6%) studies were included; 87 (36%) focused on older adult or geriatric-targeted populations and 153 (64%) on mixed-age populations with a mean age of 65 years or older. Evidence came predominantly from acute care, with few studies in geriatric settings. Thoracic POCUS was the most frequently investigated single-organ domain; multiorgan POCUS was also prominent. Diagnostic support and prognostic stratification predominated, whereas longitudinal monitoring and patient-centred outcomes were infrequent. Evidence on POCUS applications in older adults remains uneven, highlighting the need for further research in under-represented geriatric care settings and on patient-centred outcomes.

articles.title: Frailty as a predictor of chemotherapy-related outcomes in older adults with cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Chemotherapy-related adverse outcomes remain a major challenge in older adults with cancer. Frailty may compromise treatment tolerance; however, the prevalence of frailty before chemotherapy and its association with chemotherapy-related outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of pre-chemotherapy frailty and evaluate its association with chemotherapy-related outcomes in older adults with cancer.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Eight databases were systematically searched from inception to February 2026 for longitudinal studies investigating the association between pre-chemotherapy frailty and chemotherapy-related or survival outcomes in older adults with cancer. Pooled prevalence and risk estimates were synthesized using random-effects models, as appropriate. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Begg's test when at least 10 studies were available.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nineteen longitudinal studies involving 4127 older adults with cancer were included, with a pooled prevalence of pre-chemotherapy frailty of 24.6%. Frailty was significantly associated with an increased risk of chemotherapy-related toxicities, particularly non-hematologic toxicities, chemotherapy non-completion, dose reduction, unplanned hospitalization, as well as worse progression-free survival and overall survival. No significant associations were observed with hematologic toxicities, chemotherapy delay, or emergency department visits.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Frailty before chemotherapy is common among older adults with cancer and is associated with poorer treatment tolerance and adverse clinical outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating frailty assessment into routine geriatric oncology practice before chemotherapy to identify high-risk patients and inform individualized treatment planning, supportive care, and shared decision-making.

articles.title: Quality improvement project: Implementing a screening tool for acute stress disorder in pediatric trauma patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric patients who have suffered an acute traumatic injury are at an increased risk for developing mental health disorders, such as acute stress disorder (ASD). With traumatic injuries as the leading cause of emergency room visits and deaths in the pediatric population, ASD is expected to continue rising. The American College of Surgeons recently mandated screening for traumatic stress symptoms in pediatric Level I and Level II trauma centers.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The purpose of this quality improvement project was to achieve an 80% adherence rate for administration of a validated screening tool to pediatric patients admitted for a traumatic injury in an 18-month period.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The trauma social worker and trauma nurse practitioner administered the screening tool to eligible patients who suffered an acute traumatic injury. A patient's score was calculated from their questionnaire responses, determining the level of risk for developing mental health disorders. The percentage of eligible patients that received a screening tool, the patient's level of risk for developing acute stress symptoms, the mechanism of injury sustained, and the resources given to patients were collected and analyzed during the QI project (January 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Over an 18-month period, 118 patients completed screenings for ASD by receiving the Acute Stress Checklist for Kids-6. 25% of the patients who completed a screening tool showed symptoms for developing acute stress disorder. Of these 118 participants, 50 patients (42.3%) suffered an interpersonal injury, with 39 patients (33%) of the patients sustaining a firearm injury.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The results of this project suggest that implementing a process to ensure this hospital was identifying patients at risk for developing mental health problems, such as acute stress disorder, through administration of a validated screening tool allowed for goal adherence of screening tool administration.

articles.title: Pediatric stroke, transient ischemic attack, and non-vascular mimics in the emergency department: a three-group analysis of clinical predictors and diagnostic performance.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric stroke is a diagnostic challenge due to the high prevalence of stroke mimics in the emergency setting. This study aimed to identify distinguishing clinical features among confirmed stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and non-vascular mimics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort enrolled patients aged 1 month-18 years with acute focal neurological deficits presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department. Patients were classified into three groups: confirmed stroke, TIA, and non-vascular mimics. Firth penalized logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed for each pairwise comparison.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 103 patients, 25 (24.3%) had confirmed stroke, 24 (23.3%) TIA, and 54 (52.4%) non-vascular mimics. Stroke patients were younger than TIA (median 7.0 vs. 12.5 years; p = 0.002) and non-vascular mimic patients (7.0 vs. 11.0 years; p = 0.007). Symptom duration >48 h, focal seizures, and pathological reflexes were the strongest discriminators between stroke and TIA (all p < 0.05); pathological reflexes were absent in all non-vascular mimic patients. Chronic disease was more prevalent in stroke vs. TIA (48.0% vs. 16.7%; p = 0.032). Firth regression identified age (odds ratio [OR] 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67-0.99; p = 0.036) and symptom duration >48 h (OR 11.12; 95% CI 1.86-66.34; p = 0.008) as independent distinguishing clinical features of stroke vs. TIA. Combined model area under the curve (AUC): 0.898 (stroke vs. TIA) and 0.731 (stroke vs. non-vascular mimics). Routine laboratory parameters did not differ across groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Age, symptom duration, focal seizures, and pathological reflexes are key discriminators of stroke from TIA. Discriminability is substantially higher when contrasting stroke with TIA (AUC 0.898) than with non-vascular mimics (AUC 0.731), underscoring the value of separating TIA in the analytical framework. Prompt neuroimaging with systematic clinical assessment remains essential for accurate diagnosis.

articles.title: Calcium in trauma resuscitation: Transfusion volume or measurement-guided replacement?
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

articles.title: PIEZO1 activation alters membrane remodeling and aggregability of stored red blood cells.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Transfused red blood cells (RBCs) actively contribute to post-injury hemostasis due to surface phosphatidylserine (PS) exposure. We hypothesized that storage sensitizes erythrocytes to the PIEZO1-induced, calcium‑dependent, PS externalization through calcium and protein kinase C (PKC) dependent activation of the phospholipid scramblase TMEM16F.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Five units of type O whole blood were obtained for analysis at days 21 and 42 of storage. RBC PS was quantified by annexin V staining on flow cytometry at increasing extracellular CaCl₂ concentrations (0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 mmol/L), with and without the PIEZO1 agonist Yoda1 (0.2 μM), PKC agonist Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA; 6 μM) and antagonist chelerythrine chloride (CC; 10 μM), and the TMEM16 family inhibitor niclosamide (2 μM). RBC aggregometry was assessed by multiplate. Data were analyzed by analysis of variance and mixed-effects modeling.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: PS exposure increased in a Ca²⁺‑dependent manner in both day 21 and 42 RBCs (p<0.001). PIEZO1 stimulation enhanced this response to a greater extent in day 42 RBCs, with greater change in PS at 1 mmol/L (2.21% vs. -0.44%, p=0.021), 2 mmol/L (7.36% vs. 0.53%, p<0.001), and 5 mmol/L (12.09% vs. 6.40%, p<0.001) CaCl2. Compared with calcium alone, Yoda1 and PMA (+61.3%, p<0.001 for both) produced similar increases in PS externalization, whereas PKC inhibition (-45.6%, p=0.009) and TMEM16F inhibition (-4.6%, p=0.99) negated the PIEZO1 response. Yoda1 agonism preserved RBC aggregability after 42 days of storage (51.2±39.0 vs. 2.0±3.5 area under the curve, p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Storage sensitizes RBCs to PIEZO1-mediated, calcium-dependent, PS externalization through PKC- and TMEM16F-dependent signaling. Given its endogenous mechanosensitive properties, pharmacologic PIEZO1 activation highlights a potential mechanism by which mechanical stress encountered during trauma and transfusion through the injured microcirculation may promote erythrocyte phospholipid membrane remodeling and aggregability, contributing to the procoagulant activity of transfused RBCs.

articles.title: Persistent gaps in health-related quality of life measures for older adult trauma patients: A systematic review.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Older adults experience persistent functional and psychosocial consequences after trauma, but it remains unclear whether commonly used health-related quality of life (HRQoL) instruments adequately measure recovery in this population. This systematic review appraised psychometric evidence and risk of bias for HRQoL instruments used in United States trauma cohorts that included adults aged 65 years or older.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CINAHL were searched from inception through January 28, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was evaluated using an adapted Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies-of Interventions (ROBINS-I) assessment. Studies evaluating an HRQoL instrument as the target measure underwent Consensus-based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) Risk of Bias assessment for each reported measurement property. Results were rated as sufficient, insufficient, or indeterminate and synthesized by instrument.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 17,195 records, 19 studies were included. Studies most often examined isolated orthopedic trauma (n=7, 36.8%), spinal cord injury (n=6, 31.6%), other injury populations (n=3, 15.8%), polytrauma or systemic injury (n=2, 10.5%), and burns (n=1, 5.3%). Frequently evaluated domains included physical functioning (n=16), emotional or mental health (n=13), overall life satisfaction (n=13), social functioning (n=11), and physical symptoms (n=10). Although all studies used at least one previously developed patient-reported measure, none explicitly adapted or comprehensively validated an eligible HRQoL instrument for older adult trauma patients. Ten studies evaluated a target HRQoL instrument, contributing 33 COSMIN measurement property assessments: 19 sufficient, 10 indeterminate, and 4 insufficient. Overall risk of bias was low in six studies, moderate in eight, serious in three, and unclear in two.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Existing studies show that HRQoL instruments have been used in trauma cohorts including older adults, but they do not establish validity for older adult trauma patients specifically. Future studies should evaluate promising instruments in cohorts designed around older adults' recovery priorities and clinical characteristics after trauma.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Systematic Review; Level III.

articles.title: Compliance with the 2021 surviving sepsis campaign Hour-1 Bundle and impact on patient outcomes in a resource-limited setting: A quality improvement initiative in a referral hospital in Rwanda.

abstract.text: Sepsis and septic shock are common life-threatening conditions associated with high mortality globally. Compliance with the Society of Critical Care Medicine's Hour-1 Bundle for sepsis management has the potential to improve outcome, but the bundle is infrequently applied in resource-constrained settings. We assessed level of compliance with the Hour-1 bundle among patients diagnosed with sepsis and septic shock at the Accident and Emergency Department (AED) or Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of University Teaching Hospital of Butare, Rwanda. We conducted training for nurses and doctors in the AED and ICU, with the goal of improving compliance. We re-assessed bundle compliance one month after the training. We used univariate and multivariate analyses to evaluate the association of compliance and fluid resuscitation with hospital mortality while adjusting for severity of illness and other covariates. Our finding showed that seventy-eight patients were enrolled during the pre-intervention period, and 82 in post-intervention. The overall compliance with at least 4 elements of the Hour-1 bundle before the intervention was 14%, and 76% after the intervention (p < 0.001). Mortality was lower in the post-intervention period than in the pre-intervention period (51.2% vs 74.4%; p = 0.003). Non-survivors had a significantly lower bundle compliance than survivors (35% vs 80%; adjusted OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.05-0.57; p = 0.004). Administered 2 liters of IV fluids and beyond during the first hour was independently associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR 19.38, 95% CI 5.63-66.75; p < 0.001). Findings from this Quality Improvement project suggest that compliance with the Hour-1 sepsis bundle in a resource-constrained setting can be improved with training, can improve outcome.. Administration of ≥2 liters during the first hour in those was independently associated with a higher in-hospital mortality, although bundle-compliant resuscitation was not. More research is needed, both on the implementation of sepsis bundles in resource-constrained settings, to assess if all bundle elements are as effective in these settings as recommended in the international guidelines.

articles.title: LeadMix-MST: Robust Myocardial Infarction Detection from Minimal-Lead ECG Signals.
articles.journal_full: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

abstract.text: The 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is the standard for diagnosing myocardial infarction (MI), but its use in pre-hospital and resource-limited settings is limited by hardware complexity and electrode placement requirements. This study addresses a biomedical and health informatics challenge by investigating MI screening from minimal-lead ECG suitable for mobile and telemedicine applications. We propose LeadMix-MST, a lead-mixing multi scale spatio-temporal architecture for reduced-lead ECG analysis. Using three 12-lead ECG datasets, we conducted patient-level cross-dataset evaluations across devices and populations. The predefined lead set was an important design factor, with I-aVL-V5 and I-II-V3 performing most consistently. On these leads, the architecture remained competitive with larger baseline models at under 1Mparameters. A model trained on the Shandong Provincial Hospital dataset and evaluated on the Physikalisch-Technische Bun desanstalt dataset achieved an F1-score of 0.933 ± 0.003 and an AUROC of 0.937 ± 0.004 using a 3-lead configuration (I-aVL-V5), exceeding the full 12-lead setting on this dataset. The proposed framework maintains a favor able balance between diagnostic performance, parameter efficiency, and practical deployability, primarily by reducing electrode placement burden.

articles.title: Paintball-Related Ocular Injuries.
Lung clearance index and radiological pulmonary involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis: an exploratory cross-sectional study.

abstract.text: Lung clearance index (LCI) measures ventilation heterogeneity, but its relationship with pulmonary involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) remains insufficiently characterized. We examined the cross-sectional association of LCI with radiological pulmonary involvement and compared its discrimination with conventional pulmonary function measures, including diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).79 patients with LCH were retrospectively recruited: 54 with and 25 without pulmonary involvement at HRCT). Baseline nitrogen multiple-breath washout, pulmonary function testing, and high-resolution computed tomography were obtained within one week. Analyses included receiver operating characteristic curves, paired DeLong comparisons, and Firth penalized logistic regression. All analyses were exploratory.Mean LCI value in PLCH was significantly higher compared to LCH (mean difference 4.35, 95% CI 3.02-5.67). Its AUC was 0.919 (95% CI 0.861-0.978). In 77 participants with DLCO data, paired AUCs were 0.921 for LCI and 0.751 for DLCO (difference 0.169, 95% CI 0.029-0.309; Holm-adjusted p = 0.018). Higher LCI was associated with radiological pulmonary involvement after adjustment for age, sex and pack-years (adjusted OR per one-unit increase 5.09, 95% CI 2.32-16.67). At the sample-derived threshold > 9.86, sensitivity was 72.2% and specificity 96.0%, with 15 false negatives. Among 42 participants meeting fixed criteria for preserved conventional function, 25 had pulmonary involvement and 14 of these exceeded this threshold.The present study showed higher ventilatory inhomogeneity (higher LCI) in LCH patients with pulmonary involvement compared to LCH ones without it. These exploratory findings support prospective evaluation of LCI as a complementary functional measure. They do not establish early detection, longitudinal prediction, monitoring utility, or safe avoidance of HRCT.

articles.title: Alfred Russel Wallace's 1858 Theory of Natural Selection: Reassessing the Evidence for the Place of Discovery, the Source of Inspiration, and the Date of His Essay's Dispatch to Darwin.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the history of biology

abstract.text: Alfred Russel Wallace independently formulated natural selection in Southeast Asia in 1858 and sent an essay explaining the theory to Charles Darwin. The circumstances of its conception and dispatch have remained controversial because Wallace's original manuscript and cover letter are lost, while his surviving contemporary records and later recollections appear inconsistent. This study reassesses three connected questions: where Wallace conceived the theory, what prompted his insight, and when he dispatched his essay. Wallace's Travel Journal, Species Notebook, correspondence, and published accounts provide the strongest support for Dodinga, on the island then called Gilolo (now Halmahera), as the location of the fever-induced insight and initial drafting. His later placement of the episode on Ternate is best understood as a compression of events that occurred first at Dodinga and later at his Ternate base. The argument and terminology of the 1858 essay, particularly its use of "geometrical ratio," provide contemporary evidence that Thomas Robert Malthus' population theory supplied the intellectual framework. Wallace's observations of camouflage in tiger beetles did not inspire his discovery of natural selection, as has been reported. Finally, the postal and documentary evidence favors dispatch of Wallace's essay and cover letter by the March rather than the April 1858 mail. However, the date on which Darwin received the packet remains unresolved, and there is no evidence to support suggestions that he withheld or misused Wallace's manuscript.

articles.title: Suicide risk in first- and second-generation young migrants: a 12-month cohort study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Evidence on the impact of migration on suicidal behavior among adolescents remains limited. Particularly, there is scarce knowledge concerning clinical populations and second generations of migrants. This cohort study examined differences in clinical, psychosocial and behavioral profiles associated with suicidal behavior among non-migrant, first-generation and second-generation migrant adolescents presenting to a Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Emergency Department (ED) in Madrid.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adolescents aged 8-17 years (N = 1,281) presenting with suicidal ideation or behavior were identified at an index ED visit, and their electronic medical records were retrospectively reviewed over a 12-month follow-up period. Sociodemographic, clinical and psychosocial risk factors-including socioeconomic adversity, family psychiatric history, maltreatment, family conflict, victim of bullying and eating problems-were systematically recorded. Reasons for consultation, methods and severity of suicidal behavior were compared across migration groups. Cox proportional hazards regression models, including age- and sex-adjusted and two multivariable models, examined whether migration status independently predicted time to repeat suicidal behavior during follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Migrant adolescents-both first- and second-generation-presented with a higher burden of psychosocial adversity and more severe self-harm methods at index ED visit compared to non-migrants. Migrant adolescents, particularly first-generation, were less likely to have had prior outpatient mental health follow-up. In fully adjusted multivariable models accounting for sociodemographic, psychosocial and clinical covariates, including previous suicidal behavior, second-generation migrant background remained an independent predictor of repeat suicidal behavior, whereas first-generation background did not show a statistically significant effect.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Second‑generation migrant background was associated with a more severe clinical presentation and repeat suicidal behavior, even after adjusting for psychosocial and clinical covariates. These findings suggest that generational migration status is a relevant factor to consider when assessing and following up on suicide risk for adolescents of migrant origin, particularly those from a second-generation background.

articles.title: Unrecognized Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder as the Lingering Shadow of Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Thromboneurosis, though not a formally recognized diagnostic entity, describes the chronic anxiety, hypervigilance, and fear of recurrence that can follow venous thromboembolism, an under-recognized and underdiagnosed complication of pulmonary embolism (PE). Despite growing literature on its prevalence, no comprehensive, venous thromboembolism-specific psychological screening instrument, standardized diagnostic pathway, or guideline-endorsed management strategy currently exists. Consequently, cases often remain undiagnosed until significant quality-of-life decline occurs.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We report a 43-year-old man who, after appropriate treatment for intermediate-risk (Category C2) PE, presented to the emergency department 5 separate times with recurrent chest pain, dyspnea, and palpitations. He was subsequently diagnosed with thromboneurosis/post-PE post-traumatic stress disorder.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the substantial clinical and health care burden associated with delayed recognition of the psychological effects of post-PE and supports routine integration of structured psychological screening into multidisciplinary post-PE follow-up pathways.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Structured psychological screening should be integrated into multidisciplinary post-PE follow-up to reduce diagnostic delay and unnecessary acute care utilization.

articles.title: Changes in Patterns of Health Care Use Among Older Adults in Singapore Across a Decade: Repeated Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: There is limited evidence on the patterns of health care use among older adults in Singapore over the past decade.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study examines whether the proportion of specific services used within sociodemographic subgroups, the factors associated with health care use, and the network structure of health care use have changed over a decade.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used data from 2 repeated nationwide cross-sectional surveys of Singapore residents aged 60 years and older, conducted in 2013 (n=2565) and 2023 (n=2010). Health care service use was obtained from an adapted version of the Client Service Receipt Inventory and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and network analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The most significant changes between 2013 and 2023 were in the proportions of older adults who had consulted private hospital/clinic doctors (decreased by 4.6 percentage points; n=655, 26.5% vs n=425, 21.9%; P=.02), consulted public and private dentists (increased by 6.4 percentage points; n=215, 11.6% vs n=269, 18%; P<.001), and had health insurance (increased by 26.9 percentage points; n=1312, 59.9% vs n=1697, 86.8%; P<.001). Those diagnosed with high blood pressure and diabetes were more likely to consult primary care doctors, while those diagnosed with dementia and heart problems were more likely to consult public hospital doctors and health workers, visit emergency departments, and require hospitalization services in both 2013 and 2023. We also found that those diagnosed with dementia were more likely to visit intermediate and long-term care services in both 2013 and 2023. Network analysis revealed that there were strong connections between respite care, nursing homes, and hospital admissions in 2023.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study provides important data on population-level changes in health care usage among older adults across the decade from 2013 to 2023, which will help policymakers ensure better health care delivery for older adults.

articles.title: Identifying barriers to headache care for Black patients in Toronto: A community-informed qualitative study of patient experience and recommendations.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES/BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Our objective was to gain a better understanding of how Black patients in the Greater Toronto Area experience barriers and facilitators of headache care. Headache is a common, potentially serious neurological condition. Migraine specifically, can lead to emergency room visits, missed workdays, and a reduction in overall quality of life. Black and Indigenous communities experience worse headache outcomes compared to other communities. We engaged Black patients with headache in the Greater Toronto Area to learn from their perspectives on barriers they face in accessing headache care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study deployed an intersectional, community-informed qualitative research methodology. We included patients between 18 and 65 years of age who self-identified as Black and live in the Greater Toronto Area. We conducted semistructured interviews between July 2022 and September 2023. Interviews were deidentified and transcribed prior to inductive thematic analysis to reveal emerging themes and subthemes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We conducted a total of 12 interviews. Ten were included for analysis. Multiple themes and subthemes were identified, including the impact of headache on personal and family quality of life, negative experiences in emergency departments, as well as challenges navigating primary and specialist care. Patients specifically noted delays in receiving a diagnosis, lack of headache education, and difficulty accessing appropriate pharmacological therapies. Barriers to headache specialist care included difficulty getting time off work, cost of transportation, lack of access to referrals, and wait time to see a specialist.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This is the first study to document the experiences of Black patients seeking headache care in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Patients with headaches face barriers to care regardless of race, ethnicity, or socioeconomic status. This was not a comparative study; rather, we specifically sought to hear the voices of patients from historically marginalized Black communities who have not been reflected in research and for whom headache outcomes are poor relative to other communities. The participants provided key insights into areas for improvement. Participant recommendations include location of specialist clinics in Black communities, use of social media and other community news networks to promote migraine and headache education in communities, and ongoing use of virtual care models to increase scheduling flexibility and reduce financial burdens of seeking care. Physicians and clinic staff who reflect communities they serve were recommended as a way of improving physician-patient respect and communication.

articles.title: Implementation of the seizure code in a tertiary hospital: Effects on emergency care times and clinical outcomes in severe seizures.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess the impact of implementing the Seizure Code (SC), a structured multidisciplinary emergency protocol for severe seizures, on care times and clinical outcomes at a tertiary hospital.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Single-center, retrospective observational study including episodes of severe seizures in patients aged 18 years or older managed between January 2023 and December 2024, comparing pre-SC and post-SC periods. The primary outcome was time from seizure onset to administration of the first anti-seizure medication (ASM). Secondary outcomes included other care intervals, process indicators, and clinical outcomes. Care intervals were analyzed with accelerated failure time models (percentage change in median time), length of stay in a competing-risks framework, and binary outcomes with Firth-penalized logistic regression (odds ratios, OR), all adjusted for prespecified covariates and clustered by patient.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1959 episodes identified, 378 (175 pre-SC, 203 post-SC) met SC activation criteria. Time to the first ASM, the primary outcome, did not differ significantly (27% shorter, 95% CI -15% to 53% for benzodiazepines; 27%, -6% to 50% for others). Time to urgent video-EEG (VEEG) was 48% shorter (29%-61%) and the neurological assessment-VEEG interval 63% shorter (31%-80%). Pre-notification by Emergency Medical Services increased (22.9% vs. 37.8%; p = 0.003). Hospital stay (7.48 vs. 5.08 days; subdistribution hazard ratio for discharge alive 1.36, 1.02-1.89) and intensive care unit stay (3.20 vs. 1.48 days) were shorter. Thirty-day seizure recurrence was lower (8.0% vs. 3.0%; adjusted OR 0.33, 0.12-0.84). Mortality and functional status at discharge did not differ.

abstract.label: SIGNIFICANCE
abstract.text: The primary outcome, time to first anti-seizure medication, was not significantly shorter after implementation of the structured emergency protocol. The observed benefits were concentrated in secondary process and resource-utilization indicators: implementation of the Seizure Code was associated with faster access to urgent VEEG, shorter hospital and intensive care unit stays, and lower 30-day seizure recurrence, without a significant effect on mortality. These findings support protocolized emergency pathways in severe seizures.

abstract.label: PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY
abstract.text: Severe seizures are emergencies in which fast, coordinated care matters. We compared how patients were treated at one hospital before and after a new protocol, the Seizure Code, was introduced. Afterwards, patients had urgent video-EEG (a recording of brain activity) sooner and spent fewer days in hospital and in the intensive care unit, and fewer had another seizure within 30 days. However, the time to the first anti-seizure medication did not change significantly, and deaths and disability at discharge were unchanged.

articles.title: Emergency Life-Saving Technician-Performed Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma in Moving Ambulances: A Pilot Innovation Report.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: In Japan, Emergency Life-Saving Technicians (ELSTs) cannot independently perform diagnostic ultrasound under the current legal framework. If ELST-performed focused assessment with sonography for trauma (FAST) is to be introduced in the prehospital setting, technical feasibility during ambulance motion and the viability of remote physician observation must be established.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of ELST-performed FAST in moving ambulances in a controlled manikin setting and to descriptively assess an integrated monitoring system for remote observation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective observational pilot study was conducted at the Okayama City Fire Department Training Center in Okayama Prefecture, Japan on March 3, 2025. Twenty ELSTs completed structured e-learning and a hands-on workshop using standardized FAST/ER FAN manikins. Participants performed FAST under three fixed-order conditions: stationary (STOP), 15km/hour, and 30km/hour on a 250-m circular course. The primary outcome was the total Task-Specific Checklist (TSC) score (0-24 points). Secondary outcomes were examination time, site-specific TSC subscores, inter-rater agreement, and a descriptive assessment of transmitted image quality by two specialist physicians.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 20 ELSTs completed the study. Mean total TSC scores were 23.4 (SD = 0.8) in the STOP condition, 23.4 (SD = 0.9) at 15km/hour, and 23.7 (SD = 0.6) at 30km/hour. Compared with the STOP condition, the mean difference in total TSC score was 0.08 points (95% CI, -0.24 to 0.39; P for noninferiority < 0.001) at 15km/hour and 0.33 points (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.69; P for noninferiority < 0.001) at 30km/hour. Both moving conditions met the pre-specified noninferiority criterion relative to the STOP condition. Mean examination times were 36.7 (SD = 14.4) seconds in the STOP condition, 30.3 (SD = 9.8) seconds at 15km/hour, and 31.9 (SD = 14.8) seconds at 30km/hour. Inter-rater agreement for TSC scoring was moderate (weighted kappa, 0.56). Descriptive ratings suggested that transmitted image quality was generally favorable for remote review in this controlled setting.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this controlled manikin-based pilot study, ELST-performed FAST was technically feasible during moderate ambulance motion, and remote physician observation was feasible. These findings may help inform staged prehospital ultrasound training and future clinical validation under legal and operational constraints.

articles.title: Efficiency of Rescue Paramedic Hoist versus Underslung Antenna in Helicopter-Based Avalanche Searches: A Randomized Trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Survival for avalanche victims is time-dependent, and survival is often reliant on ground companion rescue. Due to the time-critical nature of burial, remote locations, and high frequency of concomitant severe trauma, helicopters are often dispatched to these incidents. While helicopter-based transceiver searches are standard, the most efficient deployment strategy, either using an underslung antenna or hoisting a rescue paramedic (RP) with a handheld transceiver, remains unknown. This study compared the operational efficiency of these two methods in the Norwegian Search-and-Rescue (SAR) Helicopter Service.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A dual randomized, experimental field trial was conducted with the on-duty SAR helicopter and crew at the Ørland Main Airforce Base (Trøndelag, Norway). A simulated avalanche area of 80 × 150 meters was used, and six avalanche transceivers were buried at approximately 0.5m depth across the area. Only one transceiver was active at each run, and the locations were randomized to prevent crew memorization. The sequence of which procedure to use was also randomized. Four operational timestamps were recorded: First Signal, Optimal Signal, RP on Ground, and Transceiver Found.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Over three days, a total of 25 trial runs were performed, 13 with Antenna Search and 12 with RP Hoist Search.
