The RP Hoist Search was significantly faster in both time to Optimal Signal, with a difference between the groups of 29 seconds (95% CI, 9 - 50), and time for RP on Ground, with a difference between the groups of 124 seconds (95% CI, 98 - 151). For the total time to Transceiver Found, the difference between the groups was 143 seconds (95% CI, 113 - 172; P <0.001). Furthermore, the RP Hoist Search resulted in significantly faster fine search on the ground.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This randomized, experimental field trial comparing two currently used standard search procedures in the Norwegian SAR service showed that the RP Hoist Search was significantly more efficient than the Antenna Search for localizing buried avalanche victims, reducing total localization time by more than two minutes. Given that survival probability is reduced after 10-15 minutes of burial, this time saving may be clinically significant. The findings support that RP Hoist Search is an effective localization strategy for SAR helicopter services with comparable hoist systems.

articles.title: Finding the Missing Link: Public Health Advisories and Computable Decision Support for Frontline Health Care Personnel.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Timely recognition and response to emerging infectious diseases are critical, yet frontline health care personnel often struggle with access to crucial information. This study assessed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Health Alert Network (HAN) advisories as potential computable data sources for clinical decision support (CDS) systems aimed at frontline health care personnel responding to emerging infectious diseases.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 89 HAN advisories using a CDS prototype designed for emergency room triage nurses managing high-impact pathogens. Two reviewers systematically annotated advisories for key elements, with a third reviewer resolving discrepancies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 89 CDC HAN advisories, 70 addressed infectious pathogens, including 50 on 13 high-consequence organisms. Among these advisories, 47% included a start date, none had an end date, 53% mentioned symptoms, and 11% described isolation precautions, which varied significantly from 0% to 27%. Early COVID-19 advisories illustrated evolving guidance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: CDC HAN advisories are often incomplete, specifically lacking dynamic time-specific details and isolation precautions. Enhancing advisories with structured, computable data and a flexible CDS system will improve the timely dissemination of actionable information to frontline health care personnel. This will enable swift, informed decision-making and more optimized patient care.

articles.title: Occupational Preparedness Among Peruvian Police Officers: Exploratory Institutional Comparisons With Army Personnel During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Non-health care first responders are essential components of public health emergency response systems, yet their occupational preparedness during health crises remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to describe occupational conditions before and during the COVID-19 pandemic among Peruvian police officers and Army personnel and explore institutional differences in preparedness-related characteristics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A secondary cross-sectional analysis was conducted using survey data from 512 active-duty personnel in Peru, including 352 police officers and 160 Army personnel. Occupational conditions before and during the pandemic were described, including work organization, transportation, training, perceived preparedness, mistreatment, and self-procurement of protective supplies. Exploratory unadjusted comparisons were performed using chi-square tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the pandemic, participants reported increased public-order assignments (26.9% vs. 18.3%), field-based work (40.3% vs. 36.0%), walking commuting (62.1% vs. 37.9%), and longer commuting times. Although 72.9% reported face-to-face COVID-19 training, 88.1% did not feel qualified to address COVID-19-related issues. Masks were self-purchased by 60.5% of participants. Institutional differences were observed in COVID-19-related health status, occupation type, and perceived preparedness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Preparedness among security forces during public health emergencies requires more than training delivery. Emergency plans should incorporate tailored education, risk communication, protective supply planning, and institutional support for non-health care first responders.

articles.title: Low-Level Pyuria and Antibiotic Prescribing for Suspected Urinary Tract Infection in Children.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Our objective was to understand the impact of urinalysis results on clinician antibiotic prescribing for pediatric patients evaluated at ambulatory visits. We hypothesized that responses to low pyuria levels contribute disproportionately to overtreatment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study combined electronic health record and abstracted symptom data from emergency department and urgent care visits to 4 Northern California settings. We sampled ambulatory visits by patients aged between 2 months and 17 years who underwent urinalysis between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess relationships between urinalysis results, clinical covariates including age, and empiric antibiotic initiation. We estimated attributable impact of these relationships on overtreatment for patients in whom urinary tract infection (UTI) was excluded by culture criteria. We similarly estimated impact on treatment for those with culture-confirmed UTI.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1150 patients with median age 6.3 years, 191 (16.6%) received antibiotics. Low pyuria levels (trace leukocyte esterase, 10-69 white blood cells [WBC]/mm,3 5-10 WBC/high-power field) were associated with antibiotic initiation with adjusted odds ratio 6.62 (95% CI 3.72-11.79) compared with no pyuria. The adjusted attributable fraction (aAF) for overtreatment at this level was 17.0% (95% CI 10.3%-23.2%), with aAF 1.8% (95% CI 1.1%-2.4%) for UTI treatment. Differential impacts on overtreatment and UTI treatment were consistent in age-stratified analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: To promote selective UTI treatment, clinicians should consider degree of pyuria in context with age, risk factors, symptoms, and other urinalysis results. Health system interventions should be designed to mitigate excess influence of low pyuria levels and promote integrated diagnostic assessments.

articles.title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

articles.title: Common acetabular fracture patterns in patients with femoroacetabular impingement.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The incidence of acetabular fractures is rising, affecting both younger and elderly patient populations. Developmental abnormalities such as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and hip dysplasia alter hip biomechanics, potentially predisposing younger patients to fracture. FAI, resulting from a cam and/or pincer deformity, is common, affecting 25% of asymptomatic males and 5% of asymptomatic females, and has been linked to hip pain and early osteoarthritis. However, the relationship between FAI morphology and acetabular fracture pattern remains unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients, 18-55 years old, treated between 2005 and 2023 for acetabular fracture, hip dislocation, or femoral head fracture were reviewed for FAI morphology using the Judet and Letournel classification systems. Statistical comparisons were conducted using Fisher's exact tests and unpaired t-tests, with significance set at p < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 294 patients (72%) exhibited plain radiographic FAI morphology, while 115 (28%) served as controls. The most common fracture pattern in both groups was posterior wall (PW) fractures (23.1% FAI, 31.3% control). Male FAI patients were significantly more likely to experience transverse fractures (p = 0.032, OR=4.6) and posterior column plus PW fractures (p = 0.035, OR=2.5) than controls. Among FAI patients, posterior column fractures were significantly more likely to occur in females (p = 0.011, OR=19). A total of 31 (27.0%) control patients and 63 (21.4%) FAI patients experienced complications.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In our data set, FAI patients accounted for 72% of patients undergoing acetabular fracture ORIF. FAI patients most commonly sustained posterior wall fractures, but male FAI patients had a significantly higher rate of transverse and posterior column plus PW. FAI patients experienced a complication rate of 21.4% compared to 27.0% in non-FAI patients.

articles.title: Robotic navigation-assisted versus conventional freehand placement of the infra-acetabular screw in acetabular fracture surgery: A retrospective comparative study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The infra-acetabular screw (IAS) is an important component of fixation constructs for complex acetabular fractures, but accurate freehand placement is technically demanding, and evidence on robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement remains limited. This study compared robotic navigation-assisted (RA) and conventional fluoroscopic freehand (CF) IAS placement in acetabular fracture surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective study, 53 patients with acetabular fractures who underwent IAS fixation between June 2022 and July 2024 were included, 28 underwent RA placement using the HoloSight robotic navigation system and 25 underwent CF placement. The primary outcome was screw-placement accuracy, graded on postoperative CT according to the Lonstein criteria. Secondary outcomes included the number of guide-wire adjustments, fluoroscopy frequency, IAS insertion time, total operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture reduction quality, hip function, and complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The grade 0 (no cortical penetration) rate was higher in the RA group than in the CF group (96.4% [27/28] vs. 60.0% [15/25], p = 0.005). RA placement was associated with fewer guide-wire adjustments (0.07 ± 0.26 vs. 3.60 ± 1.15), fewer fluoroscopies (9.32 ± 1.66 vs. 21.28 ± 3.18), shorter IAS insertion time (10.36 ± 2.50 vs. 26.68 ± 4.11 min), shorter total operative time (134.54 ± 15.46 vs. 155.80 ± 18.48 min), and less intraoperative blood loss (468.21 ± 84.68 vs. 588.40 ± 80.76 mL) (all p < 0.001). The mean follow-up duration was 15.7 ± 2.0 months (range, 13-22 months). Reduction quality, hip function, and complication rates did not differ significantly between the two groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement was associated with significantly higher screw-placement accuracy and greater procedural efficiency than the conventional freehand technique, without compromising fracture reduction quality, hip function, or safety.

articles.title: The prevalence of mental health service use after long-term minor-to-moderate motor vehicle crash injury: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Minor to moderate motor vehicle crash (MVC) injuries can lead to persistent psychological distress, yet evidence regarding mental health service (MHS) use is limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and characterise the determinants of MHS use after minor to moderate MVC injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study examined Australians with work-related, MVC injuries and workers' compensation claims exceeding 24 months duration. Claims and services data were linked with healthcare records to capture MHS use before and after injury. The injured group was divided into severity sub-groups based on hospital admission status (hospitalised, non-hospitalised). A community comparator group was matched to the non-hospitalised group based on gender and injury year. The primary outcome was MHS period prevalence within 24 months. Determinants of MHS were identified through binomial logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 574 non-hospitalised, 293 hospitalised, and 8294 community comparators included in the study cohort. The prevalence of MHS use at 24 months post injury was highest for the hospitalised group (36.9%), followed by the non-hospitalised group (31.5%) and community comparators (13.5%). The non-hospitalised group had 3.14 times greater odds (95% CI 2.53, 3.88) of MHS use compared to community comparators, and had the highest prevalence of publicly-funded MHS (18.8%). Hospitalised participants (28.3%) had a higher prevalence of workers' compensation funded MHS compared to non-hospitalised participants (19.3%). The adjusted odds of MHS use were higher among females (OR 2.05 [1.42, 2.97]), and people who had used MHS in the 12 months prior to injury (OR 4.66 [2.41, 9.50]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: People with non-hospitalised MVC injuries had a significantly higher prevalence of MHS use compared with their matched community comparator group, and people with hospitalised MVC injuries had the highest prevalence at 24 months-follow up. The highest proportion of people assessing publicly funded MHS was by people in the non-hospitalised group. These findings highlight the ongoing mental health needs of people with minor to moderate MVC injury. Monitoring for the early post injury psychological signs and symptoms, and timely referral to MHS, could reduce psychological burden following MVC injury.

articles.title: Is surgeon technique a modifiable risk factor for heterotopic ossification after posterior acetabular fracture fixation? A multi-surgeon study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Heterotopic ossification (HO) is a well-recognized complication following operative fixation of acetabular fractures through a posterior approach. Established risk factors largely reflect nonmodifiable patient and injury characteristics. Whether surgeon-controlled aspects of operative technique influence HO remains poorly defined. The purpose of this study was to determine if the individual surgeon and specific technique variables are associated with HO after accounting for established patient and injury factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 1292 patients who underwent acetabular fracture fixation through a Kocher-Langenbeck approach at two Level 1 trauma centers between 2010 and 2025 by 14 fellowship-trained orthopaedic traumatologists. Patients receiving any form of HO prophylaxis were excluded. Four surgeon-controlled variables were examined: aggressiveness of gluteus minimus debridement, trochanteric osteotomy, thrombin gel use, and closed suction drainage. HO was graded on final radiographs by two independent reviewers using the Brooker classification, with third-reader adjudication for disagreements, and categorized as little-to-no (grade 0-I), moderate (grade II), or severe (grade III-IV). Mixed-effects logistic regression models with surgeon as a random effect were used to assess the associations between patient, injury, and surgeon-controlled technique variables, as well as the individual surgeon, with severe and moderate HO formation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Little-to-no HO occurred in 1132 patients (87.6%), moderate HO in 96 (7.4%), and severe HO in 64 (5.0%). Aggressive gluteus minimus debridement was not associated with HO severity. For severe HO, the surgeon did not contribute meaningfully to model performance, and no surgeon-controlled technique variables were significant; severe head injury, mechanical ventilation beyond 72 h, African-American race, and dual surgical approaches were associated with severe HO. For moderate HO, the surgeon contributed moderately, and both trochanteric osteotomy (odds ratio [OR] 3.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-12) and closed suction drainage (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.0-3.1) were associated with increased odds of moderate HO.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Severe HO following posterior acetabular fracture fixation is predominantly driven by patient and injury characteristics rather than surgeon technique. Aggressive gluteus minimus debridement does not appear to reduce HO risk, and prevention efforts should prioritize patient-level risk stratification.

articles.title: The Burden of Upper Extremity Injuries from All-Terrain Vehicle Use: A 10-Year Analysis of the Paediatric Population.
articles.journal: J Hand Surg Asian Pac Vol
articles.journal_full: The journal of hand surgery Asian-Pacific volume

abstract.text: Background: All-terrain vehicles (ATVs) are an increasingly popular motor vehicle used for both recreation and work in the United States. However, their accessibility has raised safety concerns, particularly within the paediatric population, as ATVs have been linked to a variety of injuries in children. This study aimed to characterise ATV-related upper extremity injuries in paediatric patients. Methods: Data were collected from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) database for all ATV-related upper extremity injuries in patients aged 0-17 years between 2014 and 2023. Demographic characteristics included patient age, sex and race. Features of the injuries, such as the segment of the upper extremity affected, type of injury and patient disposition, were also recorded. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to identify patient profiles and injury trends. Results: Over the 10 years, 2,865 paediatric patients presented to emergency departments for an ATV-related injury (corresponding to 3,612 total injuries) reported to the NEISS. Of these, 2,529 patients sustained upper extremity injuries (corresponding to 2,718 injuries; 106,126 injuries nationwide). The vast majority (88.3%) of the patients presented with upper extremity injuries, and 75.2% of all injuries involved the upper extremity. Nearly half (46.4%) of injuries occurred between 2020 and 2023. The mean patient age was 11.6 years, and adolescents sustained the plurality of injuries (p < 0.0001). Males (65.6%) and white individuals (61.4%) represented significantly greater proportions of patients (p < 0.0001). The 'lower arm' was most frequently injured (p < 0.0001), and fractures represented the majority of injuries (p < 0.0001). The vast majority of patients (86%) were discharged from the emergency department (p < 0.0001). Conclusions: ATV use represents a substantial upper extremity injury risk to the paediatric population, with a recent increase since 2020. Implementation of stricter age requirements, safety equipment and training programs could mitigate these preventable injuries. Level of Evidence: Level IV (Therapeutic).

articles.title: A quality improvement initiative of implementing pediatric colonoscopy performance metrics at a tertiary medical center.
articles.journal_full: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Current guidelines for pediatric endoscopy have highlighted the importance of engaging in formal quality improvement (QI) processes to enhance procedural performance. We conducted a single-center, longitudinal QI initiative using standardized colonoscopy performance reports to monitor and improve both individual and facility key performance indicators over time.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Starting in July 2015, a multidisciplinary QI team developed and distributed standardized colonoscopy performance reports, with the primary aim of improving providers' successful ileal intubation rates to ≥90% by June 30, 2023. Secondary aims included: (1) ensuring mean colonoscopy procedure times of <60 min and (2) compliance with use of our institution's preferred language for documenting adequacy of bowel preparation in ≥95% of colonoscopy reports. We also monitored rates of emergency room visits and hospital admissions within 72 h of the procedure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 6240 diagnostic colonoscopies by 25 endoscopists over the 8-year study period were included. Endoscopists' mean terminal ileal intubation rates increased from 89.6% to 93%. Mean duration of colonoscopy remained stable at 43.1 min. Use of a preferred language to document bowel preparation improved from a mean of 89.6%-92.9%. There was no change in post-procedural emergency room visits and/or hospital admissions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: QI methodology was successfully used to review procedural performance and improve terminal ileal intubation rates, standardize documentation of bowel prep adequacy, and procedural efficiency. Future multi-center studies are needed to better understand whether ongoing monitoring and reporting of similar pediatric endoscopy performance data could be used to improve endoscopic quality more broadly.

articles.title: Heterotopic pregnancy at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Heterotopic pregnancy, defined as the coexistence of an intrauterine and an extrauterine pregnancy, is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition. While its incidence in assisted reproductive technology pregnancies is well documented, spontaneous heterotopic pregnancy remains exceedingly rare, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. We present the case of a ruptured heterotopic pregnancy in a haemodynamically unstable patient, highlighting the diagnostic and management challenges in a resource-limited setting.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We present the case of a 34-year-old Ghanaian woman, Gravida 3 Para 1 (alive) + 1 spontaneous abortion, who presented to the Emergency Unit of the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) with a 2-month history of amenorrhoea and a 1-day history of abdominal pain. Her vital signs on arrival indicated haemorrhagic shock (blood pressure 69/39 mmHg, heart rate 101 beats per minute). Bedside ultrasound revealed a live intrauterine gestation at 8 weeks with cardiac activity and a left adnexal mass with free fluid in the pelvis. She was resuscitated following the ATLS protocol and underwent emergency exploratory laparotomy under general anaesthesia. Intraoperatively, approximately 1.28 L of hemoperitoneum was drained, and a ruptured left isthmic ectopic pregnancy was identified and managed with total salpingectomy. The intrauterine pregnancy remained viable postoperatively. Progesterone supplementation (Depot Primolut injections and progesterone pessaries 400 mg twice daily) was commenced as institutional practice and continued until 16 weeks of gestation. Serial beta-hCG monitoring confirmed resolution of the ectopic component, with levels declining from 45,000 mIU/mL postoperatively to 12,500 mIU/mL by postoperative day 10. The intrauterine pregnancy progressed to 38 weeks of gestation, and the patient delivered a live female baby weighing 2.5 kg.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for heterotopic pregnancy in patients with acute abdominal symptoms, even when an intrauterine pregnancy has been confirmed. Rapid resuscitation, emergency surgical intervention with minimal uterine manipulation, and appropriate postoperative support are critical for maternal and intrauterine pregnancy survival, as demonstrated by the successful delivery at 38 weeks in this case.

articles.title: Severe Orofacial Cryogenic Injury Requiring Tracheostomy Due to Recreational Nitrous Oxide Inhalation.
articles.journal_full: Journal of medical toxicology : official journal of the American College of Medical Toxicology

abstract.text: Recreational use of nitrous oxide (N2O) has become more popular recently due to its euphoric effect as well as viral social media trends. Nitrous oxide use can cause severe frostbite injuries at any site of direct contact with the gas or canister, including the face, oral cavity, and oropharynx. We present a case of severe orofacial cryogenic injury from commercially available nitrous oxide marketed as Galaxy Gas resulting in prolonged tracheostomy dependence.

articles.title: Investigating the Physiology of Cannabis Intoxication and Impairment Using Wearable Sensors.
articles.journal_full: Journal of medical toxicology : official journal of the American College of Medical Toxicology

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Cannabis decriminalization/legalization has increased the availability and recreational use of cannabis products. Unlike ethanol, there are no standard validated assessments to identify cannabis-induced intoxication and impairment. The objective of this study was to show that wearable sensors can objectively identify cannabis intoxication.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This observational study evaluated participants who smoked their personal cannabis products. Heart rate (HR), skin temperature, electrodermal activity, and accelerometry data were continuously collected using a wrist-worn sensor (Empatica EmbracePlus). Participants were assessed using the DRUID© impairment application, the Subjective High Assessment Scale (SHAS) surveys, and 2-minute periods each of sit/stand/walk exercises. Participants performed the study protocol at home while monitored remotely by study staff. The biometric data, DRUID© scores, and subjective intoxication scores were analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired t-tests, Welch tests, and repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). This data was used to train multiple machine learning (ML) models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Statistical analysis was performed on 17/20 enrolled participants who provided complete data sets. In this cohort, cannabis intoxication caused significant changes in HR and aggregate accelerometry. Non-significant decreases in limb electrodermal activity and increases in limb temperature were recorded. Significant changes in subjective intoxication (SHAS) and objective impairment (DRUID©) were observed. The best performing proof-of-concept ML models were better at detecting subjective intoxication (balanced accuracy of 0.864) than impairment (balanced accuracy of 0.763).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Wearable sensors can detect physiologic changes in participants intoxicated with cannabis. This biometric data can be used to create ML models to detect cannabis-induced impairment and subjective intoxication.

articles.title: The initial clinical presentation and evolution of reported cases of recreational nitrous oxide intoxication in children: a 6-year French multicentric, descriptive and retrospective paediatric study.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: The purpose of this study is to describe the initial clinical signs of abusive recreational N2O intoxication in children, numbers of reported cases, treatments used and post-abuse exposition. This is a retrospective, descriptive, multicentric, epidemiological study based on national French toxicovigilance registers from poison control centres, from 2019 to 2024, among < 18 years. A total of 212 patients were included (60% (n = 128) female, median age 16 [15; 17] years). The number of cases reported each year increased from 8 to 50 cases. At diagnosis, 80.7% (n = 171) had neuropsychiatric disorders: 40.6% (n = 86) had sensory disturbance, 17.5% (n = 37) had motor deficit and 12.3% (n = 26) had gait disorders. Thirteen percent (n = 27) of children developed an acute myelopathy and/or neuropathy. Gastrointestinal symptoms affected 15.6% (n = 33) of patients, primarily nausea and vomiting. No thromboembolic complication was reported. Chronic exposure was observed in 46% (n = 99) of patients, while 34% (n = 72) had used another substance. Severe substance use disorder, including massive use, was reported in 39% (n = 83) of cases. Among the 63% (n = 134) of tests performed, 25% (n = 33/134) showed abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging and electromyography were abnormal in 17 patients (8%). Vitamin B12 supplementation was inconsistent. The outcome was unknown for 28.3% (n = 60), but at least 7.5% (n = 16) experienced aftereffects or worsening.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: N2O intoxication is increasing among French children, with a predominant female ratio. Symptoms, mainly neuropsychiatric or gastrointestinal, may include neurological sequelae, even for children. Complete cessation of use and support for substance use disorders are the only widely accepted treatments. Therapeutic evidence-based recommendations are lacking.

abstract.label: WHAT IS KNOWN
abstract.text: • The non-medical recreational use of nitrous oxide (N2O) has increased significantly since 2018, half of the cases being children and young adults (under 22 years old).

abstract.label: WHAT IS NEW
abstract.text: • Since 2022, females have been the most affected among children, presenting with non-specific neurological symptoms or sequelae and experiencing far fewer thrombotic events than adults do. • The emergence of neonatal symptomatic intoxication cases highlights a new facet of this public health issue.

articles.title: Influencing factors of the long-term predictive accuracy of the ocular trauma score.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To evaluate the performance of the Ocular Trauma Score (OTS) in predicting long-term visual outcomes after mechanical ocular trauma and to identify the key factors influencing its accuracy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study enrolled 106 patients with mechanical ocular trauma, with a median follow-up of 14 months. Retrieved variables included demographic characteristics and clinical data after the injury. The distribution of final best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was compared between the actual outcomes and the OTS-predicted outcomes. A weighted average predicted BCVA was calculated based on the BCVA probability distribution for each OTS category to classify patients into Better (actual BCVA better than OTS predicted) and Non-Better groups. Factors associated with OTS prediction discrepancies were identified using univariate analyses. Multivariable Firth logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation was performed to identify factors independently associated with better-than-predicted outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The OTS demonstrated a clear severity-dependent predictive pattern. Predictive accuracy was highest for mild injuries (OTS category 5) but showed a systematic pessimistic bias in severe injuries (OTS category 1), overestimating poor outcomes (NLP) and underestimating recovery potential (BCVA grades 3-5). For intermediate injuries (OTS categories 2-3), the likelihood of achieving moderate vision (20/200-20/50) was underestimated. Multiple surgeries were associated with better-than-predicted outcomes in the univariate analysis (p = 0.021). In the multivariable analysis, endophthalmitis (odds ratio [OR] = 2.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08-8.29, p = 0.034) and penetrating injury (OR = 3.71, 95% CI: 1.17-12.94, p = 0.026) were independently associated with better-than-predicted outcomes, whereas initial BCVA grade 2, despite a significant univariate association, did not retain statistical significance after adjustment (OR = 2.01, 95% CI: 0.79-5.10, p = 0.144).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The OTS remains a useful prognostic tool but demonstrates limited accuracy in severe mechanical ocular trauma. Endophthalmitis and penetrating injury were identified as independent modifiers, while initial BCVA grade 2 and multiple surgeries were associated with better-than-predicted outcomes in the univariate analysis. Contextualising its predictions with contemporary surgical factors and clinical modifiers may improve the individualised application of the OTS.

articles.title: Physical activity as an adjuvant strategy to pharmacological treatment of glaucoma (PhD Academy Award).
From prediction to prevention: a translational pathway for preventing frailty and falls in older adults (PhD Academy Award).
Study protocol of the SuDHO study: hyperbaric oxygen treatment added to standard care for acute idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss - a multicentre randomised controlled trial.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL) can lead to permanent sequelae with functional impairment of hearing. Hyperbaric oxygen treatment (HBOT) may improve outcomes but conclusive evidence for its efficacy is currently lacking.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: This is a multicentre, 1:1 randomised, controlled, assessor-blind trial comparing standard care alone versus HBOT plus standard care. Adult patients with ISSNHL, at least 50 dB hearing level (HL) in pure tone average (PTA4) on the affected ear and who were eligible for commencement of HBOT within 7 days from onset of hearing loss are included. Those with other causes of hearing loss and contraindications for HBOT are excluded. The primary outcome is absolute PTA4 after 14 weeks, while secondary outcomes include other measures of audiometric hearing improvement including word recognition score and patient-reported outcomes related to hearing, tinnitus, balance and quality of life. The power analyses indicated a group size of 151 participants to detect a difference in mean PTA4 of at least 10 dB HL at follow-up with 90% power based on an assumed SD of 34 dB HL with a 0.05 significance level.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: The trial has been approved by the Regional committees for medical and health research ethics (268140), by the Norwegian Medical Products Agency and is registered in the EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS, 2024-510798-84-00). User representatives have been involved in the development of the study. The results will be reported according to the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) 2025 guidelines in an international peer-reviewed medical journal as soon as possible after the last visit of the last patient.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER
abstract.text: 2021-002284-22 (primary registration 4 May 2021; initially registered in EU Clinical Trials Register (EudraCT)). From 2024 replaced by EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS): 2024-510798-84-00 (primary registration 2 October 2024).

articles.title: Low cross-sectional area of the geniohyoid muscle is associated with non-home discharge in older patients admitted to the emergency department.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Functional decline and non-home discharge are common among older patients hospitalized in acute care settings and are associated with poor prognosis. Swallowing dysfunction is a key factor affecting functional recovery; however, the association between swallowing-related muscle mass and discharge outcomes remains unclear. This study investigated the association between the cross-sectional area (CSA) of the geniohyoid muscle (GH) at admission and discharge destination in older patients admitted to an acute care hospital.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center prospective observational study included patients aged ≥65 years who were admitted from home to the emergency department, hospitalized for ≥5 days, and received rehabilitation. GH-CSA was measured within 5 days of admission using ultrasonography. Participants were classified into low and high GH-CSA groups using sex-specific cutoff values (≤194.7 mm2 for men and ≤172.5 mm2 for women). The primary outcome was discharge destination (home vs non-home). Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to examine the independent association between low GH-CSA and non-home discharge, adjusting for clinically relevant covariates. Model A was adjusted for age, sex, MUST score ≥2, CCI, circulatory disorders, pre-admission FOIS, pre-admission BI, and living alone, whereas Model B excluded MUST score ≥2.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 242 patients were included in the analysis. Patients with low GH-CSA had a significantly higher proportion of non-home discharge compared with those with high GH-CSA (53.9% vs 30.7%, p < 0.001). GH-CSA was significantly lower in patients discharged to non-home destinations than in those discharged home (median, 152.2 vs. 177.1 mm2; p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, low GH-CSA was independently associated with non-home discharge in both Model A (odds ratio [OR] 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-4.24; p = 0.017) and Model B (OR 2.63, 95% CI 1.40-4.95; p = 0.003).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Low GH-CSA at admission was independently associated with non-home discharge among older patients hospitalized in an acute care setting. Ultrasound assessment of GH-CSA may serve as a simple and objective marker for early identification of patients at high risk of adverse discharge outcomes.

articles.title: Geographic Access to Urgent Care and Pediatric Site-of-Care Patterns: A Hypothesis-Generating Analysis in One Health System.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe pediatric site-of-care utilization across three communities differing in in-network urgent care (UC) availability within one health system, generating hypotheses about geographic access to Medicaid-accepting UC and pediatric emergency department (ED) use.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis of pediatric encounters (2023-2025) at two EDs and two UCs in coastal Connecticut. Patients younger than 21 years residing in Bridgeport (in-network ED only), Fairfield (in-network UC only), or Milford (both), presenting during UC operating hours with Medicaid or commercial insurance and a principal diagnosis common to both settings, were included. Multivariable logistic regression with a Medicaid × Region interaction, adjusted for diagnosis and age band, with ZIP-level cluster-robust standard errors, estimated odds ratios for UC use.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 12,578 encounters, the adjusted odds of urgent care (vs emergency department) use among Medicaid- versus commercially insured children differed across regions (Medicaid × Region interaction, P <.001): 0.45 (95% CI, 0.37-0.53) in Bridgeport, 1.85 (1.56-2.20) in Fairfield, and 0.55 (0.49-0.63) in Milford. The pattern persisted after adjustment but cannot separate in-network access from out-of-network substitution or unmeasured community-level differences.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The Medicaid-commercial difference in urgent care use varied across communities, suggesting local access to Medicaid-accepting urgent care may shape pediatric site-of-care decisions. Single-system scope and missing patient-level social determinants and out-of-network data preclude causal inference; multi-system replication using continuous distance measures is warranted. If confirmed, expanding Medicaid-accepting urgent care may be a practical lever to reduce avoidable pediatric ED use.

articles.title: Clinical practice guideline: sudden hearing loss ‒ The Brazilian taskforce (ABORL/SBO) 2026.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To develop evidence-based Brazilian clinical practice recommendations for the evaluation and management of sudden hearing loss, with emphasis on idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multidisciplinary Brazilian taskforce composed of otolaryngologists, otologists, and neurotologists was convened by the Brazilian Association of Otorhinolaryngology and Cervico-Facial Surgery and the Brazilian Society of Otology. Each clinical statement was supported by a focused systematic literature review addressing a predefined clinical question. Reviews were conducted according to PRISMA methodology and structured using the PICOS framework. Evidence was synthesized by the panel, and recommendations were formulated considering aggregate evidence quality, benefits and harms, patient preferences, costs, availability of diagnostic and therapeutic resources, and applicability to the Brazilian healthcare context.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifteen clinical statements were developed. The guideline recommends early differentiation between conductive and sensorineural hearing loss, recognition of atypical presentations, prompt audiometric confirmation, selective use of computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging for retrocochlear evaluation, and avoidance of routine laboratory and genetic testing in typical adult-onset idiopathic cases. Systemic corticosteroids, intratympanic corticosteroids, or a combination of both are recommended as initial treatment, while hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be considered in selected patients. Intratympanic corticosteroids are also recommended as salvage therapy. Routine use of antivirals, thrombolytics, vasodilators, vasoactive substances, immunosuppressive agents, immunobiological therapies, neurotrophic factors, stem cell therapies, and other biological agents is not recommended outside specific indications or research settings. Auditory rehabilitation counseling and structured audiometric follow-up are recommended.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This Brazilian guideline provides practical, evidence-based recommendations to standardize the diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and follow-up of patients with sudden hearing loss, aiming to improve timely care and reduce unnecessary interventions.

articles.title: Early post-resuscitation profiles after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A latent class analysis.
articles.journal_full: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early cardiopulmonary heterogeneity after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) may be associated with prognosis and treatment response.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To identify early post-resuscitation profiles and explore their associations with outcomes and randomized treatment effects.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this post hoc analysis of the BOX pulmonary artery catheter substudy, latent class analysis (LCA) was applied to early clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic variables. The primary outcome was 365-day all-cause mortality. Exploratory cross-cohort replication used a separately fitted LCA in the Targeted Temperature Management (TTM) cohort, with 180-day mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 700 BOX patients, a two-class model was selected. Class 2 (n = 352) showed longer time to return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), higher lactate, greater cardiopulmonary dysfunction, higher filling pressures, and greater noradrenaline requirements. Mortality was 48% in Class 2 versus 21% in Class 1. No treatment interaction was detected for mean arterial pressure (MAP; P = 0.606), oxygenation (P = 0.483), or fever-control duration (P = 0.946). Mortality discrimination was not superior to time to ROSC alone. In 152 TTM patients, mortality was 38% versus 24% (P = 0.057), with less pronounced hemodynamic separation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Two early post-resuscitation profiles were identified after OHCA, with more pronounced separation in filling pressures than cardiac output in BOX. The profiles were associated with prognosis but did not identify differential responses to the randomized interventions.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: BOX trial, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT03141099; TTM trial, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01020916.

articles.title: The 'cost of complexity' of boarding mechanically ventilated patients in emergency department crowding: A retrospective NEDOCS analysis with deterministic scenario modelling in a Chilean university hospital.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) crowding and the boarding of critically ill patients compromise patient safety and emergency nursing care. We described crowding in the adult ED of a high-complexity university hospital using the National Emergency Department Overcrowding Scale (NEDOCS) and quantified the "cost of complexity": the additional crowding attributable to boarding mechanically ventilated patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective observational study of 21,620 adult ED episodes (2023). NEDOCS was reconstructed from electronic timestamps (12 treatment spaces; 305 hospital beds) and classified using the original levels. Because ventilated patients were not recorded, the ventilator term was fixed at zero (reference, V = 0), one (V = 1) or two (V = 2) patients, keeping all other components at observed values.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Admission was required in 23.5% of episodes; mean door-to-doctor time was 48.4 min (median 7.7), and occupancy exceeded the 12 treatment spaces during 40.1% of hours. The mean annual NEDOCS was 104.5 points ("overcrowded") in the reference scenario. Each ventilated boarder adds a constant 13.4 points: with V = 2, the annual mean rose to 131.3, days with a mean above 180 increased from 40 to 74, and months above 140 from none to four. On weekdays, NEDOCS was below 100 only from 03:00 to 10:00; an evening plateau (15:00-22:00; 164-177 points) exceeded 180 points from 14:00 to 23:00 under V = 2.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ventilated boarders add a fixed increment to NEDOCS that, in an already overcrowded ED, pushes peak days and hours into the dangerously overcrowded range. Earlier inpatient discharges, timely critical care bed allocation and NEDOCS-triggered full-capacity protocols warrant prospective evaluation to protect patient safety and nursing capacity.

articles.title: Disposition Patterns in Children With Low-Acuity Blunt Solid Organ Injury: An NTDB Analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Pediatric blunt solid organ injury (SOI) involving liver, spleen, or kidney is common. Contemporary guidelines emphasize physiologic status and clinical course rather than injury grade for management and disposition decisions. We evaluated factors associated with emergency department (ED) discharge versus short uncomplicated admission among children with low-severity blunt SOI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2017-2023 National Trauma Data Bank. Patients aged ≤18 y with blunt liver, spleen, and/or kidney injury, SOI Abbreviated Injury Scale severity ≤3, Injury Severity Score ≤15, and no severe nonabdominal injury were included. Short uncomplicated admission was retrospectively defined as hospital stay ≤2 d, discharge home, no intensive care unit admission, transfusion, angiographic intervention, operation, or in-hospital complication. Staged logistic regression was supplemented by overlap-weighted and Firth penalized analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 5749 patients, 352 (6.1%) were discharged from the ED and 5397 (93.9%) underwent short uncomplicated admission. SOI Abbreviated Injury Scale severity 3 (aOR 2.33, 95% CI 1.58-3.43) and multi-organ injury (aOR 2.67, 95% CI 1.40-5.93) were associated with higher odds of admission. Injury Severity Score category and physiologic variables were not significant. White race and pediatric trauma center care were associated with higher odds of admission, whereas older age, private insurance, and private vehicle transport were associated with lower odds. Confirmatory analyses produced similar estimates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among captured National Trauma Data Bank cases meeting the analytic criteria, ED discharge was uncommon. Disposition was associated with anatomic, demographic, and system-level characteristics. Prospective studies are needed to define and validate safe, consistently applied ED discharge criteria among selective low-severity SOI patients.

articles.title: Variation in Procedural Volume and Specialty Distribution at Trauma Centers.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The distribution of procedural workload across specialties and hospital locations at trauma centers has been poorly defined. The purpose of this study was to quantify procedural volume by specialty and hospital location at level I and II trauma centers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was performed using data from a statewide trauma registry (2019-2025). Adult patients (≥18 y) with an Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥5 who were admitted to a level I or II trauma centers were included. Procedures and procedure clusters (i.e., multiple performed in one setting) were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS) codes and categorized by provider specialty and hospital location, including the operating room (OR), emergency department, intensive care unit, and other settings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 401,063 individual procedures and 238,436 procedure clusters identified in 117,518 patients. Orthopedic surgery performed the largest share of procedures (146,932, 36.6%) and procedure clusters (84,917, 35.6%) and did four to six times the number of OR-based procedures than either general trauma surgery or neurosurgery/spine surgery respectively. General trauma surgery performed the most intensive care unit procedures and nonsurgical providers did the most in the emergency department. Level I centers performed more operations per hospital than level II centers, but collectively level II centers accounted for a greater aggregate operative burden.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Orthopedic surgery accounted for the largest share of procedures in trauma centers, whereas other specialties performed most of the procedures outside of the OR. Understanding these patterns may help trauma centers allocate resources to better match the location of actual procedural demand.

articles.title: Leadership Lessons From Implementing a Mental Health Emergency Services Unit in a Canadian Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Emergency departments are access points for people experiencing mental health and substance use crises, yet conventional emergency environments and workflows are often poorly aligned with psychiatric crisis care. Dedicated psychiatric emergency and crisis models are increasingly being implemented, including across Canadian hospitals. Drawing on the implementation of the Mental Health Emergency Services Unit at North York General Hospital and relevant literature, this article identifies five leadership lessons: treat environment as clinical infrastructure; bring mental health expertise to the front of the emergency pathway through concurrent care; build mental health capability beyond the specialized unit; integrate community partnerships into the clinical model; and embed evaluation throughout implementation. These lessons emphasize that redesign extends beyond physical capacity to include workforce, workflow, community relationships, and learning systems. Dedicated mental health emergency services should be approached as part of emergency mental health redesign, with implementation shaped by specific local context.

articles.title: Spatial accessibility and equity of emergency medical services: Evidence from Ningbo.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Timely access to emergency medical services (EMS) is essential for improving survival outcomes and public health. In rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities, disparities in EMS accessibility are increasingly shaped by the spatial distribution of hospitals, population concentration, transport infrastructure, and built environment conditions. However, relatively few studies have simultaneously compared emergency and non-emergency medical accessibility and examined their spatial equity and influencing factors in medium-sized coastal cities. This study evaluates the spatial accessibility, equity, and clustering characteristics of EMS in Ningbo, China, and identifies the key built environment factors influencing these patterns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The shortest travel time model, based on API data, was employed to measure EMS accessibility for both emergency (ambulance) and non-emergency (public transport) scenarios across five core urban districts of Ningbo. The Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient were applied to assess healthcare equity. We used global Moran's I and local indicators of spatial association (LISA) to explore spatial clustering and a multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model to analyze spatial heterogeneity in influencing factors across built environment dimensions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Both emergency and non-emergency medical services exhibited significant spatial disparities, decreasing gradually from the city center toward the periphery. The Gini coefficients for emergency and non-emergency models were 0.5156 and 0.4898, respectively, indicating substantial inequity. Strong spatial clustering was observed (global Moran's I = 0.846, p < 0.01), with high-value clusters concentrated in central districts and low-value clusters in mountainous outskirts. MGWR results revealed that accessibility was positively affected by the number of bus stops, road density, bus route density, and distance to the Central Business District (CBD), but negatively impacted by building density and development intensity. The MGWR model's explanatory power (R2 = 0.584) demonstrated significant spatial heterogeneity in these relationships. Building density and bus route density exerted the strongest local effects among the eleven built environment indicators.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: EMS accessibility in Ningbo exhibits evident spatial inequality and clustering characteristics. Peripheral and mountainous areas remain disadvantaged, especially under non-emergency public transport conditions. Improving road connectivity, expanding public transit coverage, optimizing hospital and EMS resource allocation, and strengthening services in underserved areas can help reduce healthcare accessibility inequities. These findings provide an empirical foundation for optimizing EMS resource allocation for urban policymakers as well as offer practical insights for other rapidly urbanizing cities facing similar challenges.

articles.title: Personality Traits and Professional Quality of Life in Volunteer Ski Patrollers.

abstract.text: IntroductionSki patrollers, as outdoor emergency first responders, face unique occupational trauma exposure that impacts their professional quality of life. Despite these exposures, this population has been largely understudied in trauma research. Personality traits have been associated with outcomes from occupational trauma exposure in other populations. This study investigates associations between personality traits and outcomes including compassion fatigue and satisfaction in volunteer ski patrollers.MethodsVolunteers from a ski patrol in the Pacific Northwest (n = 82) completed a cross-sectional online survey measuring trauma exposure, the 5-factor model personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion, agreeableness, openness, and conscientiousness), and professional quality of life variables of compassion fatigue (comprising burnout and secondary traumatic stress [STS]) and compassion satisfaction.ResultsThose who reported trauma exposure while patrolling endorsed higher compassion satisfaction and lower burnout. Extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness correlated negatively with burnout and positively with compassion satisfaction. Extraversion and conscientiousness negatively correlated with STS, while neuroticism positively correlated with burnout and STS but negatively correlated with compassion satisfaction.ConclusionsOur findings highlight the association between personality traits and professional quality of life outcomes. Organizations could use this data to design tailored interventions to support ski patrollers in managing occupational trauma exposure. Individuals high in neuroticism endorsed more negative outcomes and could potentially benefit most from preventative measures and intervention compared to those high in extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness.

articles.title: [A rare cause of ketoacidosis: Rapunzel syndrome].

abstract.text: A 16-year-old female patient presented to the emergency department with impaired consciousness and recurrent vomiting. Laboratory investigations revealed ketoacidosis with electrolyte imbalance in the setting of known type I diabetes mellitus managed with insulin pump therapy. Clinical examination revealed a firm palpable mass in the upper abdomen. Ultrasound demonstrated impaired gastrointestinal transit in the upper abdomen associated with a mass of unclear origin in the gastric region. Computed tomography (CT) raised suspicion of a bezoar. Subsequent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a massive trichobezoar in the stomach extending into the duodenal bulb. Despite several attempts at endoscopic removal, including the use of various snares and grasping forceps, the trichobezoar could not be retrieved. Surgical removal by laparotomy and gastrotomy was therefore necessary. Rapunzel syndrome is a rare presentation of a trichobezoar. Most patients present with abdominal pain, nausea, and signs of ileus. The tail of the bezoar may extend into the jejunum, ileum, or even the colon. The case of a patient who was admitted with what initially appeared to be a complication of her pre-existing medical conditions is reported. However, the actual cause of her clinical deterioration was a trichobezoar extending into the duodenal bulb, which could only be treated surgically.

articles.title: Unplanned return to hospital from hospital-at-home care: incidence, timing, and determinants.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Unplanned transfer from Hospital-at-Home (HaH) to conventional inpatient care-termed clinical escalation-is widely used as a safety indicator, yet its incidence, timing, and physiological patterns across heterogeneous HaH populations remain poorly characterised.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of consecutive HaH episodes from January 2021 to December 2025 was performed at a tertiary academic centre. Clinical escalation was defined as unplanned transfer from HaH requiring ≥ 24 h of inpatient care due to clinical deterioration or acute intercurrent illness, and was manually adjudicated (κ = 0.90). Physiological triggers were classified into predefined domains. Severe escalation was defined as ICU admission or in-hospital death. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with escalation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Amongst 10,167 episodes (mean age 70.9 years; 44.0% women), clinical escalation occurred in 508 (5.0%; 95% CI 4.6-5.4). Median time to escalation was 6 days (IQR 3-12); only 24.6% of events occurred within 72 h. Respiratory (30.5%) and infectious (18.1%) deterioration were the most frequent triggers. Severe escalation occurred in 169 episodes (33.3%). Higher age-adjusted Charlson index (OR per point 1.11; 95% CI 1.06-1.15) and early-discharge admission from hospital wards (OR 1.69; 95% CI 1.25-2.28 vs. direct home admission) were independently associated with escalation. Model discrimination was modest (AUC 0.68).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Clinical escalation in HaH affected approximately 1 in 20 episodes and followed identifiable temporal and physiological patterns. Risk was shaped by comorbidity burden and care trajectory rather than static admission characteristics. These findings support interpreting escalation as an expected and clinically interpretable component of acute home-based care rather than solely as a marker of programme failure.

articles.title: Cellphone-Associated Ocular Injuries Presenting to U.S. Emergency Departments.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To characterize national trends, mechanisms, and demographic patterns of cellphone-associated ocular injuries over 20 years using a nationally representative database.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cross-sectional study using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) database, encompassing emergency department (ED) visits from approximately 100 nationally representative U.S. hospitals. Cellphone-associated eye injuries, which encompass cases of globe injury where cellphones or their accessories were involved, were identified and analyzed for patient demographics, clinical information, context of injury, and weighted national estimates. Temporal trends in ED visit rates were analyzed using joinpoint regression, and annual percent changes (APCs) quantified changes in ED visit rates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Between 2004 and 2023, an estimated 16,107 ED visits from cellphone-associated eye injuries (95% CI, 13,280-18,933) were recorded in NEISS. By joinpoint analysis, ED visit rates increased significantly from 2008-2015 (APC, 22.4%; 95% CI, 9.7%-36.5%), and no statistically significant trend was observed from 2004-2008 (APC, 1.0%; 95% CI,15.9%-21.2%) or from 2015-2023 (APC, -3.9%; 95% CI, 12.1%-5.1%). Open globe injuries occurred in seven reported cases, representing 252 weighted-estimated ED visits (95% CI, 33-471) or 1.6% of all estimated ED visits. Direct mechanical (DM) injuries accounted for 83.2% (weighted n = 13,401, 95% CI, 11,002-15,800) of ED visits, predominantly from the phone body (46.2%) and screen glass (32.6%). Use-associated (UA) injuries comprised 16.8% weighted (n = 2,705, 95% CI, 1,641-3,770), with distraction-mediated activities (62.7%) being most common.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Cellphone-associated ocular ED visits increased substantially from 2008 to 2015, while no statistically significant change was detected between 2015 and 2023. Direct mechanical trauma, broken screen glass, and distraction represent commonly identified mechanisms. Eye care professionals should counsel patients on responsible handling of phones and accessories, limiting phone use while walking or driving, replacement of broken screens, and the importance of prompt assessment after penetrating or significant ocular trauma.

articles.title: Comparing Rural Versus Urban Pediatric Hospice Recipients, 2011 to 2022.
articles.journal_full: Journal of hospice and palliative nursing : JHPN : the official journal of the Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association

abstract.text: Pediatric hospice care is essential in supporting children with life-limiting conditions and their families during the last year of life, yet little is known about how geographic location influences the characteristics of children receiving care. This study examined differences between rural and urban pediatric hospice recipients using a pooled cross-sectional Medicaid dataset from 2011 to 2022. Guided by the socioecological framework, data from 17,134 deceased Medicaid-enrolled children aged 20 years and younger who received hospice services in the Midwest and Southern United States were analyzed. Rural children demonstrated greater clinical complexity, including higher rates of physical and mental health multimorbidity, technology dependence, and polypharmacy. Despite lower rates of inpatient admissions and emergency department visits, rural children received care from larger medical teams, more subspecialists, and incurred higher outpatient and primary care costs. They also lived in communities characterized by greater economic disadvantage, lower internet connectivity, longer distances to health care resources, and higher rates of residence in Appalachian and medically underserved areas. These findings suggest that rural pediatric hospice recipients experience a convergence of heightened medical complexity and structural barriers to care.

articles.title: Testing a Minimal Three-Zone Surgical Setup Under Infrastructure-Degraded Conditions.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Infrastructure degradation during conflicts and disasters may necessitate temporary surgical capability in improvised environments lacking conventional operating-room infrastructure. We operationally evaluated a minimal 3-zone surgical setup consisting of a contaminated dirty zone (12 m2), a semiclean transition zone (15 m2), and a protected procedural core (14 m2). Workflow simulations demonstrated reproducible separation of patient, personnel, material, and waste flows within a total operational footprint of 41 m2. Spatial demand was primarily determined by contamination control, workflow separation, and procedural movement geometry.

articles.title: Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ): Preliminary Validation of the Hebrew Version Among Adolescents.
articles.journal_full: Archives of suicide research : official journal of the International Academy for Suicide Research

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among adolescents. Given that most youth interact with healthcare system providers in the month preceding a suicide attempt, rapid and effective suicide screening tools are critically needed. The Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ) is a brief, evidence-based instrument specifically designed for the quick identification of adolescents at elevated suicide risk in time-critical and high-stress settings, such as Emergency Departments. This study aimed to conduct a preliminary validation of the Hebrew translation of the ASQ questionnaire, enabling its use as a rapid and evidence-based suicide-screening tool among Hebrew-speaking adolescents.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A total of 20 adolescents aged 10 to 18 participated in this study. A randomized, cross-over design was employed to assess the concordance between the original English version of the ASQ and its Hebrew translation. The two versions were administered in counterbalanced order, with an approximately two-day interval between administrations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Translation reliability between the English and Hebrew ASQ versions was extremely high, with 99% identical responses across all items. Four items showed perfect agreement, and the remaining item demonstrated near-perfect concordance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings support the strong reliability of the Hebrew translation.

articles.title: CPD focus: supporting colleagues through distressing workplace experiences.
articles.journal_full: Emergency nurse : the journal of the RCN Accident and Emergency Nursing Association

abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) are high-pressure environments in which nurses are routinely exposed to emotionally challenging clinical situations and, at times, physical aggression from patients or the public. In addition, emergency nurses are increasingly required to deliver patient care in suboptimal environments, such as corridors and ambulances, exposing them to moral injury. All of these issues can have a significant impact on nurses' psychological well-being and professional confidence. While organisational systems and leadership structures are essential in addressing such issues, peer support has an important role in how individuals process and recover from distressing work-related situations or incidents. In this article, the author suggests some practical ways in which nurses can recognise and support colleagues experiencing work-related distress. The author provides some case-based discussions to illustrate the issues discussed, alongside guidance on compassionate communication, professional boundaries and appropriate escalation.

articles.title: Decision-Making Under Uncertainty in Paramedic Students: A START Triage Perspective.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study examined whether intolerance of uncertainty and decision-making styles were associated with theoretical START triage knowledge among paramedic students. Secondary exploratory analyses assessed psychosocial differences according to self-rated decision-making under stress, perceived coping with uncertainty, professional motivation, and challenges in prehospital emergency care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this cross-sectional study, 121 students from a First and Emergency Aid Program completed a self-administered paper-based questionnaire including a sociodemographic form, the Decision-Making Styles Scale, the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12, and the START Triage Knowledge Test. Data were collected in classroom settings under researcher supervision between May and June 2025 and analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and correlation analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean theoretical START triage knowledge score was 69.99 ± 14.76. START knowledge was not significantly associated with intolerance of uncertainty or decision-making style subscale scores. Exploratory analyses identified associations between psychosocial scores and self-rated decision-making under stress, coping with uncertainty, professional motivation, and perceived challenges.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Theoretical START triage knowledge was not associated with intolerance of uncertainty or decision-making styles. Secondary findings were limited to self-reported psychosocial associations. The study assessed declarative knowledge and did not evaluate START application in simulated or field settings. Future studies should use simulation-based, scenario-based, or observational outcomes.

articles.title: Initial Emergency Department Concentrations of Serum Bicarbonate and Lactate Are Associated With Survival to Hospital Discharge in Children Following Submersion Injuries.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: There is a lack of objective measures to determine outcome and disposition following pediatric submersion injury. This study described a cohort of pediatric patients who presented to the emergency department (ED) after a submersion injury and the factors associated with survival to hospital discharge. In addition, the study examined the ability of 2 laboratory measures of acidemia, venous lactate and bicarbonate, to predict severity of injury and ED disposition following submersion.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional cohort study evaluated consecutive pediatric submersion cases from February 2018 to November 2019 seen at Arnold Palmer Hospital for Children's Emergency Department, a tertiary care pediatric level 1 trauma center. Data collected were based on Utstein recommendations for submersion injury and included demographics, event information, vital signs, laboratory data, and hospital disposition. The main outcomes included survival to hospital discharge and hospital admission.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 208 patients with submersion injuries included in the analysis; 197 survived to hospital discharge, and 11 did not (5%). There were 135 (65%) patients admitted to the hospital, and 52 (25%) admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The average age of patients was 47 months, 67% were males, and bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was performed on 66% of patients. Mean lactate levels were 4.8 mmol/L (95% CI: 4.3 to 5.4) in survivors and 12.9 (95% CI: 10.9 to 14.9) in nonsurvivors (P < 0.001), and mean venous bicarbonate levels were 19 mmol/L (95% CI: 19 to 20) and 11 (95% CI: 9 to 14), respectively (P < 0.001). Lactate levels were significantly and negatively correlated with venous bicarbonate [r = -0.69 (95% CI: -0.78 to -0.58)] and with pH on arterial blood gas [r = -0.81 (95% CI: -0.87 to -0.73)]. The area under the curve for lactate predicting mortality from submersion was 0.97 (95% CI: 0.95 to 1.00) and for predicting admission to the hospital was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67 to 0.88). The area under the curve for venous bicarbonate predicting mortality was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.87 to 1.00) and for predicting admission 0.69 (95% CI: 0.56 to 0.83).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Elevations in venous bicarbonate and lactate levels measured in the pediatric ED were significantly associated with severity of submersion injury as measured by survival to hospital discharge and hospital admission. Both correlated with arterial pH levels. Prospective studies should evaluate the utility of using these objective measures to determine hospital disposition in these children.

articles.title: Changing Patterns of Alcohol and Cannabis Acute Care Admissions by Age in the United States, 2016-2023.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Age-related differences in alcohol and cannabis use are well established, yet age-specific trends in substance-related acute morbidity remain incompletely understood. The authors examined age-specific trends in alcohol- and cannabis-related emergency department and inpatient admissions from 2016 to 2023.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective cohort study using Merative MarketScan Commercial and Multi-State Medicaid databases (January 2016-December 2023). The cohort included 1,355,161 individuals 16-64 years of age with at least one substance-related acute care encounter (ICD-10-CM codes F10-F19, excluding nicotine). Outcomes included the proportion of substance-related encounters involving alcohol or cannabis, stratified by six age groups (16-18, 19-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, and 55-64 years). Secondary analyses examined primary substance diagnoses, severe alcohol-related morbidity, and cannabis-related encounters involving psychosis or vomiting (hyperemesis). Weighted linear regression estimated age-specific annual changes in encounter proportions, and Poisson models assessed trends in total encounter volume and substance involvement per encounter.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 5,190,680 substance-related encounters, alcohol and cannabis exhibited divergent age patterns. Alcohol accounted for 19%-26% of adolescent admissions, increasing to 73%-76% among adults ages 55-64 years, whereas cannabis involvement was highest among adolescents (70%-78%) and lowest among older adults (10%-11%). Alcohol-related admissions increased significantly among adults ages 25-34 years (1.80 percentage points annually, 95% CI=1.59, 2.00) and 35-44 years (1.19 points, 95% CI=0.99, 1.38). Cannabis-related admissions increased most rapidly among individuals ages 19-24 years (1.81 points annually, 95% CI=1.57, 2.04) and 16-18 years (0.83 points, 95% CI=0.61, 1.06), with notable increases in presentations involving psychosis and vomiting. When restricted to primary diagnoses, cannabis-related trends were attenuated, with adolescents showing annual declines (-1.46 points, 95% CI=-1.98, -0.94).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Alcohol- and cannabis-related acute care presentations follow divergent age-specific trajectories, with cannabis increasingly predominant among adolescents and young adults and alcohol predominant among older adults.

articles.title: Unrecognized importance of hawking prey capture tactics in a tropical plunge-diving seabird.

abstract.text: Seabirds are critical ecosystem members providing connectivity between marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Seabird foraging is often facilitated by other marine predators (e.g. tuna) that aggregate prey at the surface. Some seabirds have been anecdotally reported to 'hawk' (catch mid-air/in-flight) flyingfish and flying squid forced into flight by subsurface predators. Hawking avoids water entry and subsequent take-off, both of which are known to be energy intensive, but its relative importance in foraging has not been quantified. We analysed footage from 25 animal-borne video cameras deployed on red-footed boobies (Sula sula) at Palmyra Atoll to estimate the frequency of hawking, plunge diving and 'other' prey capture attempts. Hawking made up 20.3% of all prey capture attempts and had a 39.3% success rate in 2022, but was not observed for the two tracked birds in 2024. An additional 17 individuals were opportunistically observed in the footage making hawking capture attempts, suggesting hawking is a common behaviour, accounting for a greater proportion of foraging effort than previously known. As hawking is only possible when subsurface predators elicit flight escape behaviours of prey, its high frequency suggests such predator facilitation interactions are stronger than currently understood.
