articles.title: A Journey Map of Health Behaviour Decision-Making Among Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who are Repeatedly Hospitalized: A Longitudinal Qualitative Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Health behaviour decision-making is central to type 2 diabetes mellitus management, but remains complex and context dependent after repeated hospitalisations. Research has focused on health behaviours and associated factors, overlooking patient-centred decision-making across care stages and limiting stage-specific decision support and continuity-of-care strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A longitudinal qualitative study was conducted in mainland China, with data collected from October 2025 to March 2026. 16 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus who had experienced repeated hospitalisations were included and participated in repeated semi-structured interviews across three stages: pre-admission (T1), hospitalisation (T2), and home management (T3). Interviews were conducted on the second day of hospitalisation, one day before discharge, and three months after discharge. The interviews explored decision-making behaviours, support needs, emotional experiences, and pain points. Longitudinal analysis involved within-participant comparison across the three care stages, followed by cross-case synthesis to identify recurrent and divergent patterns of change. The findings were then integrated into a time-based visual journey map of health behaviour decision-making.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Four stage-specific trajectories were synthesised from the longitudinal interview data within four dimensions initially identified through preliminary patient observations: (1) behavioural transition from preference-driven care-seeking decisions to structured treatment adherence and fragile self-management; (2) evolving support needs from seeking trusted decision anchors to seeking structured empowerment and transition preparation, and finally to seeking continuous and accessible out-of-hospital support; (3) emotional evolution from self-blame after initially neglecting the illness, to fragile stability, and ultimately to acceptance and coexistence with the disease under long-term burden; and (4) phase-specifc pain points, including decision-making impeded by multiple information dilemmas before admission, insufficient motivation for sustained self-management during hospitalisation, and support discontinuity with practical burdens during home management.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study extends the application of patient journey mapping to understanding health behaviour decision-making among patients with T2DM who experience repeated hospitalisations. By identifying critical disruptions in decision-making, unmet needs, and barriers to sustained management, the journey map offers actionable insights for designing stage-specific, patient-centred decision-support and continuity-of-care interventions, with particular relevance to nurse-led clinical practice.

articles.title: Association of tranexamic acid with early death or massive transfusion after severe pelvic ring fractures: A nationwide registry-based cohort study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Evidence for tranexamic acid during emergency treatment of severe pelvic ring fractures is limited. We examined its association with early death or massive transfusion.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We studied adults in the Japan Trauma Data Bank from 2019 to 2023 with blunt pelvic ring fractures of Abbreviated Injury Scale severity 3 or higher. Exposure was any in-hospital tranexamic acid. The primary outcome was death within 24 h after arrival or transfusion of at least 20 Japanese red blood cell units within 24 h after injury. We used multiple imputation, propensity-score overlap weighting, and hospital-clustered standard errors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 5288 patients, 1985 (37.5%) received tranexamic acid. The weighted primary-outcome risks were 13.0% with tranexamic acid and 18.1% without it (risk ratio 0.72, 95% confidence interval 0.60-0.87). The association was driven by 24-hour mortality (risk ratio 0.62, 95% confidence interval 0.48-0.80); massive transfusion alone (risk ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.73-1.21) and mean red blood cell use did not differ. Any red blood cell transfusion was more frequent with tranexamic acid (risk ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.30). The primary-outcome risk ratio was 0.76 (0.62-0.93) after excluding deaths within 2 h and 0.81 (0.65-1.00) when both components were assessed within 24 h after injury.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The mortality association was not accompanied by lower transfusion requirements and weakened when outcome time origins were aligned. Because treatment timing was unavailable, these findings do not establish an independent survival benefit and provide no corroborating transfusion evidence of a pelvic-specific hemostatic benefit.

articles.title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is used for life-threatening hemorrhage, but evidence has largely focused on acute outcomes. Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up. Forty-nine REBOA-treated patients were matched 1:1 to 49 non-REBOA patients by major Young-Burgess category, Injury Severity Score, and age. The primary outcome was functional status among hospital survivors, categorized as good/fair/poor. Deep surgical site infection (SSI) after definitive pelvic fixation was the key secondary outcome, and nonunion was exploratory. Main models used a propensity-score linear predictor based on age, Injury Severity Score, initial systolic blood pressure, and lactate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-five patients survived hospitalization (30 REBOA; 45 non-REBOA); median follow-up was 19 months. Good/fair/poor outcomes were 16.7%/46.7%/36.7% in REBOA survivors and 51.1%/37.8%/11.1% in non-REBOA survivors. REBOA exposure was associated with worse functional status after adjustment (common odds ratio [cOR], 3.14; 95% CI, 1.11-8.92; P = 0.032). Among 68 definitive-fixation survivors, deep SSI occurred in 44.0% versus 9.3% (adjusted OR, 7.01; 95% CI, 1.88-31.07; P = 0.003); all observed events occurred within 60 days. Nonunion occurred in 26.7% versus 6.7% (adjusted OR, 9.09; 95% CI, 2.00-53.71; P = 0.004). Sensitivity analyses for deep SSI were directionally consistent.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among hospital survivors, REBOA exposure was associated with poorer long-term functional recovery and a higher burden of deep SSI. Nonunion was more frequent but remained exploratory. These findings characterize a high-risk orthopaedic survivor phenotype but do not establish a direct causal effect of REBOA.

articles.title: Implementation and Evaluation of the Stroke Triage App Among Paramedics in Prehospital Emergency Care: Sequential Mixed Methods Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Digital decision-support tools, such as the Stroke Triage App (STA), may enhance prehospital triage and clinical decision-making for suspected patients with stroke. However, implementation of decision-support tools and their impact on clinical practice remains insufficiently studied.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to investigate paramedics' experiences with the implementation of the STA in prehospital practice by evaluating the implementation process, the implementation outcomes, and its impact on clinical workflows, while considering contextual factors that may have influenced these dimensions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: STA implementation was evaluated among paramedics in 2 emergency medical services regions in the Netherlands using a sequential mixed methods approach. Actual usage data were extracted from the STA dashboard. Usability, perceived impact, and contextual factors were explored using an online survey and semistructured interviews.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Monthly triages ranged from 52 to 153 (median 120, IQR 107-131). Paramedics' individual STA use ranged from 1 to 47 times (median 7, IQR 3-13). Out of 246 paramedics with an account, 76 (31%) completed the survey, and 9 (4%) participated in semistructured interviews. The STA was generally well accepted, supporting structured neurological assessment and communication. Swift technical support, frequent promotion, and use of local ambassadors facilitated STA use. Clinical urgency, poor workflow integration, and limited perceived added value hampered STA use. Users recommended improvements in mobile interface, login features, and additional explanation with triage advice.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study demonstrates that the STA achieved substantial reach and initial adoption within the prehospital setting. However, widespread acceptance did not consistently translate into routine integration in daily practice. Successful implementation depends as much on addressing organizational and human factors as on technical performance.

articles.title: Impact of sarcopenic obesity phenotype on long-term survival in geriatric trauma: A nationwide cohort study using weight-adjusted waist index.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: As the global population ages, identifying effective prognostic markers for elderly trauma patients has become crucial. While Body Mass Index (BMI) is commonly used, its utility is limited by the "obesity paradox," failing to differentiate between muscle and fat. This study aimed to evaluate the Weight-Adjusted Waist Index (WWI), a surrogate marker for sarcopenic obesity, as a predictor of 20-year mortality following heavy trauma in the elderly.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed a nationwide cohort of 18,366 elderly patients (age≧65) from the National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (NHIS-NSC) who experienced heavy trauma (hospitalization, surgery, or ICU admission) between 2002 and 2022. Patients were categorized into WWI tertiles. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for 20-year mortality, adjusting for demographics, lifestyle factors, comorbidities, and laboratory findings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the 20-year follow-up, the highest WWI tertile (T3) was associated with significantly higher mortality compared to the lowest tertile (T1). In the fully adjusted model, the HR for 20-year mortality in the T3 group was 1.72 (95% CI 1.55-1.91). Notably, the risk was more pronounced in obese patients (BMI≧25 kg/m2, HR 2.15) and those with low physical activity. Furthermore, high WWI was associated with a higher prevalence of hip and femur fractures (26.0% vs. 15.0%) and prolonged ICU stays.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: WWI is a superior and independent predictor of long-term mortality compared to BMI in elderly trauma patients. By effectively identifying the high-risk sarcopenic obesity phenotype, WWI provides a practical and powerful tool for risk stratification in geriatric trauma management.

articles.title: Modern targeted nerve agent incidents: toxicokinetic complexity, biomarker interpretation and forensic uncertainty.

abstract.text: Nerve agent poisoning is often linked with mass-casualty events. Typical examples are battlefield use or large terrorist attacks. However, documented incidents from the last decades show a broader and more complex picture. The perspective follows a line of documented cases. It starts with the 1978 ricin "umbrella" murder of Georgi Markov in London (non-nerve agent attack, but historically important). It then moves to the sarin attacks in Matsumoto (1994) and the Tokyo subway (1995), the VX assassinations by the Aum Shinrikyo cult (1994-1995), the 2013 sarin attack in Ghouta and the recent targeted poisonings of Kim Jong-nam (2017), Sergei and Yulia Skripal (2018), Dawn Sturgess and Charlie Rowley (2018) and Alexei Navalny (2020). We use these cases to show how route of exposure, dose, formulation and environmental persistence shape toxicokinetics, clinical presentation, biomarker formation and forensic interpretation. For each case we give the circumstances, the agent, the route, the clinical course, the treatment and the forensic confirmation in detail. We focus on acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibition, aging, protein adduct formation, dermal absorption and environmental persistence. We describe a recurring "toxicological paradox": greater control over exposure can reduce immediate lethality, but at the same time it increases diagnostic uncertainty and forensic complexity. The cases also show that mass and targeted use are not two separate historical stages. They coexist within the same period, sometimes even within one perpetrator organisation. This perspective has direct implications for emergency preparedness, biomarker development, antidotal treatment windows and international chemical incident response.

articles.title: Should Esophageal Temperature Probes Be Used within UK Search and Rescue Helicopter Services?

abstract.text: Due to the environment in which they operate, UK search and rescue helicopters (SARH) may encounter patients presenting with accidental hypothermia or hypothermic cardiac arrest. For these patients, accurate core temperature measurement allows thorough assessment of hypothermia severity and determines the recommended clinical interventions and conveyance decisions. Ongoing monitoring of core temperature also provides feedback to clinicians on the effectiveness of rewarming interventions. Currently, SARH paramedics use peripheral thermometers, which some evidence suggests may not be appropriate for assessing hypothermic patients in this environment. The implementation of esophageal temperature probes (ETPs) may allow clinicians to meet the needs of a wider range of patient presentations. This article aims to discuss the demand, practicality, and training required to implement ETPs into SARH paramedic practice and highlights an opportunity for further research.

articles.title: Compliance with French Military Health Service guidelines for prehospital transfusion of blood products during forward aeromedical evacuations in Sahel (2015 to 2023).

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The forward transfusion guideline of the French Health Service (FHS) provides guidance for prehospital blood product (BP) transfusion in casualties' evacuations from overseas operations (OO). In Sahel, aeromedical evacuation (AE) teams are provided with lyophilized plasma, packed red blood cells (PRBC), and cold-stored low-titer group O whole blood (CS-LTOWB). The main objective was to evaluate compliance with guidelines for prehospital transfusion of severely injured trauma casualties during forward AE in OO. Secondary objectives were to identify clinical and paraclinical criteria, beyond current guidelines, associated with transfusion, and to describe the factors influencing transfusion rates.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multicenter retrospective observational study was conducted on forward AE missions in the western Sahelian theater between January 2015 and July 2023. Two hundred and six patients evacuated for traumatic injuries, classified as category Alpha or Bravo, were included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sixty-four wounded received prehospital transfusion of eighty-nine BP units. Meeting transfusion criteria was associated with the requirement for transfusion (p = 10-7, relative risk (RR): 3.20 with 95% confidence interval (95% CI) [2.29-4.47]). Sixty-five percent of transfused patients did not meet the established transfusion criteria. Isolated heart rate above 110 bpm, modification of complexion, Shock Index above 1, altered mental status, penetrating trauma, pelvic trauma and effusion at Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) ultrasound were more frequent within transfused patients. Median transfusion rate was about 25 mL/min [16-50].

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A prospective evaluation of our findings is needed before proposing a revision to the current FHS guideline, including the addition of exclusion criteria.

articles.title: Clinical Criteria for Imaging in Children at Risk for Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract.text: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but serious condition in children. Clinical guidelines for imaging a suspected pediatric PE in Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) are lacking. The computerized tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) is the preferred diagnostic modality for suspected PE in an emergency department. Our study aims to introduce a simplified clinical assessment tool for ordering CTPA in children in the emergency room. This is a retrospective review of patients managed in our Emergency Department from 2000 to 2020. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes for PE, deep vein thrombosis, or similar diagnoses. The control group consisted of patients with PE symptoms, seen within the same time frame as the study group, who had negative CTPA. Twenty-five CTPA-positive patients were identified. Twenty-three of 25 CTPA-positive patients were aged 13 to 18 years. Common risk factors include protein-losing state (ie, nephrotic syndrome), oral contraceptive pill use, and obesity. Chest pain and tachypnea were the most common complaint and clinical sign, respectively. The hypercoagulability screen was negative in 65% of the patients. The mean D-dimer was 5.27 g/mL, and 6 patients, of whom 4 had saddle PE, had D-dimer > 10. Recurrence of PE and neurologic deficits were noted in 2 patients each. We present clinical criteria for ordering CTPA in children with suspected PE based on data from our center and a literature review of pediatric studies. Further multicenter studies with larger samples are needed to validate our proposed criteria.

articles.title: Hospital variation in emergency admission rates from English emergency departments.
Early warning system for deteriorating children to expand to emergency departments across England.
Impact of REACH Mental Health Training on Pediatric Mental Health Care Delivery in Primary Care: Evidence from Virginia's Mental Health Access Program.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Many primary care clinicians (PCCs) lack training in managing mental health (MH) conditions. In 2019, the Virginia Mental Health Access Program (VMAP) began offering Resource for Advancing Children's Health (REACH) MH training to PCCs. We compared changes in patient MH outcomes between clinicians who did and did not participate in REACH.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using VMAP education data, we linked REACH-trained clinicians to claims for youth aged 0-21 years in the Virginia All-Payers Claims Database (APCD) from 2016-2023. REACH-trained clinicians were matched to non-REACH trained clinicians by years of experience, specialty, and clinician type. We compared MH care delivery the year prior to training (baseline), and one and two years after training.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 425 REACH-trained clinicians were matched to 537 non-REACH trained clinicians. Two years after training, 12,750 additional children in Virginia received MH services from REACH-trained clinicians (OR = 1.04, p= 0.022). Compared with non-REACH trained clinicians, REACH-trained clinicians demonstrated a significantly greater increase in MH service provision (OR=1.08, p=0.014), care coordination (OR=1.001, p<0.001), MH diagnoses (OR=1.04, p=0.022), and prescribing MH medications (OR=1.06, p=0.008). There were no significant between group differences in diagnoses of serious mental illness, rate of children receiving psychotherapy, and the proportion of children experiencing emergency room (ER) visits or hospitalizations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: REACH training was associated with improved identification and treatment of mental health conditions, but not with psychotherapy or ER visits. Findings suggest the need for primary care supports beyond clinician training, such as embedded psychologists and urgent psychiatric services.

articles.title: Concussion Diagnosis, Management, and Functional Recovery: An Interdisciplinary and Evidence-Based Approach.

abstract.text: Sport-related concussion is a common and clinically complex form of mild traumatic brain injury with significant academic, occupational, and psychosocial consequences. Management has shifted away from prolonged strict rest to early, symptom-limited activity and targeted rehabilitation. Concussion remains a clinical diagnosis, and routine neuroimaging is typically normal. Symptoms may evolve over hours to days, and structured tools support early assessment; however, they should not be used in isolation to determine recovery or clearance. Office-based evaluation facilitates comprehensive assessment of symptom domains, comorbidities, and functional impact, and subsymptom threshold aerobic exercise testing provides a guide for early activity and individualized progression. Management includes therapies targeted to specific symptom patterns and interdisciplinary care for persistent symptoms. Pharmacologic therapy is symptom targeted and supportive, with limited evidence for select interventions and recommended avoidance of sedating agents that can confound monitoring. Nutritional and dietary supplements have theoretical benefit but insufficient clinical evidence for routine use. Functional recovery is addressed through individualized plans for return to learn, return to play, and return to drive. Prevention should focus on evidence-based risk reduction, with strongest support for policy and rule changes, and equipment and training interventions provide variable benefit. Emerging technologies are primarily research tools given limited standardization and uncertain clinical thresholds.

articles.title: Sports-Related Back Pain and Injuries: From Muscle Strain to Spondylolisthesis.

abstract.text: Back pain is common in both the general population and young athletes, with risk increasing in sports that involve repetitive extension, rotation, and axial loading. Although most cases resolve with time, accurate diagnosis is essential to distinguish common musculoskeletal causes from more serious conditions. This article reviews key causes of athletic back pain, including muscle strain, mechanical low back pain, spondylolysis and spondylolisthesis, lumbar disc herniation, and sacroiliac joint dysfunction. It also examines diagnosis, treatment, and return to play considerations. Early recognition and appropriate management help ensure a safe and timely return to sport.

articles.title: Shoulder Evaluation and Management in the Athlete: From Examination to Surgical Indications.

abstract.text: Shoulder injuries are common among athletes and encompass a wide spectrum of pathology resulting from contact, overhead motion, and repetitive loading. Evaluation of the athletic shoulder presents unique challenges because symptoms may be subtle, sport specific, and performance limiting rather than overtly painful. Accurate diagnosis requires a systematic approach that integrates a detailed history, focused physical examination, and appropriate use of imaging and diagnostic adjuncts. This article provides a clinically oriented review of shoulder evaluation and management in athletes, emphasizing common athletic shoulder pathologies, including rotator cuff disease, instability, labral injury, and overuse conditions. Principles of nonoperative management are discussed along with indications for surgical referral based on structural injury, failure of conservative treatment, and sport-specific demands. Our objective is to equip clinicians with a practical framework to guide diagnosis, management, and return-to-play decision making across a broad range of athletic contexts.

articles.title: Introduction to Special Issue: Sports Injuries: Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention, Recovery, and Return to Play.
Does a maternal history of childhood maltreatment influence prevention program impact on child outcomes? Exploratory findings from a randomized controlled trial in British Columbia, Canada.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nurse-home visiting programs starting prenatally are a promising approach for preventing child maltreatment including injuries. Understanding which families benefit the most can inform policies to ensure greater impact and efficiency.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We investigated whether maternal history of childhood maltreatment (CM) moderated Nurse-Family Partnership (NFP) impact on child outcomes.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING
abstract.text: We utilized secondary data from the Canadian NFP randomized controlled trial (RCT) involving 739 mothers aged 14-24 years and their 737 children in British Columbia (data collected 2013-2019).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Baseline data, including maternal CM history, were collected during pregnancy and before random assignment to existing services or NFP plus existing services. Data on main child outcome indicators: injuries (emergency department events), problem behaviour and language (maternal report) and language and cognition (in-home observations) were collected at age two years.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Many maternal participants reported CM exposure (73.1%), including 57% medium-to-severe and 41.8% severe thresholds. CM history significantly moderated NFP impacts on selected child outcomes including injuries (adjusted differences in rate differences =102.92, 95% CI: 15.18, 193.45) and language via maternal report (adjusted differences in mean differences = -82.52, 95% CI: -150.77, -14.27).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A maternal history of CM moderated NFP impacts on injuries and language, but not all child outcomes examined. Researchers are encouraged to harness existing RCT data to learn how prevention program outcomes vary across populations. Policymakers may then apply this nuanced guidance to inform the refinement of prevention programs for families with unmet needs, fulfilling the ethical obligation to ensure that programs are effective for all.

articles.title: Psychosocial Impact of the Vehicle-Ramming Attack on the Magdeburg Christmas Market in Germany: Protocol for the MD-Care Longitudinal Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: On December 20, 2024, a vehicle-ramming attack occurred at the Magdeburg Christmas market, resulting in 6 fatalities and more than 300 injuries. Mass violence incidents have the potential to cause long-lasting psychosocial consequences for directly and indirectly affected individuals. However, the outcomes can vary depending on relevant risk and protective factors. To improve the psychosocial aftercare of mass violence incidents in Germany, more research is essential.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The MD-Care study strives to examine the psychosocial impact of the vehicle-ramming attack on the Magdeburg Christmas market by investigating the levels, longitudinal trajectories, and associated factors and predictors regarding (1) psychosocial, mental health, and somatic burdens; (2) individual resources and protective factors; and (3) mental health service use and support needs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The MD-Care study is a prospective longitudinal epidemiological study with 3 measurement time points. Data were collected pseudonymously via the online platform LimeSurvey. The baseline survey (t1; 3-month follow-up to the incident) was completed from March to April 2025. The 6-month follow-up (t2) was completed from June to July 2025. Finally, the 15-month follow-up survey (t3) was filled out by participants from March to April 2026. The surveys comprise standardized as well as self-developed ad hoc items addressing the objectives of the study.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The t1 baseline survey was completed by 336 participants, of whom 131 reported being affected individuals. The t2 follow-up survey was completed by 256 (76.2%) participants, 110 of whom reported being affected (110/131, 84% retention of affected individuals). The t3 follow-up survey was completed by 193 (57.4%) participants, 84 of whom reported being affected (84/131, 64.1% retention of affected individuals). The average age of participants for t1 was 39.10 (SD 13.30) years, and 79.5% (267/336) of the t1 sample were women. No funding was received for the quantitative data collection of the MD-Care study. Data analysis started in October 2025 and is ongoing. The first results are expected to be published by the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The MD-Care study may contribute to the evidence base on the psychosocial impact of mass violence incidents, with a particular focus on vehicle-ramming attacks. The findings may inform the development of psychosocial emergency care, long-term support structures, and preparedness planning. Dissemination to relevant political and public health stakeholders will support the translation of the findings into practice and policy.

articles.title: A retrospective study of smart spot, a Bluetooth low‑energy real‑time location system supporting quality improvement efforts in Uganda.

abstract.text: Real-time location systems track assets and individuals, and in high-income clinical settings, they have improved patient flow. However, their use in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Smart Spot, a low-cost Bluetooth low-energy real-time location system was integrated within the Smart Triage quality improvement platform in the outpatient department of Uganda Martyrs' Hospital Ibanda. The primary objective was to evaluate whether Smart Spot data could be used to detect differences in time spent across clinical locations associated with Smart Triage implementation. The secondary objective was to assess the accuracy of Smart Spot data. At triage, children (or their caregivers) received a beacon attached to a lanyard. The beacons tracked patients' locations throughout their time in the outpatient department. Smart Spot data were collected during a 4‑month baseline phase (pre-Smart Triage) and a 12‑month Smart Triage intervention phase. An algorithm was developed to reduce noise and generate more accurate records of each patient's journey. The resulting pathways were compared to expected paths to evaluate Smart Spot's accuracy. The median durations of patient time spent in specific areas were compared between phases using quantile regression. Data cleaning improved the matching to the expected patient flow from 13.0% to 73.1%. Compared with baseline, the median time patients spent in the assessment area decreased by 51.7% (-81.9 min; CI: -95.1 to -68.8), in the emergency room by 69.1% (-44.3 min; CI: -67.7 to -20.8), and total visit duration by 58.2% (-122.9 min; CI: -138.4 to -107.3), all with p-value < 0.001. Real-time location data supported the demonstration of the Smart Triage platform's benefits. In the cleaned dataset, the intervention phase had shorter total visit time and time reductions within specific areas. Our evaluation demonstrates Smart Spot's feasibility as an effective data-collection platform for quality improvement and its utility for retrospective analyses in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Concurrent Triple-class Psychotropic Use and Postoperative Morbidity Following Single-Level Lumbar Fusion: A Propensity Score-matched Cohort Study.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine whether triple-class psychotropic exposure before single-level lumbar fusion is associated with different postoperative outcomes than selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) monotherapy in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis.

abstract.label: SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA
abstract.text: Psychiatric illness is common before spine surgery and associated with inferior outcomes, but is usually analyzed as a single categorical variable. Whether regimen complexity carries independent prognostic information is unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adults with a psychotic-spectrum or mood disorder (ICD-10-CM, F20-F39) undergoing primary single-level posterior lumbar arthrodesis were identified in TriNetX. Exposure was ascertained 365 to 1 day preoperatively; postoperative prescriptions did not contribute. Patients receiving an SSRI, benzodiazepine and antipsychotic were matched 1:1 on 75 preoperative characteristics to SSRI monotherapy. Pseudarthrosis and surgical site infection were co-primary outcomes; revision, readmission, emergency department visits and opioid use were secondary, assessed at 3 and 6 months and 1, 3 and 5 years (Bonferroni P<0.025).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 638 matched pairs, all but one characteristic achieved a standardized mean difference <0.10. Surgical site infection was more frequent at every interval (5 y, 14.73% vs 8.31%; RR 1.77, 95% CI 1.29-2.44; P=0.0003), as was readmission (5 y, 67.40% vs 57.99%; RR 1.16, 1.07-1.27; P=0.0005). Revision was approximately twofold higher from 1 year onward (5 y, 8.62% vs 4.39%; RR 1.96, 1.26-3.06; P=0.0022). Pseudarthrosis was more frequent at every interval but met the corrected threshold only at 1 year (16.87% vs 12.38%; RR 1.36, 1.04-1.78; P=0.0224). The proportion receiving any opioid was identical (97.49%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Triple-class exposure was associated with higher infection, readmission and revision than SSRI monotherapy. These associations do not establish causation and may reflect illness severity, unmeasured surgical factors or detection bias. The regimen is a risk marker warranting closer perioperative surveillance, not a treatment target.

articles.title: Readily Accessible Serum Biomarkers as Potential Indicators of Radiation Combined Burn Injury.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Radiation combined burn injury (RCBI) results in markedly greater morbidity and mortality than either insult alone, yet its early recognition remains challenging, particularly in mass-casualty events. Serum is easily accessible, and its routine biomarker alteration may aid clinicians in early decision-making.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine whether routine serum biochemical markers can serve as a reliable indicator for early detection, severity assessment, and risk stratification of radiation combined burn injury.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: In this study, a murine model of combined radiation and burn injury (4 Gy + 80°C burn) was used to evaluate serum biochemical alterations over 28 days following burn injury only, radiation injury only, and radiation combined with burn injury only groups. Assays included aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), De Ritis ratio (AST/ALT), cholesterol, triglycerides, inorganic phosphate, iron, and albumin.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Combined injury produces a distinct and time-dependent biochemical alteration, characterized by an early elevation in AST and ALT levels, a brief increase in triglycerides after one week, and a delayed rise in alkaline phosphatase levels. Elevations in albumin and iron levels, and a delayed decrease in inorganic phosphate, are more pronounced and persistent in combined injury than in either single insult alone.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These routine serum biomarkers can serve as accessible and clinically relevant indicators for early detection of radiation-combined burn injury and risk stratification for affected patients. Their collective interpretation could support decisions on early therapeutics and casualty management. Overall, the study addresses a critical challenge in mass-casualty and resource-limited settings by evaluating easily accessible diagnostic biomarkers.

articles.title: Prognostic value of the red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio in alcohol-related sarcopenia.

abstract.text: Chronic alcohol consumption is associated with sarcopenia, a metabolic disorder characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function. The red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has emerged as a composite biomarker reflecting inflammation, oxidative stress, and nutritional status. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of RAR in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia. We conducted a prospective observational study including 231 patients with chronic alcohol consumption (mean intake 200 g/day) recruited at a tertiary hospital between 2008 and 2025. Clinical, analytical, and body composition variables were assessed using densitometry and handgrip strength. Probable sarcopenia was defined according to EWGSOP2 criteria based on low muscle strength. Cox and logistic regression models and ROC curve analysis were performed. RAR was positively associated with liver dysfunction and inflammatory markers, and inversely correlated with appendicular lean mass and handgrip strength. In patients with probable sarcopenia, RAR was independently associated with 12-month mortality (hazard ratio 1.67; 95% confidence interval 1.32-2.11; p < 0.001). The predictive capacity of RAR was high (AUC 0.81; 95% CI 0.67-0.94). In conclusion, RAR is a simple, low-cost, and independent prognostic biomarker that integrates inflammatory and nutritional status in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia.

articles.title: Fixation of patellar fractures using bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide cannulated screws and subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Bioabsorbable implants offer a promising alternative to metallic fixation for patellar fractures, potentially avoiding hardware-related complications. In 2023, a new generation of bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide (HA/PLLA) cannulated screws was introduced, featuring a low-profile (2 mm) trident-shaped head and increased root diameter for enhanced strength. This study evaluates the clinical outcomes of a surgical technique combining these redesigned screws with subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Between April 2023 and May 2025, 19 consecutive patients with transverse patellar fractures (AO/OTA 34-C1/C2) underwent open reduction and internal fixation. Two bioabsorbable cannulated screws were used. High-strength nonabsorbable sutures were passed through the screw channels and a central bone tunnel using a double-loop sliding knot for compression. The sutures were systematically routed subperiosteally to minimize tissue irritation. Full weight-bearing with a brace began on postoperative day one. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were assessed. This study was approved by the institutional review board of Kainan Hospital.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean maximum articular surface gap was 8.7 ± 5.2 mm. The mean follow-up was 8.6 ± 3.0 months. Bone union was achieved in all cases. At the final follow-up, the mean knee flexion was 138.7° ± 13.0° and extension was - 1.6° ± 3.4°. No postoperative complications, including infection, loss of reduction, screw breakage, or symptomatic hardware irritation, were observed during the follow-up period. No reoperations were required during the follow-up period.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: All patients achieved bone union. No major complications or reoperations were observed during the follow-up period. These preliminary findings suggest that this technique may be feasible for transverse patellar fractures.

articles.title: Return-to-Play Outcomes After Primary Ulnar Collateral Ligament Reconstruction Vary Substantially Depending on Return Criteria: A Systematic Review Stratified by Competition Level.
articles.journal_full: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To determine how return definitions influence return to play (RTP), return to the same level of play (RTSP), advancement rates, and return timelines after primary ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction (UCLR) in baseball pitchers across levels of competition.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched from January 2000 to January 2025. Studies evaluating baseball pitchers undergoing primary UCLR and reporting RTP, RTSP, advancement, or return timing outcomes with participation-based (RTP based on a single event) or durability-based (RTP after sustained participation over a predefined threshold) criteria were included. Primary outcomes were RTP, RTSP, and advancement rate (progression to a higher level after UCLR); secondary outcome was return time stratified by return criteria. Risk of bias was assessed with the Methodological Index for Non-randomized Studies and Risk Of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tools.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-four studies met inclusion. Across these studies, 19 included Major League Baseball players (2194 players), 5 included Minor League Baseball (MiLB) players (2318 players), 4 included collegiate athletes (553 athletes), and 6 included high school athletes (258 athletes). RTP/RTSP rates were 86% to 92%/70% to 87% in high school, 84%/67% to 92% in college, 76.3% to 79%/69.1% to 100% in MiLB, and 80% to 97.2%/28.1% to 87% in Major League Baseball. Advancement was 55.7% to 63.2% in high school, 4.1% to 44.4% in college, and 22.3% to 45% in MiLB. Surgery-to-return time using the common RTSP definition ranged from 13.7 to 20.5 months (Major League Baseball), 14.6 to 16.4 (MiLB), and 11 to 17 (college and high school). Durability-based definitions were not consistently associated with longer return intervals.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Without standardized return criteria, reported RTP, RTSP, advancement rates, and return timelines after primary UCLR in baseball pitchers varied substantially across studies and competition levels. Durability-based criteria were not consistently associated with longer return timelines, indicating that return outcomes should be interpreted according to the competition level and return definition used. Standardized, tier-specific return criteria may improve clinical interpretation after primary UCLR.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level IV, systematic review of Level II to IV studies.

articles.title: Sildenafil as a Diagnostic Tool and Treatment Option for Popliteal Artery Entrapment Syndrome: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

abstract.text: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome (PAES) is characterized by activity-related, lower extremity claudication symptoms including exertional calf pain, weakness, cramping, foot paresthesia, and reports of increased calf tension. Diagnosis can be challenging and has overlap with other lower extremity exertional conditions. This case report describes a case of a 21-year-old female athlete presenting with progressive exertional bilateral calf pain during tennis matches recalcitrant to numerous treatment options. A course of sildenafil was noted to provide symptomatic relief and allowed the athlete to participate near pain free temporarily. Her symptoms worsened despite continued sildenafil use with exercise and required surgical intervention. Sildenafil may be a useful diagnostic option in the workup for PAES.

articles.title: Athlete Safeguarding-Maintaining the Call to Action.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

articles.title: Experiences and information needs of parents seeking care for children with medical complexity in emergency care settings: a mixed methods systematic review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The objective of this mixed methods systematic review was to synthesize primary research regarding parents' self-reported experiences and information needs related to seeking emergency care for their child with medical complexity.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Children with medical complexity are frequent users of emergency department and other emergency care services. While some primary research describing family experiences of caring for children with medical complexity exists, no synthesis of available evidence on this topic is available. Findings from this review can provide a better overall understanding of the experiences and information needs of parents while in emergency care settings with a child with medical complexity in order to support families and guide expectations.

abstract.label: ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
abstract.text: Primary studies of any design were included when reported in English, conducted with parents of a child < 18 years of age with medical complexity, and describing parents' experiences or information needs when in emergency care settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A search was conducted in the following electronic databases from inception to May 17, 2024: MEDLINE, Embase (Ovid), PsycINFO (Ovid), Scopus, and CINAHL Plus with Full Text (EBSCOhost). Screening and data extraction were completed by 2 reviewers independently. Eligible studies were critically appraised for methodological quality by 2 reviewers independently using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Data synthesis and integration of qualitative and quantitative data occurred simultaneously following the JBI convergent integrated approach.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifteen studies were included: 3 quantitative, 5 mixed methods, and 7 qualitative. The majority of studies were conducted in the United States (n=10, 67%) and used semi-structured interviews or focus group discussions to collect data (n=11, 73%). The most common pediatric diagnosis was sickle cell disease (n=6, 40%). Most included studies (n=12, 80%) met at least 80% of the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool criteria. Synthesized findings were grouped into 6 integrated findings: i) patient and family experiences are impacted by the need to constantly advocate for their child; ii) parents perceived a lack of skills and knowledge among health care providers in caring for children with medical complexity; iii) parents experienced challenges when accessing emergency services and during transitions in care; iv) perceptions of the care received are influenced by quality of communication, timeliness of care, and pain management; v) collaboration and coordination in care are necessary; and vi) information supporting communication and decision-making can support positive experiences in emergency care settings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This mixed methods systematic review synthesized research to explore and gain a broader understanding of the experiences and information needs of parents when presenting to emergency care settings with a child with medical complexity. Findings highlight opportunities to improve patient and family experiences through improved communication, collaboration, care coordination, pain management, and informed decision-making. Findings can be used to inform the development of knowledge translation resources (eg, videos, infographics) for parents, and to contextualize educational tools or interventions for health care providers working in emergency care settings. Creating evidence-based resources for families and health care providers that consider parent perspectives has the potential to promote informed and shared decision-making while supporting patient-centered care.

abstract.label: REVIEW REGISTRATION
abstract.text: PROSPERO CRD42024534701.

articles.title: Time to untether transitional care from hospital quality: Healthcare utilization following discharge from a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital among community-dwelling older persons.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Thirty-day performance measures (e.g., unplanned readmissions), designed to evaluate inpatient care, were neither designed to reflect the experience of patients transitioning from hospital to home, nor the impact of transitional programs to improve postdischarge outcomes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To identify transitional care outcomes by examining a range of postdischarge encounters and mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational cohort (October 2022-September 2023) included community-dwelling patients ≥65-years-old, discharged from 120 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals to home after medical or neurological admissions. The outcomes, assessed 30- and 90-days postdischarge were: mortality; planned and unplanned readmissions; observation stays; Emergency Department (ED) visits at VA or non-VA hospitals; and number of days in acute care.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 99,778 patients, 71.1% had no acute care utilization within 30 days postdischarge; 49.9% in 90 days. Unplanned readmissions occurred in 14.4% (N = 14,400) at 30 days; 27.5% (N = 27,386) at 90 days. Mortality occurred in 1.8% (N = 1750) within 30 days; 5.6% (N = 5624) within 90 days. Mortality was highest among patients with unplanned readmissions: 30 days, 6.1% (882/14,400); 90 days, 13.1% (3599/27,386). Planned readmission mortality rates were 30 days, 5.8% (59/1017); 90 days, 9.6% (258/2692). Half of patients who died within 30 days postdischarge did so after an unplanned readmission (50.4% [882/1750]); 35.0% (613/1750) had no acute care utilization. Among N = 94,154 patients who survived 90-day postdischarge, 11.2% spent ≥10 days in acute care settings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings support using the number of days in acute care within 90 days postdischarge as a transitional outcome. Thirty-day readmissions do not capture the full scope of postdischarge healthcare utilization and mortality among community-dwelling older adults.

articles.title: State of the art: thoracic ultrasound.

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF REVIEW
abstract.text: Thoracic ultrasound has continued to expand beyond simple bedside triage into a quantitative, procedure-guiding and increasingly artificial intelligence-augmented tool across pleural and respiratory medicine. This review summarizes the literature published over the past year, highlighting developments in effusion characterization, pneumothorax diagnosis, image-guided pleural procedures, artificial intelligence, training standards, critical care applications, malignant pleural effusion management, and diaphragm/interstitial lung disease assessment.

abstract.label: RECENT FINDINGS
abstract.text: Elastography and contrast-enhanced ultrasound have moved from exploratory to comparative and multicentre randomized evaluation for effusion characterization and biopsy guidance. Meta-analyses have reaffirmed the superiority of point-of-care ultrasound over chest radiography for both pneumothorax and thoracentesis guidance. Artificial intelligence tools have shown that they can close the acquisition-skill gap for novice operators, although automated interpretation (particularly B-line quantification) remains inconsistent against expert consensus. A new UK national training standard for pleural procedures has been published, alongside the first validated thoracic-specific competency assessment tool. A large multicentre randomized trial found that a point-of-care ultrasound-driven diagnostic pathway did not improve early discharge rates in emergency department patients with dyspnoea, an important negative finding. Diaphragm and quantitative lung ultrasound continue to accumulate evidence as noninvasive markers of interstitial lung disease severity and ventilator weaning readiness.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: The past year's literature confirms thoracic ultrasound's trajectory from a purely diagnostic adjunct towards a quantitative, procedure-integrated and artificial intelligence-supported modality, while also delivering important cautionary and negative findings that temper enthusiasm and clarify where evidence remains immature.

articles.title: The Nature of Pediatric Complaints in the Post-Disaster Setting: Two Natural Disasters and Two Extensive Relief Efforts.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Our objective was to review the prospectively collected data on patient demographics, chief complaints, and resource utilization of internally displaced children in congregate settings established after two natural disasters in a large metropolitan area.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Following Hurricane Katrina, providers from Texas Children's Hospital (TCH) established a Mobile Pediatric Emergency Response Team (MPERT). Similarly, after Hurricane Harvey in 2017, local Emergency Medical Services (EMS) responded and the federal Disaster Medical Assistance Team (DMAT) deployed, establishing a care area in a shelter for those that had been displaced.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective case-control study used data collected prospectively at the post-hurricane medical care areas. A database compiling diagnostic codes utilized was created. Providers labeled each diagnostic code as either acute, chronic or undecided. These labels were assessed for interrater reliability using the Fleiss kappa and presentations in the post-hurricane setting were described and compared to controls utilizing a Chi-Square analysis. When unanimous agreement was not obtained, majority consensus was utilized.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The TCH ED totaled 3,587 patients, the MPERT totaled 3,015 and the DMAT totaled 202 patients. Raters, utilizing the diagnostic code database, showed substantial agreement for all options combined (ĸ = 0.69; p-value <0.0001). 22% of patients presented with chronic complaints compared to 13.6% of the controls (Difference 8.4%, p < 0.0001, 95%CI 6.52-10.31).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In the post-hurricane setting, chronic medical complaints are the primary complaints compared to a routine pediatric EC. These data can be utilized to better prepare post-hurricane shelters.

articles.title: The role of T-peak to T-end, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance in the differential diagnosis of myocarditis.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Paediatric myocarditis, a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy (incidence 1-2/100,000 annually), challenges emergency diagnosis due to nonspecific symptoms mimicking common illnesses. This study assessed electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarisation heterogeneity-T-peak to T-end interval, T-peak to T-end/QT, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance-for diagnosing myocarditis and predicting ventricular arrhythmia risk in children aged 0-18 years.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective case-control study of 76 myocarditis patients (diagnosed by clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and cardiac MRI criteria) presenting to our paediatric emergency department from January 1, 2024, to May 30, 2025, versus 75 age-matched healthy controls. Electrocardiographic parameters were measured in leads DII and V5. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of T-peak to T-end and T peak-to-end/corrected QT (Lead II (Derivation II)). Myocarditis cases stratified by arrhythmia development (with: n = 28; without: n = 48); groups compared via t-tests, Mann-Whitney U, and chi-square (p < 0.05 significant).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Myocarditis group: 23 females (30.2%) and 53 males (69.8%); mean age 12.0 ± 4.7 years. Controls: 39 females (52.0%), 36 males (48.0%); mean age 10.3 ± 4.9 years (p = 0.03). Receiver operating characteristic (Lead II (Derivation II)): T-peak to T-end cut-off 62 ms (sensitivity 69.3%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.725, p < 0.001); T peak-to-end/corrected QT cut-off 0.19 (sensitivity 50.7%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.625, p < 0.05).The arrhythmia subgroup showed corrected QT prolongation (470 vs. 435 ms, V5; p < 0.001), T-peak to T-end (110 vs. 90 ms, V5; p < 0.001), higher T peak-to-end/corrected QT, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance (both p < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The T-peak to T-end interval, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratio, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance provide high-specificity, noninvasive electrocardiographic biomarkers for paediatric myocarditis diagnosis in the ED. Corrected QT and T-peak to T-end prolongation signals repolarisation heterogeneity and arrhythmia risk, supporting routine triage integration for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Stable Iodine Knowledge and Preferred Information Sources Among Parents in Fukushima Prefecture After the 2011 Nuclear Disaster.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Knowledge regarding stable iodine prophylaxis among populations affected by the Fukushima nuclear accident remains poorly characterized. We assessed knowledge levels and preferred information sources among parents of thyroid examination participants aged ≤18 years.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive study (April 2019 and December 2022) among parents of thyroid examination participants. Knowledge was assessed using 3 items: role recognition, distribution method awareness, and effectiveness duration (score 0-3). Preferred information providers for future emergencies were collected.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,116 participants (mean child age 12.3 years, 8.1-11.8 years post-disaster), the mean knowledge score was 1.66/3 (SD = 0.97). Only 22.1% showed high knowledge (score = 3), while 42.1% had low knowledge (score 0-1). Although two-thirds (67.8%) correctly recognized stable iodine's role, distribution method awareness was most limited: 54.3% lacked awareness of how stable iodine is distributed. Regarding effectiveness duration, 51.2% correctly answered. Health professionals were largely preferred as information providers (90.5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Substantial knowledge gaps existed regarding stable iodine prophylaxis, particularly distribution methods. Health professionals, as the most trusted information source, may play a key role in addressing these gaps by communicating preparedness information to communities.

articles.title: Predictors of Antibiotic Overuse in Febrile Children: A Sub-analysis of the Prospective, Multicenter AutoPilot-Dx Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Antibiotic overuse contributes to antimicrobial resistance. Mechanisms that drive overuse, including diagnostic uncertainty, are thought to be complex. We aimed to investigate predictive factors for antibiotic overuse in a large pediatric cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a subanalysis from the AutoPilot-Dx study, which enrolled febrile children 90 days to 18 years old presenting to the pediatric emergency department with respiratory tract infection or fever without source, including both hospitalized children and those discharged home. We analyzed patient flow from being treated with antibiotics at recruitment to definitive antibiotic treatment after assessment, depending on physician judgment. Variables significantly associated with antibiotic overuse in univariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of antibiotic overuse, defined as receipt of antibiotic treatment following clinical assessment in cases with viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis. Diagnostic uncertainty was assessed by treating physicians.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Upon recruitment, 127/1008 (12.6%) were receiving antibiotic treatment. Overall, 186 of 628 cases with a viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis were judged to have antibiotic overuse. Factors with significant association in univariate analysis were diagnostic uncertainty, nonexudative tonsillitis, rales and younger age. Presence of a diagnostic test result upon presentation to the hospital and current antibiotic treatment were found not to be associated with overuse. Among 566 of 1008 cases with complete data on all model covariates, multivariable logistic regression yielded diagnostic uncertainty [odds ratio (OR), 2.09; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-3.93; P = 0.015], nonexudative tonsillitis (OR, 2.78; 95% CI: 1.72-4.59; P < 0.001) and rales (OR, 1.82; 95% CI: 1.15-2.86; P = 0.01) to be positively associated with antibiotic overuse, while age showed a negative association in complete-case analysis (OR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.85-0.99; P = 0.038), which attenuated and was no longer significant in a multiple imputation sensitivity analysis (OR, 0.96; 95% CI: 0.91-1.01; P = 0.150).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Diagnostic uncertainty contributes to antibiotic overuse, alongside clinical factors. Future studies should investigate the impact of improved diagnostic algorithms on antibiotic prescribing in patients with respiratory tract infections in whom physicians experience diagnostic uncertainty.

articles.title: Electroencephalography-based machine learning models for hyperacute detection of large vessel occlusion stroke.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Electroencephalography (EEG) has shown potential as a prehospital triage instrument for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO-a) stroke. In this study, we determined the diagnostic accuracy of EEG-based machine learning algorithms for LVO-a stroke detection.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Anterior circulation large vessel occlusion stroke detection machine learning models were developed using EEG data from the ELECTRA-STROKE (NCT03699397) and AI-STROKE (NCT05437237) studies. Single 2- to 3-min EEG recordings were obtained using 8 dry electrodes in adults with suspected stroke in prehospital and in-hospital settings. Patients with a clean EEG segment of ≥ 5 s (visually selected) were included and EEG symmetry features were extracted. We assessed the performance of multiple machine learning models using nested cross-validation (CV), optimising models with 3-fold CV (inner loop) and evaluating them with leave-one-out CV (outer loop).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1293 patients with suspected stroke, 336 (26%) were included (74% prehospital, 26% in-hospital). Median age was 72 (IQR 61-80) years, and 231 (69%) were male. Sixteen (5%) patients had LVO-a stroke, 140 (42%) non-LVO-a ischaemic stroke, 52 (15%) TIA, 13 (4%) haemorrhagic stroke and 115 (34%) a stroke mimic. Naïve Bayes achieved the highest observed area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.85 [95% CI, 0.77-0.93]), with a sensitivity of 69% (95% CI, 44%-86%) and specificity of 86% (95% CI, 82%-89%).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Machine learning models for LVO-a stroke detection based solely on EEG showed moderately high diagnostic accuracy. These results support the potential of EEG-based LVO-a stroke detection, but improved EEG data acquisition is needed before clinical implementation can be considered.

articles.title: Development and validation of methods to predict ground- and helicopter-based emergency medical service travel times.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Helicopter-based Emergency Medical Services (EMS) are a costly and finite resource and should only be deployed when they provide substantial benefits to patients. One such benefit is a more rapid response to incidents and transport to hospital compared to Ground-based EMS. This study evaluates methods for estimating travel times for the purpose of optimizing the selection of helicopter vs. ground EMS.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Ground EMS travel times were estimated using an open-source routing tool, the estimates of which were adjusted using linear regression and gradient boosting models based on historical travel times. Helicopter travel times were similarly estimated based on great circle distances adjusted by historical data. Models were evaluated using several measures of predictive accuracy to enable comparison with other studies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In validation data collected after finalization of the methods, the best performing prediction models for Ground EMS travel times explained a substantial portion of variation in drive times to location and to hospital (R2 0.79 and 0.70 respectively), and less for helicopter flight times (R2 0.46 and 0.38 respectively). Mean average percentage error was 18-20% for all investigated estimation techniques and time intervals.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Integrating tools based on the open-source code provided with this study has the potential to improve the ability of dispatchers to estimate relative travel times and assess the potential time benefit of directing the most appropriate resources to a given patient.

articles.title: Frequency-matched comparison of early complications after thermocautery, bipolar sleeve and scalpel guillotine circumcision in 31 100 boys.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Thermocautery assisted circumcision is widely used, but comparative evidence rarely accounts for age, calendar period or surgeon.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare operative time and early complications between thermocautery guillotine, bipolar dorsal sleeve and scalpel guillotine circumcision. We hypothesised that thermocautery would be associated with shorter operative time and fewer early complications, particularly bleeding requiring intervention, and that these associations would persist after frequency matching for age and stratification by calendar period and surgeon.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort of 31 100 boys circumcised in hospital between June 2012 and November 2021 b y bipolar dorsal sleeve (n = 2050), scalpel guillotine (n = 3050) or thermocautery guillotine (n = 26 000). Outcomes were operative time and any complication within 21 days, with bleeding requiring suture ligation as the key secondary outcome. The primary comparison used 1:5 frequency matching by completed year of age, with Mantel-Haenszel risk ratios stratified by age band, calendar period and surgeon as sensitivity analyses. One hundred children referred after out-of-hospital circumcision were described separately and excluded from comparisons.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean operative time was 8 ± 3 min with thermocautery against 16 ± 4 and 20 ± 5 min (P < 0.001). At least one early complication occurred in 0.60% of thermocautery, 8.68% of bipolar sleeve and 7.21% of scalpel guillotine patients, with frequency-matched risk ratios of 14.1 (95% CI 10.6 to 18.8) and 12.1 (95% CI 9.5 to 15.4) against thermocautery. Bleeding requiring suture ligation occurred in 0 of 26 000 thermocautery, 15 of 2050 bipolar sleeve and 25 of 3050 scalpel guillotine patients. Oedema was least frequent with thermocautery (0.29% against 1.71% and 0.49%). The direction of association was consistent across age bands, calendar periods and surgeons, although its magnitude varied between surgeons. Among the 100 referred children, three had glans amputation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Thermocautery was associated with shorter operative time and fewer early complications, above all bleeding that required a procedure. The excess of oedema reported with thermocautery in earlier studies was not reproduced. Catastrophic injury was seen only among children referred after circumcision by non-physician providers, a group without a denominator.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Thermocautery assisted circumcision was associated with shorter procedure time and fewer early complications, particularly bleeding. Catastrophic injury occurred only among children referred after circumcision by non-physician providers, a selected group in which its incidence cannot be estimated, and the findings reinforce the importance of circumcision by appropriately trained providers.

articles.title: Telemedicine and Cardiac Service Utilization After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
Generative Artificial Intelligence and Maternal Health Outcomes in Pregnant and Postpartum Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to support maternal health, but randomized evidence is limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate whether access to a generative AI maternal health chatbot improved 12-month maternal health outcomes.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This 2-group randomized clinical trial enrolled 400 participants from October 2023 to December 2024, with 12-month follow-up completed in December 2025. Participants were recruited online across 49 US states and the District of Columbia. Eligible participants were English-speaking, aged 14 years or older, pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months, and self-identified as members of racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive access to the chatbot or an active control consisting of monthly children's books.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms at 12 months measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Secondary outcomes included emergency department visits, pregnancy-related complications, postpartum care checkups, effective contraception use, and sleep duration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 400 randomized participants, the mean (SD) age was 32.6 (5.1) years; 200 (50%) were parenting an infant at enrollment; and 10 (2%) identified as American Indian or Alaska Native, 80 (20%) Asian, 188 (47%) Black or African American, 57 (14%) multiracial, and 65 (16%) Hispanic or Latino. The AI chatbot was not associated with differences in anxiety scores (adjusted mean difference, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.77 to 0.96) or depression scores (adjusted mean difference, -0.23; 95% CI, -1.05 to 0.59), nor with emergency department visits, postpartum care, contraception use, or sleep duration. Among participants pregnant at enrollment, the chatbot was associated with more self-reported pregnancy-related complications in the secondary 12-month end point analysis, but not in longitudinal analyses. Higher chatbot engagement was associated with longer sleep duration and higher anxiety scores in exploratory within-group analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this randomized clinical trial of pregnant and postpartum individuals from racial and ethnic minoritized groups, access to a generative artificial intelligence maternal health chatbot did not improve maternal anxiety or depression at 12 months compared with an active control. Secondary and exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06053515.

articles.title: Spontaneous Enterococcus faecalis Meningitis in an Elderly Patient: A Rare Cause of Community-Acquired Bacterial Meningitis.

abstract.text: Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis) is an uncommon cause of bacterial meningitis in adults, typically associated with neurosurgical procedures, central nervous system devices, or underlying comorbidities. Community-acquired meningitis caused by this microorganism is particularly rare. We report the case of a 76-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with acute prostration and altered mental status, without classical meningeal signs. Initial cranial CT revealed no acute abnormalities. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed findings strongly suggestive of bacterial meningitis, and E. faecalis was subsequently identified as the causative pathogen. Intravenous ampicillin and ceftriaxone were administered, with progressive neurological improvement. An extensive diagnostic workup, including cranial MRI, transthoracic echocardiography, thoracoabdominal CT, and colonoscopy, failed to identify a definitive source of infection. This case report highlights the diagnostic challenges of E. faecalis meningitis in older adults, particularly in the absence of classical meningeal manifestations and an identifiable infectious source. It also underscores the importance of early recognition, comprehensive microbiological investigation, and appropriate antimicrobial therapy in the management of this rare clinical entity.

articles.title: Handheld Ultrasound Implementation and Structured Point-of-Care Ultrasound Training Across the Indo-Pacific: Programmatic Lessons From the PEARLS Program.
articles.journal_full: Australasian journal of ultrasound in medicine

abstract.text: In many remote Indo-Pacific communities, clinicians must make critical decisions without access to advanced diagnostic imaging. Handheld ultrasound can help bridge this gap by providing real-time, bedside imaging that improves diagnostic confidence and guides patient management. Drawing on lessons from the PEARLS ultrasound training program, employinghandheld ultrasound across multiple Pacific nations, this article discusses how successful implementation depends not only on the technology itself, but also on ongoing training, mentorship, quality assurance, and internet connectivity. Our findings suggest that pairing handheld ultrasound with structured education programs can support sustainable improvements in healthcare delivery in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Distribution of Fentanyl-induced Pruritus in Spinal Anaesthesia with Hyperbaric Bupivacaine: A Prospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The incidence of fentanyl-induced pruritus in spinal anaesthesia with hyperbaric bupivacaine is highly variable, ranging from 30% to 60%.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: In our study, we analysed the incidence, risk factors and pattern of distribution of pruritus following intrathecal administration of fentanyl with bupivacaine.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital from August 2025 to January 2026. Adult patients (>18 years) receiving standard spinal anaesthesia with bupivacaine and fentanyl were included. The primary outcome was the incidence and anatomical distribution of pruritus, while secondary outcomes assessed the onset time, duration and severity of pruritus using a Numeric Rating Scale.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 100 patients (60% of males; mean age: 46.19 ± 18.16 years), the overall mean fentanyl dose was 22.95 ± 2.57 µg. Intraoperative pruritus occurred in 70% of patients and was predominantly facial (78.6%). Patients experiencing pruritus received significantly higher fentanyl doses compared to those who did not (23.43 ± 2.34 µg vs. 21.83 ± 2.78 µg; P = 0.006). Logistic regression indicated a 27% increase in pruritus odds per 1 µg increase in fentanyl. Symptoms were generally mild, with a mean onset of 18.90 ± 9.07 min and a mean duration of 7.07 ± 3.78 min.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The majority receiving spinal anaesthesia had mild pruritus, with the face being the most affected area. The frequency of pruritus significantly correlated with the dosage of fentanyl.

articles.title: Return to play and performance in Division I collegiate pitchers following ulnar collateral ligament surgery: a retrospective case series.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The purpose of this study was to evaluate return to play, postoperative performance, and career advancement in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I baseball players following ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: NCAA Division I pitchers undergoing UCL surgery between 2015 and 2024 were identified using the Tommy John List. Outcomes included return to play, level of return to play, advancement to professional baseball, and pre- and postoperative earned run average (ERA), walks and hits per innings pitched (WHIP), strikeout-to-walk ratio, and innings pitched per season. Comparisons were made between performance outcomes from all preoperative seasons versus all postoperative seasons for pitchers who returned to Division I.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 264 pitchers were included, with 239 (90.5%) returning to play following UCL surgery. Return-to-performance analysis included 156 pitchers who returned to play at the Division I level. The only significant difference in pre- and postoperative performance for the full cohort was an increase in innings pitched per season (median difference, 6.25; P=0.002). Subgroup analysis of Power 5 pitchers demonstrated significantly higher postoperative ERA (median difference, 0.42; P=0.01) and WHIP (median difference, 0.05; P=0.03), along with a significant increase in innings pitched per season (median difference, 7.94; P=0.01).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Division I pitchers returned to play at high rates following UCL surgery. Among those who returned to Division I, no significant differences were observed in postoperative ERA, WHIP, or strikeout-to-walk ratio for the full cohort. However, Power 5 conference pitchers displayed small but statistically significant increases in postoperative ERA and WHIP. Level of evidence: IV.

articles.title: Differentiated effect of hypothermia versus normothermia after cardiac arrest by neurological status and clinical correlates of ischemic burden.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The optimal temperature target after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain, as major randomized trials have not demonstrated a clear benefit of lower-target hypothermia compared with normothermia.
