The lesion was non-displaced and initially described as a greenstick-type fracture. Conservative treatment with a plaster splint and non-weight-bearing was initiated. No analgesics were required.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Distal fibular fractures in young athletes may occur through unusual, contactless mechanisms with minimal symptoms, even in a suprasyndesmotic Weber C fracture pattern. Clinical assessment must remain the cornerstone of decision-making, while complementary imaging is useful to rule out complications, such as pseudarthrosis. Conservative management allowed full and safe return to sport in this patient after 4 months.

articles.title: Donation After Circulatory Versus Brain Death Among Adult Trauma Donors: A Retrospective Multicenter Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) is an increasingly important source of organs and tissues, yet differences between DCD and donation after brain death (DBD) among trauma donors remain incompletely characterized. We compared DCD and DBD donors among trauma patients who proceeded to donation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adult trauma patients who died during hospitalization across four trauma centers from January 1, 2016, through July 15, 2022, were retrospectively screened; the analytic cohort comprised patients who proceeded to donation. Multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with DCD versus DBD among donors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 173 donors, 90 (52%) were DCD and 83 (48%) were DBD. Compared with DBD donors, DCD donors were older (median 52 vs. 31 years, p = 0.006), more often White (78% vs. 47%, p < 0.001), had fewer severe head/neck injuries (AIS ≥ 3: 61% vs. 87%, p < 0.001), higher admission GCS (13-15: 24% vs. 8%, p = 0.003), and were less often admitted to the ICU (79% vs. 98%, p = 0.002). DCD donors had a lower median number of organs and tissues recovered (2 [IQR 1-3] vs. 3 [2-4], p < 0.001). After adjustment, GCS 9-15 vs. 3-8 (AOR 3.62, 95% CI (1.22-10.77)), White race (5.41, (2.24-13.06)), head/neck AIS ≤2 vs. ≥ 3 (5.15, (1.99-13.34)), and trauma center were independently associated with DCD.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among trauma donors, DCD and DBD donors differed in neurologic injury severity, hospital course, and organ and tissue recovery patterns. Studies that include all potential trauma donors are needed to identify factors that may influence referral, authorization, and conversion.

articles.title: Severe acute gastric volvulus: A case report with perforation and extra-gastric ischemic findings.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.text: Acute gastric volvulus is a rare but life-threatening surgical emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Its nonspecific clinical presentation may delay diagnosis and treatment, potentially leading to severe complications. Gastric ischemia, necrosis, and perforation can result in rapid clinical deterioration and life-threatening consequences. A 36-year-old male patient presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset abdominal distension and respiratory distress. On admission, he exhibited severe hemodynamic instability and signs of an acute abdomen. Imaging revealed intraperitoneal free air, prompting emergency surgical intervention. Emergency laparotomy demonstrated a 270° gastric volvulus complicated by ischemia and perforation. Additionally, pneumatosis intestinalis of the small bowel and perforation of a Meckel's diverticulum were observed, likely secondary to increased intra-abdominal pressure. Despite early surgical intervention, the patient died in the early postoperative period following the development of refractory shock. This case highlights the rapidly progressive and potentially fatal nature of acute gastric volvulus, particularly when accompanied by multiple intra-abdominal complications. Acute gastric volvulus should be considered in patients presenting with sudden abdominal distension, respiratory distress, and rapid clinical deterioration. Although early diagnosis and emergency surgical intervention are essential, mortality remains high in hemodynamically unstable patients..

articles.title: Emergency department evaluation of injuries caused by falls from horses: A retrospective study.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Since their domestication, horses have played an important role in human life. Today, horseback riding is widely practiced for recreational and therapeutic purposes. Despite this, horseback riding-related injuries remain an underreported public health problem in the emergency medicine literature. The aim of this study was to evaluate the injury patterns, management strategies, and clinical outcomes of patients presenting to the emergency department after falls from horses.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included patients who presented to the emergency department of Sancaktepe Martry Prof. Dr. Ilhan Varank Education and Research Hospital between 2019 and 2024 following falls from horses. Patient data were obtained from the hospital information system and Picture Archiving and Communication System. Demographic characteristics, injury location, treatment modality, length of hospital stay, and clinical outcomes were recorded and analyzed statistically.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 86 patients were included in the study, of whom 43 (50%) were male and 43 (50%) were female. The mean age was 34±12.1 years (range: 7-69 years). Eight patients (9.3%) were under 18 years of age, while 78 patients (90.7%) were adults. Eighteen patients (20.9%) required hospital admission, whereas 68 patients (79.1%) were managed on an outpatient basis in the emergency department. Injury severity was assessed using the Injury Severity Score, with a mean value of 7.6. The majority of patients had minor injuries. The most commonly injured body region was the upper extremity, observed in 39 patients (45.3%). Surgical intervention was required in 18 patients (20.9%). Pelvic and spinal injuries were significantly more common among female riders, whereas lower extremity injuries predominated among male riders (p<0.05). Five patients (5.8%) required post-operative intensive care. One patient with severe head trauma (Glasgow Coma Scale 5) who was not using protective equipment died during follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Horseback riding-related injuries frequently involve multiple organ systems and may present to the emergency department with varying levels of severity. Although many patients sustain high-energy trauma, most are managed within the scope of orthopedic and traumatology services, with a considerable proportion requiring surgical or conservative intervention. This study represents the first comprehensive evaluation in Turkey of patients presenting to the emergency department after falls from horses. Given the potential risk of severe injury and mortality, the absence of protective equipment in the fatal case suggests a possible role of safety measures; however, further studies are needed to better define their impact.

articles.title: Burnout and Related Occupational and Psychological Outcomes Among Emergency Nurses in Saudi Arabia: A Scoping Review.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To map primary Saudi studies reporting burnout, occupational fatigue, anxiety, depression, psychological distress, or sleep disturbance among emergency-department (ED) nurses.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Scoping review.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following PRISMA-ScR, PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL Complete, ProQuest Nursing & Allied Health and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on 15 September 2026 using PCC-based controlled vocabulary and free-text terms. Primary quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods studies (1 January 2015-15 September 2026) that meet the inclusion criteria were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardized form, resolving disagreements by discussion. Charted data covered design, setting, sample and ED-nurse denominator, outcome construct and instrument, scoring, nurse-specific results and associations. Synthesis was descriptive and grouped by construct; meta-analysis was not planned given heterogeneity in constructs, measures, thresholds and reporting.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The four sources yielded 1694 raw record instances; 15 Saudi ED-nurse records were included. Seven quantitative reports measured burnout, while two qualitative studies described burnout-related experiences. Other records examined fatigue, anxiety/depression, occupational stress, or secondary traumatic stress. Variation in measures, thresholds, sampling and reporting precluded meta-analysis or a defensible pooled estimate.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Evidence from selected Saudi emergency settings signals concerns across burnout and related outcomes, but limited geographic coverage and predominantly cross-sectional designs preclude national prevalence or causal conclusions. Distinguishing burnout from adjacent constructs is essential.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE
abstract.text: Nursing leaders should monitor constructs separately using validated tools and ED-nurse-specific denominators, and pair confidential support with organizational action on modifiable work conditions. Future multisite longitudinal and intervention studies should assess feasibility and outcomes before wider adoption.

articles.title: Geriatric Emergency Management Programs and Days at Home Among People Living With Dementia in Ontario.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: People living with dementia frequently present to emergency departments (EDs) and are at increased risk of hospitalization, institutionalization, and other adverse outcomes. Geriatric Emergency Management (GEM) programs are designed to improve emergency care for older adults, but their effectiveness among people living with dementia remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between attendance at an ED with an active GEM program and days alive and at home among older adults living with dementia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort of Ontario residents aged 65 years or older with identified dementia who had an index ED visit between April 1, 2021, and March 31, 2024. The exposure was attendance at an ED with an active GEM program.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 145,874 individuals, including 110,288 who presented to EDs with GEM programs and 35,586 who presented to EDs without GEM programs. The median age of the population was 81 years and 58.5% of participants were female. After propensity score overlap weighting and adjustment for facility characteristics, individuals who visited GEM EDs spent 7.5 (95% CI, 3.1-12.0) more days alive and at home during the following year than those who visited non-GEM EDs. Approximately half of this difference was attributable to fewer days spent in long-term care homes. Visits to GEM EDs were also associated with fewer subsequent ED visits, although index ED length of stay and hospital admission rates were higher.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Among older adults living with dementia, care in EDs with GEM programs was associated with more days alive at home over the following year. These findings support continued investment in GEM programs to promote aging at home and to delay institutionalization among people living with dementia.

articles.title: Characteristics of Emergency Department Visits by Adults With Down Syndrome: A Single-Institution Retrospective Perspective.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Down syndrome, also known as Trisomy 21, is the most common chromosomal abnormality causing intellectual disability. The life expectancy for people with Down syndrome has increased considerably over the last few decades, and many of these patients struggle with the transition from pediatric to adult medical care. There is currently no information on how adults with Down syndrome use emergency departments (EDs). The objective of this study was to describe visits by adult patients with Down syndrome to an academic medical center.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective chart review study of all adult patients (age ≥ 18 years) with Down syndrome who presented to The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center (OSUWMC) EDs from January 1, 2019 to December 31, 2023. Selected patient and visit characteristics were collected by chart review. This was a descriptive study with data presented as n and percentage.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 177 ED visits by 106 adults with Down syndrome during the study period. Most patients had a single ED visit (69.8%) and more than half the patients were under age 40 (52.9%). The most common chief complaints were abdominal pain (10.2%) and seizure (7.9%). The majority received laboratory testing (82.5%) and/or imaging (74.6%) This pattern was present across the age span. Most were discharged to place of residence (51.4%) but admission rates were higher (38.4%). Laboratory testing, imaging and admission rates were higher compared to local and national rates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This description of ED visits by adult patients with Down syndrome provides insight into common presenting complaints, testing patterns, disposition, and post-ED visits. Study data suggest that adult patients with Down syndrome may require different considerations when they present to adult EDs compared to a typical ED patient. Further studies are needed to generalize these results and identify ways to improve their ED care.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Haloperidol, Droperidol, and Ondansetron for Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) is an increasingly frequent emergency department (ED) presentation. Although ondansetron is commonly used, emerging evidence suggests haloperidol and droperidol may provide more effective symptom control. Robust comparative effectiveness data, particularly regarding short-term ED recidivism, remain limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network from 2014 to 2024. Adults presenting to the ED with vomiting-related and cannabis-related ICD-10 diagnoses who received haloperidol, droperidol, or ondansetron during the index encounter were included. Patients with alternative causes of vomiting or major confounding conditions were excluded. Propensity-score matching was performed for three pairwise comparisons: haloperidol versus ondansetron, droperidol versus ondansetron, and droperidol versus haloperidol. The primary outcome was 72-h ED recidivism. Secondary outcomes included 72-h hospital admission, 7-day ED recidivism, and coded adverse events. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling evaluated independent predictors of 72-h ED recidivism.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After matching, haloperidol was associated with lower 72-h ED recidivism compared with ondansetron (8.2% vs. 15.1%; OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.41-0.62; p < 0.0001). Droperidol was also associated with lower 72-h ED recidivism compared with ondansetron (7.4% vs. 14.0%; OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.32-0.76; p = 0.0014). Droperidol and haloperidol did not differ significantly in 72-h ED recidivism (7.5% vs. 9.8%; OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.47-1.20; p = 0.23). In the multivariable model, haloperidol (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.79) and droperidol (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.83) were independently associated with lower return risk, whereas ondansetron was not. Coded adverse events were rare across all groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this large multicenter cohort, haloperidol and droperidol were associated with lower short-term ED recidivism than ondansetron among adults meeting a suspected CHS phenotype. These findings support prospective studies evaluating haloperidol and droperidol for ED management of CHS, including optimal dosing, route, medication sequencing, discharge treatment, and safety monitoring.

articles.title: Trends and determinants of organ and tissue donation at a level I trauma centre in north India (2022-2025).
articles.journal_full: The Indian journal of medical research

abstract.text: Background and objectives Globally, India ranks the third highest for the number of organ transplants performed; however, its deceased organ donations remain limited. Despite numerous brain injury cases and potential brain-dead donors, the organ retrieval rates and donor conversions remain low across trauma centres. This study evaluated the donor pathway, conversion rates, and barriers to organ donation in a tertiary trauma centre. Methods We conducted a retrospective audit of prospectively collected data from potential deceased brain donors at a level I Trauma Centre from January 2022 - December 2025. Yearly trends in donor conversion, family consent, medical exclusion, organ yield, workflow timelines, and barriers to successful donations were assessed. Results Of 1575 hospital deaths, 805 (51.1%) were identified as potential donors. Total 148 (18.4%) progressed to brainstem death declaration; consent was obtained in 47 (31.7%) of these. A total of 43 patients proceeded to organ donation, yielding an overall donor conversion rate of 29% (which declined from 39.5% in 2022 to 16.1% in 2025 despite increased donor identification). Hemodynamic instability was the leading cause of medical exclusion, while family refusal accounted for most non-conversions after brainstem death declaration. A total of 187 organs and tissues were retrieved, with an overall mean yield of 4.35 per donor (2.5 organs and 1.84 tissues per donor). Kidneys (n=59) and corneas (n=64) were the most frequently retrieved, while thoracic organ retrieval remained limited (16 hearts and 4 lung donations). Interpretation and conclusions Our data showed that despite consistent donor identification, the donation and consent rates remained low. Hemodynamic instability was the major barrier to potential organ donation, suggesting that strengthening early donor stabilisation, structured counselling, faculty sensitisation, and donation after circulatory death programmes may improve conversion in organ yield. We recommend routine audits for course correction and to support the development of stronger donation programmes nationwide.

articles.title: Foodborne outbreak following a mass gathering in Karnataka, India: Epidemiological and environmental evidence implicating an uncooked food item.
articles.journal_full: The Indian journal of medical research

abstract.text: An outbreak of acute diarrhoeal disease followed a mass gathering in Shivamogga, Karnataka, in January 2023. We investigated the source. Of the 1,337 event attendees, 720 were interviewed and 268 met the case definition (attack rate 37%). The epidemic curve indicated a point-source outbreak with median incubation of 34 h. Shigella spp. were isolated from two stool samples. Water testing at the catering site showed faecal contamination and pipeline damage. Consumption of uncooked coconut chutney was strongly associated with the outbreak [Odds ratio (OR) 7.6, 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.5-16.4], suggesting a foodborne outbreak linked to contaminated water used in food preparation.

articles.title: Moving in Sand: Effects of Sex and Morphology on Performance in the Sandfish Skink (Scincus scincus).

abstract.text: An animal's morphology directly influences its ability to perform fundamental tasks, which can be vital to its survival and reproduction. This is especially true in harsh or extreme environments, like the shifting-sand desert of the Sahara. Additionally, sexes can differ in their morphology, performance, or in the relationship between morphology and performance, with implications for behaviors such as habitat selection, predator avoidance, and reproduction. Despite being common across a broad geographic range, little is known of the ecomorphology and sexual dimorphism of the sandfish skink (Scincus scincus). To investigate this, we first validated the uses of molecular sexing protocols and morphology (hemipene eversion) to identify the sex of our animals. We then tested for differences in body size, the multivariate morphological phenotype, and coloration between the sexes. While patterns generally suggested male bias in both body size and limb dimension in concordance with previous studies, these differences were not statistically significant. Additionally, we found several exceptions to the standard color-based sex assignment of these animals, especially for females. We then conducted an experiment to test how body size and dimensions affect performance at optimum temperatures. We quantified three different types of movement: sprinting on top of sand (used in hunting behavior), swimming under sand (an undulatory form of locomotion used in thermoregulation), and diving into sand (an important escape behavior). Overall, skinks with larger body sizes sprinted faster and swam faster through sand. Female skinks sprinted faster than male skinks even after accounting for differences in body size. Larger heads, wider bodies, and longer limbs were negatively correlated with swim speed. Diving performance exhibited the lowest among-individual variation, did not differ between the sexes, and was not dependent on body size or shape. Finally, we found no evidence of among-individual correlations in performance measures, suggesting each performance is independent of the others. Overall, this experiment provides insight into morphology-performance relationships across a number of ecologically important aspects of locomotion for a species inhabiting an extreme desert environment.

articles.title: Pain-Related Outcome Domains and Measures in Randomized Controlled Trials of Treatment for Acute Abdominal Pain: A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Acute abdominal pain frequently presents to emergency departments, yet outcome domains in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remain poorly characterized. This review identified pain-related domains and outcome measures used in RCTs on acute abdominal pain.

abstract.label: DATABASES AND DATA TREATMENT
abstract.text: This PRISMA-guided systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025630171). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for RCTs (January 2000-February 2025). Eligible studies included adult and paediatric patients with acute abdominal pain reporting pain assessment. Outcome domains extracted included pain intensity, rescue analgesia, adverse effects, pain interference, quality of life (QoL), and psychological function. Bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB2.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 826 records, 43 RCTs were included; eight included children. In adult trials, pain intensity was assessed using the visual analogue scale (n = 19) or the numeric rating scale (n = 15). Rescue analgesia (44%) and adverse effects (84%) were frequently reported. No study assessed pain interference or psychological function, and QoL was listed as an outcome in one trial. All were conducted in emergency settings, with short-term follow-up within the first hours.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pain assessment in acute abdominal pain RCTs is predominantly limited to intensity measures and short-term outcomes. While appropriate for immediate analgesic effects, this approach may be insufficient when broader treatment goals or longer follow-up are relevant. Context-specific outcome selection is needed, aligning domains with clinical purpose and time frame.

abstract.label: SIGNIFICANCE
abstract.text: RCTs on acute abdominal pain assess pain incompletely, focusing predominantly on intensity rather than broader domains such as pain interference and psychological function. None adhered to the INTEGRATE framework for pain assessment. This review provides the first systematic mapping of outcome domains in this area, offering a foundation for context-specific outcome selection aligned with what matters to patients.

articles.title: Association of Care Coordination and Discontinuity With Patterns of Care and Outcomes in Childhood Cancer Survivors With Multiple Chronic Conditions: A Report From the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Given the substantial chronic condition burden among adult survivors of childhood cancer, we explored associations between care coordination and discontinuity with patterns of care and health status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data from Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (CCSS) participants with multiple chronic conditions who completed the validated CC-MC measure of care coordination and discontinuity in 2022 were linked with data from 2019 to 2021 on emergency department [ED] visits, hospitalizations, risk-based survivorship care advice, recommended screenings, and health status (SF-36, Brief Symptom Inventory [BSI-18]). Independent variables included three CC-MC coordination summary scores: main provider (knowing the patient and coordinating their care), multiple provider (coordinating care within and across clinics), patient-provider partnership (explaining things, considering patient goals); and discontinuity (dichotomous). Adjusted generalized linear models estimated prevalence ratios (PR), rate ratios (RR), and beta coefficients.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants (n = 365) were mean age 48.2 years, 68.5% female, 90.1% non-Hispanic White. Better main provider (RR = 0.87; 95% CI: 0.77-0.99) and multiple provider (RR = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.80-0.90) scores were associated with less ED use; better multiple provider scores with fewer hospitalizations (RR = 0.88; 95% CI: 0.81-0.96); and better patient-provider partnership scores with receiving risk-based survivorship care advice (PR = 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.08). We found no consistent associations between CC-MC scores and recommended screening, though screening rates were generally high. All three CC-MC summary scores were associated with fewer BSI global severity score elevations (PR range: 0.62-0.84). Discontinuity was associated with more hospitalizations (RR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.03-2.51) and BSI global severity score elevations (PR = 4.20; 95% CI: 1.74-10.16).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Promoting care coordination across multiple providers and improving continuity may improve care and outcomes in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: When Misinformation Becomes a Clinical Risk for Emergency Nurses.

abstract.text: During disasters, social media serves as both a critical communication channel and a source of misinformation that can complicate emergency response. Although platforms allow rapid sharing of evacuation orders, shelter locations, and health guidance, they also enable false or misleading information to spread just as quickly. For emergency nurses, this misinformation has real clinical consequences. Patients may delay seeking care, refuse evidence-based treatments, arrive fearful or distrustful, or challenge clinical recommendations based on what they have seen online. These behaviors disrupt workflow, prolong triage, and increase conflict in already strained emergency departments. This article examines misinformation commonly encountered during disasters including false claims about treatment safety, evacuation guidance, hospital operations, and resource availability and outlines practical strategies emergency nurses can use to reduce harm, strengthen communication, and protect patient safety.

articles.title: Clinical Decision Rules and Reduction of Ankle X-Rays in Pediatric Population: An Intervention Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Ankle injuries are common in pediatric patients and have a low incidence of fractures. This study aimed to evaluate the implementation of a protocol based on clinical decision rules to reduce the number of radiographs requested during nursing triage, thereby decreasing radiation exposure, waiting times, and health care costs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A quasi-experimental pre- and postintervention study with nonequivalent groups was conducted. Patients aged 3 to 16 years presenting with ankle injuries to the emergency department were included. The number of radiographs requested before and after the protocol's implementation was compared. The protocol incorporated the Ottawa Ankle Rules and the Low-Risk Ankle Rule, which were applied during nursing triage and medical assessment. The absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction, and number needed to treat were calculated, along with the emergency department length of stay and associated economic savings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 252 patients were included (preintervention: 132 and postintervention: 120). Radiograph requests decreased significantly, with an absolute risk reduction of 46.81% (95% CI, 36.59%-57.03%), a relative risk reduction of 51.93% (95% CI, 40.57%-61.12%), and a number needed to treat of 2 (95% CI, 1-2). Interobserver agreement between nursing staff and physicians was good to very good (Cohen's kappa of 0.779 for Ottawa Ankle Rules and 0.825 for Low-Risk Ankle Rule).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The implementation of clinical decision rules by nursing staff significantly reduces radiograph requests in pediatric ankle injuries without compromising safety. This strategy reduces radiation exposure, health care costs, and emergency department length of stay.

articles.title: [Attendances at Landspitali (the National University Hospital of Iceland) due to e-scooter accidents, summers 2023-2025].

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Electric scooters have become a common means of transport in the Reykjavik area. A previous study from the summer of 2020 revealed that, on average, 1.6 individuals presented to the Emergency Department (ED) daily after an e-scooter accident. The aim of the current study was to gather data on the incidence, causes, severity of injuries, and changes between study years, due to the use of e-scooters in the Reykjavik area during the summers of 2023, 2024, and 2025.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Data were gathered from a standardised documentation of the location and cause of the accident, use of protective equipment, and of recreational drugs and alcohol. The study group consists of those presenting to the ED during the summer months, from the 1st of June until the 31st of August, in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Diagnosis and treatment data were gathered from hospital records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the study period, 513 presented to the ED for e-scooter injuries, on average 1.86/day but more frequently during the weekends. Median age was 30 years (range 6-85 years). Younger than 18 years of age were 118 (23%). A significant decrease in incidence was observed, from an average of 2.52 per day during the summer of 2023 to 1.47 per day during the summer of 2025. The number of injured children decreased by half. Of those 17 years and older, 138 (34%) reported having used alcohol or recreational drugs with no significant change during the study period. Half of the patients had upper extremity injuries, and 53.4% needed two or more healthcare visits or admission to the hospital because of the injuries.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite increased use of e-scooters in the area, a decline was found in the number of ED visits for e-scooter injuries but the injury rate is still high for this mode of transport.

articles.title: Perceived diagnostic and system-related barriers to timely referral and interfacility transfer of trauma patients in Namibia: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.journal_full: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Patient transfers aim to ensure continuity of care, but referral-transfer pathway processes are often time-consuming and encounter various delays. This study determined healthcare workers' perceptions of clinical and non-clinical factors contributing to delays in the transfer process of critically injured trauma patients from the Otjozondjupa District Hospitals to the Windhoek Referral Hospitals and explored mitigation strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2023 at three district hospitals, private and parastatal ambulance services in the Otjozondjupa region, Namibia. Healthcare workers employed in Emergency Centres and Prehospital Emergency Care Providers, working in the setting for 6 months or longer, were eligible to participate. We used convenience and snowball sampling.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 50 respondents, 64.0% (n = 32) worked in Emergency Centres. Thirty-nine (n = 39, 78.0%) perceived referral/transfer delays. Diagnostic imaging and medical procedures were perceived clinical factors contributing to delays. Non-clinical/system-related factors included bed, ambulance, and medical doctor availability, a lack of human resources and management protocols, and limited knowledge of existing policies and procedures. Suggested mitigating strategies centred on targeted training needs, improved resource allocation, and enhanced Information Technology systems.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Healthcare workers perceived diagnostic processes, stabilisation procedures, and system-related constraints as barriers to timely interfacility transfer of critically injured trauma patients. Improving time to definitive care may benefit critically injured trauma patients while easing pressure on facilities caring for other urgent patients. These findings may inform local reviews of trauma-transfer processes and support future prospective studies that measure actual transfer times and objectively confirmed causes of delay.
