articles.title: Digital pathways to self-harm: Modafinil-induced mania and AI-assisted operationalization of suicidal intent in a law student: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Modafinil is a wakefulness-promoting (eugeroic) agent increasingly used off-label for cognitive enhancement. Although generally regarded as having a favorable psychiatric safety profile, it can precipitate manic or hypomanic episodes in vulnerable individuals, and the boundary between a self-limited substance-induced episode and the unmasking of an underlying mood disorder is not always clear at presentation.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We report the case of a 20-year-old female law student admitted to the emergency unit after a suicide attempt by polypharmacy overdose during escalating off-label modafinil use. A notable feature was her use of an artificial intelligence (AI) conversational platform to inform about the preparation of the attempt: the AI did not generate her suicidal motivation but contributed to operationalizing an already-formed intent. The acute presentation was characterized by logorhoea, affective expansiveness, and behavioral disinhibition, initially consistent with a substance-induced manic episode. Over the three-month follow-up, however, subsyndromal hypomanic features persisted after discontinuation of modafinil and after withdrawal of a serotonergic antidepressant, while the patient was maintained on a mood stabilizer - raising the possibility that modafinil acted as a precipitant unmasking an underlying bipolar diathesis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case illustrates modafinil's potential to precipitate affective destabilization in a high-achieving young person under sustained academic pressure, and the difficulty of distinguishing a transient substance-induced episode from an emerging bipolar-spectrum disorder without longitudinal follow-up. It also highlights an emerging risk: the role of large language models (LLMs) in operationalizing - rather than originating - suicidal intent. The case underscores the need for careful psychiatric screening before prescribing wakefulness-promoting agents, for continued longitudinal monitoring, and for attention to patients' interactions with AI platforms during crisis assessment.

articles.title: The association of ABO Rh blood groups with 30-day mortality following traumatic injury - A retrospective observational study in the East of England.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: ABO and RhD antigens are expressed on the surface of red blood cells; ABO antigens are also expressed on the surface of endothelial and some epithelial cells. Associations between ABO blood groups and disease have been reported in numerous areas of medicine. Recently there have been conflicting reports of an association between blood group O and mortality following trauma, none of which examine a combination of ABO and RhD groups. The aim of our study was to identify associations between all ABO RhD groups and trauma mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis of trauma patients ≥ 16-years-old admitted to the East of England Major Trauma Centre, and who were included in the Trauma, Audit, & Research Network (TARN) database, 2016-2019. The primary outcome was a comparison of 30-day all-cause mortality between all eight ABO RhD groups. Secondary outcomes included injury pattern analysis on outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 4188 patients were included; median age 59.3 [IQR 39.0-77.9] years old, and 2634 (62.9%) were male. The median injury severity score was 19.0 [10.0-25.0]. 30-day mortality was 9.3%, and there were significant differences in mortality across groups (p = 0.0094). O negative was associated with greater 30-day mortality compared to all other seven ABO RhD groups combined: 15.1% vs 8.8%; relative risk (RR) 1.7 (95%CI 1.3-2.2), p = 0.0002.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this UK study we have demonstrated that blood group O negative is associated with a greater risk of 30-day all-cause mortality in undifferentiated trauma patients. Future trauma studies should consider including ABO RhD blood group as a baseline characteristic to ensure this does not confound results.

articles.title: Association between mechanical ventilation with positive end-expiratory pressure and outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: The effect of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) during intermittent positive pressure ventilation in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on outcome is unknown. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between the use of PEEP during cardiopulmonary resuscitation and clinical outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-centre observational cohort study using a retrospective analysis of data collected prospectively within a dedicated research registry of adult OHCA patients managed by a physician-staffed prehospital emergency medical team. All included patients were intubated and ventilated either with mechanical ventilation using PEEP or with manual ventilation without PEEP. Intratracheal pressure was continuously recorded via a catheter connected to a portable device, allowing objective verification of PEEP application and ventilation rate. The association between mechanical ventilation with PEEP use and clinical outcomes was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for relevant confounders.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 362 patients were included, with a median age of 65 years (54-79), of whom 250 (69.1%) were male. Median ventilation rate was 15 breaths/min (10-19). Of all patients, 149 (41.2%) achieved Return Of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC) and 31 (8.6%) survived to hospital discharge. The adjusted odds ratio (OR) of mechanical ventilation with PEEP for achieving ROSC was 1.58 (95% CI 1.01-2.50, p = 0.048). The unadjusted OR of mechanical ventilation with PEEP for survival to hospital discharge was 2.22 (95% CI 1.03-4.78; p = 0.037).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The use of mechanical ventilation with PEEP during CPR in OHCA patients was associated with higher likelihood of ROSC.

articles.title: Lumbopelvic fixation for high-energy sacral fractures and spinopelvic dissociation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of complications, unplanned revision and implant removal.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Secondary procedures after lumbopelvic fixation (LPF) include planned implant removal, removal for symptoms and revision for complications. Their differing indications, together with limited comparative evidence, complicate counselling and surgical planning.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420251036375) for comparative and single-arm studies (≥10 LPF patients). High-energy injuries and fragility fractures were considered separately. Random-effects models summarised complications, unplanned revision, implant removal and within-study comparisons of surgical approaches and fixation strategies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-five studies were included (22 high-energy, 3 fragility). Across 19 high-energy LPF cohorts (564 patients), pooled surgical-site infection was 9.3% (95% CI 6.1-14.1), implant loosening or failure was 5.3%, nonunion occurred in 4 of 389 patients (1.0%) and loss of reduction in 2 of 355. Pooled unplanned revision was 11.9% (95% CI 8.7-16.0; prediction interval 5.3-24.3), most often for infection or wound complications. Implant removal was 79.0% in routine-removal series and 17.3% in selective-removal series. Four studies compared minimally invasive and open LPF. Pooling three studies showed less blood loss with minimally invasive LPF (mean difference -271 mL, 95% CI -367 to -175) and shorter operative time (-51 min, -97 to -5); the operative-time association did not persist with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Infection (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.09-1.83) and revision (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.09-1.43) estimates were inconclusive. Four cohorts comparing LPF with posterior pelvic-ring fixation alone reported higher odds of revision after LPF (OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.63-9.60), with substantial potential for confounding by indication. Certainty was very low.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Nonunion and loss of reduction were infrequent after LPF, while unplanned revision most often involved infection or wound complications. Implant removal varied with institutional policy and warrants separate counselling. Minimally invasive LPF was associated with less blood loss, but comparative evidence remains insufficient to establish lower complication rates, equivalent mechanical outcomes or superiority of either fixation strategy.

articles.title: Layperson naloxone administration and subsequent emergency medical services care for opioid overdose.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Layperson-administered naloxone is increasingly common before emergency medical services (EMS) arrival. However, EMS care following naloxone administered by laypeople rather than trained responders remains poorly characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study used the 2023 National EMS Information System dataset and included 9-1-1 activations for individuals aged ≥ 16 years with an EMS impression of opioid overdose and documented naloxone administration before EMS arrival. Exposures were layperson-administered naloxone (LAN) or trained responder-administered naloxone (TRAN; e.g., police, firefighter). The primary outcome was subsequent EMS naloxone administration. Secondary outcomes included total number of EMS naloxone administrations, advanced airway intervention, cardiac arrest, and EMS transport. We used descriptive statistics, t-tests, and multivariable logistic regression estimating adjusted odds ratios (aOR).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 26,087 EMS activations, 8016 (30.7%) received LAN and 18,071 (69.3%) TRAN. Any subsequent EMS naloxone administration was less frequent following LAN (24.4% vs. 34.8%; P < .001); when EMS did administer additional naloxone, the mean number of administrations was slightly higher following LAN (mean difference 0.05, 95%CI 0.02-0.09; P = .001). Advanced airway attempts (1.6% vs. 1.4%, P = .160) and cardiac arrest (6.6% vs. 6.0%, P = .080) were uncommon. EMS transport occurred less often after LAN (79.4% vs. 84.4%, P < .001). In adjusted analyses, LAN was associated with lower odds of subsequent EMS naloxone administration (aOR 0.73; 95%CI 0.68-0.78) and EMS transport (aOR 0.78; 95%CI 0.73-0.84).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Layperson-administered naloxone was associated with less frequent EMS naloxone administration and lower rates of EMS transport. These findings support layperson overdose response while highlighting the need to better understand post-overdose care trajectories.

articles.title: Fracture characteristics in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus: Clinical significance of medial trochlear involvement.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus exhibit diverse fracture-extension patterns that are not fully characterized by conventional classification systems. The clinical significance of fracture extension into the medial or lateral column remains incompletely understood. This study investigated fracture-extension patterns beyond the conventional Dubberley classification and evaluated their associations with clinical outcomes and bone-related complications.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter retrospective study included surgically treated coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus with a minimum follow-up of 12 months at four affiliated institutions between 2012 and 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO/OTA and Dubberley systems. Computed tomography (CT) images were reviewed to assess medial trochlear involvement, lateral column involvement without posterior condylar comminution, and isolated trochlear fractures. Clinical outcomes included elbow range of motion (flexion, extension, and arc of motion) and postoperative complications. Univariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with bone-related complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 374 surgically treated distal humeral fractures, 35 coronal shear fractures were included in the final analysis. Medial trochlear involvement was identified in 8 fractures (23%) and was most frequently observed in Dubberley type 3 fractures. Patients with medial trochlear involvement had significantly greater loss of elbow extension at final follow-up than those without medial trochlear involvement (-29° vs. -16°, P = 0.042). Bone-related complications were more frequent in fractures with medial trochlear involvement than in those without (50% vs. 7%, P = 0.016). In univariate logistic regression analysis, medial trochlear involvement was significantly associated with bone-related complications (odds ratio, 12.5; 95% confidence interval, 1.69-92.3; P = 0.013). Neither the AO/OTA nor the Dubberley classification was significantly associated with bone-related complications.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Medial trochlear involvement was significantly associated with greater loss of elbow extension and bone-related complications at final follow-up in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus. Preoperative CT assessment of medial trochlear involvement may provide clinically useful information complementary to conventional fracture classification systems and may aid surgical planning.

articles.title: Global research on cricket injuries (1982-2025): A bibliometric analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cricket is one of the most widely played sports worldwide and carries a significant burden of musculoskeletal injuries, particularly among fast bowlers. Over the past four decades, research in cricket injury epidemiology, biomechanics, workload monitoring, and surveillance has expanded substantially.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global cricket injury research, identifying growth trends, influential publications, leading contributors, collaboration networks, and major thematic domains.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Publications from 1982 to 2025 were systematically analyzed using bibliometric indicators including annual growth, authorship productivity, institutional and country contributions, citation impact, total link strength (TLS), and co-authorship networks. The top 100 cited papers and the top 10 highly cited papers (HCPs) were examined in detail to identify landmark contributions and research priorities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A sharp rise in publications occurred after 2003, with nearly 90% of output produced in the last two decades. Australia, the United Kingdom, and South Africa led in productivity, citation impact, and collaborative link strength. The top 10 HCPs accounted for 10% of papers but 37.25% of total citations, underscoring concentrated scholarly influence. Fast bowlers consistently demonstrated the highest injury incidence, particularly lumbar spine and lower limb injuries. Workload spikes were strongly associated with increased injury risk, establishing load monitoring as a central preventive strategy. Biomechanical factors such as mixed bowling action, trunk rotation, and front-knee mechanics were linked to lumbar stress injuries. Standardized injury definitions and international consensus surveillance frameworks significantly improved research quality and comparability.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Cricket injury research has evolved into a mature, collaborative, and high-impact domain centered on fast bowling biomechanics, workload regulation, and surveillance standardization. Expanded global participation and integration of advanced analytics are essential for future injury prevention strategies.

articles.title: Discrepancies between radiography and magnetic resonance imaging in acute wrist trauma among women aged 50 years and older: A prospective exploratory study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objectives of the study are to describe traumatic wrist findings on conventional radiographs and supplemental magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in women aged 50 years or older with acute wrist trauma. The main focus was to describe discrepancies between radiography and MRI, including radiograph-negative MRI findings, additional or differently located fracture sites, and MRI characterization of intra-articular involvement.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, single-center exploratory paired imaging study included 50 women aged 50 years or older referred to the emergency department with acute wrist trauma and clinical suspicion of wrist fracture. All patients underwent standard wrist radiography followed by MRI within 3 h. Radiographs and MRI examinations were evaluated independently. MRI was used for comparison with radiography and not as an independent reference standard. Imaging findings were categorized as concordant findings, radiograph-negative MRI findings, additional MRI findings, or differences in fracture characterization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean patient age was 67.7 ± 11.5 years (range 50-95 years). Radiographs demonstrated traumatic abnormalities in 31 of 50 patients (62%), whereas MRI demonstrated traumatic findings in 40 of 50 patients (80%). Radiography and MRI were concordant for the presence or absence of any traumatic finding in 39 patients: 30 patients had traumatic findings on both modalities, and 9 patients had no traumatic finding on either modality. Discordant findings occurred in 11 patients, including 10 radiograph-negative MRI-positive cases and one radiograph-positive MRI-negative case. Radiograph-negative MRI-positive traumatic findings were present in 10 patients (20%) and included fractures, bone bruises, and soft-tissue injuries. MRI identified additional or differently located fractures in 9 patients (18%) and demonstrated intra-articular involvement or clearer intra- articular fracture characterization in 15 patients (30%). Six patients (12%) had scaphoid fractures on MRI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Supplemental MRI demonstrated additional traumatic findings and provided further fracture characterization compared with initial radiography in women aged 50 years or older with acute wrist trauma. The added value was mainly related to radiograph-negative MRI findings, additional fracture sites, and intra-articular involvement. These findings support the selective use of MRI as a supplemental imaging tool when radiographs are negative, equivocal, or insufficient for fracture characterization.

articles.title: Profile of motorcycle trauma in a referral hospital in Northeast Brazil.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to analyze the profile of motorcycle accident victims treated at Hospital Monsenhor Walfredo Gurgel, a trauma referral center in Rio Grande do Norte, between February and October 2024.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was an observational, retrospective, and descriptive study. Data regarding epidemiological profiles, mode of arrival, medical specialties involved, length of hospital stay, and clinical outcomes were extracted from electronic medical records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 7,176 recorded victims, there was a clear male predominance (75.52%, n=5,420), while females accounted for 24.47% (n=1,756). Analyzing victims aged 21-70 years, most cases occurred in the 21-30 age group (40.67%), followed by the 31-40 age group (28.66%). Most patients (71.27%) were admitted using specialized transport, including rural and state SAMU ambulances. General Surgery was the specialty most frequently involved in care (52.89%, n=3,178), followed by Orthopedics and Traumatology (36.98%), with Neurosurgery, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Neurology, and Urology accounting for smaller proportions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Motorcycle injuries predominantly affect young, economically active men aged 21-40 years, accentuating the need for preventive strategies to reduce the burden on health services and improve pre-hospital and in-hospital care.

articles.title: Hollow viscus injury (HVI) score in adult patients sustaining non-motor vehicle collision blunt trauma: A single-center retrospective validation study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Delayed diagnosis of hollow viscus injury (HVI) from blunt trauma (BT) carries increased morbidity. An HVI prediction tool (HVI Score), incorporating vital signs, physical examination, and computed tomography (CT) findings has been validated in patients injured by motor vehicle collision (MVC) with an abdominal seatbelt sign. This study investigated the HVI Score performance in patients with non-MVC blunt trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center study conducted between 2020 and 2024 included adult (>18-years-old) patients sustaining non-MVC BT who underwent CT imaging of the abdomen/pelvis prior to any abdominal operation. The primary outcome was operatively confirmed HVI. HVI Score model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve and by calibration (ratio of observed to expected events, calibration-in-the-large, and calibration slope).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 752 non-MVC BT patients admitted, 19 (2.5%) were high-risk (scores >10), 105 (14.0%) moderate-risk (scores 6-9), and 628 (83.5%) low-risk (scores <5), with 19 (2.5%) having an HVI. The high-risk cohort had increased rates of abdominal tenderness (36.8% vs. 27.6% vs. 12.1%) as well as increased CT findings of free fluid (100.0% vs. 89.5% vs. 6.1%), soft tissue contusion (73.7% vs. 46.7% vs. 28.8%), mesenteric stranding (36.8% vs. 21.0% vs.7.6%), mesenteric hematoma (42.1% vs. 13.3% vs. 7.8%), bowel wall thickening (47.4% vs. 5.7% vs. 3.3%), and pneumoperitoneum (26.3% vs. 1.9% vs. 0.0%) compared to moderate and low-risk patients (all p < 0.001). The HVI Score achieved an AUROC of 0.96 (CI 0.94-0.98). Observed events numbered 19 against 26 expected (observed-to-expected ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.47-1.15), with a calibration slope of 0.96 (95% CI 0.64-1.28). At the low-risk threshold, sensitivity and NPV were both 100%; at the high-risk threshold, specificity was 99% and PPV 47%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The HVI Score, which was originally validated for MVC patients with a seatbelt sign, had excellent performance in predicting HVI among patients with non-MVC BT.

abstract.label: SOCIAL MEDIA SUMMARY
abstract.text: The Hollow Viscus Injury (HVI) prediction score has excellent performance in predicting HVI among patients with non-MVC blunt abdominal trauma, thus extending its utility to all blunt trauma patients.

articles.title: Comparative trends of musculoskeletal injury in pickleball and tennis: An 11-year analysis of U.S. emergency department visits.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pickleball participation continues to surge, with many recreational tennis players transitioning to the sport due to perceived ease of play and social appeal. The aim of this study was to compare 11-year injury patterns between patients presenting to the Emergency Department (ED) for pickleball and tennis injuries.

abstract.label: HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: We hypothesized that (1) pickleball-related ED visits would increase over time while tennis-related visits would remain stable or decrease; (2) injury patterns would differ between sports by anatomical site, diagnosis, and mechanism; and (3) older adults would account for a higher proportion of fall-related injuries requiring hospital admission.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective comparative epidemiologic study LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III METHODS: National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) data between 2014 and 2024 were sorted for pickleball (product code 3235) and tennis (product code 3284). Cases were manually reviewed to confirm sport participation and exclude non-musculoskeletal injuries. Anatomical site, diagnosis, injury mechanism, treatment disposition, and date of ED visit were extracted. Group comparisons used t-tests and chi-square tests, and linear regression evaluated annual trends.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 4141 cases were included (pickleball n = 1442; National Estimates (NE) 80,553; tennis n = 2699; NE 110,480). Pickleball-related ED visits increased over time, while tennis-related visits remained stable. Pickleball players were older than tennis players (60.1 (SD 16.7) yr vs. 40.9 (SD 23.3) yr; p < 0.01), with individuals ≥ 65 years accounting for 52.1% of pickleball-related injuries. Wrist injuries were the most common in pickleball (17.0%) and ankle injuries were most common in tennis (18.3%). Fractures were more frequent in pickleball (43.1%), while sprains/strains were more common in tennis (46.4%, p < 0.01). Falls were the leading mechanism in both sports (Pickleball 52.2%, Tennis 33.8%). Pickleball injuries occurred most frequently in the Winter (30.3%) while tennis injuries occurred most frequently in Summer (29.1%). Hospital admissions were more frequent for pickleball players (7.8% vs 3.9%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The rapid rise in pickleball-related injuries necessitates proactive efforts in education, conditioning, and injury prevention to safeguard participants, particularly older adults.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: As participation in pickleball grows, especially among older adults, targeted conditioning, emphasizing neuromuscular control and safety education may help reduce injury rates.

articles.title: Use of multimedia patient education tools for adults and children in the emergency department: A scoping review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This scoping review was conducted to collate and characterize the published research literature on multimedia patient education tools used in emergency medicine (EM).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using PRISMA-ScR methodology, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and ERIC from database inception through March 2025. Included studies were conducted in an emergency care setting and evaluated a multimedia patient education tool. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts with consensus resolution. Data extraction focused on target patient population, tool modality, educational aim, and outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1401 studies screened, 96 met inclusion criteria. The literature was dominated by video-based interventions (91%), with minimal representation of interactive applications or other modalities. Adult patients were most frequently targeted, followed by caregivers of pediatric patients. Educational aims included discharge or presenting concern-specific education (51%), public health intervention (20%), general medical knowledge (13%), informed consent (6%), public safety (5%), patient experience (4%), and other aims (1%). Among included studies, the outcomes assessed were patient/caregiver knowledge acquisition (52% of studies), clinical outcomes (28%), patient satisfaction with tool (27%), acceptance of a public health intervention (9%), patient satisfaction with the ED visit (4%), desire to change behaviors (4%), and utilization of tool (1%). Outcome improvements were reported in patient satisfaction (85%), knowledge acquisition (94%), and acceptance of public health interventions (89%). In contrast, only 56% of studies assessing clinical outcomes demonstrated benefit. Few studies addressed implementation, workflow integration, sustainability, or equity considerations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Multimedia patient education research in emergency medicine is dominated by video-based interventions and primarily focuses on discharge education, presenting concern-specific education, and public health interventions.

abstract.label: PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: These findings provide a foundation for future research, which would benefit from expanding the range of multimedia modalities studied and addressing implementation, workflow integration, sustainability, and equity to inform effective integration into emergency care.

articles.title: Machine learning models with SHAP explanations for predicting neurosurgical intervention and six month functional outcome after traumatic brain injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Admission information can help describe surgical treatment and subsequent functional outcomes following traumatic brain injury (TBI). We developed interpretable machine learning models to address these two tasks.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 673 adults evaluated at a single center between December 2018 and December 2023. Outcomes recorded were neurosurgical intervention and six-month Glasgow Outcome Scale status, dichotomized as favorable (scores 4-5) or unfavorable (scores 1-3). Patients were randomly allocated to training and internal validation sets in a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select predictors for the XGBoost and random forest models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, along with classification and prediction error metrics, was employed for model evaluation. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret model predictions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 75 unfavorable outcomes and 66 surgical interventions. The reported validation accuracy for XGBoost was 87.56% for predicting functional outcomes and 95.02% for surgical interventions. Validation Brier scores were 0.083 and 0.035, respectively. The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), pupillary light reflex, and blood glucose levels contributed significantly to functional outcome predictions, while GCS, fibrinogen, and white blood cell count were key predictors for surgical interventions. Interpretation of threshold-dependent measures is limited by class imbalance and incomplete specification of outcome coding.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The models combined routinely collected admission variables to characterize the treatment received and functional outcomes in a selected traumatic brain injury (TBI) cohort. These findings require confirmation through analysis replication and independent validation before they can be applied clinically.

articles.title: Wild spine infections: Long-term outcomes and surgical strategies in refractory postoperative spinal infections.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Most postoperative spinal infections resolve with timely debridement and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy. A minority, however, progress to persistent infection with osseous destruction, mechanical instability, and repeated surgical failure. Evidence-based strategies for managing this high-risk salvage population remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term clinical, neurological, and radiological outcomes of patients undergoing definitive reconstructive surgery after multiple failed revision procedures for refractory postoperative spinal infection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent two or more revision surgeries for refractory postoperative spinal infection with associated instability or deformity. Clinical outcomes were assessed with the visual analog scale (VAS), Oswestry disability index (ODI), and Frankel neurological grade; radiological outcomes focused on sagittal alignment. All patients underwent aggressive debridement followed by posterior, anterior, or combined reconstruction, with adjunctive antimicrobial therapy and hyperbaric oxygen. Given the limited sample size, statistical analyses were considered hypothesis-generating.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirteen patients (mean age, 47.7 years) with a mean follow-up of 64 months and a mean of 4.9 prior spinal surgeries were included. Mean VAS score decreased from 9.5 preoperatively to 1.7 at 1 year (p < 0.001), and mean ODI improved from 62.4 to 19.2 (p < 0.001). Neurological improvement occurred in 53.8% of patients, with complete recovery in 30.8%. Sagittal segmental alignment improved significantly after surgery, but the magnitude of radiological correction did not correlate with pain or functional outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In refractory postoperative spinal infection requiring salvage reconstruction, restoration of mechanical stability, rather than radiological correction, is the principal determinant of clinical and neurological recovery. Early recognition and timely definitive reconstruction may improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Unintentional suffocation emergencies associated with autism and common Co-occurring diagnoses.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: People with autism are at heightened risk of specific injuries and injury-related death. As autism prevalence rises, epidemiologic data describing specific injuries, such as suffocation, across the lifespan are essential for prevention efforts. We describe the risk of unintentional suffocation-related events associated with autism and common co-occurring diagnoses among people treated in United States (US) emergency departments (EDs).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using a repeated cross-sectional study design, we analyzed data from the 2016-2021 Nationwide Emergency Department Sample (NEDS), the largest US all-payer ED visit claims database. Using ICD-10-CM codes, children ≥ 1 year and adults diagnosed with autism, intellectual disability (ID), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and Alzheimer's disease and related dementia (ADRD) were identified and evaluated. Weighted multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of unintentional suffocation-related ED visits in persons with and without autism, ID, ADHD, and ADRD. Each model was adjusted for the other conditions, age, sex, urbanicity, and payor.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The 2016-2021 NEDS recorded a weighted total of 803,777,608 ED visits; of these, 1,012,210 (0.13%) were related to unintentional suffocation. Unintentional suffocation accounted for 0.35% of ED visits in patients with autism, 0.67% of ED visits in patients with a diagnosis of ID, 0.07% of ED visits in patients with a diagnosis of ADHD, and 0.34% of ED visits in patients with a diagnosis of ADRD. The odds of unintentional suffocation were increased 75% for patients with autism (aOR = 1.75; 95% CI: 1.65, 1.86), 556% for patients with ID (aOR = 6.56; 95% CI: 6.2, 6.94), 44% for patients with ADHD (aOR = 1.44; 95% CI: 1.35, 1.53), and 106% for patients with ADRD (aOR = 2.06; 95% CI: 2.01, 2.12). Across the lifespan, unintentional suffocation accounted for a larger proportion of ED visits among autistic than non-autistic patients.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Children and adults with autism have a significantly increased odds of unintentional suffocation requiring emergency care. ID, ADHD, and ADRD, diagnoses that often co-occur with autism, also have increased odds of unintentional suffocation, with intellectual disability conferring the greatest risk.

articles.title: Assessing Swedish guidelines for prehospital bleeding control: a cross-sectional appraisal using AGREE II.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High-quality clinical practice guidelines are essential for safe and consistent prehospital bleeding control, particularly in settings with variable geography and transport times. This study appraised the methodological quality of Swedish regional prehospital guidelines for traumatic external haemorrhage using the AGREE II instrument.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study included clinical practice guidelines requested from all 21 Swedish healthcare regions. Guideline quality was assessed independently by two appraisers using AGREE II, which evaluates 23 items across six domains. Domain scores were calculated as percentages of the maximum possible score.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Complete responses were obtained from 15 of 21 regions. Overall methodological quality was low across the included guidelines. The highest median domain score was observed for clarity of presentation, whereas rigour of development, stakeholder involvement, applicability, and editorial independence scored poorly. Most guidelines lacked explicit descriptions of evidence search strategies, criteria for selecting evidence, links between recommendations and supporting evidence, update procedures, and declarations of editorial independence.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Swedish regional prehospital guidelines for traumatic external bleeding control showed limited methodological quality when assessed using AGREE II. Future guideline development should prioritise transparent evidence linkage, multidisciplinary stakeholder involvement, clear implementation considerations, scheduled updating, and adaptation to regional differences in transport and evacuation times.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Geography matters: Variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Geodemographic factors create divergent clinical patterns between urban and rural settings. Level-II trauma centers are a vital trauma-care infrastructure for both urban and rural communities. This study compares neck trauma patterns, resource utilization, and outcomes at these distinct geodemographic nodes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis (2014-2024) of neck trauma at an urban center (UC, n = 65) and a rural center (RC, n = 60). Demographics, mechanism, treatments, interventions, and outcomes were analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: RC patients sustained more blunt, transport-related multisystem trauma with higher ISS. UC patients predominantly presented with localized penetrating injuries. Rural patients had higher ICU admission rates, longer ICU stays, more transfers to level-I centers yet underwent fewer operative interventions, invasive airway procedures, and CT angiogrophy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: There are significant variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers. An "intervention paradox" exists were rural centers stabilize high-severity blunt trauma for transfer, while urban centers provide definitive care for penetrating wounds. These findings necessitate geodemographically tailored protocols. Understanding geodemographic variations is a critical aspect of optimizing trauma systems.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: II Retrospective cohort.

articles.title: Multidomain progression phenotypes in Parkinson's disease: Five-year trajectories in the COPPADIS cohort.

abstract.text: Parkinson's disease (PD) progression is heterogeneous and is incompletely represented by single-domain outcomes. We identified multidomain progression phenotypes over five years in the prospective multicenter COPPADIS cohort and examined baseline predictors and external clinical validity. Among 694 participants with PD, 497 with sufficient longitudinal data were analyzed across motor severity, motor complications, non-motor burden, cognition, functional independence, and health-related quality of life. Individual annual slopes were standardized and directionally harmonized; Gaussian mixture modeling identified progression classes. Healthy controls (n = 207) provided a longitudinal reference. Two classes were supported by Bayesian information criterion and clinical parsimony: slow/relatively resilient (n = 319, 64.2%) and accelerated multidomain progression (n = 178, 35.8%). Accelerated progressors worsened significantly faster in all six domains. Baseline freezing-of-gait severity was the strongest independent marker of accelerated progression (OR 1.58 per SD, 95% CI 1.22-2.06), followed by higher levodopa-equivalent daily dose (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.77). Compared with healthy controls, accelerated progressors showed excess cognitive decline and worsening depressive symptoms and fatigue, whereas the slow/resilient group showed no significant control-referenced differences after multiplicity correction. Accelerated progression was also associated with first hospitalization (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.16-2.42), emergency-department attendance (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.08-1.83), and incident falls (HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.56-3.08). Five-year PD progression segregates into clinically meaningful multidomain phenotypes with distinct prognostic profiles.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection for anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome: A case series.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome (ACNES) is an uncommon, non-emergent cause of chronic abdominal wall pain arising from entrapment of the terminal branches of the T7-T12 intercostal nerves at the anterior rectus sheath. It is usually recognized only after laboratory and imaging studies have excluded intra-abdominal causes, often after repeated evaluations. Prior abdominal surgery is a recognized risk factor due to fascial scarring. Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection with 5% dextrose in water (D5W) and dilute lidocaine has been described in case reports as a minimally invasive treatment that may relieve pain and release the entrapped nerve. We present two patients who developed post-surgical ACNES following laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and laparoscopic cholecystectomy, respectively. Each presented to the ED with severe abdominal wall pain (NRS 9/10 and 10/10) and negative intra-abdominal workup. Both patients met diagnostic criteria including positive Carnett's sign, positive pinch test, and >90% pain reduction after ultrasound-guided hydrodissection. On chart review, pain relief was sustained at 6 weeks (Case 1) and 4 weeks (Case 2), and neither patient received other treatment after discharge. In these selected patients, bedside ultrasound-guided hydrodissection was feasible and was followed by rapid pain relief. Prospective, comparative studies are needed to establish its place within the ACNES treatment algorithm and to assess durability beyond the short-term follow-up reported here.

articles.title: Multiple Organ Failure Secondary to Pancreatitis Due to Biliary Ascariasis in a Young Patient: A Case Report on the Importance of a Good Anamnesis.

abstract.text: Biliary ascariasis is an uncommon trigger of acute abdomen in endemic areas that can lead to severe biliary obstruction and acute pancreatitis. In low-resource settings, self-medication prior to presentation can create diagnostic distractors, confounding the clinical picture with drug-induced liver injury (DILI). A 22-year-old male from rural Honduras presented in refractory shock (BP 60/40 mmHg), hepatic encephalopathy (GCS 6), jaundice, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding following the massive ingestion of analgesics and herbal extracts. Laboratory findings demonstrated severe hepatic dysfunction (AST 12,750 U/L, ALT 13,150 U/L, total bilirubin 6.7 mg/dL, INR 3.53), acute kidney injury (creatinine 5.04 mg/dL), and rhabdomyolysis. Initial supportive management targeted suspected fulminant drug-induced hepatitis. Subsequent targeted anamnesis on day 7 identified a pre-hospital history of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with antalgic positioning. Re-evaluation of day 3 diagnostics revealed a serum lipase of 905 U/L and abdominal ultrasonography demonstrating tubular, "railway-track" hyperechoic images within the common bile duct, confirming severe acute pancreatitis secondary to biliary ascariasis overlapping with acute DILI. The patient was managed conservatively with hemodynamic support, blood products, and hemodialysis. Spontaneous oral expulsion of Ascaris parasites occurred during the acute phase, with follow-up ultrasonography confirming biliary clearance. Organ function gradually improved, and the patient was discharged with residual organ sequelae requiring outpatient surveillance. Severe acute pancreatitis due to biliary ascariasis can co-exist with or be masked by drug-induced hepatic toxicity. Clinicians in endemic regions must maintain a high index of suspicion for mechanical parasitic obstruction, using systematic anamnesis and pancreatic enzyme evaluation to prevent diagnostic anchoring biases during critical organ failure management.

articles.title: Limb preservation and optimization: A whole-patient approach to comprehensive care after catastrophic extremity injuries.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to describe the Limb Preservation and Optimization Center's (LPOC) components and mechanisms in treating catastrophic extremity injuries and report the initial patient demographics, indications, and outcomes using data from an established registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective observational study was performed including all patients entered in the LPOC registry since January 1, 2014. Patient demographics, injury types and treatments, and outcomes, including functional outcomes. Descriptive statistics were calculated to determine proportions, means, standard deviations, and ranges.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 992 patients were included with a mean final follow-up of 20.5 months (SD:22.1, range 0-114); 178 (17.9%) underwent an amputation. Of those who reported RTW, 164 patients (71.6%) reporting RTW at full capacity. Lower extremity injuries were most common (74.9%). Demographic, health insurance, living setting, and presentation variables were similar among LPOC patients. Fractures and soft tissue injuries predominated across all injury categories with fracture fixation and wound coverage treatments most common. Upper extremity joint injuries and all types of combined injuries were associated with the highest reoperation rates. Treatment failure rates ranged from 11% to 100% with fracture and bone-related injuries being associated with the most favorable outcomes across categories.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Fractures and soft tissue injuries were the primary types of problems affecting all patients utilizing the LPOC. Fracture fixation and wound coverage treatments were the most performed procedures. Return to the operating room to address the limb preservation and optimization goal was extremely common across categories such that patients may expect at least 4 reoperations. Patients return to some type of work 75-88%. Treatment failure rates varied from 11% to 100%, with fracture and bone-related injuries being associated with the most favorable outcomes across categories. Overall, the results are encouraging and will help shape care in these patients.

articles.title: Performance of the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway prehospital triage system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates: a quality-control study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Accurate identification is one of the cornerstones of prehospital care for patients with suspected acute ischaemic stroke (AIS). In the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway triage system, emergency medical service (EMS) providers use dedicated criteria to identify acute reperfusion candidates and call a coordinated medical team (CMT, including a neurologist and an emergency physician), which can activate the stroke code pathway. The objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of the system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective single-centre quality-control study conducted in a Swiss university-based stroke centre, from 1 January 2019 to 31 May 2022. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥18 years, for whom the EMS called the CMT or patients with AIS eligible for acute reperfusion managed by the EMS. The main outcomes were the performance of both the EMS and the CMT in detecting AIS patients eligible for acute reperfusion, as assessed through their respective under- and overtriage rates. A secondary outcome was the identification of alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1071 patients included, the EMS phone-contacted the CMT for 937 (87.5%) of them. Among the 1071 patients, 440 (41%) had an AIS eligible for reperfusion. The system's undertriage rate was 30% (133 patients without stroke pathway activation among the 440 patients with an AIS eligible for acute reperfusion). The undertriage rates were 21% for the EMS and 11% for the CMT. The overtriage rates were 63% for the EMS and 57% for the CMT. The main alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients were seizures (14%), intracranial haemorrhages (9.9%) and functional disorders (6.5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Undertriage and overtriage rates were relatively high, but both were reduced by the CMT call, highlighting the added value of a second expert assessment step, with a higher level of expertise. Concerning overtriage, a better prehospital identification of alternative diagnoses, such as seizures or functional disorders, could help to better classify our patients.

articles.title: Implementation of a heat-responsive care management initiative for Medicare advantage members residing across the United States.
articles.journal_full: The journal of climate change and health

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Extreme heat events are increasing in frequency and intensity and disproportionally affect older adults and individuals with chronic conditions.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective evaluation of a quality improvement initiative among care‑managed Medicare Advantage members of a U.S.-based payer randomly assigned to standard or enhanced outreach. Extreme heat forecasts were reviewed weekly to identify members in affected counties for outreach. Standard outreach involved routine nurse‑led telephonic care management. Enhanced outreach added brief heat‑specific education tailored to clinical risks. Outcomes included implementation measures and exploratory emergency department (ED) and inpatient admissions 30 days before and after heat‑triggered identification.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 3,978 older adults (mean age: 75±9 y; 58% women) with high chronic disease burden. Standard care management outreach was delivered to 88.3% (3,514/3,978) of identified members, with no between-group differences (standard: 88.7% vs enhanced: 88.0%; P=0.53), demonstrating high fidelity. Engagement among outreached members was similar (standard: 86.5% vs enhanced: 86.7%; P=0.76). Heat-specific outreach was delivered to 17.3% of members assigned to enhanced outreach, with 79.5% engagement; limited crossover occurred in the standard group (2.9% outreached). ED visits and inpatient admissions declined modestly in both groups, with differences-in-difference estimates of -25 ED visits (95% confidence interval [CI]: -46 to 13; P=0.198) and -7 inpatient visits (95% CI: -44 to 46; P=0.84) per 1,000 members.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Heat‑responsive outreach was feasibly integrated into existing care management workflows while maintaining routine delivery and engagement. Future work should refine reach to evaluate clinical impact.

articles.title: A retrospective assessment of intubation prior to burn center arrival.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pre-burn center intubation is frequently performed in burn patients with suspected inhalation injury because of concern for progressive airway edema. However, contemporary studies suggest that many of these intubations may be unnecessary. We evaluated factors associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation following pre-burn center intubation in burn-injured patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of burn patients admitted to a single regional burn center from July 1, 2015, to June 30, 2023 who were intubated in the field or at referring facilities prior to arrival. Patients intubated through tracheostomy were excluded. Patients were stratified by duration of post-admission mechanical ventilation. Demographics, burn characteristics, inhalation injury findings, and documented intubation criteria were analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression identified factors associated with prolonged ventilation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 306 patients who met inclusion criteria, 147 (48%) were extubated within 24 h of admission. Patients requiring over 24 h of ventilation had larger burns, more inhalation injuries, longer hospital length of stay, and higher rates of ventilator-associated pneumonia and sepsis. Traditional findings such as singed facial hair, soot in the oropharynx, and suspected smoke inhalation poorly discriminated prolonged ventilator needs. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that indoor fire mechanism (OR 1.98, p = 0.004), signs of respiratory distress (OR 1.98, p = 0.008), and anticipated transfer of a patient with major burn without qualified medical professional to intubate en route (OR 2.69, p < 0.001) were associated with longer ventilation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our data suggests that physiology-based indicators of respiratory compromise may be more effective than traditional physical exam findings in optimizing airway management strategies before transfer to a burn center.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and comparison of clinical outcomes between conservative and surgical treatment for rib fractures in South China: A 10‑year retrospective cohort study of 4085 cases with propensity score‑matching analysis.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To systematically describe the epidemiological characteristics of rib fractures in South China and compare the clinical characteristics, hospital stay, and total costs between patients receiving conservative versus surgical treatment, thereby providing evidence‑based support for clinical decision‑making and public health prevention.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis was performed on 4085 hospitalized patients with rib fractures admitted to the Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Southern Medical University between January 2014 and December 2023. Data on gender, age, injury mechanism, fracture type, complications, blood group, and occupational distribution were collected. A subgroup analysis comparing conservative (n = 586) versus surgical treatment (n = 137) was conducted among 723 patients admitted between January 2021 and December 2023. Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics between the two groups, and differences in hospital stay, total costs, and injury mechanisms were compared.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: (1) Epidemiological characteristics: Of the 4085 patients, 68.13% (2783/4085) were male, and the 41-60 year age group accounted for the highest proportion (50.35%). Autumn and winter were the peak seasons for injury (54.71%). Traffic accidents were the leading cause of injury (51.18%), followed by falls (21.82%) and height‑related falls (19.13%). Multiple fractures predominated (75.52%). The most common complication was pulmonary contusion (45.14%), followed by traumatic pneumothorax/hemothorax/hemopneumothorax/pleural effusion (40.02%). Among occupations, freelancers were the largest group (34.37%), followed by farmers (23.18%). Blood group O was the most prevalent (42.15%), while blood group B was the least common (5.55%, P < 0.001), suggesting that blood group O may be a potential risk factor for rib fractures. (2) Comparison of treatment modalities: The conservative group had a significantly shorter hospital stay than the surgical group [3 (2-6) days vs. 17 (13-26) days, P < 0.001] and significantly lower total costs [5879 (2570-8877) RMB vs. 69,588 (54,499-89,845) RMB, P < 0.001]. The distribution of injury mechanisms differed significantly between the two groups (P < 0.001): the conservative group was mainly injured by falls/slips (44.4%), whereas the surgical group was mainly injured by height‑related falls/ground‑level falls (30.7%). The proportion of concomitant hemopneumothorax was higher in the surgical group than in the conservative group (21.9% vs. 3.4%, P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Based on a large sample of 4085 cases, this study is the first to systematically delineate the full epidemiological profile of rib fractures in South China, with a sample size more than ten times larger than the previous largest regional report. The results indicate that middle‑aged males, freelancers, and farmers are high‑risk populations, with traffic accidents and multiple fractures being predominant, and a unique autumn peak seasonal pattern in South China is reported for the first time. Treatment strategies should be tailored according to injury mechanism and fracture severity. The novel association between blood group O and increased rib fracture risk, reported here for the first time, provides a new perspective for precision prevention; the potential mechanism may involve impaired hemostatic response due to lower baseline levels of von Willebrand factor and factor VIII in individuals with blood group O.

articles.title: Does greater orthoplastic integration reduce deep infection after open tibial fracture? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Combined orthoplastic management of open tibial fractures is widely recommended, but existing evidence has not quantified whether the degree of care-pathway integration, beyond a binary orthoplastic-versus-orthopaedic distinction, is associated with a graded difference in outcome. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified deep infection and secondary outcome rates across four care-pathway models of increasing team continuity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and grey literature were searched in collaboration with a specialist medical librarian. Studies were classified into four care-pathway groups: Group 1, single-setting simultaneous fixation and soft tissue coverage; Group 2, staged care with continuous orthoplastic team involvement; Group 3, discontinuous or delayed plastic surgical involvement; Group 4, purely orthopaedic management. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled deep infection, limb salvage, reoperation, and non-union rates per group. Comparative meta-analyses used genuine within-study comparator arms. Confounding was assessed via meta-regression and subgroup analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-eight studies (81 classified arms) were included. Pooled deep infection rates rose progressively with decreasing care-pathway integration: 8% (95% CI 5-12%) in Group 1, 16% (9-24%) in Group 2, 28% (11-49%) in Group 3, and 37% (25-50%) in Group 4. A similar gradient was observed for non-union (4-26% across groups). Limb salvage was near-universal (94-99%) and did not discriminate between pathways. Leave-one-out and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness for Groups 1, 2, and 4; Group 3's estimate was substantially influenced by a single Critical-risk-of-bias study, with deep infection rates attenuating from 28% to 23% on exclusion. No significant publication bias was detected. Certainty of evidence, per GRADE, was Very Low for majority of the pooled estimates, reflecting serious risk of bias and inconsistency, and Low where heterogeneity was minimal.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Progressive care-pathway integration is associated with a consistent, graded reduction in deep infection and non-union risk following open tibial fracture, independent of injury mechanism. These findings support continued investment in combined orthoplastic care, including partial integration models where single-setting surgery is not achievable.

articles.title: Deaths in correctional custody: A six-year autopsy-based medico-legal study of 365 cases.
articles.journal_full: Journal of forensic and legal medicine

abstract.text: Deaths during correctional custody require independent medico-legal investigation because they involve healthcare, institutional accountability, and public oversight. This study aimed to characterize mortality patterns and medico-legal features among pre-trial detainees and sentenced prisoners using a large autopsy-based series from Türkiye. We retrospectively reviewed all eligible deaths investigated at the Istanbul Morgue Department between January 2019 and December 2024. The study included individuals who remained legally in correctional custody at the time of death, including those who died during hospital care after transfer. Demographic characteristics, autopsy findings, ancillary examination results, causes and manners of death, and reported locations of death were evaluated. All 365 cases underwent complete autopsy, histopathological examination, and toxicological analysis. The mean age was 50.0 ± 14.5 years, and 95.6% of the deceased were male. Natural deaths accounted for 88.2% of cases, with cardiovascular (41.3%), respiratory (14.8%), and neoplastic diseases (12.6%) representing the leading causes. Unnatural deaths accounted for 11.8%, and hanging was the most frequent mechanism (9.6%). Cardiovascular mortality increased significantly with age (p = 0.001), whereas deaths due to hanging decreased across older age groups (p < 0.001). Deaths were most commonly reported from intensive care units and emergency departments. Mortality during correctional custody was therefore dominated by natural disease, with distinct age-related patterns. Systematic autopsy-based investigation remains essential for accurate classification and transparent review of these deaths.

articles.title: Current Use and Practice of Opioids and Opiophobia in Modern Medicine: A Structured Narrative Review.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Opioids remain indispensable analgesics for acute, cancer-related, and selected chronic pain, yet their use is increasingly constrained by the opioid crisis and by opiophobia, an excessive, often irrational fear of opioid prescribing and use. This review synthesises evidence on opioid pharmacology, clinical applications, adverse effects, and opiophobia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This structured narrative review followed the SANRA criteria; PRISMA and PRISMA-ScR frameworks were not applied. Five databases (Google Scholar, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE; 2010-2026) were searched, prioritising systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomised trials, and guidelines. Sixty-nine sources were synthesised.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Opioids act mainly via μ-opioid receptors, suppressing ascending nociceptive transmission and enhancing descending inhibition. Agents differ in potency, onset, duration, metabolism, and adverse-effect profiles. Constipation, nausea, and sedation are common; respiratory depression, although uncommon at titrated doses, is the most serious hazard. Opiophobic attitudes were reported in up to 80.2% of emergency physicians, and up to 64.4% of cancer patients held extreme addiction concerns. The pooled prevalence of opioid use disorder or dependence during long-term opioid therapy for chronic non-cancer pain was 9.3% (95% CI 5.7-14.8%).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Attitudinal barriers, rather than pharmacological limitations alone, drive undertreatment of pain, and regulatory overcorrection after the opioid crisis has created a secondary burden of inadequate analgesia. Risk stratification, multimodal analgesia, and structured monitoring can limit opioid exposure while preserving effective analgesia.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Opioids remain effective and manageable under appropriate supervision. Balanced, evidence-based prescribing frameworks, combined with prescriber and patient education, are essential to reduce harm from both opioid misuse and inadequate analgesia.

articles.title: Impact of the provider-in-triage model on computed tomography and ultrasound imaging in renal colic.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Physician-in-Triage (PIT) models may influence diagnostic imaging decisions in the emergency department (ED). We evaluated the association between PIT exposure and imaging utilization among patients with renal colic and examined the influence of physician ultrasound training on imaging selection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with an ED diagnosis of renal colic at a single tertiary ED from January 2024 through December 2025. A prespecified lower-risk subgroup included patients aged <51 years with prior nephrolithiasis, no infection, and normal creatinine. The primary exposure was PIT evaluation. Outcomes included computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis (CTAP), point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), and radiology-performed renal ultrasound (RUS) utilization. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between PIT exposure and each imaging outcome after adjustment for age, gender, emergency severity index, admission, and race.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1041 patients, 596 (57.3%) were exposed to PIT. CTAP utilization was higher among PIT-exposed patients than non-PIT patients (72.9% vs 66.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.85). PIT exposure was associated with lower POCUS utilization (10.3% vs 18.6%; aOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34-0.70), while RUS utilization was similar (10.1% vs 9.0%; aOR 1.17, 95% CI 0.76-1.79). Overall ultrasound utilization (POCUS or RUS) was also lower among PIT-exposed patients (20.1% vs 26.7%; aOR 0.69, 95% CI 0.51-0.93). In the lower-risk subgroup, PIT exposure remained associated with greater CTAP utilization (63.6% vs 48.1%, p = 0.028) and lower POCUS utilization (14.4% vs 30.4%, p = 0.008). Ultrasound-trained attendings used CTAP less frequently than non-ultrasound-trained attendings (57.8% vs 71.8%; aOR for non-ultrasound-trained physicians 1.86, 95% CI 1.18-2.93).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PIT exposure was associated with greater CTAP and lower ultrasound utilization in patients with renal colic, including among a prespecified lower-risk cohort. Ultrasound-trained physicians used ultrasound more frequently and CTAP less frequently in renal colic patients.

articles.title: Geographic disparities in fall-related emergency department visits among older adults in Korea: a nationwide time-series analysis and projection study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Falls impose a mounting burden on emergency care systems in ageing societies. Critical uncertainties remain regarding geographic disparities and future trajectories beyond demographic ageing. We examined patterns and projections of fall-related emergency department (ED) visits in Korea, one of the world's most rapidly ageing societies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analysed 943 692 fall-related ED visits among adults aged ≥65 years from Korea's nationwide registry (2016-2023). Geographic disparities were characterised by area type (metropolitan vs non-metropolitan) and population density tertiles. Age-standardised and sex-standardised rates were calculated. Generalised additive models assessed non-linear temporal trends and pandemic-associated structural breaks. Future projections (2024-2040) were generated under three incidence scenarios, with component decomposition quantifying contributions from demographic ageing versus incidence rate changes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A geographic paradox emerged: metropolitan and high-density areas exhibited higher visit rates, whereas non-metropolitan and low-density areas demonstrated greater clinical severity. Hospital admission rates followed a density gradient-46.7% in low-density, 44.0% in middle-density and 34.3% in high-density areas. Non-metropolitan areas showed disproportionate vertebral column injuries (17.4% vs 13.5%). Temporal trends revealed a pandemic-associated structural break followed by steep rebound from 2022. Projected visits will increase 2.0-fold to 4.1-fold by 2040. Demographic ageing alone guarantees doubling of burden. If pre-pandemic trends resume, rising intrinsic risk will contribute 67.9% of total increase, exceeding demographic effects (32.1%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Korea faces a bifurcated geographic burden: metropolitan areas confront volume pressure, while non-metropolitan areas experience disproportionate severity. The future burden will be shaped by both unavoidable demographic ageing and potentially avertable increases in intrinsic fall risk. These findings have critical implications for rapidly ageing societies across East Asia facing comparable urban-rural disparities, necessitating regionally differentiated prevention and trauma care strategies that integrate capacity expansion with targeted risk reduction.

articles.title: The care of the contact athlete's shoulder: rotator cuff, proximal biceps, pectoralis and latissimus injuries-a narrative review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Injuries are common in contact and collision sports such as American football, soccer, hockey, lacrosse, wrestling, basketball, and rugby. Traumatic shoulder injuries are frequently encountered, with a range of presentations that demand prompt and accurate diagnosis to guide return-to-play decisions and treatment planning. While common injuries such as glenohumeral dislocations and acromioclavicular (AC) joint separations are well described in the literature, less common pathologies-including traumatic rotator cuff tears, acute proximal biceps tendon injuries, pectoralis major ruptures, and latissimus dorsi ruptures-are less well-represented in the literature. These rare, contact injuries can be diagnostically challenging and lack well-defined management algorithms, in particular for in-season athletes. The aim of this paper is to synthesize the available literature and to guide the accurate diagnosis and management of these relatively rare contact injuries of the shoulder.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We systematically searched multiple electronic databases for papers regarding acute pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi, rotator cuff, and biceps tendon tears, specifically in contact athletes. Sources were reviewed and excluded if they focused on chronic or non-contact injuries or were greater than 20 years old.

abstract.label: KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS
abstract.text: These injuries predominantly occur in contact and collision sports where the mechanism of injury often involves forceful impact or eccentric overload. Sideline assessments prioritize immediate triage and gross deformity recognition, whereas clinic-based evaluations afford more comprehensive musculoskeletal examination and imaging, facilitating nuanced diagnoses. This review outlines the clinical presentation, diagnostic considerations, and current evidence-based management strategies for these uncommon shoulder injuries sustained by contact athletes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Although there is limited published about these rare, contact shoulder injuries, this narrative review aims to provide orthopedic surgeons and team physicians with practical insights for optimizing care in high-demand athletic populations.

articles.title: Management of acutely traumatized cartilage of the knee-a narrative review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Traumatic cartilage injuries are common in the general population, affecting up to 50% of athletes, as well as a higher portion of the general population, many of whom remains asymptomatic. Although a large volume of literature focuses on the natural history, diagnosis and management of widespread degenerative cartilage disease in the form of osteoarthritis (OA), there is less evidence available for the management of acute cartilage injuries following trauma. Following a previous review by Brittberg in 2018 as well as the recently published consensus statements on the topic of cartilage injuries, the aim of this study was to perform a review on the topic of acute traumatic cartilage injuries, in hope of providing a contemporary description of their diagnosis and management with respect to recent literature.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following invitation, a thorough review of current literature was performed by two authors with the aim of analyzing contempory diagnostic and therapeutic aspects of traumatic cartilage management in the knee.

abstract.label: KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS
abstract.text: A summary of measures to be considered in the diagnosis of acute traumatized cartilage is provided, alongside the comtemporary non-operative and operative options are discussed. Specific focus on cell-based therapies and return to play (RTP) metrics are discussed in the text.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: It is clear that in the last number of decades that our knowledge of the natural history surrounding acute traumatic cartilage injuries, their diagnosis and optimal management has been ever growing. However, these injuries are still troublesome for the young symptomatic patient, particularly those athletes hoping for early and effective RTP. Careful patient selection with thorough lesion assessment and characterization through clinical exam and radiological evaluation is warranted when managing traumatic cartilage lesions, particularly as unsuccessfully treatment has been shown to demonstrate a clear progression to early degenerative change in the form of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA). Treatment options vary in morbidity, effectiveness and regulatory approval, yielding international consensus statements and guidelines that cannot yet offer strong recommendations based on heterogenous evidence. Ultimately, consistency in licensing and technique will permit reliable randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses, upon which definitive international clinical guidance can be based.

articles.title: Impact of MRSA nasal PCR in the emergency department on duration of vancomycin and linezolid for pneumonia.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a common cause of nosocomial pneumonia, often prompting empiric anti-MRSA therapy despite low prevalence in emergency department (ED) presentations. MRSA nasal polymerase chain reaction (PCR) offers a rapid, non-invasive method to guide de-escalation of MRSA-targeted therapy. This study aims to evaluate the impact of pharmacist-driven MRSA nasal PCR ordering in the ED on the duration of anti-MRSA therapy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control study at a single academic center using data from an electronic health record. Adult ED patients with suspected pneumonia who received anti-MRSA therapy in the ED and were subsequently admitted were included. Emergency department pharmacists were responsible for ordering MRSA nasal PCR in compliance with a pre-existing hospital protocol. ED nurses facilitated MRSA nasal PCR collection in the ED.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 200 patients were included in the final analysis. The median duration of anti-MRSA therapy was 5.90 h and 1.13 h for pre- and post-intervention groups, respectively (p = 0.006). Incidence of MRSA nasal PCRs ordered increased from 69.4% pre-intervention to 86.3% post-intervention (p = 0.18). Median length of hospital stay was not significantly different between groups (5.0 days vs. 6.0 days, p = 0.10).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pharmacist-driven MRSA nasal PCR ordering in the ED significantly reduced anti-MRSA therapy duration without adversely affecting 30-day readmission rates or all-cause 30-day mortality. These findings highlight the value of pharmacist engagement in antibiotic stewardship in the ED.
