articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of serum procalcitonin for pneumonia in patients with acute dyspnea: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Several studies have investigated the diagnostic value of serum procalcitonin (PCT) for pneumonia in patients with acute dyspnea, but results have been inconsistent. This systematic review aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of serum PCT for pneumonia in patients with acute dyspnea.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched the PubMed and Web of Science databases to identify studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of serum PCT for pneumonia-associated acute dyspnea published before October 1, 2025. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the revised Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS-2). We used a bivariate model to be pooled sensitivity and specificity. The overall diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using a summary receiver operating characteristic curve (sROC). Deek's test was used to assess publication bias.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 6 studies involving 2341 patients (576 with pneumonia and 1765 without). Serum PCT's pooled sensitivity and specificity for diagnosing pneumonia-related acute dyspnea were 0.67 (95% CI: 0.58-0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI: 0.67-0.83), respectively. The area under the sROC curve (AUC) was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.73-0.80). The positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) were 2.8 (95% CI: 2.0-3.8) and 0.44 (95% CI: 0.34-0.56), respectively. The diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) was 6 (95% CI: 4-10). The included studies showed no significant publication bias.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Serum PCT has only moderate diagnostic value for pneumonia-related acute dyspnea and is insufficient to confirm or exclude pneumonia when used alone.

articles.title: Design assessment and preliminary performance evaluation of a novel device for non-invasive emergency treatment of acute respiratory failure.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Acute respiratory failure (ARF) requires rapid intervention to prevent patient deterioration and life-threatening complications. Early respiratory support through prehospital Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) has been shown to improve ARF outcomes. However, existing CPAP devices present technical barriers for use in out-of-hospital emergency scenarios. This study presents the design and preliminary performance evaluation of a novel portable, ready-to-use CPAP device for out-of-hospital respiratory support. The device includes a blower providing steady air insufflation through a face mask, with Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (PEEP) regulated by two fixed-point PEEP valves. To identify optimized operational conditions ensuring target respiratory support, a lumped-parameter model (LPM) was developed to simulate device-patient interaction. Input data for the LPM included experimental characteristics of the device components. Simulations were conducted using breathing profiles representing varying ARF-like conditions and severity. Additionally, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis was performed to assess the risk of CO2 rebreathing through the mask. LPM simulations described the dynamic interaction between the breathing profile and device performances, and the consequent pressure and flow patterns during the respiratory cycle. Across all simulated conditions and device settings, PEEP remained close to the predefined target of 5 cm H2O without reaching critical thresholds, confirming design choices efficacy. CFD analysis indicated an end-expiratory residual CO2 concentration of ~2%, suggesting a low risk of rebreathing between cycles. Our results confirmed the validity of our design solutions and suggest a potentially safe and efficient profile as a promising solution for early CPAP use in emergency settings.

abstract.label: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
abstract.text: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13534-026-00619-3.

articles.title: Tachycardia and rhabdomyolysis after use of melanotan and an uncommon synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonist.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Various medicinal and non-medicinal substances are available on the internet for a variety of intended effects such as recreational use, performance enhancement, and modification of body appearance. Melanotans are synthetic agonists of melanocyte stimulating hormone (a-MSH) used to promote tanning. We describe a young adult male presenting to the ED with tachycardia and tremors reportedly following melanotan injection. Clinical suspicion and laboratory confirmation led to detection of an undisclosed synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonist (SCRA) seldom reported in the US. We discuss the likely contributions of both substances to the findings in this case.

articles.title: Secure chat and critical/urgent imaging-result communication in a multisite emergency department system.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Closed-loop communication of critical and urgent imaging findings is essential for patient safety, but traditional verbal-only workflows can introduce friction and limit communication throughput. Epic Secure Chat, an EHR-integrated messaging platform, may reduce friction while preserving closed-loop communication requirements. This study evaluated communication volume, radiologist interpretation throughput, clinician experience, and reported safety events following implementation of a Secure Chat-first protocol.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective pre-post cohort study of operational outcomes was conducted across 26 emergency departments within a large academic health system, with a concurrent post-implementation survey. Following a 205-day overnight Secure Chat pilot, operational data were compared with a 161-day pre-implementation period using paired t-tests. Communication and examination volumes were normalized by time period. Linear regression was used to assess the association between Secure Chat volume and interpretation throughput change.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Survey responses were obtained from 48 emergency physicians (20.2%) and 19 radiologists (48.7%). Most emergency physicians (77%) and radiologists (95%) supported Secure Chat as a supplemental modality and reported improved communication ease. Documented critical and urgent result communications increased by 26.5% (mean increase 21.4 communications per radiologist; 95% CI 2.9-39.8; p=0.026). Radiologist interpretation throughput did not significantly change (+0.58%; p=0.833), with no association between Secure Chat volume and throughput change (R2=0.023; p=0.508). No Secure Chat-associated safety events were identified across 1087 reviewed communications.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Implementation of a Secure Chat-first protocol with a verbal failsafe was associated with increased communication volume without a reduction in radiologist throughput or identified safety events.

abstract.label: PRIOR PRESENTATIONS
abstract.text: American College of Emergency Physicians National Meeting, Salt Lake City, Utah 2025.

articles.title: Management of meniscal pathology at the time of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in performance athletes: a systematic review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Meniscal pathology is a frequent and clinically important finding at the time of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, particularly in performance athletes who place high demands on knee stability, load tolerance, and return-to-sport expectations. While meniscal management in the general ACL population has been widely studied, athlete-specific literature is limited. This review evaluates the incidence, tear patterns, treatment strategies, and outcomes of meniscal pathology in professional athletes undergoing ACL reconstruction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a search of PubMed was conducted from inception to September 2025. Studies including professional athletes older than 18 years old who underwent ACL reconstruction with detailed management of concomitant meniscus tears were included. Data on incidence, tear patterns, treatment strategies, and outcomes were extracted. Study quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-randomized Studies (MINORS).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five studies including 519 patients (18% female) with a weighted mean age of 23.7 years were included. Four studies reported outcomes at minimum 1 year follow-up. Across cohorts, meniscal injuries were highly prevalent, with reported rates ranging from 59% to 86%. Longitudinal posterior horn tears were the most common tear morphology, while ramp lesions and lateral posterior root tears were also frequently identified. Meniscal preservation was strongly favored, with repair performed in most reparable tears. Medial meniscal tears demonstrated higher failure and secondary meniscectomy rates than lateral tears, especially when repaired with all-inside techniques, whereas inside-out and suture-hook techniques appeared more favorable for medial-sided pathology. Sport-specific differences were noted, with soccer players demonstrating more medial and posterior root pathology and skiers exhibiting relatively more complex and lateral-sided lesions. Despite variability in rehabilitation protocols, meniscal repair did not appear to compromise return-to-sport and may support longer athletic career longevity compared with meniscectomy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Current evidence supports a preservation-first strategy for meniscus tears during ACL reconstruction in performance athletes. Meniscectomy should be reserved for irreparable or nonfunctional tissue. Although available data are limited by retrospective designs and heterogeneity, meniscal preservation at the time of ACL reconstruction appears to optimize both return-to-play potential and long-term joint health in this high-demand population.

articles.title: Added value of brain perfusion ultrasound to prehospital stroke scales-a secondary analysis of the SONAS trial.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Accurate prehospital identification of acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is critical to guide selection of an optimal target hospital for either intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) alone and/or mechanical thrombectomy (MT). The novel portable non-imaging brain perfusion ultrasound (BPU) device SONAS(TM) indicated similar sensitivity and specificity as prehospital stroke scales. In this study, we reanalyzed data from the original 20 patient cohort to evaluate whether combining BPU with prehospital stroke scales (ph-SS) can further improve LVO detection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Clinical data and NIHSS scores of all patients suffering from acute ischemic stroke with and without proven LVO in the SONAS trial were collected and applied to 16 different phSS. As an exploratory analysis we also applied a prehospital score for intracerebral hemorrhage (ph-ICH) to this cohort. The positive and negative predictive values as well as sensitivity and specificity were analyzed retrospectively for both methods.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The best performing phSS, CG-FAST, and RACE, showed comparable performances to BPU, but still misdiagnosed patients. However, in our specific cohort, the combination of both methods allowed for a reliable classification into three groups: (A) "highly probably LVO", (B) "highly probable non-LVO" and (C) "not assessable" (including all patients misdiagnosed by one method alone). The addition of BPU resulted in shifts towards higher sensitivity and NPV. When using the ph-ICH score three patients were classified as ICH (false positive), and all of them showed severe perfusion deficits in BPU indicating LVO.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The combination of BPU with phSS may hold the potential to enhance prehospital triage of acute stroke patients selecting patients to (A) endovascular-capable centers, (B) the nearest stroke unit for, i.e., IVT or (C) either depending on other clinical factors and local circumstances. However, validation is critical in stroke-call patients in the prehospital setting including application by paramedics with/without emergency physicians or telemedical support, and compared to other prehospital point-of-care diagnostics both in respect to sensitivity/specificity, timeline and, ultimately, costs. In the future, the addition of serum biomarkers for ICH may open new opportunities for early ICH treatment or even enable prehospital IVT, and/or streamline direct to angio-suite approaches in confirmed LVO.

articles.title: Vision loss following tranexamic acid injection during an elective sinus surgery.
articles.journal_full: American journal of ophthalmology case reports

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Intravenous tranexamic acid (TXA) is commonly used preoperatively to reduce surgical bleeding; however, its antifibrinolytic effects may increase the risk of thromboembolism. When retinal vessels are involved, urgent ophthalmologic evaluation is essential to preserve vision.

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: A 19-year-old female developed acute vision loss in the right eye following elective endoscopic sinus surgery during which intravenous tranexamic acid was administered to reduce intraoperative blood loss. Funduscopic examination revealed an atypical thrombus within the central retinal artery, and fluorescein angiography confirmed a branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO). Anterior chamber paracentesis was unsuccessful in dislodging the thrombus. She subsequently underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy and was started on aspirin. Although her visual acuity improved and the thrombus resolved, she continued to demonstrate visual field defects, delayed arterial filling, and marked loss of contrast sensitivity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our case illustrates a rare but serious retinal vascular event occurring following intraoperative use of tranexamic acid. Additionally, other perioperative use of vasoconstrictors such as intranasal epinephrine may have contributed. Prompt diagnosis of retinal complications with a dilated funduscopic exam can allow for potentially vision-saving treatments, such as hyperbaric oxygen therapy. With an increase in indications for tranexamic acid use and a wider trend of adoption among surgeons, it is imperative that each patient be carefully assessed for thrombotic risk. Importantly, potential drug interactions, including concurrent use of local injections of vasoconstricting medications, should be taken into account to reduce the chance of irreversible vision loss.

articles.journal_full: Journal of hospice and palliative nursing : JHPN : the official journal of the Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association

articles.title: Prehospital tranexamic acid decreases mortality, transfusion requirements, and improves shock physiology in trauma patients receiving whole blood.
From hypoxia to thrombosis: a hypothesis-driven framework for pulmonary embolism risk in deep underground environments.

abstract.text: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. These factors may interact dynamically with oxygen sensing, cardiopulmonary compensation, venous return, endothelial function, and coagulation-inflammation pathways. However, the relationship between deep underground exposure, thrombogenesis, PE recognition, and prevention remains insufficiently conceptualized. Direct epidemiological evidence linking deep-underground occupational exposure to incident venous thromboembolism or PE remains scarce, and existing PE prediction tools have not been specifically validated in deep-underground occupational populations. Therefore, this review does not assume that underground exposure independently increases PE incidence or that established clinical tools are inadequate. Instead, we develop a hypothesis-driven framework to examine whether exposure-related factors-including oxygen fluctuation, heat and dehydration, restricted mobility, altered hemodynamics, and inflammatory stress-could modify thrombotic susceptibility, symptom interpretation, or the operational performance of conventional PE pathways. We summarize the environmental and physiological stressors relevant to PE, examine how they may amplify Virchow's triad, and discuss research questions concerning symptom recognition, anticoagulation, reperfusion decision-making, preventive interventions, and the staged development of dynamic risk warning models. This review aims to provide a conceptual foundation for future surveillance, prevention, and clinical research on PE in deep underground occupational populations.

articles.title: Impacts of paid sick leave policy adoption on heat-associated emergency department visit rates in two New Jersey municipalities: a quasi-experimental study.

abstract.text: By supporting well-being, paid sick leave (PSL) policies may reduce heat vulnerability. A quasi-experimental difference-in-difference study of associations between early PSL policy adoption and heat-related morbidity outcomes in Jersey City and Newark, NJ, was conducted. Using data from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Emergency Department Database, a panel dataset of monthly counts of municipality-level all-cause emergency department (ED) visits among adults aged 18-64 from May to September 2011-2016 was constructed. The study linked these with monthly averages of daily minimum and maximum temperatures and was calculated using Oregon State University's PRISM Group data. Multivariable fixed-effect Poisson models were used with panel Newey-West sandwich covariate estimators and finite-sample corrections to estimate associations between monthly average temperature and ED visit rates before and after PSL adoption. Models included the main temperature parameter; an interaction between temperature and an indicator for PSL adoption (pre-2014 = 0; 2014-2016 = 1); terms for monthly fine particulate matter (μg/m3) and precipitation (mm); and a population offset term. Rates of ED visits were 1.2% (95% CI: 0.995, 1.030) higher for every 10 Celsius increase in monthly average maximum temperature, pre-policy enactment; associations were modestly attenuated post-policy enactment (rate ratio: 1.005, 95% CI: 0.993, 1.018). However, comparison municipalities, which did not adopt a PSL policy during the study period, experienced similar attenuation post-policy enactment, suggesting that associations might be explained by other factors, aside from the PSL policy. Additional research evaluating the impacts of PSL and other labor policies on heat vulnerability, with larger data sets and greater temporal granularity, is needed.

articles.title: Analysis of nursing practice environment and its influencing factors: a cross-sectional study in a maternal and child specialized hospital in China.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aims to evaluate the current status of the nursing practice environment in a maternal and child specialized hospital, identify its associated influencing factors, and provide an empirical reference for formulating targeted optimization strategies for the nursing practice environment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A questionnaire survey was conducted using the Chinese version of the Nursing Practice Environment Scale among 1,154 nurses working at a tertiary maternal and child specialized hospital in Chengdu.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The total mean score of the nursing practice environment in the investigated maternal and child specialized hospital was (78.46 ± 14.67). The highest domain score was for quality management (89.52 ± 14.07), while the lowest was for participation in hospital management (59.65 ± 29.28). Department, gender, and professional position were identified as influencing factors of the nursing practice environment (P < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The score of the nursing practice environment in the maternal and child specialized hospital in Chengdu was lower than that in similar hospitals in coastal regions, indicating a need for further improvement. Administrators should focus on addressing the differentiated needs of nurses working in emergency departments and intensive care units, male nurses, and staff nurses. Effective mechanisms should be established to enhance nurses' participation in hospital management, thereby strengthening their sense of professional belonging. Continuous optimization of the practice environment is essential to promote nursing workforce stability and improve the quality of nursing care.

articles.title: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries: A 13-year retrospective review of injury characteristics, treatment, and outcomes.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries are rare but potentially devastating. Due to low incidence, optimal perioperative management remains poorly defined, and evidence is scarce. This study evaluates the injury characteristics, surgical treatment, age-specific functional outcomes, and challenges in this population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review was conducted on 79 pediatric patients (mean age 6.84 ± 4.27 years; 67.1% male) who underwent surgical repair for flexor tendon lacerations between 2010 and 2023. Outcomes were assessed using Total Active Motion (TAM), Strickland score, grip/pinch strength, Semmes-Weinstein monofilament, two-point discrimination, and QuickDASH questionnaire, with a mean follow-up of 59.9 ± 32.8 months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Zone 2 was the most common injury site (45.6%), with glass being the predominant mechanism (67.1%). Nerve injury was present in 35.4% of cases. Overall, good/excellent results were achieved in 81.9% (TAM) and 89.0% (Strickland) of patients. The 0-5 years age group had significantly lower Strickland scores than the 6-12 years group (74.28% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.05). Zone 5 injuries demonstrated significantly better outcomes than Zone 2 and 3 (p < 0.001). The overall complication rate was low (5.1%), with a rerupture rate of 2.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pediatric flexor tendon repairs yield favorable functional outcomes with low complication rates. Age-related differences in functional outcomes should be interpreted cautiously because of developmental differences in patient cooperation and age-dependent rehabilitation strategies. Concomitant nerve injury was associated with poorer functional outcomes. The modified Kessler technique remains a reliable repair method.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in dogs with clinical signs due to heartworm disease.

abstract.text: Estimates suggest that over 1 million dogs in the United States are infected with heartworm (Dirofilaria immitis). Although dogs often have no, or only mild clinical signs with heartworm infection, some dogs develop life-threatening cardiopulmonary disease. Point-of-care ultrasound is a useful tool to assess dogs with severe heartworm disease and varies from a quick 'fluid check' to more comprehensive exams that utilize standardized views. Ultrasound is commonly used to diagnose cavitary effusions and intracardiac heartworms. With more advanced training, ultrasound can be used to identify interstitial lung abnormalities and evaluate the morphology of the right heart.

articles.title: 'Pericardial hyperechoic ring' on point-of-care ultrasound during cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
Pharmacogenetic testing to improve care in the emergency department.

abstract.text: Nearly 20% of emergency department (ED) encounters involve medications with actionable pharmacogenomic (PGx) guidance available, and population-based studies suggest over 90% of patients carry at least one PGx variant potentially affecting drug response. Despite this, PGx testing in emergency medicine remains rare. This perspective summarizes current evidence supporting PGx implementation in the ED, key barriers to integration, and future directions for PGx testing in acute care. Feasibility studies demonstrate that PGx testing can be incorporated into ED workflows. Observational data suggest clinically important associations between CYP2C19 variability and clopidogrel-related bleeding, CYP2D6 metabolism and opioid-related ED visits, and a high prevalence of actionable gene-drug interactions in older adults presenting with falls. In pediatric psychiatric populations, combinatorial PGx testing has been associated with differences in drug exposure and clinical outcomes. However, no randomized controlled trials testing the clinical utility of PGx testing have been conducted in ED populations. Key barriers to implementation include prolonged PGx testing turnaround times, lack of standardized ordering workflows, limited clinician familiarity with PGx interpretation, inconsistent reimbursement, and challenges integrating results into clinical decision support systems. Future priorities should include prospective interventional trials assessing clinical outcomes, targeted implementation focused on high-risk gene-drug pairs, and incorporation of PGx education into emergency medicine training. Although current evidence is largely feasibility-based, the ED represents a potentially high-yield setting for PGx integration given frequent exposure to actionable medications and the high burden of potentially preventable adverse drug events.

articles.title: Decision tree models to guide endotracheal tube selection in dogs.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Choosing an endotracheal tube (ETT) of an appropriate size is critical for effective airway management in dogs undergoing anesthesia or emergency care. Conventional methods often rely on body weight (BW), palpation of external tracheal diameter, nasal septum width, or subjective clinician experience. However, these approaches are frequently imprecise and lack well-established guidelines. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a machine learning-based decision tree model to standardize ETT size using measurable anatomical parameters in dolichocephalic, mesocephalic, and brachycephalic breeds.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis was conducted on data from dogs undergoing anesthesia or emergency care at the Northern Regional Veterinary Healthcare and Learning Center, Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Chiang Mai University, (NOVEL CMU) Thailand between January and December 2024. We investigated the relationship between the internal diameter (ID) of the ETT used and multiple patient variables, including BW, sex, age, breed, and internal tracheal diameter (ITD) measured at the thoracic inlet on radiographs. Decision tree analysis was used to determine the ETT selection. We hypothesized that a decision tree model integrating BW and ITD would accurately predict appropriate ETT sizing in dogs, but that upper airway anatomical differences would necessitate separate models for non-brachycephalic breeds (Group DM, including dolichocephalic and mesocephalic conformation) and brachycephalic breeds (Group B).

abstract.label: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The results demonstrated that Group B required ETTs with a significantly smaller ID compared to Group DM of the same BW. Variable importance analysis identified BW and ITD as the primary predictors of ETT size in both groups. Conversely, sex and age demonstrated negligible predictive value and were not significant factors in the selection process. Hence, the decision tree model successfully generated distinct algorithmic pathways for Group DM and Group B. The developed decision tree models offer a practical, non-invasive method for standardizing ETT sizes in clinical practice, thereby enhancing skilled veterinary human capital. This algorithmic approach accounts for individual anatomical variations in the respiratory tract, particularly in brachycephalic dogs. For clinical application, clinicians should prepare tubes within ±0.5 mm of the predicted size to ensure optimal airway management and patient safety.

articles.title: Electrocorticographic characteristics of rats exposed to hyperbaric nitrox.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study aimed to characterize and compare the dynamic changes in cortical electrophysiological activity during hyperbaric nitrox exposure and subsequent hyperbaric heliox exposure in rats receiving continuous electrocorticographic (ECoG) recording.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Male rats were randomly assigned to the 3% O2-N2, 16% O2-N2, and 100% O2 groups (n=8 per group). Rats in the 3% O2-N2 and 16% O2-N2 groups were exposed to their respective gas mixtures at 700 kPa for 60 min, whereas those in the 100% O2 group were exposed to pure oxygen at 200 kPa for 60 min. Following hyperbaric nitrox exposure, the 16% O2-N2 mixture was replaced with a 16% O2-84% He mixture at the same pressure for additional 60 min. ECoG was continuously recorded, and power spectral density (PSD), absolute power in the δ, θ, α, β, and γ bands, delta-theta/alpha-beta ratio (DTABR), median frequency (MF), sample entropy (SampEn), and Higuchi fractal dimension (HFD) were calculated and compared among groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Rats in the 3% O2-N2 and 16% O2-N2 groups exhibited increased slow-wave activity and a shift in spectral power toward lower frequencies, accompanied by increased δ-, θ-, α-, and β-band power, decreased γ-band power, increased DTABR, and reduced MF, SampEn, and HFD as compared to the baseline levels. Changes in several ECoG parameters emerged earlier in the 3% O2-N2 group than in the 16% O2-N2 group. Compared with the 100% O2 group, rats in the 3% O2-N2 and 16% O2-N2 groups generally exhibited lower MF, SampEn, and HFD, whereas ECoG parameters in the 100% O2 group showed relatively minor changes as compared to the baseline levels. Following substitution with hyperbaric heliox, DTABR tended to decrease, whereas MF, SampEn, and HFD tended to increase, suggesting a trend toward baseline ECoG characteristics.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hyperbaric nitrox exposure was associated with a shift in ECoG activity toward lower frequencies, reduced signal complexity, and greater regularity in rats. Following substitution with hyperbaric heliox, these ECoG characteristics showed trends toward baseline levels. These findings characterize cortical electrophysiological alterations associated with hyperbaric nitrox exposure and may provide a basis for future investigations into the electrophysiological characteristics of nitrogen narcosis.

articles.title: The median effective dose of hyperbaric ropivacaine and lateral decubitus time for unilateral spinal anesthesia in lower extremity varicose vein surgery: a dose- and time-finding study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to determine the median effective dose (ED50) of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for motor block in the non-surgical extremity and the median effective lateral decubitus time (ET50) for preventing motor block in the non-surgical extremity during lower extremity varicose vein surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Sixty patients undergoing unilateral lower extremity varicose vein surgery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia were enrolled in two sequential phases: a dose-finding phase (n = 30) and a time-finding phase (n = 30). All patients received intrathecal 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine. A modified Dixon up-and-down method was applied sequentially. In the dose-finding phase, the lateral decubitus position was maintained for 20 min. In the subsequent time-finding phase, patients received the ED5 of hyperbaric ropivacaine estimated in the dose-finding phase, corresponding to a 5% probability of motor block in the non-surgical extremity. Successful prevention of motor block was defined as a modified Bromage score <1. For probit analysis, motor block (modified Bromage score ≥1) was coded as the positive response in the dose-finding phase, whereas successful prevention of motor block in the non-surgical extremity was coded as the positive response in the time-finding phase. The ED50 and ET50 were treated as the primary estimates, whereas additional quantile estimates derived from the fitted probit models were considered exploratory.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The ED50 of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for motor block in the non-surgical extremity was 12.683 mg (95% CI: 12.367-12.997 mg). The ET50 of lateral decubitus time for preventing motor block in the non-surgical extremity was 13.887 min (95% CI: 13.390-14.338 min). The exploratory ED5, corresponding to a 5% probability of motor block, was 11.956 mg (95% CI, 10.304-12.303 mg), while the exploratory ET95 was 14.957 min (95% CI, 14.455-17.016 min). Adverse events were infrequent, and intraoperative hemodynamics remained stable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The ED50 of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for non-surgical extremity was 12.683 mg (95%CI: 12.367-12.997 mg), and the ET50 of lateral decubitus time for preventing motor block was 13.887 min (95% CI: 13.390-14.338 min).

articles.title: Case Report: Pediatric group A streptococcal toxic shock syndrome complicated by acute necrotizing tracheobronchitis requiring veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

abstract.text: Group A streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (STSS) in children is uncommon and can progress rapidly to multi-organ failure. Acute necrotizing tracheobronchitis (NTB) is a rare airway complication of severe infection and has seldom been reported during extracorporeal support. We describe a previously healthy 7-year-old girl admitted with 6 days of fever and 3 h of chest tightness and dyspnea. She developed septic shock, severe pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), acute kidney injury, and multi-organ dysfunction. Blood and sputum cultures were negative at 48 h. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of blood and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid identified Streptococcus pyogenes. Serial fiberoptic bronchoscopy was used for airway clearance and extubation assessment. Procedure records described progression from mucosal congestion to erosive necrosis with pseudomembrane-like plaques, followed by healing included broad-spectrum antimicrobials, corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), tocilizumab, hemoperfusion, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) from hospital days 2 to 9. Lung ultrasound during ECMO showed confluent B-lines with regional A-lines. Ultrasound images were acquired on day 3; a day-4 progress note recorded a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 62% and mild tricuspid regurgitation. In the setting of markedly elevated troponin, these findings favored sepsis-associated myocardial injury over fulminant myocarditis. ECMO was discontinued on day 9, CRRT on day 10, and the patient was extubated on day 13 after bronchoscopy showed improved airway necrosis. She was discharged on hospital day 28, 27 days after admission. At follow-up, an intratracheal granulation-tissue lesion was excised endoscopically, and the family reported preserved neurocognitive function. Together, these findings show that NTB can complicate pediatric group A streptococcal STSS and that serial bronchoscopy may help guide ventilator and ECMO weaning; as one case without a comparison group, it does not establish which treatments were responsible for recovery.

articles.title: Diagnostic triage for ultrasound-detected subclinical insulin injection-related lipohypertrophy in older adults with diabetes: development and internal validation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Subclinical insulin injection-related lipohypertrophy can remain undetected after routine injection-site examination. We developed and internally validated a model to prioritize confirmatory ultrasound in older adults with diabetes after negative visual inspection and palpation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center cross-sectional study included 818 adults aged 60 years or older from the endocrinology outpatient clinics and inpatient wards of Beijing Hospital between January 2025 and January 2026; 129 had ultrasound-detected subclinical lipohypertrophy. An 11-predictor ridge logistic model combined sex, age, body mass index, insulin injection duration, daily injection frequency, needle reuse, site rotation, injection area, immediate injection after refrigeration, glycated hemoglobin, and weekly glucose-variability frequency. It was compared with a 9-predictor core model that excluded the two metabolic markers. Internal validation used 2,000 bootstrap resamples and repeated nested 10-fold cross-fitting. Out-of-bag bootstrap validation assessed thresholds targeting 90% and 95% sensitivity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Subclinical lipohypertrophy was detected in 15.8% (95% CI, 13.4%-18.4%). The core model had an optimism-corrected receiver operating characteristic (ROC) area under the curve of 0.758 (95% interval, 0.720-0.808) and Brier score of 0.117 (0.100-0.130). The extended model had an optimism-corrected ROC area under the curve of 0.774 (95% interval, 0.741-0.823), precision-recall area under the curve of 0.423 (0.353-0.527), and Brier score of 0.113 (0.097-0.126). At the validated thresholds, mean sensitivities were 89.7% and 94.4%, and 337 and 220 ultrasound examinations per 1,000 patients, respectively, were avoided.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The model stratified the probability of ultrasound-detected subclinical lipohypertrophy after a negative routine examination. Its high-sensitivity operating points quantify the balance between ultrasound use and missed lesions, providing a basis for evaluating selective ultrasound referral in older adults receiving insulin. The core model warrants evaluation as a lower-burden option. Temporal and multicenter geographic external validation is required before clinical software deployment or widespread protocol adoption.

articles.title: Case Report: Mislabeling of an online "alprazolam triazolobenzophenone" pill leads to severe intoxication with the novel synthetic opioid cychlorphine.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mislabeling of illicit drug products poses a serious risk to public health, especially in the rapidly evolving market for new psychoactive substances (NPS). Products sold as benzodiazepines may contain undisclosed novel synthetic opioids (NSOs), exposing opioid-naïve users to life-threatening respiratory depression.

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: A 34-year-old man ingested a pink tablet purchased online and labeled as "alprazolam triazolobenzophenone", a ring-opened alprazolam prodrug, also known as "alprazafone". Approximately 45 min after ingestion, he developed snoring and gasping respiration, hypoxemia and deep coma (Glasgow Coma Scale 3). Prehospital bag-valve ventilation and subsequent intubation resulted in prompt stabilization. The patient could be extubated 6 hours later. Contrary to the labeling, neither alprazolam nor its prodrug was detected in the tablet, blood or urine. Instead, the tablet contained approximately 1 mg of N-propionitrile chlorphine (cychlorphine), a piperidine benzimidazolone opioid of the emerging "orphine" class. Routine immunoassay screening for opioids and benzodiazepines was negative; identification required targeted LC-MS/MS. Six hours after ingestion, cychlorphine concentrations were 0.46 ng/mL in blood and 5.0 ng/mL in urine-to our knowledge the first human concentrations reported for this substance. In vitro, cychlorphine activated the µ-opioid receptor with an EC50 of 2.7 nM, i.e. 4.5-fold more potent than fentanyl (EC50 = 12.2 nM) within the same assay, with a binding affinity of Ki = 1.09 nM (fentanyl: Ki = 1.91 nM). The nitazene protonitazepyne was additionally detected in urine but not in blood or serum, indicating earlier intake and terminal elimination at the time of the event.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case documents cychlorphine as a highly potent NSO capable of causing life-threatening respiratory depression at sub-nanogram-per-millilitre blood concentrations, and illustrates the specific danger of benzodiazepine products adulterated with opioids. No pharmacokinetic data are available for cychlorphine. The concentration, measured 6 hours post-intake, therefore likely underestimates peak exposure. Clinicians should consider NSO exposure in unexplained respiratory depression after NPS use, even where a benzodiazepine was expected. Accessible drug-checking services, take-home naloxone and NSO-capable confirmatory analysis are needed.

articles.title: Ethical aspects of triage in civil and military contexts: a qualitative research of physicians' attitudes and knowledge regarding ethics in triage scenarios in.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Triage in the medical context is a screening procedure used to determine resource distribution in situations of severe restriction of medical resources. Originally, triage was designed as a method to ascertain the treatment priority of wounded soldiers on battlefields. However, ethical discussions about clinical triage were raised during the COVID-19 pandemic. In the focus stood prioritization of care in situation of limited resources.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The purpose of our investigation was comparison of experiences and ethical attitudes towards triage among military and civil physicians. To date, there is no research available on this topic.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted 26 semi-structured, qualitative, exploratory interviews among military and civilian physicians in Germany. All the interviews were digitally audio-recorded, transcribed and anonymized. We analyzed the transcripts via the structured qualitative content analysis method.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Triage scenarios bring distinctive ethical challenges for the attending physicians. Military and civil physicians share a similar approach to solve the ethical conflicts arousing in such situations. Triage situation does not allow for an individual medical gold standard in the treatment of patients; therefore, the principles of autonomy, beneficence and nonmaleficence should be subordinated to the principle of social justice. Because of restriction of the patient's autonomy, the final decision-making authority lies with medical professionals. Pre-clinical triage conditions also restrict patient-physician relationship.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The ethical justification of triage follows the imperatives of life-preservation and maximization of the number of survivors. According to interviewed physicians, in both pre-clinical and clinical triage situations, medical decisions should aim rather at maximizing the well-being of the collective - whether of wounded or of a society - than at maximizing the well-being of an individual patient. Restriction of patient autonomy regarding treatment discontinuation - ex-post triage - is unavoidable in a pandemic situation.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided haemodynamic profiling in haemodialysis patients: a single-centre prospective observational study protocol.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) and chronic fluid overload are common and clinically important complications of maintenance haemodialysis, yet routine volume assessment remains imprecise. Multi-organ point-of-care ultrasound may provide a structured bedside assessment of cardiac reserve, pulmonary congestion and venous congestion.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: This single-centre prospective observational cohort study will enrol approximately 60 adult patients receiving maintenance haemodialysis. Participants will undergo integrated ultrasound profiling immediately before and after dialysis at baseline and at 3, 6 and 9 months, with clinical outcomes followed for 12 months. The ultrasound protocol includes focused cardiac ultrasound, eight-zone lung ultrasound B-line quantification and a modified VEXUS assessment using inferior vena cava, hepatic vein and portal vein findings. Event-triggered intradialytic scans may also be performed for current IDH or suspected mismatch between the prescribed target weight and the best clinically tolerated weight. These examinations will not be pooled with scheduled assessments. A separate exploratory post-scan association analysis will include only scans completed while the patient is clinically stable, before the first same-session IDH and not in response to evolving current-session haemodynamic instability; the outcome is subsequent IDH before session end. Scans obtained during or after IDH or during evolving instability will be described only. The main descriptive objective is to characterise pre- and post-dialysis ultrasound-derived haemodynamic profiles and their within-session and longitudinal variability. The primary prespecified analysis for Objective 2 is an exploratory and non-confirmatory assessment of the within-patient association between pre-dialysis ultrasound parameters and same-session IDH using a scheduled-session case-crossover design. Secondary analyses include the separate event-triggered post-scan association analysis and an exploratory scheduled-session mixed-effects analysis. Event-triggered examinations will not contribute cases to the primary analysis. Exploratory objectives assess clinician-perceived usefulness and documented clinician-implemented prescription changes after delayed disclosure, without assessing clinical benefit.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: The study has received ethics approval and will be conducted after written informed consent. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific meetings.

articles.title: Association of the prognostic nutritional index with in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events among emergency department patients with acute heart failure.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute heart failure (AHF) is prone to early clinical deterioration. The prognostic nutritional index (PNI), derived from serum albumin and lymphocyte count, is readily available. We evaluated the association of early PNI with incident in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events and its incremental prognostic value.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort included consecutive adults presenting to the emergency department with AHF from March 2022 through March 2026. PNI was calculated from measurements obtained within 24 h and classified as low (<45) or high (≥45). The primary outcome was a post-index composite of all-cause death, cardiogenic shock, sustained ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, acute myocardial infarction, or worsening AHF requiring treatment escalation. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations; missing covariates were handled using multiple imputation. Discrimination was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 367 patients (156 low PNI; 211 high PNI), 112 (30.5%) experienced the primary outcome. Events occurred in 43.6% and 20.9%, respectively (P < 0.001). After adjustment, low PNI remained associated with higher odds of the primary outcome (odds ratio [OR], 1.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10-3.35; P = 0.022). Each 5-point PNI increase was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.56-0.90; P = 0.003). PNI alone yielded an AUC of 0.714. Adding PNI increased the conventional model AUC from 0.776 to 0.829 (increase, 0.053; 95% CI, 0.021-0.085; P = 0.001); bootstrap-corrected AUCs were 0.752 and 0.803, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Low PNI was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events. PNI provided modest incremental prognostic information and may serve as a complementary marker for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Demographic and Clinical Spectrum of Forensic Cases in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Analysis of 25 887 Presentations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study aims to evaluate the demographic and temporal characteristics of forensic presentations involving physical or psychological harm, negligence, or intentional injury and to analyze the specific factors influencing mortality among these presentations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study was conducted on forensic presentations presenting to the emergency department. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, seasonal variations, and clinical outcomes were evaluated. Data retrieved from the hospital's electronic health record system were analyzed statistically. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 25887 presentations were included in the study. Of the participants, 79.8% were adults and 68.9% were male, with a mean age of 34.0 ± 18.8 years. Motor vehicle accidents (21.0%) and falls from height (17.2%) were the most common injury mechanisms. Forensic presentations peaked in August (11.1%). While discharge rates were significantly higher in adults (61.9% vs. 41.3%; P < .001), mortality was significantly higher in pediatrics (2.1% vs. 1.2%; P < .001). Multivariable regression analysis identified firearm injuries (adjusted odds ratio = 7.12) as the mechanism most strongly associated with mortality in the adjusted model of mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Forensic presentations to the emergency department showed a significant concentration among young adult males and during the summer months. Although motor vehicle accidents and falls from height were the most frequent etiologies, multivariable analysis identified firearm injuries as the mechanism most strongly associated with mortality in the adjusted model of mortality. These findings suggest that the findings may help inform triage and resource-planning studies for high-risk injury mechanisms and pediatric populations. Furthermore, healthcare facilities should implement strategic resource and personnel planning to account for the seasonal surges in forensic presentations. Cite this article as: Tortum F, Tekin E, Kök AN. Demographic and clinical spectrum of forensic cases in the emergency department: a retrospective analysis of 25 887 patients. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1626, doi: 10.5152/eurasianjmed.2026.261626.

articles.title: Incidence and characteristics of foot and ankle injuries among pilgrims during Hajj.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The Hajj pilgrimage represents one of the largest recurrent mass gatherings globally, posing unique injury-related public health challenges. Foot and ankle injuries are particularly common due to prolonged walking, crowd density, and environmental exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted during Hajj 1444H, including approximately 1.8 million pilgrims. Injury data were extracted from healthcare facilities. Missing data were addressed using a distribution-based stochastic imputation approach designed to preserve the observed distribution of the available data. Incidence rates were calculated per 100,000 pilgrims.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 943 foot injuries were identified (incidence: 52.4 per 100,000 pilgrims; 95% CI 49.1-55.8). Males accounted for 74.1% of cases and adults aged 31-64 years represented 50.2%. Superficial injuries were most common (57.3%), followed by ankle/foot injuries (14.8%) and fractures (8.2%). In an exploratory complete-case analysis, the overall distribution of injury categories differed by sex; however, this analysis included only 443 records and contained several sparse categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Foot injuries during Hajj are common and largely preventable. Demographic findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial missingness and the unverifiable Missing At Random assumption. Targeted preventive strategies remain essential to reduce healthcare burden during mass gatherings.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of emergency visits for acute poisoning among children and adolescents: a single-center retrospective study (2021-2025) in China.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate the clinical characteristics of acute poisoning in children and adolescents, and to provide a basis for developing targeted prevention and control strategies. This study analyzed the clinical characteristics and temporal trends of acute poisoning cases admitted to the Emergency Department of a tertiary general hospital in Zunyi, Guizhou Province during 2021-2025.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data of children and adolescents with acute poisoning presenting to the Emergency Department from January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2025 were collected retrospectively. Descriptive analysis was conducted on age, gender, seasonal distribution and patient discharge disposition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,202 cases of acute poisoning among children and adolescents were enrolled, including 932 valid cases with an effective rate of 77.54%. The annual number of acute poisoning in children and adolescents showed a continuous upward trend from 2021 to 2025, with 40 cases in 2021, 139 cases in 2022, 184 cases in 2023, 240 cases in 2024 and 329 cases in 2025. There were 358 male patients and 574 female patients. Most patients were aged 12-18 years (645 cases, 69.21%), followed by those aged 3-6 years (109 cases, 11.70%), 1-3 years (100 cases, 10.73%), 6-12 years (70 cases, 7.51%), and aged 0-1 year (8 cases, 0.86%). Drug poisoning ranked first (641 cases, 69%), followed by pesticide poisoning (131 cases), chemical poisoning (85 cases) and food poisoning (75 cases). Among patients with drug poisoning, 208 were male and 433 were female. Chemical poisoning, pesticide poisoning and drug poisoning predominantly occurred in the 12-18 age group, while food poisoning was mainly seen in aged 6-12 years. Seasonal distribution analysis showed that the largest number of cases occurred in spring (240 cases, 25.75%), followed by summer (184 cases, 19.74%), autumn (139 cases, 14.91%) and winter (40 cases, 4.29%). Drug poisoning and pesticide poisoning were predominant in spring; drug poisoning and food poisoning were the main types in summer and autumn; drug poisoning and chemical poisoning prevailed in winter. The daily number of drug poisoning was significantly higher than that of the other three poisoning types, with the highest volumes on Mondays and Wednesdays. The afternoon shift received the largest total number of patients (392 cases), especially on Wednesdays (78 cases). The overall intensive care unit (ICU) admission rate for acute poisoning was 7%. The admission rate for pesticide poisoning (84%) was markedly higher than that of other poisoning types. Children with drug poisoning and food poisoning were more likely to receive observation and follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The number of emergency visits for acute poisoning among minors increased year by year during the study period. Drug poisoning was the leading type, which mainly affected female adolescents aged 12-18 years. Spring was the peak season of onset, and most visits occurred during the afternoon shift. Pesticide poisoning had the highest hospital admission rate. The epidemiological features and clinical outcomes of acute poisoning in local minors are distinct. Clinical and public health interventions should primarily target adolescents and high-risk factors associated with drug poisoning. Targeted health education and early interventions should be implemented according to the risks of severe cases, as well as seasonal and time-based patterns of poisoning, so as to reduce the incidence of acute poisoning and the risk of severe complications.

articles.title: Clinical and diagnostic factors associated with 72-h unscheduled return to high-priority pediatric emergency care: a health services retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Seventy-two-hour unscheduled return visits reflect short-term emergency care reutilization, discharge-transition safety, and disease progression in children. Evidence is limited for children managed through high-priority pediatric emergency care pathways, where triage acuity, observation needs, and disease-specific care processes differ from standard emergency department care. This study examined clinical and diagnostic factors associated with 72-h unscheduled return to such a pathway and assessed whether these associations differed between red-zone and yellow-zone encounters.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 30,170 pediatric visits from 24,479 children managed through an institutionally defined high-priority pediatric emergency care pathway at a tertiary women's and children's hospital in China in 2025. The primary outcome was unscheduled return to the same pathway within 72 h after the index visit. Visits were ordered chronologically within each child. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a patient-level random intercept was used to account for repeated visits. Zone and triage level were not included together because they were structurally linked in the institutional workflow.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 1,507 index visits were followed by a 72-h return (5.0%). In the primary model, yellow-zone encounters had higher odds of return than red-zone encounters (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34-3.87). Oncologic conditions showed the strongest association with return (aOR, 6.48; 95% CI, 3.54-11.87), followed by hematologic diseases (aOR, 2.49; 95% CI, 1.06-5.89). The zone-by-diagnosis interaction model indicated that the oncologic risk signal was amplified in the yellow zone (interaction aOR, 5.10; 95% CI, 1.25-20.84; p = 0.023). The oncologic association remained stable across sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this high-priority pediatric emergency care pathway, 72-h unscheduled return was more closely related to the underlying diagnostic category than to initial vital-sign abnormality. Yellow-zone children with oncologic conditions may require strengthened discharge assessment, explicit return precautions, and short-interval follow-up to improve care-transition safety and support risk-informed use of high-priority emergency resources.

articles.title: Caregivers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding household product safety and poisoning prevention in children in Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Household product poisoning is a common cause of emergency department visits and hospital admissions among children. Global variations reflect socioeconomic disparities and the presence of other contributing factors. This study evaluated caregivers' knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) regarding household product safety and childhood poisoning management.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional survey was administered to caregivers across Saudi Arabia between December 2024 and March 2025. The survey collected demographic characteristics and evaluated caregivers' KAP regarding household product poisoning. Total KAP scores and domain-specific scores ≥60% were considered satisfactory. Different respondent groups were compared using logistic regression analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 1,917 caregivers completed the survey. Although satisfactory attitude (86%) and practice (87%) scores were high, only 37% of respondents demonstrated satisfactory knowledge about childhood poisoning risks. Higher total KAP and knowledge were associated with healthcare-related employment, higher educational attainment, and having ≥3 children. Conversely, lower KAP outcomes were observed among caregivers who were male or aged <25 years. Respondents reported potentially harmful interventions, indicating misconceptions regarding appropriate poisoning management.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Despite positive attitudes and practices, deficiencies remain in caregivers' understanding of household poisoning risk and appropriate management. A long-term approach for improving child safety that integrates behavior, education, technology, and regulation is needed to reduce household childhood poisoning across Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Current European landscape of in-hospital cardiac arrest registries mapped by a cross-sectional survey including barriers and enablers setting up a registry.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) has a high mortality rate. To measure and improve resuscitation outcomes, data collection through registries plays a key role. This study aims to evaluate the current landscape of IHCA registries across national resuscitation councils affiliated with the European Resuscitation Council.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional survey was distributed among national resuscitation councils collecting data on the presence and type of IHCA registries, registry coverage and data variables collected. Findings informed an expert discussion on barriers and enablers establishing such registries and potential next steps.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 30/34 (88%) national resuscitation councils replied to the survey. Seven have no IHCA registry (23%), 11 a local registry (37%), two a local and regional registry (7%), five a national registry (17%), and two countries participate in a national registry in another country (7%). Of the included registries 17 (94%) are collecting cardiac arrests in adults, 13 (72%) in children, and four (22%) in neonates. Most registries are collecting location of cardiac arrest (95%), the initial rhythm (95%), and if return of spontaneous circulation is achieved (100%), while long term neurological outcome is only collected by four registries (21%). Overall, the AI-assisted descriptive content analysis demonstrated broad consensus regarding the value of registries, while highlighting substantial logistical, legal, and financial barriers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our survey demonstrates considerable variation in the existence, population coverage, and data collection practices of IHCA registries. While core cardiac arrest variables are collected by most registries, data on long-term outcomes remain limited.

articles.title: Consensus Statement on Traumatic Brain Injury in First Responders: The 1st International Conference on TBI in First Responders.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To develop the first interdisciplinary consensus recommendations for the recognition, diagnosis, and management of traumatic brain injury (TBI) in first responders (ie, law enforcement/corrections officers, firefighters, emergency medical services [EMS] personnel).

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The first International Conference on TBI in First Responders, held at The Ohio State University in March 2026.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: An interdisciplinary author group of 52 clinicians, researchers, policy and organizational professionals, and first responders with lived or operational experience.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Six expert workgroups conducted a best-evidence synthesis of first responder-specific literature and relevant evidence from military personnel, athletes, and other populations. Preliminary recommendations were developed over 6 months and refined using a modified Delphi process with 2 rounds of anonymous voting via Microsoft Forms. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement without reservations or with minor reservations.

abstract.label: MAIN MEASURES
abstract.text: Evidence quality and recommendation strength were graded using the Strength of Recommendation Taxonomy (SORT). The primary outcome was the percentage of agreement for each recommendation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-nine preliminary statements were evaluated across 6 domains: injury risk, recognition, and reporting challenges; early assessment and diagnosis; return to duty; mental health; prevention; and workplace and policy context. In round 1, 27 of 29 statements reached consensus. After group discussion, review of anonymous comments, wording refinement, and consolidation of related statements, 28 final recommendations were evaluated in round 2; all reached consensus.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These recommendations provide the first interdisciplinary framework for TBI in first responders. They emphasize shared organizational responsibility, standardized terminology, nonpunitive reporting and referral pathways, clinician-guided care, occupation-specific RTD progression, mental health screening and treatment, exposure mitigation, and first responder-engaged research. Implementation of these recommendations may improve timely care, operational readiness, and the evidence base for first responders with TBI.

articles.title: Traumatic Left Main Coronary Artery-Left Anterior Descending Artery Dissection in an Adolescent: A Case Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In adolescents with high-energy blunt chest trauma, electrocardiography (ECG) findings suggestive of myocardial infarction together with markedly elevated cardiac enzymes should raise immediate suspicion for traumatic coronary artery dissection (TCAD).

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: We report the case of a 16-year-old male who sustained blunt chest trauma in an electric bicycle accident. During venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support, non-ECG-gated contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography (CT) was performed. Thin-slice (1.25 mm) delayed-phase images incidentally revealed a double-lumen sign from the left main coronary artery to the proximal left anterior descending artery, along with diffuse myocardial hypoperfusion. These findings prompted angiographic confirmation and urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). WHY SHOULD AN EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN BE AWARE OF THIS?: This case highlights that, in hemodynamically unstable trauma patients, when ECG-gated coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) is not feasible, careful evaluation of routinely obtained contrast-enhanced CT images, particularly coronary root morphology and myocardial perfusion, may provide critical diagnostic clues to this life-threatening condition.

articles.title: Decreased early bystander CPR initiation despite stable overall rates: a nationwide time-to-event analysis during the COVID-19 pandemic.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Timely bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (BCPR) is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). While overall BCPR rates during the COVID-19 pandemic have been inconsistently reported, BCPR initiation timing has received limited attention. This study assessed BCPR initiation within 10 min after witnessed OHCA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study used the All-Japan Utstein registry. Adults with non-traumatic, layperson-witnessed OHCA during March 11-December 31 of 2019 and 2020 were included. The primary outcome was BCPR initiation within 10 min after witnessing. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models were used for time-to-event analyses. Exploratory logistic regression examined associations between BCPR timing and 1-month outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 56,082 eligible cases (27,770 pre-pandemic; 28,312 pandemic), overall BCPR rates were stable (58.7% vs. 58.6%, p = 0.759). However, time-to-event analysis detected a modest difference in early BCPR initiation (log-rank p = 0.010), with a lower hazard during the pandemic (aHR 0.96; 95% CI 0.93-0.98). Among BCPR recipients, earlier initiation was associated with higher odds of a favorable neurological outcome at 1 month (aORs 3.27, 2.66, and 1.68 for 0-3, 4-7, and 8-10 min, respectively; reference >10 min). The pandemic period remained associated with lower 1-month survival after adjustment for BCPR initiation timing (aOR 0.86; 95% CI, 0.80-0.92).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Although the overall BCPR rate remained unchanged during the pandemic, time-to-event analysis identified a modest reduction in early BCPR initiation. Earlier BCPR was associated with better outcomes, but differences in its timing did not fully explain the lower survival during the pandemic.

articles.title: Effect of orientation and contact area on foot chest compression quality: a simulation study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Concerns about fatigue and safety have prompted investigation of foot chest compressions as an alternative technique. To evaluate the effect of foot contact area heel vs ball-of-the-foot and foot orientation longitudinal vs transverse on the quality of foot chest compressions and physiological response in healthcare professionals.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This 2 × 2 mixed-design simulation study examined heel and ball-of-the-foot techniques in longitudinal and transverse orientations over the sternum. Participants performed two consecutive two-minute sets of foot chest compressions on a Resusci Anne QCPR manikin. Compression quality parameters included depth, rate, recoil, and compression-to-release ratio. Heart rate was continuously monitored, energy expenditure was estimated using the Keytel equation, and perceived exertion was assessed using the Borg scale. Non-parametric statistical tests were applied with significance set at p < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighty healthcare professionals completed the study. Mean compression depth ranged from 51 to 55 mm and the rate ranged from 118 to 123 compressions per minute across all conditions. The heel technique produced greater mean compression depth (54.2 ± 6.2 vs 51.6 ± 7.1 mm; p < 0.001), a higher percentage of compressions with adequate depth (81.8 ± 29.8% vs 72.7 ± 34.6%; p < 0.001), and a higher compression-to-release ratio (1.1 ± 0.3 vs 0.9 ± 0.2; p = 0.002) than the ball-of-the-foot technique. Compression rate, complete recoil, energy expenditure, heart rate, and perceived exertion were comparable between techniques. No significant differences were observed between longitudinal and transverse orientations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Foot chest compressions achieved guideline-consistent depth and rate regardless of foot orientation. The heel technique produced greater mean depth and a higher percentage of adequate-depth compressions than the ball-of-the-foot technique. Physical demand was similar between techniques. These findings support the use of foot chest compressions as a feasible adjunct when hand compressions are not possible and justify further clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Mechanical ventilation vs bag-valve ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a randomized crossover noninferiority trial.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Evidence guiding mechanical ventilation (MV) during CPR is limited, and device-calculated inspired tidal volume (VTi) during ongoing chest compressions may differ from the set volume during compressions. We compared VTi with protocolized MV and bag-valve ventilation (BVV) through an endotracheal tube for noninferiority.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center randomized crossover noninferiority trial enrolled 104 intubated adults meeting termination-of-resuscitation criteria without return of spontaneous circulation to receive BVV and MV in randomized order within a 5-min peri-termination window. Device-calculated VTi was recorded for 1 min per method during ongoing compressions. The primary outcome was the between-treatment difference in per-participant median VTi; the noninferiority margin was -150 mL (MV minus BVV).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 99 participants completing both periods, mean per-participant median VTi was 514.4 mL with BVV and 368.0 mL with MV; coefficients of variation were 40.1% and 28.3%. The adjusted mean difference was -146.2 mL (95% CI, -187.0 to -105.5). Because the lower bound crossed -150 mL, noninferiority was not demonstrated. Median VTi exceeded 10 mL/kg predicted body weight in 31.3% with BVV and 0% with MV, whereas values below 6 mL/kg occurred in 26.3% and 45.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Protocolized MV produced lower and less variable device-calculated VTi than BVV but did not meet noninferiority. BVV had a wider upper tail, whereas MV more often produced values below 6 mL/kg. The unvalidated analyzer and absence of clinical outcomes limit interpretation.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Clinical Trials Registry - India; CTRI/2024/08/072738.

articles.title: Inflammatory Biomarkers Comparison Between Breath-Hold and SCUBA Divers.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The pathogenesis of decompression sickness is multifactorial, involving bubbles and oxidative stress that lead to inflammatory responses. Ex vivo evidence indicates that oxidative stress occurs rapidly while at depth, prompting our hypothesis that biomarkers of inflammation would be similar between 12 subjects performing breath-hold (BH) dives lasting 1 to 2 minutes and 10 subjects performing Self-contained underwater breathing apparatus (SCUBA) (S) dives lasting 16 to 40 minutes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Consenting experienced diver research subjects traversed depths of 15 and 40 meters of seawater (msw). Laboratory measures were conducted on blood obtained prior to and following each dive. Vascular gas emboli were assessed by cardiac ultrasound.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Post-dive, there were significant elevations (p < 0.05, two-way within-subject ANOVA) in all divers for circulating levels of microparticles measured by flow cytometry, and post-diving microparticles (MPs) from S and BH divers exhibited equal propensity for activating human neutrophils. There also were significant elevations of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, IL-10 and vascular cell adhesion molecule measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays, and reactive oxygen species from electron paramagnetic resonance measurements. Mean fold-elevations for 15 msw BH dives were 1.51 ± 0.34 (standard deviation (SD)) and for S dives, 1.81 ± 0.67 (no significant difference, NS). For 40 msw dives, fold-elevation values for BH were 2.21 ± 0.81 and for S, 2.21 ± 0.86 (NS). For reactive oxygen species (ROS), TNF-α and IL-1β, some values were greater for S versus BH dives. Cardiac bubbles were rare for all divers with no significant difference between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We conclude that even among BH divers, oxidative stress and inflammatory responses to pressure occur rapidly. Some biomarkers are greater among S divers, which may reflect longer dive durations and higher systemic oxygenation.

articles.title: Young ERC Resuscitation Science Masterclass Journal Club article: "Estimating bias from withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment".
Changes in vital signs of hospitalized patients may not identify the need to escalate care as well as other bedside observations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Most Rapid Response Team activations rely on vital signs, frequently aggregated into weighted scoring systems, such as the National Early Warning Score (NEWS). Nevertheless, a substantial proportion of avoidable in-hospital deaths still result from delayed recognition of evolving pathophysiology and under-appreciation of patient or family concerns.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To compare the performance of NEWS with observations that can be rapidly assessed at the bedside without equipment or calculation, using death within 24 h as a surrogate marker for patients requiring immediate attention.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis of data collected prospectively on Rapid Response Team arrival to 4581 adult patients in general medical, surgical, or intermediate care units at a 450-bed regional medical center in California, USA.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight observations were identified that required no equipment to assess, which had a significant association with 24-h mortality; ranked by adjusted odds ratio these were (1) jaundice, (2) need for supplemental oxygen, (3) capillary refill time, (4) part or all of the body feeling cold, (5) objectively distressed breathing, (6) altered mentation, (7) dry skin, and (8) cyanosis. A logistic regression model of these 8 variables had a significantly higher discrimination for death within 24 h of Rapid Response Team arrival than NEWS (i.e., AUC of 0.790 SE 0.014 versus 0.707 SE 0.020, p < 0.0001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In patients who trigger a Rapid Response Team call, bedside information that can be obtained rapidly without equipment or calculation, may provide earlier and more reliable signals of illness severity than NEWS and other early warning scores based on traditional vital signs.

articles.title: Isolated midbrain neurocysticercosis presenting as trochlear nerve palsy.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Neurocysticercosis (NCC) is a neurological infection caused by the larval stage of the tapeworm Taenia solium. It can be found in the brain parenchyma or in the intraventricular and subarachnoid spaces and the spinal cord, giving rise to different clinical manifestations and prognoses. Isolated brainstem NCC is rare, with few cases reported in the literature. We describe a case of isolated NCC in the midbrain. The clinical presentation, diagnostic approach, and surgical management with histopathological confirmation are reported.

abstract.label: CASE DESCRIPTION
abstract.text: A 33-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 1-month history of increased diplopia during the vertical gaze. Neurological examination revealed a positive Bielschowsky's head tilt test, consistent with a right trochlear nerve palsy.
