Magnetic resonance imaging of the head revealed a cystic lesion in the left midbrain. The patient underwent a suboccipital craniotomy with a telovelar approach, and gross total resection of the lesion was achieved. Histopathological analysis revealed a brainstem cysticercus. Following surgery, the patient received albendazole and steroids. Conjugate eye movements were recovered during the 1-year follow-up period.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case report highlights the importance of considering NCC as a differential diagnosis for cystic lesions of the brain, even when they are found in atypical locations. Surgical excision should be considered in cases with mass effect or uncertain diagnosis.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics, Etiologies, and Outcomes of Adults Presenting With Altered Mental Status to the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.text: Background Altered mental status (AMS) is a common emergency presentation with diverse neurological, infectious, metabolic, toxicological, and systemic causes. Objective The objective of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, underlying etiologies, management patterns, and clinical outcomes of adults presenting to the emergency department with AMS, and to identify independent clinical factors associated with in-hospital mortality. Methods This retrospective cohort study was conducted at Allama Iqbal Teaching Hospital, Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan, from April 2024 to April 2026 and included 210 adult patients presenting with AMS. Demographic and baseline clinical characteristics, including age, gender, body mass index, smoking status, presenting symptoms, duration of AMS, known comorbidities, medication history, substance use, and relevant previous neurological or systemic illnesses, were recorded. Results Of 210 patients, 174 (82.9%) survived, and 36 (17.1%) died. The mean age was 61.74±16.64 years, and 118 (56.2%) were male. Neurological causes were most common (29.0%), followed by infectious (21.4%), metabolic/endocrine (16.2%), and toxicological causes (11.9%). Non-survivors were older than survivors (72.10±13.80 vs. 59.60±16.40 years, p<0.001) and had lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores (6.90±3.20 vs. 11.60±3.10, p<0.001), lower oxygen saturation (89.10±8.00% vs. 94.60±4.40%, p<0.001), and higher serum lactate levels (4.80±2.70 vs. 2.30±1.60 mmol/L, p<0.001). Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was required in 61 (29.0%) patients, while 42 (20.0%) required mechanical ventilation. Conclusion Altered mental status was associated with considerable ICU utilization and in-hospital mortality. Neurological and infectious causes predominated, while severe impairment of consciousness, elevated lactate, hypoxemia, hypotension, infectious etiology, and advanced age were independently associated with increased odds of mortality.

articles.title: Aortoduodenal Syndrome: A Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Causing a Small Bowel Obstruction With Stroke-Like Symptoms.

abstract.text: Aortoduodenal syndrome is a rare complication of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in which extrinsic compression of the duodenum results in gastric outlet or small bowel obstruction. We present the case of a 73-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with dizziness, profuse vomiting, cerebellar neurologic findings, and absent palpable lower-extremity pulses. Imaging demonstrated a large infrarenal AAA with findings concerning for contained rupture and extrinsic compression of the duodenum, resulting in gastric and duodenal dilation and at least a partial small bowel obstruction. The patient underwent emergent endovascular aortic repair with stent graft placement and was successfully discharged home on postoperative day 1. This case highlights the variable presentation of aortoduodenal syndrome, which may include gastrointestinal obstructive symptoms, hemodynamic instability, vascular compromise, and stroke-like exam findings. Given the rarity of this condition, clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for aortic pathology when these findings occur concurrently. Although computed tomography angiography is generally preferred when feasible, the choice of imaging modality should account for patient stability, availability, and diagnostic accuracy. Prompt recognition and definitive vascular intervention are essential to prevent catastrophic complications associated with ruptured AAA.

articles.title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: An Emergency Medicine-Focused Narrative Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a nontraumatic, noniatrogenic dissection of a coronary artery.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This narrative review provides emergency clinicians with a focused overview of the presentation, evaluation, and management of SCAD.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: SCAD is an underrecognized and potentially deadly disease that can result in coronary artery occlusion and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). It traditionally affects young-to-middle aged females, with increased risk in the peripartum period. Patients with SCAD most commonly present with signs and symptoms consistent with ACS, and a significant proportion of patients will have ST elevation myocardial infarction on electrocardiogram. Emergent cardiology consultation for angiography is necessary for diagnosis. Following diagnosis, a conservative approach is often followed, as most lesions heal spontaneously without intervention. Revascularization in the form of percutaneous coronary artery intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting is necessary in those with ongoing or recurrent ischemia with electrocardiogram or troponin changes, hemodynamic instability, ventricular dysrhythmias, or dissection of the left main coronary artery. Patients can have recurrence of SCAD, and noninvasive imaging modalities, such as coronary computed tomography, may be considered to diagnose recurrence.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Emergency physicians should consider SCAD in patients presenting with ACS, particularly younger women and those without traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Early recognition and prompt consultation with cardiology to guide selection of conservative vs. revascularization strategies are essential to optimize patient outcomes.

articles.title: Gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription after long bone fracture fixation is associated with increased 1-year nonunion.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Gabapentinoids are increasingly incorporated into multimodal analgesia after orthopaedic surgery, yet their impact on outcomes following fracture fixation remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between early postoperative gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription and clinical outcomes after operative fixation of closed long bone fractures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using TriNetX, we identified opioid-naïve and gabapentinoid-naïve adults undergoing intramedullary or plate-and-screw fixation of isolated closed diaphyseal tibia, humerus, or femur fractures. Patients prescribed gabapentin or pregabalin and opioids within three days after surgery were compared with patients receiving opioids alone. Propensity score matching (1:1) incorporated demographics, medical comorbidities, fracture location, fixation method, mental health disorders, and substance use disorders. Primary outcomes were prolonged (30-90 days) and chronic (90-180 days) postoperative opioid use. Secondary outcomes included 30-day emergency department (ED) visits and readmissions, and 1-year nonunion and reoperation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After matching, each cohort consisted of approximately 2000 patients (range, 1946-2012). Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with higher rates of prolonged (21.0% vs 16.1%; RR 1.31; p < 0.001) and chronic (9.8% vs 7.4%; RR 1.33; p = 0.007) postoperative opioid use. Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with fewer 30-day ED visits (25.1% vs 42.5%; RR 0.59; p < 0.001), while 30-day readmission rates were similar between cohorts (p = 0.174). One-year rates of nonunion (4.3% vs 1.9%; RR 2.21; p < 0.001) and reoperation (7.1% vs 4.2%; RR 1.68; p < 0.001) were significantly higher among patients receiving gabapentinoid-opioid therapy. In a sensitivity analysis that defined the opioid-only cohort based on the absence of gabapentinoid prescriptions during the first 3 postoperative days, rather than the 1-year postoperative medication window used in the primary analysis, the associations with prolonged and chronic opioid use and reoperation were no longer statistically significant, whereas the association with nonunion remained significant (RR 1.62; p = 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with fewer ED visits and higher rates of prolonged and chronic opioid use, nonunion, and reoperation; in sensitivity analysis, ED visits and nonunion remained significant, whereas opioid use and reoperation did not. These findings suggest that potential short-term analgesic benefits may be offset by adverse long-term outcomes, warranting caution and further study of gabapentinoid-opioid prescribing for acute perioperative fracture pain.

articles.title: Hereditary Angioedema Presenting With Acute Abdominal Symptoms and Progressive Upper Airway Compromise: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare but potentially life-threatening disorder that may present with abdominal symptoms and airway compromise, often mimicking surgical or allergic emergencies. We report the case of a 21-year-old female patient who presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and abdominal distension, followed by progressive facial and tongue swelling, muffled voice, and inspiratory stridor during observation. Initial laboratory testing showed no leukocytosis, electrolyte disturbance, or acid-base abnormality, while plain abdominal radiography showed no free intraperitoneal air or obstructive bowel gas pattern. The patient showed no clinical improvement with conventional anaphylaxis management, including epinephrine, corticosteroids, and antihistamines. A history of recurrent abdominal pain episodes, family history of swelling episodes, absence of urticaria or hypotension, and evolving angioedema prompted consideration of hereditary angioedema. Because disease-specific therapy was unavailable, two units of fresh frozen plasma were administered, followed by improvement in abdominal and upper airway symptoms. Endotracheal intubation and surgical intervention were not required. Following stabilization, low serum C4 and C1 esterase inhibitor levels supported the diagnosis of hereditary angioedema type I. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges associated with atypical presentations of hereditary angioedema and emphasizes the importance of early recognition, airway vigilance, and resource-appropriate management in emergency settings.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Suspected Rib Fractures in Blunt Thoracic Trauma: A Proposed Emergency Department Protocol.

abstract.text: Blunt thoracic trauma accounts for substantial emergency department admissions, with rib fractures representing a predominant injury pattern. Undetected or inadequately characterised rib fractures exacerbate the risks of hypoventilation, atelectasis, secondary pneumonia, and delayed pleuropulmonary complications, particularly in older adults. Conventional initial diagnostic evaluation relies heavily on plain chest radiography, which exhibits recognised diagnostic insensitivity for undisplaced cortical breaches and injuries traversing the costochondral junctions. Although computed tomography provides definitive anatomical resolution, routine acquisition in stable, minor blunt trauma imposes ionising radiation burdens, emergency department delays, and escalating healthcare expenditures. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) offers an accessible, radiation-free imaging adjunct possessing high sensitivity for superficial cortical breaches, chondral disruptions, and adjacent pleural complications. To address persistent diagnostic blind spots and documentation deficits in acute thoracic care, a structured emergency department POCUS workflow is proposed. The operational protocol integrates targeted high-frequency linear interrogation of symptomatic cortical margins, multi-zone transducer exclusion of pleural collections and pneumothorax, standardised sonographic criteria, and a structured clinical escalation algorithm. When integrated with comprehensive clinical assessment, this proposed POCUS protocol is intended to support acute trauma stratification, facilitate targeted regional anaesthesia, optimise clinical documentation, and complement conventional radiography in acute care environments. Prospective implementation studies are required to determine its diagnostic accuracy and impact on patient outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond Trauma: Splenic Rupture While Surfing Revealing Occult Infectious Mononucleosis.

abstract.text: When a young patient collapses with haemoperitoneum after physical activity, trauma is the presumptive diagnosis; Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infectious mononucleosis (IM) is easily overlooked. However, IM carries a rare but potentially fatal complication: splenic rupture, occurring in approximately 0.1-0.5% of symptomatic cases. We report the case of a previously healthy 21-year-old man who presented with sudden-onset abdominal pain and presyncope while surfing, without any fall or direct abdominal impact. Over the subsequent two hours, he developed progressive haemodynamic instability. A focused assessment with sonography for trauma (FAST) was positive for free intraperitoneal fluid. Following initial resuscitation, contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a grade V splenic injury, splenomegaly, and massive haemoperitoneum, prompting emergency splenectomy. Intraoperatively, the spleen was markedly enlarged, approximately three times the expected normal weight, friable, and extensively lacerated. The initial diagnosis was traumatic splenic rupture. However, on postoperative day three, persistent fever prompted investigation for an infectious cause. Serology confirmed acute EBV infection. This case highlights that severe splenic rupture occurring during ordinary physical activity, particularly when accompanied by splenomegaly disproportionate to the reported mechanism, should prompt postoperative evaluation for EBV infection, even in the absence of classic symptoms of IM. Earlier recognition of the underlying diagnosis might also help avoid unnecessary investigations and treatments during the postoperative period.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Intranasal Opioids vs. Intravenous Morphine for Acute Moderate-to-Severe Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intranasal (IN) opioids may provide noninvasive analgesia without delays associated with intravenous (IV) access, but their efficacy and safety vs. IV morphine remain uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To synthesize randomized evidence comparing IN opioids with IV morphine for acute moderate-to-severe pain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults or children with acute moderate-to-severe pain in emergency, prehospital, procedural, or postoperative settings. Eligible trials directly compared IN opioids with IV morphine. The primary outcome was change in pain score from baseline at 20 and 30 minutes. Secondary outcomes included rescue analgesia and adverse events. Outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMD) or risk ratios (RR) using random-effects models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ten RCTs involving 1164 participants were included. IN opioids showed comparable analgesic efficacy to IV morphine at 20 minutes (SMD = -0.05, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.24 to 0.14; p = 0.59; I² = 11.94%) and 30 minutes (SMD = -0.05, 95% CI: -0.24 to 0.15; p = 0.64; I² = 0.00%). Rescue analgesia was comparable (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.81-1.25; p = 0.98). No significant differences were observed in overall adverse events, serious adverse events, respiratory complications, hypotension, gastrointestinal events, dizziness, or rhinorrhea. Dysgeusia was borderline increased.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: IN opioids provide analgesic efficacy comparable to IV morphine at 20 and 30 minutes, with no clear increase in systemic adverse events. Larger trials should confirm safety for rare serious events and optimize dosing.

articles.title: Development and Initial Assessment of a Low-Cost Skin Tear Management Task Trainer for Paramedic Education.

abstract.text: Inappropriate management of skin tears can result in pain, delayed healing, infection, and reduced mobility. There is growing interest in expanding the paramedic scope of practice to include skin tear management. However, a lack of scalable, low-cost task trainers poses barriers to the implementation of structured training initiatives. Hence, this technical report describes the development of a scalable, low-cost skin tear management task trainer for paramedic education using digital technologies and additive manufacturing, and provides an initial assessment of its perceived acceptability. Three skin tear management task trainer prototypes (type 1, no skin loss; type 2, partial skin loss; type 3, complete skin loss) were co-developed by a team of researchers and an advanced care paramedic. The development process consisted of two iterative rounds of prototyping, testing, and refinement, after which 14 type 1 task trainers were fabricated, integrated into a paramedic training initiative, and assessed across three domains, including (1) self-efficacy, (2) realism, and (3) educational value. Quantitative and qualitative data were collected and analyzed. Approximate fabrication time per unit was 20-30 minutes of active labor and 80-90 minutes of curing, depending on the skin tear type. The total cost of the materials used to fabricate the task trainer was 35.29 Canadian dollars (including taxes). This amount excludes capital equipment, including the three-dimensional printer, computer-aided design and slicing software, and reusable molds and templates, which are amortized across multiple task trainers. Participants rated the task trainer highly for perceived self-efficacy (4.68/5), realism (4.64/5), and educational value (4.85/5). These scores reflect participants' perceptions rather than objective measures of skill acquisition. Qualitative data yielded three descriptive categories: (1) visual and tactile realism, (2) pathological realism, and (3) procedural complexity and adaptability. Overall, both quantitative and qualitative data indicated that participants perceived the task trainer as an acceptable training tool. This technical report demonstrates the feasibility of developing a scalable, low-cost skin tear management task trainer using digital technologies and additive manufacturing. Future work will focus on standardizing skin flap thickness and developing task trainers with varying skin tear shapes and sizes, anatomical locations, wound presentations, and levels of procedural complexity. Next steps involve implementing the task trainer broadly across paramedic training initiatives and formally evaluating its impact on procedural skill acquisition and maintenance, confidence, and decision-making abilities.

articles.title: Paraplegia Following Decompression Sickness (Caisson Disease): A Journey to Near-Complete Recovery.

abstract.text: Decompression sickness (DCS), also known as "Caisson disease," is a potentially life-threatening condition caused by the formation of inert gas bubbles during rapid decompression, most commonly affecting deep-sea divers. Neurological involvement, particularly spinal cord injury leading to paraplegia, represents one of the most severe manifestations. We report the case of a 44-year-old Filipino male professional diver who developed acute paraplegia following a routine dive. Despite adherence to decompression protocols, he experienced sudden-onset bilateral lower limb weakness during ascent. Initial management included oxygen therapy followed by hyperbaric oxygen therapy, after which he was referred for intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation within a few days. At presentation, the patient exhibited significant motor weakness with Medical Research Council grading of 2/5 in the left lower limb and 3/5 in the right lower limb, sensory loss below the T8 level, impaired bladder and bowel control, and complete dependence for mobility. Over a period of approximately three months of structured physiotherapy, including conventional therapy, robotic-assisted rehabilitation, neuromuscular stimulation, and gait training, he demonstrated remarkable functional recovery. Muscle strength improved to 4/5, with restoration of independent ambulation, improved sensory function, and regained bladder control. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, prompt hyperbaric therapy, and intensive rehabilitation in achieving near-complete recovery following severe neurological DCS.

articles.title: Audit of Conservative Management of Acute Ureteric Stones and Factors Influencing Treatment Outcome in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ureteric stones are a common cause of presentation to the emergency department. Management options include conservative therapy, urinary diversion (ureteric stent /nephrostomy), ureteroscopy, or extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy. Conservative management is known to have a high success rate in appropriately selected patients. This audit evaluates compliance with evidence-based standards in acute ureteric stones management and identifies factors influencing successful conservative treatment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective audit reviewed 143 patients who presented with renal colic to the Emergency Department between January and December 2025 and were offered conservative management. Data collected included patient demographics, laboratory findings, CT parameters, administration of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) and tamsulosin, re-presentation rates and treatment outcomes. The audit benchmarked against NICE guidelines. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics and appropriate statistical tests (t-test, Fisher's exact test and Mann-Whitney U test) with significance set at p < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 143 patients met the inclusion criteria. The average age of patients was 48 years. This comprised 101 males (70.63%) and 42 females (29.37%). NSAIDS were administered to 103 patients (72%) at presentation, while 49 patients (34.3%) with distal ureteric stones received tamsulosin. The success rate for the conservative therapy was 93.7%. Seventeen patients (11.9%) re-presented to the emergency department with colic. Among all the variables analyzed (C-reactive protein, white blood cell (WBC), creatinine, perinephric stranding, stone position), stone size was the only variable that showed a significant association with the outcome of conservative treatment (p< 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our audit findings revealed that NSAIDS and tamsulosin were sub-optimally administered in eligible patients; however, there was a very high rate of successful conservative treatment. Stone size was the only variable that showed significant association with successful conservative treatment.

articles.title: Barriers to Routine Use of Ultrasound-Guided Fascia Iliaca Blocks in High and Low-Resource Emergency Departments.

abstract.text: Background Ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia, such as fascia iliaca (FI) blocks, represents an alternative pain management strategy with decreased risk of oversedation and respiratory depression for emergency department patients. Methodology This is a two-site, descriptive, 12-month follow-up survey to evaluate FI block uptake and perceived barriers after training resident physicians at two academic training sites: an urban academic tertiary center in the United States and a resource-limited referral hospital in Malawi. Results In total, 34 participants from the US site and seven participants from the Malawi site completed the survey, with response rates of 87% and 28%, respectively. Nearly all participants agreed that FI blocks were useful and improved patient care (median = 4 on a five-point Likert scale), and the majority reported confidence in performing the procedure. Despite this, most participants had not performed an FI block in the preceding 12 months (62% US participants and 57% Malawian participants). Perceived barriers were rated with "time to perform the procedure" ranking the highest among US participants and "time to perform the procedure" and "patient disinterest/refusal" ranking the highest for Malawian participants. Lack of equipment or supervision was commonly noted as a reason Malawian participants had considered but not performed an FI block, but not for US participants. Patient comorbidities (25%) and orthopedic reluctance (20%) were reasons US participants had considered but not performed the procedure, but were not noted by Malawian participants. Conclusions Reported barriers varied according to location, and the findings suggest that barriers are multifactorial and highly context-dependent.

articles.title: Beyond Time Loss: Position-Specific Injury-to-Performance Pathways After Hand Fractures in Elite European Football.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hand fractures are common sports injuries, but the same diagnosis may carry different performance consequences according to how essential the hand is to a player's role. We investigated whether fracture burden and the broader injury-to-performance pathway differed by playing position, from injury phenotype and acute absence to competitive reintegration and sustained participation.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective matched cohort study linked manually validated public injury reports with league appearances from the five major leagues, Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, and Ligue 1 from 2007/08 through 2024/25. Of 35,952 injury records, 329 candidate records with possible hand or wrist injuries (0.9%) were reviewed, from which 148 fracture events (45.0% of candidates) in 142 players were retained. Primary analyses compared incidence, time loss, competitive return, and one-year participation after the publicly reported injury end. Exploratory analyses tested position-specific fracture phenotype and the time period from the public injury-end milestone to first subsequent appearance in one of the five major leagues.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fracture phenotype differed by position (chi-square = 21.48, P < .001; Cramér's V = 0.38): finger/phalangeal fractures accounted for 31 of 63 goalkeeper events (49.2%) versus 15 of 85 outfield events (17.6%) (odds ratio (OR), 4.52; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.15-9.52), whereas metacarpal fractures accounted for 10 of 63 goalkeeper events (15.9%) versus 34 of 85 outfield events (40.0%) (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.13-0.63). Goalkeepers faced greater time loss than outfielders, even within the same fracture subtype (position-by-subtype interaction, P = .407). Median time loss was 43 days among 63 goalkeeper events versus 18 days among 85 outfield events (adjusted ratio, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.58-2.79). By 90 days, 17 of 45 goalkeepers (37.8%) versus 55 of 68 outfield players (80.9%) had reappeared competitively. Of 103 fracture episodes with an observed appearance after the reported injury end, 14 of 35 goalkeeper episodes (40.0%) versus seven of 68 outfield episodes (10.3%) required more than 90 additional days to reappear (aOR, 6.94; 95% CI, 2.06-23.41; false discovery rate-adjusted q = .005). In the matched cohort, a 30% or greater participation decline occurred in 10 of 18 goalkeeper fracture cases (55.6%) versus 21 of 72 goalkeeper controls (29.2%) (aOR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.08-10.08), with a fracture-by-goalkeeper interaction OR of 5.74 (95% CI, 1.46-22.66); this interaction estimate was based on a small subgroup of 18 goalkeeper fracture cases.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The important positional signal extends beyond the already expected higher fracture incidence in goalkeepers. Playing position was associated with differences in fracture phenotype, acute burden, the transition from the publicly reported injury-end milestone to subsequent competitive selection, and subsequent participation. Return-to-play counseling should therefore distinguish the publicly reported injury-end milestone from subsequent competitive reintegration and incorporate role-specific hand function rather than calendar time alone.

articles.title: Administered opioids and benzodiazepines and the interpretation of positive trauma urine drug screens.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Urine drug screening (UDS) is routine in trauma care, and results populate trauma registries, quality review, and research. Trauma patients receive opioids and benzodiazepines before urine is collected, so a positive class-matched screen may reflect administered drug rather than pre-injury use. We estimated the magnitude of this effect by drug class and its impact on reported prevalence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort of all trauma patients at a Level II center, 2023-2024 (n = 2538), of whom 1420 (55.9%) underwent UDS. Medication administration was matched to the corresponding immunoassay channel, with fentanyl analyzed against its dedicated assay and opiate-assay-matched opioid against the opiate assay. Logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score, activation, intubation, and substance use disorder. Treatment-associated positives were estimated by g-computation with bootstrap confidence intervals; cannabinoids, amphetamines, and cocaine were negative controls.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Class-matched positivity greatly exceeded unexposed positivity: 70.0% versus 12.5% for the fentanyl assay (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 15.3, 95% CI 11.5-20.4), 59.0% versus 19.0% for the opiate assay given an opiate-assay-matched opioid (aOR 5.9), and 51.6% versus 8.9% for benzodiazepines (aOR 6.1). Restricting exposure to pre-hospital administration, which necessarily precedes collection, preserved the effect (fentanyl aOR 19.9). Negative controls showed minimal association (amphetamine aOR 1.1). By g-computation, an estimated 62.8% (56.9-68.6) of fentanyl-assay positives, 33.7% of opiate positives, and 29.3% of benzodiazepine positives were associated with administered drug. Any-positive prevalence was 64.4% overall and 37.3% among patients given neither class.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Administered fentanyl was associated with a model-estimated majority of positive fentanyl-assay screens; administered opiates and benzodiazepines were associated with smaller shares of their corresponding positive screens. Class-matched results should be interpreted alongside the medication record. These findings do not establish the source or analytical validity of an individual positive result.

articles.title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Awareness of Skin Donation Among Healthcare Professionals and Students.
articles.journal_full: Annals of burns and fire disasters

abstract.text: The usage of cadaveric allografts for the early coverage of burn wounds has helped to reduce morbidity and mortality. The main issue faced by skin banks is the paucity of skin donors due to a lack of awareness and misconceptions about skin donation. This study was conducted to assess awareness about skin donation among hospital care personnel and to increase awareness. After ethical committee clearance, all healthcare personnel of Kasturba Hospital and affiliated medical and paramedical institutes were included in the study. The Google Form Link, which included the questionnaire and an information sheet, was emailed to the participants. A total of 1006 participants took part in the study. 74.8% were aware of skin donation, with 51.6% willing to donate skin. 60% of the participants were aware that skin has to be harvested within 6 hours after death. 37.8% of participants were aware that HLA/ blood group matching was not required between skin bank donors and recipients, 88.7% knew that cadaveric skin can be used for burns and trauma patients, and 52.1% thought that cadaveric skin is a permanent solution for burn wounds. 76.9% of the study participants knew that malignancy is a contraindication. We observed that most participants were aware of skin donation and skin banking, and about 50% were willing to donate skin. Skin donation and banking as a topic in the undergraduate syllabus of medical, paramedical and nursing courses can increase awareness among health personnel.

articles.title: Pre-operative proton pump inhibitor use is associated with increased post-operative complications following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.journal_full: Journal of shoulder and elbow arthroplasty

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are frequently prescribed in the perioperative setting for gastrointestinal prophylaxis. However, emerging evidence suggests that pre-operative PPI exposure may influence post-operative outcomes through effects on host immune function, nutritional status, and bone metabolism. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between pre-operative PPI use and post-operative complications following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients undergoing primary anatomic TSA between 2005 and 2023 were stratified by pre-operative PPI use. Patients with a history of gastrointestinal bleeding were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed for demographic characteristics, modified frailty index variables, additional comorbidities, medications, and body mass index, yielding 7,075 patients per cohort. Ninety-day medical and 1-year and 2-year surgical complications were compared using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Within 90 days, PPI exposure was associated with increased risks of readmission and acute kidney injury. Rates of emergency department utilization were also higher among patients receiving PPIs, whereas differences in pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, post-operative infection, and stroke did not reach statistical significance. At 1 year, perioperative PPI use was associated with significantly higher rates of periprosthetic joint infection (1.7% vs. 1.2%; RR, 1.45; P = .008), dislocation (2.0% vs. 1.5%; RR, 1.33; P = .027), aseptic loosening (0.8% vs. 0.4%; RR, 1.71; P = .016), and mortality (1.2% vs. 0.9%; RR, 1.40; P = .044). At 2 years, PPI use remained associated with increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (2.4% vs. 1.6%; RR, 1.52; P < .001) and mortality (2.5% vs. 1.7%; RR, 1.48; P = .001). No significant differences were observed in revision arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, dislocation, or aseptic loosening at 2 years.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pre-operative PPI use following TSA was associated with increased early medical complications and higher rates of implant-related complications at midterm follow-up. These findings highlight the importance of careful medication review and risk stratification in patients undergoing anatomic TSA.

articles.title: Fluid-intolerance signals as bedside safety limits during early septic shock resuscitation: a multicenter randomized trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fluid resuscitation in early septic shock has a narrow therapeutic index. Signals of fluid intolerance are frequently present during early resuscitation, yet current resuscitation strategies do not incorporate them to guide when to limit fluid administration. We evaluated whether integrating fluid-intolerance signals as safety limits could reduce fluid-induced harm without compromising hypoperfusion resolution.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this multicenter, open-label randomized trial in three Chilean ICUs, mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock, persistent hypoperfusion, fluid responsiveness, and at least one high-risk criterion for fluid-induced harm were randomized 1:1 to a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy or standard care during a 6-hour protocol window. In the intervention arm, before each bolus, fluid-intolerance signals (lung ultrasound score, VExUS, E/lateral e', and central venous pressure) were graded as traffic-light: green received a 500-mL bolus, yellow 250 mL, and red no further fluid. Standard care delivered 500-mL boluses while hypoperfusion and fluid responsiveness persisted. The primary outcome was the change in PaO2:FiO2 from baseline to 6 h (ΔPaO2:FiO2).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Recruitment was discontinued before the planned sample size was reached because continued enrollment was no longer feasible. Among 113 screened patients, 36 of a planned 62 were randomized, and 35 were analyzed (18 standard care, 17 intervention). The intervention group received a lower protocol bolus volume during the 6-hour intervention window than the standard-care group (250 [125-500] vs. 650 [500-1500] mL; between-group difference, - 500 mL [95% CI, - 750 to - 250]). Cumulative fluid exposure from pre-randomization through the end of the protocol window was similar between groups (3375 [2375-3875] vs. 3750 [1875-4851] mL; between-group difference, - 150 mL [95% CI, - 1470 to 1250]). The primary outcome favored the intervention: median ΔPaO2:FiO2 was 40.5 [24.0-58.5] versus - 37.9 [-69.2 to -12.5]; p < 0.001 (between-group median difference + 78.3 points; 95% CI 50.5 to 110.0), and 0-6-hour changes in lactate and capillary refill time did not differ.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Because the trial was stopped early, the effect of a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy on oxygenation remains uncertain. A larger trial would be needed to determine whether this strategy improves oxygenation. Such a trial appears feasible.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT06568744, registered August 21, 2024.

articles.title: Changes in Antiviral Treatment for Hospitalized Adults with Influenza in United States Emergency Departments.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early administration of an antiviral reduces influenza-related complications, and multiple guidelines recommend prompt antiviral treatment for all hospitalized patients with influenza. However, there is limited data on early antiviral treatment within the Emergency Department (ED).

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Our epidemiological study assesses temporal trends in the initiation of antiviral treatment for adults hospitalized with influenza in the ED and identifies factors associated with nonadherence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study examined antiviral treatment patterns among adults hospitalized with influenza in a U.S. ED from 2016 to 2025, using Epic Cosmos. Patients with ICD-10-coded or laboratory-confirmed influenza A/B were included. The primary outcome was the proportion of hospitalized patients who received oseltamivir, peramivir, baloxavir, or zanamivir in the ED.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 483,459 hospitalized ED patients with influenza, 416,982 (86.25%) received an antiviral in the ED. Antiviral treatment ranged from 72.7% in 2021 to 91.08% in 2020, rebounding to 85.11% in 2025. Differences in demographics between treated and untreated patients were observed across age, ethnicity, race, and spoken language. The likelihood of antiviral therapy was lower in the South (odds ratios [OR] 0.95; 95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.93-0.97) and West (OR 0.78; 95% CI 0.76-0.80) compared to the Northeast of the United States. The rate of antiviral treatment was moderately correlated with the national rate of influenza positivity in the ED (Pearson correlation 0.59).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although prompt administration of an antiviral for hospitalized patients reduces influenza-related complications, antiviral administration is not universal in the ED. Our study highlights a critical gap that requires urgent implementation of mitigation strategies.

articles.title: Prevalence of Large Vessel Occlusion Across Contemporary Stroke Care Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In the post-late-window thrombectomy era, reliable characterization of the range of large vessel occlusion (LVO) prevalence is essential to inform stroke systems of care, prehospital triage strategies, and population-level modeling. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to characterize the distribution of reported LVO prevalence across contemporary acute ischemic stroke (AIS) care environments and to summarize context-specific estimates.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library for articles published between January 1, 2018, and August 25, 2025, that reported the prevalence of LVO among adult patients with AIS. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to summarize the distribution of reported study-level LVO prevalence across heterogeneous care settings rather than to estimate a single common prevalence. Subgroup analyses were performed according to country income level, mode of hospital arrival, and diagnostic category in suspected stroke cohorts.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 18 studies were included, comprising 460 176 patients with AIS, of whom 135 315 patients had LVO. Reported study-level LVO prevalence ranged from 11.2% to 40%. The random-effects summary across all included care environments was 23.1% (95% CI, 19.6-27.03). Studies from high-income countries yielded a pooled LVO prevalence of 23.8% (95% CI, 20.3-27.7). In suspected stroke/stroke-alert populations, the estimated prevalence of AIS was 54.6% (95% CI, 44.3-64.5), hemorrhagic strokes were 12.3% (95% CI, 9.8-15.4), and stroke mimics were 23.3% (95% CI, 14.5-35.2). Among emergency medical services transported patients, the estimated prevalence of LVO was 29.3% (95% CI, 24.6-34.4).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Across contemporary studies, LVO prevalence among AIS populations varied widely by care environment. The overall estimate of ≈1 in 4 should be interpreted as a summary across heterogeneous care settings rather than a single true prevalence. Higher LVO prevalence in patients transported by emergency medical services and prehospital triage-selected populations highlights the need for context-specific estimates when developing stroke triage strategies and destination decision tools.

articles.title: Survival From Traumatic Cardiac Arrest After Sequential Decompression of Dual-Tension Thoracic Physiology Without Chest Compressions.

abstract.text: Traumatic pulseless electrical activity arrest from simultaneous dual-tension thoracic physiology-bilateral tension pneumothorax and tension pneumomediastinum-with concurrent oropharyngeal hematoma causing airway obstruction has not been described as a unified presentation in the published literature. We report a 28-year-old male who sustained penetrating machete injuries producing this presentation and arrested in pulseless electrical activity on arrival. A sequential surgical resuscitation was performed without external chest compressions: hemostasis and evacuation of an oropharyngeal hematoma restored ventilation, with return of peripheral photoplethysmographic signal consistent with pseudo-pulseless electrical activity physiology; bilateral finger thoracostomies achieved pleural decompression; digital exploration through the manubrial wound vented tension pneumomediastinum, producing an audible air rush, immediate resolution of jugular venous distension, and confirmed return of spontaneous circulation. The patient ambulated independently within hours of arrest and was discharged neurologically intact on day 7. This case illustrates that mechanically mediated pulseless electrical activity arrest from dual thoracic obstructive physiology may be reversible by sequential surgical decompression, and that persistent jugular venous distension following pleural decompression may signal residual mediastinal tension warranting urgent decompression.

articles.title: The Effect of Mobile X-Ray Services Access in Long-Term Care Facilities on Residents' Hospital Encounters.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Use of mobile X-ray (MXR) imaging in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) has the potential to reduce emergency department (ED) presentations and hospital admissions. In 2019, a subsidy was introduced by the Australian Government Medicare Benefits Schedule to encourage MXR use in this setting. This study compared the risk of unplanned and specific ED and hospital admissions among residents of LTCFs with and without MXR access.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: This study was a retrospective cohort analysis using data from the Registry of Senior Australians National Historical Cohort.

abstract.label: SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Older (≥65 years) nonindigenous individuals who were residents in an LTCF in 4 Australian geographical regions between November 1, 2019 and June 30, 2020.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: ED presentations and unplanned hospital admissions (and types of hospitalizations) were outcomes of interest. MXR access in LTCF was the exposure of interest. Propensity score matching at the LTCF level and multivariable negative binomial regression were used to estimate the risk ratio (RR) of the outcomes in LTCFs with and without MXR access.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 1157 LTCFs with 118,172 resident episodes during the study period, with a median age of 86 years (interquartile range, 80-90), 63.5% (N = 75,035) women, and 53.3% (N = 62,987) living with dementia. Analysis of the propensity score-matched cohort (325 LTCFs with and 325 without MXR access) showed no differences in most ED presentations (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.98-1.12) or unplanned hospitalizations (RR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.98-1.09) in LTCFs with or without MXR access, except for ED presentations for falls, which were higher in those with MXR access (RR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.02-1.27).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Access to subsidized MXRs in LTCFs was not associated with a reduction in ED presentations or unplanned hospitalizations. Further evidence on the outcomes of MXR use, which considers resident experiences and concerns, is required.

articles.title: Comparison of Soccer-Related Injuries at US Emergency Departments Between High School-Aged and College-Aged Athletes: A 10-Year NEISS Analysis, 2015-2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Soccer is widely played in the United States (US), yet contemporary national data comparing soccer-related emergency department (ED) injuries between high school-aged and college-aged athletes remain limited.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To provide a comparative assessment of soccer-related injuries among high school-aged and college-aged athletes and to characterize the burden of these injuries on US EDs.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Descriptive epidemiological study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The National Electronic Injury Surveillance System was queried for soccer-related injuries among patients aged 14 to 23 years from 2015 to 2024. Patients aged 14 to 18 years were categorized as high school-aged and those aged 19 to 23 years as college-aged. Weighted national estimates were calculated using National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) sampling weights. Participation denominators were derived from National Federation of State High School Associations boys' and girls' soccer participation for the high school-aged group and National Collegiate Athletic Association men's and women's soccer participation across Divisions I, II, and III for the college-aged group. Incidence rates were expressed per 100 participants, and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% CIs were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 29,144 NEISS cases corresponded to a weighted national estimate of 877,548 soccer-related injuries treated in US EDs. High school-aged athletes accounted for 687,302 injuries, whereas college-aged athletes accounted for 190,246. The incidence rate was 8.19 per 100 participants among high school-aged athletes and 34.73 among college-aged athletes (IRR, 4.24; 95% CI, 4.22-4.26), indicating an approximately 4-fold higher per-participant rate among college-aged athletes. Per-participant rates were higher in the college-aged group in every study year and across all body region, diagnosis, and disposition categories. The ankle (157,321 injuries; 17.9%), knee (137,030; 15.6%), head (127,695; 14.6%), and wrist (52,940; 6%) were the most frequently injured body regions; strains and sprains were the most common diagnosis (262,189; 29.9%). Most injuries were treated and discharged (96.8%), whereas transfers or admissions were uncommon (1.9%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: College-aged athletes had over a 4-fold higher rate of soccer-related ED injury than high school-aged athletes, despite high school-aged athletes accounting for most total ED visits. These findings highlight important differences between absolute ED burden and participation-indexed injury rates. They may help inform injury-prevention priorities, ED counseling, and postinjury follow-up strategies across scholastic and collegiate soccer populations.

articles.title: Emergency Department Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract.text: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a common concern in the Emergency Department (ED) and has a wide variety of presentations. The initial stage of ED workup involves the calculation of pretest probability, using a clinical calculator or experienced clinician gestalt, and then progresses to diagnostic testing, which may involve D-Dimer measurement or radiographic imaging (typically computed tomography and ultrasonography). Management of PE depends primarily on the function of the right ventricle and the presence of shock. Low-risk PEs can be treated with outpatient oral anticoagulation, while patients who are in shock should undergo systemic thrombolysis.

articles.title: Complicated acute cholecystitis: Diagnostic imaging in the emergency department.

abstract.text: When appropriately diagnosed and treated, the prognosis of acute cholecystitis (AC) is excellent. However, complicated forms of AC-including gangrenous, haemorrhagic, emphysematous and acalculous-have high morbidity and mortality, posing clinical and radiological challenges. Imaging plays a key role in diagnosis according to the 2018 Tokyo Guidelines, which recommend ultrasound as the initial technique due to its availability and lack of radiation. However, its sensitivity for detecting complications may be limited. Complicated AC may be masked by comorbidities, or confused with other diagnoses, leading to perforation or even fistulisation with adjacent structures. Urgent evaluation with ultrasound and, if necessary, with computed tomography (CT) is essential for early diagnosis and management to prevent serious consequences. This work reviews the pathophysiology of AC complications and ultrasound and CT findings, highlighting the complementary role of CT when ultrasound results are inconclusive.

articles.title: Echocardiography and Point-of-care Ultrasound in Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract.text: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a life-threatening condition with a wide range of clinical presentations from asymptomatic cases to sudden death. While computed tomography pulmonary angiography remains the diagnostic gold standard in hemodynamically stable patients, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), and cardiac point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) are valuable in unstable patients and serve key roles in risk assessment and guiding therapy. This article consolidates current evidence, society guidelines, and quantitative data surrounding the diagnostic utility, prognostic implications, therapeutic influence, and practical applications of TTE, TEE, and cardiac POCUS in the evaluation and management of PE.

articles.title: The Omokhodion Method: A High-Success, Low-Force Technique for Shoulder Dislocations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shoulder dislocation is a common emergency presentation, and reduction may be complicated by pain, involuntary muscle guarding, patient positioning, clinician experience, associated injury, and the need for analgesia or procedural sedation. Because no single reduction maneuver is optimal for every patient or clinical setting, emergency physicians benefit from having multiple safe, reproducible, low-force techniques available.

abstract.label: CLINICAL PROBLEM
abstract.text: Many established reduction methods rely to varying degrees on traction, leverage, sustained positioning, or sequential rotation. Although these approaches may be effective, escalating force can worsen pain and protective muscular contraction in some patients, making reduction more difficult.

abstract.label: TECHNIQUE
abstract.text: This technical report describes the Omokhodion method, a standardized low-force shoulder reduction technique based on upright positioning when feasible, continuous two-point support of the affected extremity, maintenance of approximately 90° of elbow flexion, supported abduction, controlled external rotation, gradual adduction toward the ipsilateral hip, and final internal rotation across the abdomen. Movement is performed slowly within the patient's tolerated range, and progression is paused when pain or guarding increases. Forceful longitudinal traction and abrupt leverage are avoided.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The proposed biomechanical rationale is that continuous limb support, controlled positioning, progressive soft-tissue accommodation, and deliberate pacing may reduce gravitational loading and counterproductive muscle guarding while facilitating restoration of glenohumeral alignment. The method is intended to complement, not replace, established shoulder reduction techniques, and standard principles of neurovascular assessment, analgesia, procedural sedation, imaging, immobilization, and orthopedic consultation remain applicable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Omokhodion method provides a structured and reproducible low-force option for shoulder dislocation reduction and procedural education. Prospective clinical and biomechanical studies are needed to define its effectiveness, safety, optimal indications, reproducibility, and comparative performance relative to established reduction techniques.

articles.title: The need for enhanced disaster preparedness in emergency medicine.
articles.journal_full: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association

articles.title: Conference on Medical Education and Research Writings during Arbaeen at College of Medicine, University Warith Al-Anbiyaa, and University of Karbala 22-23 and 26 July 2026.
articles.journal_full: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association

abstract.text: An academic programme spanning three days took place in Karbala, Iraq on 22-23 and 26 July 2026, linking medical education and training in scientific writing to the service orientation of the Arbaeen pilgrimage. Workshops held at the College of Medicine, University of Warith Al-Anbiyaa and at the College of Medicine, University of Kerbala brought together Iraqi and Pakistani educators and clinicians to discuss responsible artificial intelligence, qualitative research, scientific writing, curriculum integration, regenerative medicine, precision geriatric care, radiology, surgery, and disaster management. Practical workshops enabled participants to move away from information transfer to application. A critical synthesis revealed four interlinked themes: service and scholarship as an integrated continuum; learning by doing; responsible innovation; and academic solidarity across borders. The programme provided a forum for future mentorship and collaboration in research but future events will need to include prospective evaluation and follow-up of the results of the academic activities. These areas can shape the planning and evaluation of future conferences.

articles.title: Integrating clinical care and medical education during the 2026 Arbaeen mass gathering.
articles.journal_full: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association

abstract.text: The Arbaeen pilgrimage in Karbala, Iraq, creates substantial temporary healthcare demand while providing opportunities for education in mass-gathering medicine. During the 18th Annual Arbaeen Medical Mission, Imamia Medics International operated a multidisciplinary Medical Camp and Teaching Field Hospital from July 28 to August 4, 2026. During this period, 32,064 patient encounters were recorded, comprising 27,189 medical, emergency and specialtycare encounters, 2,525 eye-care encounters and 2,350 dental encounters. Clinical service was integrated with structured medical education. Forty-four medical students from two Iraqi universities participated in scheduled clinical rotations with supervised clinical exposure and structured assessment. Fourteen educational programmes were delivered through 15 teaching sessions, generating 172 participantattendances and covering clinical medicine, procedural skills, emergency response, trauma, mass-casualty management and artificial intelligence. This experience demonstrates the feasibility of integrating high-volume mass-gathering healthcare with structured clinical education and workforce development through a Teaching Field Hospital model.

articles.title: A Framework for Standardizing Emergency Triage for Chronic Disease Exacerbations in Youth Held in Custody: Sickle Cell Disease as a Model.

abstract.text: Children and adolescents in custody are entitled to prompt medical care, but few specialty organizations provide specific guidance for managing acute episodes of chronic illnesses in detention settings. We reviewed evidence-based guidelines for six severe pediatric chronic conditions and found minimal accommodations for custody-specific implementation. Using sickle cell disease (SCD) as a case study, we outline a practical approach that uses Emergency Severity Index level 2 as an objective triage anchor for time-sensitive clinical events, then assesses whether evidence-based guidelines for SCD recommendations can be operationalized given staffing, scope of practice, formulary, and transportation limitations.

articles.title: Genetic susceptibility to decompression sickness: molecular mechanisms, genomic advances, and precision prevention strategies.

abstract.text: Decompression sickness (DCS) is a multisystem disorder caused by rapid environmental pressure reduction, which causes the dissolved gas in the body to come out as bubbles, and subsequent multi-organ injury. A notable feature is great individual variation in sensitivity. Under identical pressure exposure conditions, some individuals develop severe DCS while others remain unaffected, indicating that host genetic background may play an important modulatory role in DCS. Recently, using selectively bred DCS‑resistant rat lines along with multi‑omics platforms such as genomics, transcriptomics, miRNomics and metabolomics, the molecular underpinnings of the susceptibility have started to emerge. Polymorphisms in innate‑immunity genes like MYD88 and NFKB1, variants in transthyretin (TTR), miRNA regulatory networks, and typical intestinal metabolic profiles are proposed as candidate elements for a multi-layered susceptibility architecture, although most current evidence comes from animal studies and needs to be validated in humans. In parallel, candidate biomarkers such as plasma gelsolin (pGSN), peripheral‑blood tau, and circulating extracellular vesicles offer potential tools for individual risk quantification. This review gathers recent progress, critically appraises the strength and independence of the underlying evidence, proposes a four‑layer susceptibility framework integrating genetic, molecular/epigenetic, metabolic/microbial, and physiological factors, contrasts this framework with classical bubble‑centered models, and discusses research gaps and translational priorities.

articles.title: Alignment with ambition: knowledge, attitude, and perceived preparedness of undergraduate nursing and paramedical students towards WHO 90-70-90 cervical cancer elimination targets: a comparative study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) has launched the ambitious 90-70-90 strategy for cervical cancer elimination, aiming by 2030 to achieve 90% vaccination coverage in girls by age 14, 70% screening coverage in women at ages 35 and 45, and 90% treatment for identified cases. These objectives may remain aspirational without adequate knowledge and preparedness of healthcare trainees, especially nursing and paramedical students. This study compares the knowledge, attitude, and perceived preparedness of undergraduate nursing and paramedical students to implement the WHO's cervical cancer elimination strategy. Perceived preparedness was assessed as a distinct construct from general attitude, recognizing that positive attitudes do not necessarily translate to confidence in practical implementation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted among 304 final-year students: Group A (nursing students, n = 152) and Group B (paramedical students, n = 152) across three healthcare institutions in Jammu and Kashmir, India. A 35-item structured questionnaire (25 knowledge items, 10 attitude/perceived preparedness items) was used. Knowledge was assessed across four domains aligned with WHO targets: basic virology and burden, HPV vaccination, screening and triage, and WHO targets. Attitude and perceived preparedness were evaluated on a 5-point Likert scale. Bivariate analysis (chi-square, independent t-test) and multivariate logistic regression were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean knowledge score across all participants was 58.7% (SD = 16.2). Nursing students demonstrated significantly higher knowledge (65.3%, SD = 14.1) compared to paramedical students (52.1%, SD = 15.3), with a mean difference of 13.2% and p < 0.001. Significant knowledge gaps were observed regarding WHO recommended strategies in which only 31.6% of nursing and 12.5% of paramedical students were aware of the single-dose HPV vaccine recommendation (p < 0.001), and: 44.1% of nursing vs. 21.7% of paramedical students correctly identified HPV DNA testing as the primary screening method(p < 0.001). Knowledge of WHO 90-70-90 targets was particularly low, with less than 35% of students in either group were able to correct to specify the targets. While as 80% of students in both groups held positive attitude towards cervical cancer elimination, a deficit in perceived preparedness was evident. Only 33.6% of nursing and 14.5% of paramedical students felt prepared to educate patients about WHO strategy. Multivariate analysis confirmed that having a dedicated cervical cancer lecture was the strongest independent predictor of good knowledge (aOR = 5.18, 95% CI 3.02-8.89) and high perceived preparedness (aOR = 3.91, 95% CI 2.23-6.86).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Current health science curricula are misaligned with the competencies required to achieve the WHO's 90-70-90 elimination targets. The findings suggest an urgent need for standardized interdisciplinary curriculum reform that integrates contemporary elimination strategies and equips future healthcare professionals with the knowledge and practical confidence to act as effective agents of cervical cancer elimination. However, as this is a cross-sectional study, interventional studies are needed to evaluate the effectiveness of specific educational strategies.

articles.title: Bougie guided versus Endotracheal tube with Stylet guided intubation in critically injured patients with Difficult airway characteristics (BEST trial): randomised clinical trial.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency airway management in critically injured trauma patients is frequently complicated by distorted anatomy, airway contamination, cervical spine immobilisation, and prior airway manipulation. Although bougie and stylet are commonly used adjuncts for tracheal intubation, evidence comparing their effectiveness in difficult trauma airways remains limited. We aimed to compare first-pass intubation success between bougie-guided and stylet-guided tracheal intubation in critically injured trauma patients with predefined difficult airway characteristics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective randomised clinical trial, 188 adult critically injured trauma patients requiring emergency tracheal intubation and having at least one predefined difficult airway characteristic were randomised to bougie-guided intubation (Group B, n = 94) or stylet-guided intubation (Group S, n = 94). All first-attempt intubations were performed by trauma anaesthesia senior residents using video laryngoscopy and a standardised drug-assisted delayed sequence intubation protocol. The primary outcome was first-pass intubation success. Secondary outcomes included time to intubation, rescue airway interventions, need for alternate adjunct or front-of-neck access, and peri-intubation complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: First-pass intubation success was achieved in 67 of 94 patients (71.3%) in Group B and 63 of 94 patients (67.0%) in Group S, corresponding to an absolute difference of 4.3% points (95% CI, - 8.9 to 17.2; p = 0.53). Time to successful first-attempt intubation was similar between groups (39.55 ± 11.72 s in Group B versus 37.97 ± 13.54 s in Group S; mean difference 1.58 s, 95% CI - 2.80 to 5.97; p = 0.48). Emergency front-of-neck access was required in one patient in Group B. Oesophageal intubation occurred in five patients (5.3%) in Group S and in none in Group B; this difference did not reach statistical significance using Fisher's exact test (p = 0.059). On multivariable logistic regression, polytrauma with facial fractures was associated with increased odds of first-pass intubation failure (adjusted OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.10-5.83; p = 0.028).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In selected trauma patients with predefined difficult-airway characteristics undergoing protocolised delayed sequence intubation with video laryngoscopy, no statistically significant difference in first-pass success was observed between bougie-guided and stylet-guided intubation. Oesophageal intubation occurred only in the stylet group, an exploratory finding that requires confirmation in larger studies.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: The trial was approved by the Institute Ethics Committee (IEC-INT-2022/MD-543) and registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2022/11/047043).

articles.title: Prognostic value of shock index, modified shock index, and age shock index in emergency department patients with hemoptysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hemoptysis is a challenging respiratory emergency ranging from mild symptoms to life-threatening conditions. Early identification of patients at risk for hemodynamic collapse and massive bleeding is crucial for guiding admission to respiratory wards or intensive care units. This study aimed to assess the prognostic performance of the shock index (SI), modified shock index (MSI), and age shock index (ASI) in predicting 30-day mortality and life-threatening hemoptysis (LTH).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult patients admitted to the ED with hemoptysis. SI, MSI, and ASI were calculated using initial vital signs. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality; the secondary outcome was LTH. To evaluate predictive performance, we performed multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and Cox proportional hazards models. Exploratory LASSO regression was used only for preliminary screening of candidate variables.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 592 patients, the 30-day mortality rate was 8.4%. All three indices demonstrated significant discrimination for mortality (AUCs: 0.854 for ASI, 0.836 for SI, 0.819 for MSI). ASI achieved the highest IDI (0.057) and NRI (0.943) improvement over the base model. In Cox regression, a 1-SD increase in the ASI was associated with a higher hazard of mortality (HR: 1.813; 95% CI: 1.449-2.268) and the highest model concordance (C-index: 0.870). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed significantly lower survival in high-risk groups (log-rank p < 0.001 for all indices). For the secondary outcome (LTH), simple hemodynamic indices (SI and MSI) outperformed ASI, which was not an independent predictor in multivariable analysis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Each index demonstrates a distinct prognostic strength in the management of hemoptysis. The ASI may have utility for initial triage risk assessment due to its association with 30-day mortality, whereas the MSI and the SI appear more reflective of acute hemodynamic crises such as LTH. These findings suggest that a tailored application of shock indices may contribute to improved risk stratification in hemoptysis management; however, this potential two-tiered approach warrants further prospective validation.

articles.title: Impact of timing on outcomes following redo-sternotomy after initial CABG or valvular surgery.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The optimal timing of reoperation for those who need repeat coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and valve surgery is not well established. Early re-entries may be technically challenging due to adhesions and incomplete healing, while delayed interventions may expose patients to progressive cardiac disease.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients undergoing redo-sternotomy for CABG and valve surgery were identified from the TriNetX database and categorized into three cohorts based on the interval from their initial sternotomy: <1 year, 1-5 years, and > 5 years. Redo-sternotomies performed < 30 days after the initial procedure were excluded, as these typically represent early interventions for acute complications rather than planned reoperations. Two independent propensity score-matched analyses compared < 1 year vs. 1-5 years and 1-5 years vs. > 5 years, with separately matched 1-5 years cohorts for each comparison. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on demographics, comorbidities, prior cardiac procedures, medications, and laboratory parameters including BMI. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and emergency department or hospital readmissions. Secondary outcomes included postoperative infection, atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury, dialysis, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, and cerebrovascular events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After PSM in the < 1 year vs. 1-5 years analysis (N = 305 in each group), redo-sternotomy within 1 year showed no significant differences in mortality, MACCE or readmissions. Combined cerebrovascular events were significantly reduced in the < 1 year group. In the 1-5 years vs. > 5 years analysis (N = 439 in each group), outcomes were similar between groups, with no significant differences in mortality, MACCE, or readmissions. Atrial fibrillation was significantly higher in the 1-5 years group. All other secondary outcomes, including combined cerebrovascular events, were comparable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Redo-sternotomy within 1 year appears to be equally safe compared to later intervals, with comparable rates of adverse events, including mortality, MACCE, readmissions, postoperative infection, or AKI.

articles.title: Emergency obstetric referrals in public primary health care centres in Benin City, Nigeria: a qualitative study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to assess the mechanisms, procedures, and processes of the referral system for emergency obstetric care (EmOC) in public primary health care centres (PHCs) in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria, with recommendations offered to address the challenges.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative study was conducted in Egor Local Government Area (LGA), purposively selected from the three LGAs in Benin City. From the 11 public PHCs in Egor LGA, nine were selected based on their provision of maternal care and performance of EmOC in the three months preceding this study. Nine key informant interviews were conducted using a semi-structured interview guide, with one nurse or midwife, serving as a senior health care provider or health facility manager, selected as the participant per PHC. Data saturation was achieved with this sample. The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically using NVivo V.12.0 software.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From the responses of all the participants, three themes emerged following data analysis: (1) mechanisms, procedures, and processes for the referral of obstetric emergencies. From many of the participants' responses, the associated categories were availability of emergency transport vehicles; process for receiving feedback and follow-up, among others; (2) Challenges encountered with the referral system. From many of the participants' responses, the associated categories were infrastructural deficits such as nonavailability of ambulances. For some participants, other challenges mentioned were presence of bad roads leading to the PHCs; logistics constraints such as shortage of staff and stock-out of referral letters; and patient-related challenges such as financial constraints, and preference for traditional care; and (3) recommendations for improving the referral systems. From many of the participants' responses, the associated categories were strengthening the infrastructure through addressing logistics and resource challenges.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Public PHCs in Egor LGA have existing procedures for referring obstetric emergencies. However, challenges exist in terms of nonavailability of written referral protocols and emergency transportation, poor two-way communication, inadequate staffing and logistics, thereby limiting its effectiveness. Strengthening these health system components could improve the quality of referrals and contribute to reducing preventable maternal mortality in Edo State, with implications for the rest of Nigeria.

articles.title: CT-Defined diagnosis and laparoscopic management of isolated liver and gallbladder injury with hemobilia after penetrating trauma: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Penetrating gallbladder injury is rare and usually occurs with associated intra-abdominal injury. In hemodynamically responsive trauma patients, distinguishing hemobilia from hollow viscus or other adjacent organ injury may be challenging, and multiphasic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) can play an important role in clarifying the source of bleeding and guiding management.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 28-year-old male presented following a stab wound to the right upper quadrant with initial hemodynamic instability that resolved with resuscitation.
