CT demonstrated a segment IVb liver laceration extending into the gallbladder, with arterial-phase contrast extravasation into the gallbladder lumen and progressive venous-phase tracking through the biliary system into the duodenum. This phase-dependent pattern localized the bleeding source to the gallbladder and indicated hemobilia rather than hollow viscus injury. The patient underwent fully laparoscopic exploration, methylene blue instillation to exclude gastrointestinal perforation, and laparoscopic cholecystectomy. No additional injuries were identified. The key operative steps are illustrated in the accompanying video. Recovery was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 2.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In selected hemodynamically stable patients with isolated penetrating hepatobiliary injury, multiphasic CT may help localize the bleeding source and support single-stage laparoscopic management when gallbladder-origin hemobilia is identified without additional injuries.

articles.title: End-of-life care patterns associated with hospital-based palliative care consultation: a single-center cohort with national data linkage.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In routine oncology practice, palliative care (PC) is commonly delivered through hospital-based consultation services integrated within existing workflows. Evidence describing real-world end-of-life (EOL) care patterns associated with consultation-based palliative care remains limited. We examined EOL care patterns associated with hospital-based palliative care consultation using linked clinical and nationwide data.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study used linked data from a tertiary hospital and the Korean National Health Insurance Service. We included 18,048 decedents with advanced lung, stomach, colorectal, liver, or pancreaticobiliary cancer between 2018 and 2022. To minimize selection bias, 1:2 propensity score matching was performed. Outcomes included advance care planning documentation completion, aggressive EOL interventions, hospice utilization, and medical costs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After matching 4,102 patients with PC consultation and 7,910 controls, the consultation group showed significantly higher completion of advance statements (58.0% vs. 32.1%) and more patient-led decisions. During the final month of life, the consultation group had significantly fewer intensive care unit admissions (4.9% vs. 10.3%), emergency department visits (48.6% vs. 54.4%), and cardiopulmonary resuscitations (2.9% vs. 10.7%) (all P < 0.001). Hospice utilization was substantially higher in the consultation group (73.2% vs. 19.5%). Furthermore, PC consultations were associated with significantly lower medical costs during the final month and last two weeks of life.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hospital-based palliative care consultation was associated with higher rates of advance care planning and hospice use, lower use of high-intensity EOL interventions, and modestly lower medical costs. These findings suggest that consultation-based palliative care within routine oncology workflows may meaningfully influence EOL care delivery.

articles.title: Delayed rupture of vaginal wall haematoma causing secondary postpartum haemorrhage-successful management with bilateral uterine artery embolisation: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Secondary postpartum haemorrhag (PPH), defined as excessive bleeding occurring between 24 hours and 6 weeks after delivery, is less common than primary PPH but may cause substantial maternal morbidity if diagnosis or intervention is delayed. Vaginal wall haematomas are usually recognised in the early postpartum period and are rarely implicated in delayed haemorrhage. Delayed rupture of a concealed vaginal wall haematoma is exceptionally uncommon.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 32-year-old Han Chinese primiparous woman presented to the Emergency Department of the New District Branch of Gansu Provincial Hospital on postpartum day 11 with sudden-onset profuse vaginal bleeding. She had undergone forceps-assisted vaginal delivery with mediolateral episiotomy approximately 11 days earlier and delivered a healthy male infant weighing 3800 g. On postpartum day 4, pelvic examination and ultrasonography identified a right vaginal wall haematoma, which was initially managed conservatively because she was haemodynamically stable. On postpartum day 11, the haematoma ruptured abruptly, causing massive vaginal bleeding, transient loss of consciousness, and haemodynamic instability. Emergency angiography demonstrated active contrast extravasation from branches supplying the vaginal wall region. Bilateral uterine artery embolization (UAE) was performed successfully, and haemostasis was achieved immediately.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Delayed rupture of a concealed vaginal wall haematoma should be considered in women presenting with secondary postpartum haemorrhage after instrumental delivery, episiotomy, or documented vaginal wall trauma. Early imaging assessment and close surveillance are important when a postpartum vaginal haematoma is identified. UAE is a safe, effective, and fertility-preserving treatment option when bleeding arises from deep pelvic or vaginal wall vessels and surgical access is difficult.

articles.title: Health effects associated with emissions from household generators used for backup power in Africa: a scoping review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In many low- and middle-income countries, unreliable electricity supply has led to widespread reliance on petrol (gasoline) and diesel generators. The type of fuel influences both the quantity and composition of emissions, which contribute substantially to air pollution and pose significant health risks. Emissions from household generators, similar to diesel exhaust, contain volatile organic compounds and particulate matter linked to adverse outcomes, including cancer. This review synthesizes evidence on health impacts associated with domestic generator emissions in Africa and proposes mitigation recommendations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched PubMed and Google Scholar for English-language studies using combinations of terms related to backup generators, emissions, air pollution, human health, and households. Studies were included if they explicitly examined household generator use as the exposure of interest in relation to health outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nine articles met the inclusion criteria. Generator emissions were found to contain harmful pollutants such as nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur dioxide (SO₂), and fine particulate matter (PM₂.5 and PM₁₀), all associated with well-established health risks. Exposure was linked to respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and increased mortality. However, epidemiological evidence was limited, with only 2% of screened studies addressing health outcomes directly. Overall, the included studies indicated high levels of pollution associated with generator use and suggest potential public health impacts, though measurement of exposures and outcomes remains insufficiently developed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Evidence on the health effects of generator emissions in Africa is limited and methodologically inconsistent. While some studies indicate associations with respiratory symptoms, carbon monoxide poisoning, and possible long-term risks such as cancer and hypertension, these findings largely rely on indirect evidence, self-reports, or modelling approaches rather than robust epidemiological data. No studies established a direct causal relationship between generator-related air pollution and health outcomes. Strengthening the evidence base through well-designed epidemiological studies is essential to better understand and quantify the health burden associated with household generator use.

articles.title: Association of structured out-of-hospital continuity of care with wound healing and quality of life in severe diabetic foot ulcer: a retrospective exploratory study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To evaluate the association of a structured out-of-hospital continuity of care intervention with diabetic ulcer healing and patient-reported outcomes in individuals with severe diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), and to identify prognostic factors influencing healing.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective comparative study included 91 inpatients with severe DFUs (Wagner grades 4-5). The intervention group (n = 45) received a structured out-of-hospital care protocol comprising domiciliary visits, remote monitoring, and access to specialized care as needed. The control group (n = 46) was provided with standard post-discharge follow-up. Outcomes included ulcer healing status, time to complete wound closure, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Factors related to wound healing were assessed using Fine-Gray competing risks regression, with major amputation and death treated as competing events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Over a mean follow-up of 10.74 ± 9.05 months, the intervention group showed a higher ulcer healing rate compared to the control group (82.22% vs. 63.04%; difference 19.20%, 95% CI: 0.80% - 37.50%, p = 0.060). In the Fine-Gray competing risks analysis, the intervention group was associated with a significantly higher probability of healing (subdistribution hazard ratio = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.08-2.83, p = 0.024). Regarding HRQoL, a transient between-group difference in EQ-5D-5L was observed at 6 months (p = 0.029), but the group-by-time interaction was not significant (p = 0.220), indicating no sustained improvement.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this exploratory retrospective study, structured out-of-hospital continuity of care was associated with a statistically non-significant increase in crude healing rates. After accounting for competing risks, a significant association was observed in the primary analysis. However, this effect was attenuated and no longer significant in additional baseline severity factors (ABI and ulcer location). A transient improvement in quality of life at 6 months was not sustained. Ulcer severity and peripheral artery disease were identified as independent prognostic factors. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these exploratory findings.

articles.title: Severity and resource utilisation among trauma patients undergoing trauma team activation in four Danish trauma units: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Evidence on trauma epidemiology and outcomes largely originates from major trauma centres, while data from regional trauma units remain limited. The aim of this study was to describe the epidemiology, management, and outcomes of patients undergoing trauma team activation in the trauma units of Region Zealand, Denmark.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective multicentre observational study across four regional trauma units in Region Zealand, Denmark, between 1 March 2024 and 28 February 2025. All consecutive patients undergoing trauma team activation were included. Data included demographics, injury mechanisms, injury severity, in-hospital management, and mortality. Analyses were descriptive.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1611 patients were included. Median age was 38 years [IQR 20-58], and 60.5% were male. The most common injury mechanisms were traffic-related injuries (53%), falls (22%), and equestrian-related accidents (13%). Median Injury Severity Score was 1 [IQR 0-5] and 94% had Injury Severity Score < 16. Secondary transfer to a major trauma centre occurred in 3.8% of cases, and 90-day mortality was 2.6%. Trauma admissions occurred predominantly outside regular daytime workflow, with a peak in the late afternoon and early evening. Median TTA duration was 58 minutes [IQR 43-76] and CT imaging was performed in 86.7% of cases. Following trauma team activation, 55.2% of patients were discharged directly and 4.6% required intensive care unit admission.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Most patients undergoing trauma team activation in regional trauma units had minor injuries, were discharged directly from the emergency department, and infrequently required intensive care unit admission or secondary transfer. Despite this, trauma team activation had a median duration around one hour and showed marked diurnal variation, with a peak in the late afternoon and early evening when staffing and clinical resources are typically more limited. These findings highlight opportunities to optimise trauma team activation criteria and organisational structures to better align resource utilisation with patient acuity.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy modulates immune aging in a personalized manner: a linear mixed-effects analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Immunosenescence, characterized by telomere shortening, senescence-associated T-cell subsets, and chronic inflammation, is a hallmark of biological aging. Whether these aging-related immune biomarkers can be modulated through short-term intervention and whether responses differ according to individual characteristics remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of short-term hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) on senescence-related biomarkers and explored factors associated with individual responsiveness.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a prospective cohort study, participants underwent 30 HBOT sessions (2.5 ATA, 100% oxygen, 60 min per session). Relative telomere length (2^-ΔΔCt) and proportions of senescence-associated T-cell phenotypes (CD28⁻/CD27⁻ CD4⁺ or CD8⁺ T cells) were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), while plasma concentrations (pg/mL) of inflammatory cytokines, including pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-1β) and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, were quantified using multiplex bead-based immunoassays at baseline and after 10, 20, and 30 sessions. Linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate longitudinal HBOT-associated changes and interactions with age, sex, and BMI.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In this clinically heterogeneous cohort comprising apparently healthy individuals and patients receiving HBOT for clinical indications, HBOT was associated with a significant, time-dependent increase in relative telomere length (up to + 29.0% after 30 sessions; p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.70) and reduced proportions of senescence-associated T-cell phenotypes, particularly within CD8⁺ T-cell subsets. TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-10 did not show significant overall time-dependent changes across the cohort. However, subgroup analyses suggested that HBOT-associated responses varied according to age, sex, and BMI: younger (20-39 years) and middle-aged adults (40-59 years), females, and individuals with normal BMI exhibited greater reductions in senescence-associated T-cell phenotypes, whereas middle-aged groups, males showed significant reductions in inflammatory cytokines after 10 sessions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Short-term HBOT was associated with changes in multiple immunosenescence-related biomarkers, including increased relative telomere length, reduced proportions of senescence-associated T-cell phenotypes, and dynamic modulation of circulating inflammatory profiles. These responses were heterogeneous and influenced by demographic and metabolic factors, suggesting potential differences in individual HBOT responsiveness. These findings indicate that HBOT may modulate selected markers of immune aging; however, further controlled studies are required to determine the durability, clinical relevance, and mechanisms underlying these effects. This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500110103).

articles.title: Emergency care competencies for non-emergency medicine specialists in Japan: a modified Delphi study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Physicians from specialties other than emergency medicine (non-EM specialists) provide first-contact emergency care in many health systems. Existing emergency care courses and competency frameworks address resource-limited first-contact care or rural self-sufficient practice, but do not define the role-specific competencies expected of non-EM specialists in high-resource, specialist-limited settings. This study aimed to develop a consensus-based set of core emergency care competencies for non-EM specialists in Japan.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a modified Delphi consensus study from January to March 2026. A balanced national panel of 50 specialists, comprising 25 EM and 25 non-EM specialists, rated emergency care items on a 7-point Likert scale. Items were adopted if they met all predefined criteria: median score ≥ 6, ≥ 80% of ratings in the 6-7 range, and quartile deviation ≤ 1.0. Items were classified as consensus non-adoptions if median score ≤ 3, ≥ 70% of ratings in the 1-3 range, and quartile deviation ≤ 2.0, or as non-adopted by persistent lack of consensus if they met neither set of criteria across two consecutive rounds. Items were generated from a structured review of training documents and iteratively revised using panellist feedback.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 50 enrolled panellists, 48, 42, and 41 completed Rounds 1, 2, and 3, respectively. From an initial pool of 121 items, 38 reached adoption consensus: 23 in Round 1 and 15 in Round 2. Adopted competencies clustered around recognition of acute deterioration, interpretation of laboratory and imaging findings, initial stabilisation, judgement of indications for specialist-level intervention, and timely escalation. Several high-risk invasive procedures, including cricothyrotomy, chest tube insertion, pericardiocentesis, and intubation for non-arrest patients, did not reach consensus as universal core competencies for non-EM specialists.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Expert consensus defined a distinct, role-specific competency profile for non-EM specialists in Japan, weighted towards recognition, diagnostic interpretation, clinical judgement, initial stabilisation, and escalation rather than a reduced version of EM specialist training. The resulting 38 competencies provide content validity evidence for a minimum core of emergency care education aligned with the role non-EM specialists are expected to perform.

articles.title: Comparison of treatment delays and in-hospital outcomes between self-transported and EMS-transported patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing PCI.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The effectiveness of reperfusion therapy in patients with myocardial infarction (MI) depends largely on timely treatment. This study aimed to compare treatment delays and in-hospital outcomes between self-transported and EMS-transported patients with STEMI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational cohort study included 208 patients with AMI who underwent PCI between March 2022 and June 2023. Of these, 92 patients arrived at the hospital by self-transport and 116 were transported by EMS. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study population was predominantly male (78.4%), with a mean age of 58.05 ± 12.06 years. Significant differences were observed between self-transported and EMS-transported patients in onset-to-door time (P < 0.001) and door-to-balloon time (P = 0.001). However, no significant differences were found in AMI-related complications, including stroke, cardiogenic shock, heart failure, pericarditis, and dysrhythmias. Likewise, in-hospital outcomes, including left ventricular ejection fraction, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, and mortality, did not differ significantly between the two groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although EMS transport was associated with acceptably shorter treatment delays in patients with STEMI, total treatment times remained longer than recommended guideline targets. Our findings suggest that improving EMS utilization alone may be insufficient to improve clinical outcomes when overall system delays remain prolonged. However, given the limited sample size and low event rates, the results should be interpreted with caution. Patient-related factors may also influence treatment outcomes. Future large-scale studies are warranted to identify modifiable factors associated with treatment delays throughout the STEMI care pathway and to determine whether addressing these factors improves clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Probable naltrexone-precipitated opioid withdrawal in a patient receiving methadone maintenance after use of a weight-loss medication obtained through a direct-to-consumer telemedicine platform: a case report.
articles.journal_full: Substance abuse treatment, prevention, and policy

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Naltrexone-precipitated opioid withdrawal among patients with opioid dependence is well reported in the medical literature. However, we are not aware of any published report of probable naltrexone-precipitated opioid withdrawal associated with a medication procured through a direct-to-consumer online service.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We describe a 45-year-old man receiving methadone maintenance who experienced probable severe precipitated opioid withdrawal that occurred after first ingestion of a naltrexone-containing weight loss "medication kit" obtained from a large online direct-to-consumer telemedicine platform. He presented to the emergency department in severe distress and COWS of 27. His symptoms improved after he received the remainder of his daily dose of oral methadone, and he was discharged the following day.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case illustrates a preventable medication-safety event involving a contraindicated opioid-antagonist in a patient receiving methadone treatment. Widespread use and expanding scope of services provided through direct-to-consumer telemedicine platforms may pose unique risks. We provide an overview of liabilities that exist in the current regulatory landscape. These platforms should enhance medication reconciliation, contraindication screening, patient-facing warnings, and counseling. We also discuss the pharmacology of naltrexone-precipitated opioid withdrawal and the utility of full agonist opioids in management in select cases.

articles.title: Prevalence and patterns of prescription errors and potential drug-drug interactions in Yemeni healthcare facilities: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Medication errors, particularly prescription errors, are a major source of preventable patient harm. Errors in handwritten prescriptions can compromise treatment outcomes, increase healthcare costs, and lead to adverse drug events. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and types of prescription errors, as well as potential drug-drug interactions (DDIs), in Dhamar city, Yemen.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted over three months (March-May 2024) across emergency departments and outpatient clinics in multiple specialties, including internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, and others, in both public and private hospitals. A total of 628 handwritten prescriptions were reviewed, with 300 prescriptions identified as containing errors. Data were collected on prescriber details, patient information, and medication parameters. Potential DDIs were assessed using validated drug interaction databases (Micromedex, Medscape, and WebMD). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data as frequencies and percentages. The chi-square test was used to assess associations between prescriber qualification and potential DDIs, while Spearman's rank correlation was applied to evaluate the relationship between the number of prescribed medications and the occurrence of DDIs. All analyses were performed using SPSS v26.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 628 prescriptions reviewed, 300 (47.8%) contained one or more prescription errors, totaling 2,008 errors (average 6.7 errors per prescription). The most common errors were medication-related (39.3%), followed by patient-related (34.2%), prescriber-related (13.9%), and general prescription errors (12.4%). Potential DDIs were identified in 133 prescriptions (44.3%), with most requiring close monitoring (78.2%) and 6.7% classified as serious. Polypharmacy and high-risk populations, including elderly patients and those with chronic diseases, were associated with a higher likelihood of interactions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prescription errors are highly prevalent in handwritten medical prescriptions in Dhamar city, Yemen, with medication-related omissions being most common. Potential DDIs are frequent, particularly in prescriptions with multiple drugs and in vulnerable populations. The findings highlight the need for improved prescribing practices, enhanced prescriber education, and greater involvement of clinical pharmacists to improve medication safety in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Fatal methanol poisoning with paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity, and putaminal hemorrhage: a case report and brief literature review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Methanol poisoning is a widespread issue worldwide. In this case report, we describe a patient with methanol poisoning who experienced tonic spasms, cerebellar and putaminal hemorrhages, and severe neurological complications. Additionally, this report emphasizes the potential link between methanol poisoning and paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH).

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 31-year-old male was referred to the emergency department with blurred vision, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, restlessness, and severe respiratory distress. Two days ago, he drank a locally prepared alcoholic beverage while having dinner. The initial laboratory data showed metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap. The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) with a GCS of 4/15. General supportive treatment (normal saline, DVT prophylaxis, stress ulcer prophylaxis, etc.), sodium bicarbonate, ethanol, dialysis, methylprednisolone, and folic acid were initiated for poisoning management. In the brain CT scan, cerebellar and putamen hemorrhage, and brain edema were reported. We stopped heparin due to the brain hemorrhage, but after a few days, DVT occurred. During hospitalization, the patient experienced several brief and spontaneous tonic spasms with diaphoresis, tachycardia, and tachypnea, so paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) was suspected. He was treated with midazolam and metoprolol for PSH treatment. Unfortunately, the patient developed sepsis and died after 53 days of stay in the ICU.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study highlights that exposure to methanol can result in a range of neurological complications. The administration of heparin in cases of methanol poisoning remains controversial and requires careful evaluation. Furthermore, paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity is an uncommon complication that can result from cerebral injury attributed to methanol poisoning.

articles.title: Assessment of intravenous thrombolytic therapy response in acute ischemic stroke using NIHSS changes and laboratory parameters.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Acute ischemic stroke is one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in adults. Although intravenous thrombolytic therapy (IVTT) can improve neurological recovery in appropriate patients, the treatment response shows variability among individuals. Although the NIHSS score is widely used to monitor clinical response, it should be evaluated together with laboratory parameters to more accurately predict prognosis. In this study, the relationship between NIHSS score change and laboratory parameters in acute ischemic stroke patients treated with IVTT was investigated.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Thirty-three acute ischemic stroke patients who presented to the emergency department in 2024 and received IVTT were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline and 24-hour NIHSS scores were recorded. Hemogram and biochemical parameters were analyzed. Clinical response was defined as a ≥ 4-point reduction in NIHSS score at 24 h after IVTT, and its associations with mortality and hemorrhagic complications were statistically evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Three-month mortality was 15.2%, and the hemorrhage rate was 9.1%. Platelet levels were found to be significantly lower in patients who died. The second NIHSS score was significantly associated with mortality and hemorrhage. Serum calcium and basophil levels were associated with clinical improvement. In ROC analysis, basophil showed a relatively higher discriminative ability than calcium in predicting clinical improvement; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and the exploratory nature of the analysis.

articles.title: Emergency department providers' perspectives on patients' use of cannabis: therapeutic potential, risks, and prescribing experience.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cannabis legalization in Canada has increased both therapeutic and recreational use. Emergency department (ED) providers encounter patients using cannabis recreationally, to self-manage symptoms, or under medical authorization, often without a clear distinction between these contexts at the point of care. However, provider attitudes toward cannabis in the emergency setting remain poorly understood, and no Canadian studies have specifically explored this group. This knowledge gap limits the development of clinical guidance and education for ED staff.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of physicians and nurses working in the Adult Emergency Department at the Health Sciences Centre (HSC), Winnipeg, Manitoba, from October 2024 to February 2025. The survey evaluated attitudes toward legalization and medical use, perceived legal, social, and health risks, and prescribing experience. Descriptive statistics were used. Survey reporting followed best practice guidelines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-five providers completed the survey. Most (71.1%) supported legalization, and 86.7% believed cannabis has therapeutic value. Nearly all (95.6%) agreed that eligible patients should have access to cannabis. Legal (91.1%) and social (77.3%) risks were perceived as low, while views on health risks varied; 38.6% perceived moderate or high health risks. No participants had prescribed cannabis, although 42.2% were in prescribing roles.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This is the first study to examine Canadian ED provider attitudes toward cannabis. While most respondents supported legalization (71.1%) and endorsed the therapeutic potential of cannabis (86.7%), with nearly all (95.6%) agreeing that eligible patients should have access, prescribing experience was limited, and many of those surveyed held uncertain or mixed views on cannabis safety, particularly relative to prescription pain medications. These findings highlight the need for targeted education, clinical tools, and evidence-based guidance to support cannabis-related care in emergency settings.

articles.title: Undertriage of geriatric trauma patients in the emergency department: A retrospective single-center study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To analyze emergency department (ED) triage outcomes in geriatric trauma patients and evaluate undertriage in relation to injury severity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis was conducted on anonymized medical records of patients aged ≥ 65 years admitted to the ED of the University Hospital in Kraków, Poland, due to trauma between 2018 and 2020. Among 111,615 total ED admissions, 4,922 geriatric trauma cases were identified. Triage categories (adapted ESI) were evaluated in relation to the Injury Severity Score (ISS), Trauma and Injury Severity Score (TRISS), and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS). Undertriage was defined as an ISS ≥ 16 with assignment to lower-risk triage priorities (3-5).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Undertriage occurred in 34.4% of severely injured geriatric patients, exceeding the recommended threshold of < 5%. Head and neck injuries were the most severe across triage categories (AIS 3-4). Among patients with head and neck injuries, those in the undertriage group 65 + had significantly higher GCS scores (median 15) than those in the correct triage group 65+ (median 5), suggesting that preserved consciousness may mask severe injuries. Overtriage was observed in 37.6% of cases, frequently involving head trauma with high GCS scores.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings highlight the need for age-specific approaches to ED triage, particularly in cases of head trauma. In this cohort, commonly used physiological triage parameters, including the GCS, were associated with limitations in identifying patients with more severe injuries. These findings support further research on geriatric-specific triage approaches that account for age-related factors potentially affecting triage accuracy and the management of older trauma patients.

articles.title: Association between arterial PaCO2 and long-term osteoporosis risk in older patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Osteoporosis is a highly prevalent disease among older adults. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and associated hypoxia may contribute to the development of osteoporosis. This study aimed to further investigate the impact of CO₂ retention (another key pathophysiological feature of COPD) on osteoporosis, providing a novel perspective for understanding COPD-related bone metabolic disorders.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 611 older patients with acute exacerbation (AE) of COPD were enrolled from the hospital's emergency department and completed a 1-year follow-up. Arterial PaO₂, PaCO₂, FEV₁% predicted, and FEV₁/FVC were recorded at baseline (AE phase), 2-week recheck (stable COPD phase), and during AECOPD recurrence during follow-up. Lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD) was measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry at baseline (immediately after AECOPD discharge) and at the end of follow-up. Patients were divided into the BMD-drop group (n = 231) and BMD-stable group (n = 380) based on the degree of BMD reduction during follow-up, and multivariate logistic regression was used for analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Adverse associations: Elevated PaCO₂ at baseline, 2-week recheck, and during AECOPD recurrence were associated with an increased risk of BMD reduction during follow-up (P<0.001, P = 0.006, P<0.001, respectively). Favorable associations: Higher PaO₂, FEV₁% predicted, and FEV₁/FVC at these three time points were associated with a decreased risk of BMD reduction during follow-up (all P<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Elevated arterial PaCO₂ may be associated with long-term BMD reduction in older patients with COPD and thus could represent a potential risk factor for osteoporosis in this population.

articles.title: Urinary kidney injury molecule-1 as a diagnostic biomarker for persistent severe acute kidney injury: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Despite the vast amount of literature dedicated to biomarkers and acute kidney injury (AKI), the persistent state of AKI has been relatively neglected. The objective of this study was to systematically review relevant studies and evaluate the diagnostic value of urinary kidney injury molecule 1 (uKIM-1) for persistent severe AKI in adults.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched the PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials databases up to December 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients and assessed the diagnostic value of uKIM-1 for persistent severe AKI. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) was used for quality assessment. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve (AUC) and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) values were calculated via a Bayesian bivariate diagnostic meta-analysis model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight studies with 2349 patients were selected for meta-analysis. 378 patients were diagnosed with persistent severe AKI. The included studies were published between 2011 and 2025 and involved heterogeneous clinical settings, including intensive care, emergency department, postoperative, sepsis, COVID-19, and liver transplantation populations. The estimated sensitivity of uKIM-1 was 0.67 (95% CrI, 0.59-0.75), and the specificity was 0.73 (95% CrI, 0.61-0.84). The pooled DOR was 5.91 (95% CrI, 2.91-11.20), and the AUC was 0.75 (95% CrI, 0.62-0.84). Sensitivity analyses using alternative cutoff selections and prior specifications showed generally stable estimates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This Bayesian meta-analysis indicates that uKIM-1 has moderate diagnostic value for persistent severe AKI in adults. Current evidence does not support its use as a standalone biomarker, and future studies should evaluate its incremental value in combination with other biomarkers and clinical variables.

articles.title: High-fidelity simulation and pediatric emergency preparedness among healthcare students: a systematic review and meta-analysis using the GRADE approach.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric emergencies demand rapid, accurate, and coordinated clinical responses; however, healthcare students often have limited opportunities to gain hands-on experience in such high-risk situations during training. High-fidelity simulation (HFS) has emerged as a widely adopted educational strategy to bridge this gap by providing realistic, safe, and controlled learning environments. Despite its increasing use, the magnitude and consistency of its effectiveness across different educational outcomes remain unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A comprehensive systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ProQuest for studies published between January 2012 and December 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized controlled trials (non-RCTs), and mixed-methods studies evaluating high-fidelity simulation (HFS) in pediatric emergency training among healthcare students were included. Outcomes of interest included knowledge, psychomotor skills, clinical performance, decision-making, teamwork, confidence, and other learner-related outcomes. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool for RCTs, the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool for non-RCTs, and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) for mixed-methods studies. Meta-analyses were conducted using a random-effects model for studies reporting comparable outcomes, while studies with non-comparable outcomes were synthesized narratively. The certainty of the evidence for each meta-analyzed outcome was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 23 studies involving 2,734 healthcare students were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in knowledge scores favouring HFS (mean difference = 3.03; 95% CI: 0.34-5.73; p = 0.03), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I² = 93%). Skill-related outcomes, pooled from two studies, showed a large and statistically significant effect favouring HFS (mean difference = 8.74; 95% CI: 7.98-9.50; p < 0.001), with no observed heterogeneity (I² = 0%). Narrative synthesis revealed consistent improvements in clinical decision-making, critical thinking, teamwork, self-confidence, and learner satisfaction. Overall, the certainty of evidence was rated as low due to methodological limitations and variability across studies.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: High-fidelity simulation is an effective educational approach for improving pediatric emergency preparedness among healthcare students. While the findings support its use in enhancing both technical and non-technical competencies, further high-quality studies are required to strengthen the evidence base and evaluate long-term educational and clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: The review protocol was prospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025631603).

articles.title: The coverage gap in PREVENT: Why cardiovascular risk prediction needs a lab-free complement.

abstract.text: The American Heart Association's PREVENT equations are now embedded in three major AHA/ACC guidelines governing hypertension, dyslipidemia, and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, including a specific risk threshold that gates initiation of GLP-1-based therapy and SGLT2 inhibitors. This rapid guideline uptake has outpaced a persistent limitation: PREVENT requires laboratory values, chiefly lipids and estimated glomerular filtration rate, that are frequently missing in the populations where risk prediction matters most, including patients seen in community health centers, emergency departments, and substance use treatment programs. Real-world validation studies across multiple health systems show that PREVENT underestimates cardiovascular risk most severely in these same subgroups, with the largest underestimation among Medicaid-insured, uninsured, and Black patients. Imputation, whether simple substitution or multiple imputation, does not resolve this problem because the probability that a laboratory value is missing is itself associated with the underlying risk the model is trying to estimate, a form of informative missingness that standard imputation methods are not designed to address. We argue that the field should invest in developing and validating a standalone cardiovascular risk prediction model that does not require laboratory measures. Such a model would function as a complement to PREVENT, not a replacement, providing risk estimates for patients without laboratory data and helping identify those who warrant expedited evaluation. As PREVENT becomes the gatekeeper for guideline-directed therapy across three clinical domains simultaneously, closing this coverage gap is no longer a methodological refinement but a clinical implementation imperative.

articles.title: Exploring contributing factors to fatalities occurring within an emergency department: a qualitative analysis informed by root cause analysis principles.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency Departments (EDs) are highrisk and timepressured workplaces where latent system failures can quickly culminate in fatal outcomes. Understanding the underlying causes contributing to mortality in these units is therefore essential for designing effective safety interventions. This qualitative study, informed by Root Cause Analysis (RCA) principles, aimed to identify factors contributing to ED fatalities in a referral hospital in Urmia, Iran.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All ED deaths recorded during 2021-2022 (n = 595) were reviewed. Because medical records contained limited information on contributory factors, the study integrated non-participant observations, semi-structured interviews with five purposively selected key informants, and a targeted literature review. Qualitative content analysis was used to identify themes, which were subsequently organized into a fishbone diagram using RCA principles.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The most common immediate causes of death were cardiac arrest, loss of consciousness, shortness of breath, and road traffic injuries. Seven interacting categories of contributing factors emerged: patient-related issues, communication and teamwork failures, individual staff performance lapses, physical and social environment constraints, managerial and organizational deficiencies, equipment/medication/supply failures, and external factors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Frontline staff perceived that multiple systemic vulnerabilities, particularly communication gaps, resource shortages, and organizational constraints, interact to increase the risk of fatal outcomes in this ED. However, this exploratory study cannot establish direct causality or determine the proportion of preventable deaths. The findings highlight the need for an integrated Electronic Health Record (EHR) system, standardized team training for shift handovers, adequate staffing aligned with national standards, and patient safety education to foster a proactive safety culture. The effectiveness of these proposed interventions should be evaluated in future formal, case-level RCA studies.

articles.title: Revalidation of the M-DIRECT scale in prehospital identification of acute stroke patients for endovascular treatment.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE
abstract.text: The M-DIRECT scale was implemented for prehospital triage of acute stroke, such that patients with an M-DIRECT score ≥ 2 are transferred directly to an endovascular treatment (EVT)-ready center (EVT-C) instead of a nearer stroke unit (SU). Our aim is to evaluate the performance of M-DIRECT at five years post-implementation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective observational study of consecutive prehospital code stroke patients attended by regional emergency medical services during 2022 in an urban network of 6.75 million inhabitants. Basal characteristics, time metrics, presence of large or medium vessel occlusion (LVO/MeVO), and treatments were compared between EVT-C and non-EVT-ready SU groups according to the M-DIRECT score.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1950 patients were included. Of these, 992 (51%) were first attended at an EVT-C and 958 at a nearer SU (49%). Furthermore, 706 (36%) patients were M-DIRECT positive, of which 413 (58%) had an LVO/MeVO, and 354 (50%) underwent EVT. Of 1244 M-DIRECT negative patients, 204 (16%) had an LVO/MeVO and 105 (8%) underwent EVT. M-DIRECT showed 77% sensitivity, 76% specificity, and 77% diagnostic accuracy for EVT from prehospital triage, with an AUC (95% CI) of 0.768 (0.742-0.793). A positive M-DIRECT score was independently associated with EVT adjusted for age, sex, NIHSS, and unknown onset, with aOR (95% CI) 3.05 (1.65-5.68), and consistently across every arterial segment. Only 46 out of 459 (10%) EVT required a secondary transfer.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: M-DIRECT scale accurately identifies EVT candidates prehospital, reduces secondary transfers, and independently predicts EVT likelihood across different vessel occlusions.

articles.title: Serial cardiac ultrasound in acutely ill adults: a systematic review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiopulmonary symptoms frequently prompt emergency department (ED) visits. Serial as-sessment of dynamic cardiac ultrasound parameters may support monitoring, but their asso-ciation with patient outcomes and role in guiding management is uncertain. This systematic review evaluated whether serial changes in ejection fraction (EF), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and the right ventricular-to-left ventricular (RV/LV) ratio are associated with mortality, readmissions, length of stay, or intensive care unit trans-fer in acutely ill patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase (Ovid), CENTRAL (Wiley), Scopus (Elsevier), Web of Science (Clarivate), Google Scholar, ProQuest, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the International Clini-cal Trials Registry Platform. The initial search was conducted on 16 April 2024 and updated on 31 October 2025. We included randomized and non-randomized trials and observational stud-ies of adults (≥18 years) undergoing at least two in-hospital cardiac ultrasound assessments and reported mortality, readmission, length of stay, and/or intensive care unit transfer. Risk of bias was assessed with study design-specific tools. Results were summarized using synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 15,174 screened records, 11 studies with a total of 941 patients were included. Study popu-lations were defined by presenting symptoms (dyspnea, hypotension) or by clinical conditions (toxicological, infectious, and cardiopulmonary diseases). Echocardiography was most used, and patients underwent 3-4 scans during admission. Overall risk of bias was moderate to high. Four studies compared serial changes in EF, TAPSE, and/or the RV/LV ratio with outcomes and found no consistent pattern. One randomized study evaluated ultrasound-guided treatment and found no difference compared with usual care. Across studies, EF, TAPSE, and RV/LV ratio were generally stable or improved over time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Available evidence is limited and does not demonstrate a consistent association between serial cardiac ultrasound parameters and outcomes in acutely ill adults. However, serial changes are frequently observed, highlighting the need for trials evaluating whether decision-linked, ultrasound-guided management strategies can improve outcomes.

abstract.label: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION NUMBER
abstract.text: PROSPERO, CRD42024524740.

articles.title: Intracerebral nodular involvement in neurobrucellosis: case report and review of the literature.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Brucellosis is a systemic disease with a wide range of clinical presentations that can mimic many infectious and non-infectious diseases. Neurobrucellosis (NB) is a significant clinical entity of brucellosis that can lead to serious neurological sequelae if appropriate treatment is not initiated after an early diagnosis. The clinical course of the disease is relatively insidious, and although it is frequently subacute or chronic, it can present with acute manifestations. We report the case of a 31-year-old male patient who presented to the emergency department with neurological symptoms and was found to have an intracerebral nodular lesion, a rare manifestation of NB.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 31-year-old male livestock worker presented to the emergency department with complaints of headache, dizziness, and impaired consciousness lasting for two days, following 20 days of night sweats and musculoskeletal pain. Initial cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed pleocytosis, increased protein levels, and decreased glucose levels. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed leptomeningeal enhancement and nodular lesions measuring millimeters in size, with contrast enhancement in the right temporal lobe. Although the initial cultures were negative, a positive serum Brucella tube agglutination test at a 1/5120 titer, CSF analysis, and radiological findings showing neurological involvement confirmed the diagnosis of NB. The patient was treated with a triple-antibiotic regimen consisting of ceftriaxone, doxycycline, and rifampicin. This intervention resulted in complete clinical recovery and radiological resolution of the intracerebral lesions during the follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This case highlights the importance of including NB in the differential diagnosis of intracerebral nodular lesions, particularly in endemic regions. This case suggests that NB, although rare, may present with intracerebral lesions that can regress with appropriate antimicrobial therapy. An integrated clinical, serological, and radiological evaluation may aid timely diagnosis, and when a rapid response to antibiotic treatment is observed, it may help reduce the need for invasive diagnostic procedures, such as brain biopsy, in selected cases.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Limitations of NEWS2 for predicting 48-hour emergency department revisits: a real-world retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early revisits to the emergency department (ED) are commonly used as a quality indicator and reflect challenges in discharge decision-making. Although the National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) is widely used to detect clinical deterioration, its ability to predict early ED revisits after discharge remains unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary university hospital ED in Thailand from January 2019 to June 2022. Adult patients discharged from the ED were included. The primary outcome was an unplanned same-institution ED revisit within 48 h. Initial triage NEWS2 scores were analyzed, and predictive performance was assessed using overall area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and threshold-specific operating characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 75,609 eligible index visits, 182 (0.24%) were followed by an unplanned ED revisit within 48 h. Initial triage NEWS2 showed no clinically useful discrimination (AUROC 0.54, 95% CI 0.49-0.58). A cut-off ≥ 2 provided modest sensitivity (58.2%) but low specificity (52.3%); higher cut-offs improved specificity at the expense of sensitivity. Positive predictive values were extremely low and likelihood ratios were close to 1.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: NEWS2, when used alone at initial ED triage, is insufficient for predicting unplanned 48-hour ED revisits. Early revisits may be influenced by multiple clinical, patient, and system-level factors beyond initial physiological abnormality. Multidimensional risk assessment tools may be more appropriate for supporting safe ED discharge decisions.

abstract.label: REGISTRATION TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: TCTR20230816010, registered on 16 August 2023 (Thai Clinical Trials Registry, www.thaiclinicaltrials.org).

articles.title: The relationship between endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in acute myocardial infarction patients admitted in emergency department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: In this study, we aimed to explore the relationship between endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: This retrospective study was based on the clinical data of the AMI patients admitted in emergency department of Changsha Central Hospital from August 2020 to January 2023. Different models were constructed by multivariable regression analysis for investigating the relationship between EASIX index and MACE risk. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was utilized for further validating the potential nonlinear relationship. The receiver-operator characteristic (ROC) analysis of EASIX index for predicting MACE risk in AMI was done.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 805 AMI patients with 193 individuals in MACE group were included. After adjusting potential confounders, with per unit increasement in EASIX index, the risk of MACE increased by 16% (OR = 1.16, 95%CI: 1.04-1.29, p = 0.0054). The RCS showed the nonlinear relationship between EASIX index and the incidence of MACE was not significant. The predictive performances of EASIX index were showed as follow: an AUC of 0.687 (95%CI:0.642-0.732) and a cut-off value of 2.42.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A significant relationship between EASIX index and the incidence of MACE in AMI was identified.

articles.title: Management of well-appearing febrile infants aged 29-90 days: a multicenter survey on current practices and guideline adherence.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fever without a source in well appearing young infants remains a challenge in pediatric emergency departments (PEDs). Although evidence-based decision rules exist, limited data are available on how these patients are managed in daily clinical practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional survey among pediatricians working in 20 Italian PEDs. The 22-item questionnaire explored the definition of "well appearing", clinical assessment, diagnostic workup, use of standardized protocols, antibiotic prescribing, and self-reported competence in managing well-appearing febrile young infants aged 29-90 days. Descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests were used to compare responses by geographic area and physician seniority.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 273 (response rate 84%) participated in the study. Half of them worked in Northern Italy, and 47% had < 5 years of experience. Standardized protocols were used by 56%, most commonly the Step-by-Step approach (28%) or local institutional guidelines (32%). Criteria used to define "well appearing" were highly heterogeneous. Urine dipstick testing was routinely performed by 80%, with culture obtained based on dipstick positivity in 66%. Inflammatory markers were routinely tested by 58%, and lumbar puncture was reserved for neurologic signs or clinical deterioration (63%). When inflammatory markers were within normal ranges, 67% discharged patients with close follow-up, while 83.5% reported using a conditional approach to antibiotic initiation guided by diagnostic findings (inflammatory markers and/or viral testing), mainly amoxicillin-clavulanate. Regional and seniority-related variability was significant.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Italian PED physicians show moderate adherence to standardized protocols for managing well-appearing febrile young infants, but there is no shared definition of "well appearing". These findings underscore the need for harmonized national guidelines and shared definitions to promote evidence-based care.

articles.title: Validation of the BREST score for diagnosing acute heart failure in emergency department patients with dyspnea: added value of NT-proBNP and biomarkers.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a leading cause of dyspnea among patients presenting to the emergency department (ED), necessitating timely diagnostic approaches. The BREST score is a pragmatic bedside tool developed to support the early identification of AHF using clinical and electrocardiographic findings. This study aimed to prospectively validate the diagnostic performance of the BREST score and assess the incremental diagnostic value of NT-proBNP and selected inflammatory biomarkers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study prospectively enrolled consecutive adult patients presenting with dyspnea to the ED of Gaziantep City Hospital between January 2024 and May 2025. At presentation, BREST score components were recorded using standardized clinical forms. Biomarker levels, including NT-proBNP, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), were collected during routine diagnostic evaluation. The diagnosis of AHF was established by board-certified cardiologists, blinded to the BREST score, through adjudication of echocardiographic findings, laboratory data (including NT-proBNP), and clinical documentation. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1215 screened patients, 1000 were included in the final analysis. The median age was 68 years (IQR: 59-76), and 48% were male. AHF was diagnosed in 736 patients (73.6%) based on the reference standard. At the optimal BREST cut-off (≥ 5), the score yielded an AUC of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.849-0.900), with 93.8% sensitivity and 69.3% specificity. The addition of NT-proBNP improved the AUC to 0.895 (95% CI: 0.873-0.917), while the full biomarker panel provided no significant additional benefit (AUC: 0.898). In subgroup analysis, the BREST score retained good discrimination in de novo heart failure (AUC 0.824) and performed strongly in known chronic heart failure (AUC 0.943); this difference indicates that its diagnostic performance is not identical across presentation types.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This prospective validation demonstrated that the BREST score is an accurate and efficient diagnostic tool for AHF in ED patients presenting with dyspnea. Its reliance on readily available clinical and ECG data supports its integration into routine ED workflows. Adding NT-proBNP produced a modest, non-significant numerical increase in discrimination, which may still be clinically useful in cases of intermediate clinical probability, while other inflammatory biomarkers added no further value.

articles.title: Prospective identification of risk factors for patients with severe acute poisoning in emergency departments in northern Taiwan.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Poisoning remains a major public health issue and a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits in northern Taiwan. Identifying predictors of severe poisoning is crucial for risk stratification and improved patient outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, multicenter, cross-sectional cohort study enrolled 2,470 patients with acute poisoning over a consecutive two-year period across two tertiary medical centers in northern Taiwan. Data on demographics, clinical features, toxic agents, and vital signs were collected at ED triage. The primary outcome was severe poisoning, defined as a Poisoning Severity Score (PSS) of 3-4. For descriptive purposes, patients were categorized into non-severe (PSS 0-2) and severe groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of severe poisoning, reporting adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Poisoning accounted for 4.7 cases per 1,000 ED visits during the study period. Ingestion was the most common exposure route (55.2%), followed by inhalation (16.6%). Prescribed medication represented the largest toxicological category (32.5%), whereas pesticides accounted for 9.8% of exposures but contributed disproportionately to mortality. Overall, 77 patients (3.1%) died, with paraquat being responsible for 59.7% of all fatalities, making it the most lethal agent observed. Other substances associated with fatal outcomes included warfarin, amphetamines, hydrochloric acid, benzodiazepines, digoxin, carbon monoxide, and methotrexate. Most patients (88.5%) experienced non-severe poisoning (PSS 0-2), while 11.5% experienced severe poisoning (PSS 3-4). In multivariable analyses, significant predictors of severe poisoning at ED presentation included increasing age, abnormal vital signs at triage, suicidal intent, and pesticide ingestion. These associations remained robust in the supplementary model, which excluded all ED triage vital signs, where age, intentional exposure, illicit drugs and pesticide ingestion continued to independently predict severe poisoning.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Advanced age, abnormal vital signs, suicidal intent, and pesticide exposure, particularly paraquat, are strong predictors of severe poisoning and mortality in this cohort from northern Taiwan. Early identification of high-risk patients based on clinical features available at ED triage may facilitate timely risk stratification and resource allocation for acute poisoning, particularly in regions with similar poisoning patterns to northern Taiwan.

articles.title: Examining the performance of the EMS system during the COVID-19 pandemic: a cross-sectional study in Iran.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: In many countries, the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) serve as the frontline of healthcare systems, playing a critical role in responding to health emergencies, including epidemics and pandemics. Assessing the current preparedness and performance of the EMS, along with regular monitoring, can be essential initial steps in enhancing the EMS system's ability to respond to health emergencies and disasters. The current study aimed to assess the performance of Hamadan province's EMS during the coronavirus pandemic, utilizing the standard tool.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study, all EMS centers in Hamadan province were assessed to evaluate their performance in responding to coronavirus disease (COVID-19) in 2021. The data were gathered using a standardized 74-question checklist provided by the World Health Organization (WHO). The collected data were analyzed using SPSS software, utilizing descriptive statistics (such as frequency, mean, and standard deviation) along with analytical methods, including Spearman's rank correlation test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The results indicated that a majority of the EMS centers in Hamadan province (67%) achieved a favorable score for performance in response to COVID-19. The analysis of the number and types of missions conducted during the study period revealed that the majority (61.5%) of ambulance requests were for clinical emergencies, while only 4.5% were related to respiratory problems suspected of COVID-19. Furthermore, regarding the correlation between EMS center performance score and the variable of "holding training courses on COVID-19 management," the Spearman's rank correlation test showed no significant association between the two variables (P = 0.705).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings of this study indicate that, although only a small percentage of the ambulance missions were related to COVID-19, the preparedness and performance of the Hamadan EMS centers in responding to COVID-19 were satisfactory. However, the absence of a dedicated ambulance for COVID-19 patients and the fatigue and emotional exhaustion reported among emergency technicians were challenges faced by Hamadan's EMS in managing COVID-19. EMS managers and officials need to develop strategies to address these issues.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Remote guidance for emergency calls capability and associated factors among emergency department medical staff in China: a mixed methods study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Remote Guidance for Emergency Calls (RGEC) is the main link between the public and emergency medical services, yet the specific competencies of emergency department medical staff in providing these instructions remain underexplored. This study aimed to evaluate RGEC capacities and experiences among medical staff and identify its key determinants through a mixed-methods design.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A mixed-methods design was conducted. A total of 405 medical staff from 23 healthcare institutions completed a cross-sectional survey by cluster sampling. We employ Nurses' Clinical Communication Competency (NCCC), Chinese Version of the Critical Thinking Disposition Inventory (CTDI-CV), and Remote Guidance for Emergency Calls Capability (RGECC). Quantitative data were analyzed using multivariate stepwise regression. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 13 participants, followed by content analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants had a mean age of 34.97 ± 7.56 years, and 69.14% were female. The full-score rates for RGECC (2.96%), NCCC (17.28%), and CTDI-CV (4.69%) were low. Factors associated with RGEC included clinical communication competency, critical thinking, providing proactive pre-hospital RGEC, pre-hospital RGEC experience, professional title, and total employment duration (p < 0.05). Two themes were revealed: (1) Remote emergency rescue challenges (bystander barriers, rescue passivity, and a lack of experience in remote rescue guidance), and (2) Strategies for promoting RGEC (improving emotional management, enhancing public first aid capabilities, standardizing first-aid guidance protocols, and strengthening specialized training for remote guidance).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The RGECC of emergency department staff in China still requires improvement. A comprehensive, multi-pronged strategy must be adopted, focusing on strengthening emotional management, standardizing operational procedures, providing training, and conducting public first aid education.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Chinese Clinical Trial Register: ChiCTR2600120316; reg. date: March 12, 2026.

articles.title: Understanding the experience of healthcare providers in delivering care to older adults presenting in emergency departments: a qualitative study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Knowledge gaps remain regarding the current challenges of delivering care to meet the needs of older adults presenting in the Emergency department (ED). This study aimed to explore the experiences of ED healthcare providers (HCPs) in providing care to older adults (OA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative descriptive approach was employed in this study, which was part of an ongoing five-year experience-based co-design project. Participants who were Australian registered clinicians (e.g. medical, nursing, and allied health), non-clinical staff who support clinical care (e.g., clerks and orderlies), or who manage the delivery of patient care were recruited from the EDs of three public hospitals in Sydney, Australia from March 2023 to April 2024. Semi-structured interviews and a focus group took place either in-person or via videoconference, depending on the participants' preferences. Inductive thematic analysis was employed with no predetermined list of codes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-five semi-structured interviews and one focus group were conducted with 52 participants. A total of 34.6% participants were aged between 34 and 53 years old; 34 of 52 participants were female. Participants comprised 44% nurses, 27% doctors, and 17% allied health providers. Five major themes were identified: (1) patient complexity challenges care delivery, (2) organisational constraints challenge care delivery, (3) workforce issues undermine quality of care, (4) physical environments do not meet geriatric care needs, and (5) system interface issues constrain care transition. HCPs reported that excessive workload within time constraints, lack of resources, poor physical environment, and system interface issues create challenges in providing quality care to OAs with medical complexity. These challenges were further exacerbated by the mismatch between ED models of care and the needs of OAs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The development of a geriatric-specific ED pathway is likely to improve ED performance and better meet the needs of OAs. Partnering with ED HCPs and OAs offers a feasible approach to co-design a sustainable ED model of care and deliver quality of care that is geriatric-friendly.

articles.title: Oncological emergencies in radiology: Classic presentations and current challenges.

abstract.text: The number of oncology patients requiring emergency care continues to rise. Many of these emergencies are life-threatening and may result either from the underlying malignancy or the diagnostic and therapeutic procedures employed. In this context, imaging techniques play a fundamental role by enabling early detection and guiding clinical management. Among the most challenging scenarios are opportunistic infections in patients undergoing haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, where pulmonary involvement presents a significant diagnostic challenge. In addition to being familiar with complications related to conventional treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, radiologists must also be able to recognise adverse effects associated with immunotherapy modalities, which can also require urgent consultations. This article provides an illustrative review of the main oncological emergencies, highlighting the radiologist's role in their identification.

articles.title: Violence-related measures against ambulance personnel: a study protocol for a scoping review with multi-framework conceptual mapping.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Violence against ambulance personnel is a recognised occupational hazard. Between 57% and 93% of prehospital responders report at least one episode of verbal or physical violence during their career. Despite this exposure, violence-related measures remain insufficiently mapped in the literature, and no review known to the authors has described their distribution across complementary safety science and human factors frameworks.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This scoping review aims to identify and map violence-related measures targeting ambulance personnel as reported in peer-reviewed literature, and to describe their distribution across five conceptual frameworks: levels of prevention, hierarchy of controls, Safety-I/Safety-II, typology of situations, and levels of the sociotechnical system. Sub-objectives address the isolated versus bundled nature of measures, their relation to the mission cycle, the types of violence targeted, and the proportion of measures that are insufficiently described for coding.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The review follows JBI methodology for scoping reviews and will be reported according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines, which is adaption of the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews checklist. Eligibility criteria follow a Population - Concept - Context structure. The population is ambulance personnel involved in mission-related work. The concept covers violence-related measures targeting Type II and Type V violence. The context is prehospital ambulance services, including mission-related dispatch interfaces. Searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, covering English-language peer-reviewed sources published between 1 January 2014 and 15 May 2026. Title/abstract screening will be conducted by the principal investigator with calibrated eligibility criteria. Data will be extracted using a piloted charting form and coded according to a predefined codebook. The protocol is registered on the Open Science Framework ( 10.17605/OSF.IO/DYUWC).

articles.title: AI decision-support in the initial management of orthopedic trauma: a systematic review.
articles.journal_full: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early orthopedic trauma care requires rapid, high-stakes decision-making under conditions of physiologic instability and diagnostic uncertainty. Conventional clinical scores and guideline-based tools aim to standardize early management but often demonstrate limited patient-level accuracy and variable performance across care settings. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based decision-support tools have been proposed as adjuncts to support early trauma decisions, yet their scope and performance in orthopedic trauma remain uncharacterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted of prediction-model and implementation studies published between January 2010 and October 2025 using MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies evaluated AI/ML-based tools designed to predict or support early orthopedic trauma decisions in the emergency department, trauma bay, or prehospital setting. Target decision domains included hemorrhage control, operative versus nonoperative management, limb salvage versus amputation, and level-of-care or interfacility triage. Data extraction focused on study design, clinical decision targets, model inputs, validation strategy and reported performance metrics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 361 identified records, 9 studies met inclusion criteria. Study populations, modeling approaches, and clinical targets were heterogeneous. Reported discriminatory performance was generally moderate to favorable, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values ranging from 0.67 to 0.97 across decision domains. External validation was limited, and reporting of calibration and decision-analytic metrics was inconsistent. Imaging-adjacent AI tools enabled automated computed tomography (CT) based hematoma quantification for pelvic trauma and real-time CT auto-segmentation workflows for maxillofacial trauma (Dice ≈0.92-0.93) with substantial time reduction. However, the included studies did not directly evaluate downstream effects on clinician decisions or workflow throughput beyond segmentation tasks, or patient-centered outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AI/ML-based decision-support tools for early orthopedic trauma management show strong technical feasibility and encouraging performance in existing validation studies, supporting their potential role as adjuncts to clinician judgment in early, high-stakes decisions. The current literature is dominated by retrospective evaluation and offers limited evidence on real-world impact. Next steps should prioritize prospective, workflow-integrated studies with standardized reporting of calibration and decision utility to determine how these tools can most effectively improve care delivery and patient outcomes in early orthopedic trauma.

articles.title: Severe Exacerbation Trajectories After Inhaled Corticosteroid Initiation in Young Children With Asthma: A Longitudinal Quasi-Experimental Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICSs) are foundational therapy in pediatric asthma; however, evidence guiding initiation and response in preschool-aged children remains limited because of diagnostic uncertainty and inflammatory heterogeneity.

abstract.label: RESEARCH QUESTION
abstract.text: Among young children with asthma, is initiation of ICSs associated with changes in severe asthma exacerbation trajectories?

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal quasi-experimental study using electronic health record data from the Indiana Network for Patient Care (2010-2024). Children who initiated ICSs between 2010 and 2023 and had ≥ 12 months of observation before and after initiation were included (N = 1,396). Annualized severe asthma exacerbations (hospitalization or emergency department visits) were analyzed using piecewise generalized linear mixed-effects models to estimate preinitiation and postinitiation slopes. Recurrent exacerbations were evaluated using Andersen-Gill models, and marginal structural models were applied to address time-varying confounding.
